class ParseError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


COMPARE = ("==", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">=")
TYPES = ("int", "bool", "str")


class Parser:
    def __init__(self, tokens):
        self.tokens = tokens
        self.pos = 0

    def peek(self, ahead=0):
        return self.tokens[min(self.pos + ahead, len(self.tokens) - 1)]

    def at(self, *texts):
        tok = self.peek()
        return tok.kind in ("OP", "KEYWORD") and tok.text in texts

    def advance(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "EOF":
            self.pos += 1
        return tok

    def error(self, message):
        tok = self.peek()
        return ParseError(message, tok.line, tok.col)

    def expect(self, text):
        if not self.at(text):
            raise self.error(f"expected '{text}'")
        return self.advance()

    def expr(self):
        return self.or_expr()

    def or_expr(self):
        left = self.and_expr()
        while self.at("or"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.and_expr())
        return left

    def and_expr(self):
        left = self.not_expr()
        while self.at("and"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.not_expr())
        return left

    def not_expr(self):
        if self.at("not"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("not", self.not_expr())
        return self.compare()

    def compare(self):
        left = self.sum()
        if self.at(*COMPARE):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.sum())
            if self.at(*COMPARE):
                raise self.error("comparisons cannot be chained")
        return left

    def sum(self):
        left = self.product()
        while self.at("+", "-"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.product())
        return left

    def product(self):
        left = self.unary()
        while self.at("*", "/", "%"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.unary())
        return left

    def unary(self):
        if self.at("-"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("-", self.unary())
        return self.call()

    def call(self):
        expr = self.primary()
        while self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            args = []
            if not self.at(")"):
                args.append(self.expr())
                while self.at(","):
                    self.advance()
                    args.append(self.expr())
            self.expect(")")
            expr = Call(expr, args)
        return expr

    def primary(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind == "NUMBER":
            self.advance()
            return Num(int(tok.text))
        if tok.kind == "STRING":
            self.advance()
            return Str(tok.text)
        if tok.kind == "IDENT":
            self.advance()
            return Var(tok.text)
        if self.at("true", "false"):
            self.advance()
            return Bool(tok.text == "true")
        if self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            inner = self.expr()
            self.expect(")")
            return inner
        raise self.error("expected an expression")

    def program(self):
        stmts = []
        while self.peek().kind != "EOF":
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        return Program(stmts)

    def statement(self):
        if self.at("let"):
            return self.let_stmt()
        if self.at("print"):
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Print(value)
        if self.at("if"):
            return self.if_stmt()
        if self.at("while"):
            self.advance()
            cond = self.expr()
            return While(cond, self.block())
        if self.at("fn"):
            return self.fn_stmt()
        if self.at("return"):
            self.advance()
            value = None if self.at(";") else self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Return(value)
        nxt = self.peek(1)
        if self.peek().kind == "IDENT" and nxt.kind == "OP" and nxt.text == "=":
            name = self.advance().text
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Assign(name, value)
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return ExprStmt(value)

    def name(self):
        if self.peek().kind != "IDENT":
            raise self.error("expected a name")
        return self.advance().text

    def type_name(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "IDENT" or tok.text not in TYPES:
            raise self.error("expected a type")
        return self.advance().text

    def let_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        self.expect("=")
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return Let(name, type_, value)

    def if_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        cond = self.expr()
        then = self.block()
        else_ = None
        if self.at("else"):
            self.advance()
            else_ = self.if_stmt() if self.at("if") else self.block()
        return If(cond, then, else_)

    def block(self):
        self.expect("{")
        stmts = []
        while not self.at("}"):
            if self.peek().kind == "EOF":
                raise self.error("expected '}'")
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        self.advance()
        return Block(stmts)

    def param(self):
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        return (name, type_)

    def fn_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        self.expect("(")
        params = []
        if not self.at(")"):
            params.append(self.param())
            while self.at(","):
                self.advance()
                params.append(self.param())
        self.expect(")")
        ret = None
        if self.at("->"):
            self.advance()
            ret = self.type_name()
        return Fn(name, params, ret, self.block())


def parse_program(tokens):
    return Parser(tokens).program()


SYNC = ("let", "print", "if", "while", "fn", "return")


def parse_all(tokens):
    parser = Parser(tokens)
    stmts = []
    errors = []
    while parser.peek().kind != "EOF":
        start = parser.pos
        try:
            stmts.append(parser.statement())
        except ParseError as e:
            errors.append(str(e))
            if parser.pos == start:
                parser.advance()
            while parser.peek().kind != "EOF" and not parser.at(*SYNC):
                skipped = parser.advance()
                if skipped.kind == "OP" and skipped.text == ";":
                    break
    return Program(stmts), errors
--- hint
Drive the loop yourself: remember `start = parser.pos`, then call `parser.statement()` inside `try`. In `except ParseError as e`, append `str(e)` to the errors.
--- hint
After recording an error: if `parser.pos == start`, call `parser.advance()` once. Then loop while the next token is not `EOF` and not one of the keywords (`parser.at(*keywords)`): advance, and stop right after advancing past a `;`.
--- check case | The example from the task
parse_all(tokenize("let x = ; print 1; let = 2; print 3;"))
=> (Program([Print(Num(1)), Print(Num(3))]), ["1:9: expected an expression", "1:24: expected a name"])
--- check case | A correct program has no errors
parse_all(tokenize("let a = 1; print a;"))
=> (Program([Let("a", None, Num(1)), Print(Var("a"))]), [])
--- check case | A missing semicolon: resume at the next keyword
parse_all(tokenize("let x = 1 print x;\nprint 2;"))
=> (Program([Print(Var("x")), Print(Num(2))]), ["1:11: expected ';'"])
--- check case | Stray tokens are skipped up to the next keyword or past the next ;
parse_all(tokenize(") ) print 1; ) 5 + 2;"))
=> (Program([Print(Num(1))]), ["1:1: expected an expression", "1:14: expected an expression"])
--- check case | An error inside a block cascades to its closing brace
parse_all(tokenize("while x { let = 1; print 2; } print 3;"))
=> (Program([Print(Num(2)), Print(Num(3))]), ["1:15: expected a name", "1:29: expected an expression"])
--- check case | An error at the end of the input
parse_all(tokenize("print 1; print"))
=> (Program([Print(Num(1))]), ["1:15: expected an expression"])

+++ question | Why x == 1; is not an assignment
--- ask
The statement parser treats a statement as an assignment when its first token is an IDENT and its second token is the operator `=`. Why does it correctly parse `x == 1;` as an expression statement?
--- choice
Because it tries the assignment first and backtracks when that fails.
--- choice correct
Because the lexer's maximal munch makes `==` a single token, so the second token is `==`, not `=`.
--- choice
Because `x == 1` has no semicolon inside it.
--- choice
Because expression statements are checked before assignments.
--- why
The two-token test only works because `==` arrives as one token. If the lexer produced two `=` tokens, `x == 1;` would look like an assignment of `= 1` to `x`. Lexing and parsing are separate stages, but each relies on the other's rules.

+++ question | The tree of an else if chain
--- ask
Which tree does Comet's parser build for `if a { } else if b { } else { }`?
--- choice
`If(a, Block([]), Block([If(b, Block([]), Block([]))]))`
--- choice correct
`If(a, Block([]), If(b, Block([]), Block([])))`
--- choice
`If(a, Block([]), If(b, Block([]), None))`, with the last `else` dropped
--- choice
One `If` node holding a list of three branches
--- why
After `else`, the grammar allows either a block or another `if` statement, and the parser puts that `If` directly into `else_`. A `Block` holding an `If` is what `else { if b { } else { } }` gives: same behaviour, different tree.

+++ question | Counting top-level statements
--- ask
How many statements are in the top-level list of the `Program` that `parse_program` builds for this source?

```text
let x = 1;
while x < 3 {
    x = x + 1;
    print x;
}
print "done";
```
--- answer
3
three
--- why
The top level holds `let`, `while` and `print`. The assignment and the `print x;` belong to the `while` statement's `Block`, not to the program's list.

=== plc-06 | A tree-walking interpreter: running Comet programs
--- teach
Last lesson's parser turns a whole Comet program into a tree, and lesson 1's evaluator computed the value of an arithmetic tree. This lesson joins them: an **interpreter** that runs whole programs, with values of three types, variables, printing, `if` and `while`, and runtime errors that stop the program with a clear message. It walks the tree directly, node by node, which is why it is called a **tree-walking interpreter**. Two things wait for later lessons: blocks with their own variables (lesson 7) and functions (lesson 8). Here one set of variables serves the whole program.

### Values, and Python's surprises

Comet has three kinds of values: integers, booleans and strings. The simplest representation is Python's own `int`, `bool` and `str`. But reusing Python's values does not mean reusing Python's rules, and Python's rules differ from Comet's in ways that bite:

```python
print(isinstance(True, int), True + True, True == 1)    # True 2 True
print(type(True) is int, type(True).__name__)           # False bool
print(bool(""), bool(7))                                # False True
```

In Python, `bool` is a [[subclass of int|bool-int]], so `True + True` is 2 and `True == 1` is true. And any value can stand in for a condition: empty strings count as false, other numbers as true. Comet allows none of this. `true + true` is an error, `1 == true` is an error, because `==` needs two values of the same type, and a condition must be a real boolean. The interpreter has to enforce Comet's rules itself.

So it needs a reliable way to ask "which Comet type is this?". Test for `bool` **before** `int`, because every bool also passes the `int` test:

```python
def kind(value):
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "bool"
    if isinstance(value, int):
        return "int"
    return "str"

print(kind(True), kind(0), kind("0"))    # bool int str
```

### The environment

Variables need a place to live. The **environment** maps each variable's name to its current value. In everyday words it is a whiteboard of labelled boxes: `let` draws a new box, assignment rubs out what is in a box and writes something new, and using a variable reads its box. In Python it is a dictionary.

- `let x = e;` evaluates e, then binds `x` to the value.
- `Var("x")` looks `x` up. If there is no box called `x`, that is a runtime error: "undefined variable x".
- `x = e;` needs the box to exist already, so it catches typing mistakes: assigning to an undeclared name is a runtime error too.

In the rules, the environment is written σ (sigma), and σ[x ↦ v] means "σ, with x now mapping to v". So the rule for `let` reads: if `⟨e, σ⟩ ⇓ v`, then `⟨let x = e;, σ⟩ ⇓ σ[x ↦ v]`. Expressions now need σ too, to look up variables, and statements **produce** a new environment instead of a value.

In this lesson there is only one environment for the whole program. A `let` for a name that already exists simply replaces its value, and a block does not get variables of its own. Lesson 7 changes both, giving every block its own scope.

### Evaluating expressions, with type checks

Each operator checks the types of its operands before it computes anything:

| operator | operands | result |
|---|---|---|
| `+` | two ints, or two strings | their sum, or the strings joined |
| `-` `*` `/` `%` | two ints | an int; `/` and `%` round toward zero, and a zero divisor is an error |
| `<` `<=` `>` `>=` | two ints | a bool |
| `==` `!=` | any two values **of the same type** | a bool |
| `and` `or` | two bools | a bool, with short-circuiting (below) |
| `not` | a bool | a bool |
| `-` in front | an int | an int |

Anything else is a **runtime type error**: `"a" + 1`, `"a" < "b"`, `1 == true`, `not 5`. Because these checks happen while the program runs, Comet is so far a **dynamically checked** language, like Python. Lesson 9's type checker will reject such programs before they run.

### Short-circuit evaluation

`and` and `or` do not always evaluate their right operand. Evaluate the left one first, and check that it is a bool. For `and`, if it is `false`, the whole expression is `false`, whatever the right side would be, so the right side is **never evaluated**. For `or`, a `true` left side decides the same way. Only otherwise is the right side evaluated, checked, and returned.

This is not just a speed trick: it changes what programs do. In `n != 0 and 10 / n > 1`, the division only happens when n is not zero, so the program never divides by zero. As rules, `and` has two:

- if `⟨l, σ⟩ ⇓ false`, then `⟨l and r, σ⟩ ⇓ false`, and r is not looked at;
- if `⟨l, σ⟩ ⇓ true` and `⟨r, σ⟩ ⇓ b` for a bool b, then `⟨l and r, σ⟩ ⇓ b`.

One consequence: in `false and 1`, the `1` is never evaluated, so its type is never checked, and the result is simply `false`.

### Executing statements

Each kind of statement has its own case:

- `Let`, `Assign`: as above.
- `Print(e)`: evaluate e and write it out: an int as its digits, a bool as `true` or `false`, and a string as its characters, without quotes. Python's `print(True)` writes `True`, which is not Comet.
- `ExprStmt(e)`: evaluate e and throw the value away.
- `If(cond, then, else_)`: evaluate the condition, which must be a bool, then execute `then`, or `else_` if there is one. `else_` may be a `Block` or another `If`: executing it with the same method handles both.
- `While(cond, body)`: evaluate the condition (a bool); while it is true, execute the body and check again.
- `Block(stmts)`: execute the statements in order.

An interpreter that prints straight to the screen is hard to test. This course's interpreter appends each printed line to a list, `self.output`, so a test can read exactly what was printed. Keeping the [[input and output at the edge|io-edge]] of a program is good design in general.

### Runtime errors

A runtime error raises `CometError` with a message, and the program stops there. Output printed before the error stays printed, because it has already happened. For this program:

```text
print "start";
print 10 / (3 - 3);
print "never";
```

the output is `start`, and then the program stops with "division by zero". Comet has no way to catch errors, so a `CometError` always ends the program. Keep it separate from Python's own exceptions: a `TypeError` escaping from the interpreter is a bug in the interpreter, not an error in the Comet program.

### The rules for if and while

With σ for the environment, the rules for `if` and `while` are:

1. If `⟨c, σ⟩ ⇓ true` and `⟨s₁, σ⟩ ⇓ σ′`, then `⟨if c s₁ else s₂, σ⟩ ⇓ σ′`; the same with `false` and s₂.
2. If `⟨c, σ⟩ ⇓ false`, then `⟨while c b, σ⟩ ⇓ σ`: the loop does nothing.
3. If `⟨c, σ⟩ ⇓ true`, `⟨b, σ⟩ ⇓ σ′` and `⟨while c b, σ′⟩ ⇓ σ″`, then `⟨while c b, σ⟩ ⇓ σ″`.

Rule 3 mentions `while c b` on both sides, so the loop is defined by **unfolding**: `while c { b }` means exactly the same as `if c { b; while c { b } }`. A Python `while` loop carries out that unfolding one pass at a time, which is why it is the right way to implement Comet's `while`.

### Why the interpreter is correct

The interpreter has one case per rule, and each case does what its rule says: evaluate the parts the rule evaluates, in the same order, and combine them the same way. The proof that the interpreter produces σ′ exactly when the rules derive ⟨s, σ⟩ ⇓ σ′ is by induction on the size of the derivation: the number of rule applications in it. For a loop, that is induction on the number of passes: a loop that runs k + 1 times is rule 3 applied to a body run and a loop that runs k times.

If a program runs forever, like `while true { }`, no finite derivation exists and the interpreter never returns. No interpreter can always detect that in advance: that would solve the [[halting problem|halting]] from the Theory course.

### What it costs

The running time is proportional to the number of node evaluations the program performs: a loop that runs a million times evaluates its body's nodes a million times. Each evaluation does a constant amount of work, plus an average O(1) dictionary lookup for a variable, plus O(length) to join two strings.

The constant is large, though. Each node costs a chain of `isinstance` tests to find its case (O(k) for k kinds of node; a dictionary from class to method makes it O(1), which is what the [[visitor pattern|dispatch]] is about), a Python call, and following pointers from node to node scattered in memory. A bytecode virtual machine, lessons 15 and 16, removes most of that overhead by flattening the tree into a list of instructions first.

The space is the environment, one entry per variable, plus a recursion depth equal to the nesting depth of the tree. A loop does not deepen the recursion, because `while` runs its passes in a Python loop.

### Where it is used

- The first Lisp interpreter, in 1960, was a tree walker: the `eval` function over lists. Ruby's standard interpreter walked its trees until version 1.9 replaced it with a bytecode VM in 2007.
- Shells, template languages, configuration languages and many small languages inside larger programs are tree-walking interpreters, because they are the quickest to build and easy to extend.
- Python's `ast.literal_eval` walks a parsed tree to compute the value of a literal such as `[1, (2, "x")]`, safely, without running arbitrary code.
- Spacecraft command sequencers run uploaded scripts with small interpreters that can be checked and bounded, which you will see in the practice problems.

**Watch out:** the classic tree-walker bugs all come from Python leaking through.

- Testing `isinstance(v, int)` without first excluding `bool`, so `true + true` quietly gives 2.
- Comparing with Python's `==` before checking types, so `1 == true` is `true` instead of an error.
- Evaluating both operands of `and` and `or` before looking at the left one, which breaks programs that rely on short-circuiting.
- Using Python's truthiness, `if value:`, so `if 1 { }` runs instead of failing.
- Printing with Python's `str(True)`, which gives `True` instead of `true`.

::: context bool-int Why True is an int
Python had no booleans until version 2.3 in 2003; before that, programs used 1 and 0. PEP 285 added `True` and `False` as a subclass of `int`, equal to 1 and 0, so that all the old code, such as summing a list of conditions to count them, kept working. It was a compatibility decision. A language designed from scratch, like Comet, Java or Rust, can keep booleans and integers apart, and then the interpreter must not let Python's history leak in.
:::

::: context io-edge Keeping input and output at the edge
If a function prints, a test has to capture the screen; if it returns what it would have printed, a test can simply compare lists. So well-designed programs keep their logic pure and push printing, reading and other effects to a thin outer layer, which the Python expert course called "pure logic, thin I/O". The interpreter's `output` list is that idea: the core runs programs, and whoever calls it decides whether the lines go to a terminal, a file, or a test.
:::

::: context halting Why loops cannot be checked in advance
The halting problem asks whether a given program eventually stops on a given input. Turing proved no algorithm can answer it correctly for every program, and Comet with `while` and unbounded integers can simulate any Turing machine. So no Comet interpreter can refuse exactly the programs that loop forever. Practical systems bound the work instead: a step budget, or a time limit, which practice problem 2 adds.
:::

::: context dispatch Finding the right case quickly
A chain of `isinstance` tests tries the node kinds one by one. A dictionary from each node class to the method that handles it finds the case in one lookup: `handlers[type(node)](node)`. The visitor pattern from object-oriented design does the same with method calls, giving each node class a method that calls back the right handler. Either way, adding a new node kind means adding one entry, and missing one gives a clear error instead of a silent fall-through.
:::
--- task
The starter gives the lexer, the AST classes, the parser (`parse_program`), `CometError`, `comet_div` and `comet_mod` (Comet's division, from lesson 1), and an `Interpreter` with an environment `self.env` (a dictionary), an output list `self.output`, and `run(program)`. `run_source(source)` parses and runs a program and returns the pair `(output, error)`, where `error` is the `CometError`'s message or `None`. Write the interpreter's `execute(stmt)` and `evaluate(expr)`, with any helpers you like.

- Values are Python `int`, `bool` and `str`; `true` and `false` are `True` and `False`.
- Expressions follow the lesson's table of operators and types, with short-circuit `and` and `or`. Any other combination of types raises `CometError`. So do an undefined variable and a zero divisor.
- `Let` binds the name (replacing it if it already exists, since there is one environment in this lesson). `Assign` raises `CometError` if the name was never declared. `Print` appends one string to `self.output`: an int's digits, `true` or `false`, or the string itself. `ExprStmt` evaluates and discards. `If` and `While` need a bool condition, or raise `CometError`. A `Block` executes its statements in order, in the same environment.
- Functions come in lesson 8: raise `CometError` for `Fn`, `Return` and `Call` nodes.

For example, `run_source("let n = 3; let f = 1; while n > 1 { f = f * n; n = n - 1; } print f;")` is `(["6"], None)`, and `run_source("print 1; print 1 + true;")` returns `["1"]` with an error message.
--- starter
from dataclasses import dataclass

KEYWORDS = {"let", "fn", "return", "if", "else", "while", "print",
            "true", "false", "and", "or", "not"}
TWO_CHAR = {"==", "!=", "<=", ">=", "->"}
ONE_CHAR = set("+-*/%<>=(){},;:")
ESCAPES = {'"': '"', "\\": "\\", "n": "\n"}
DIGITS = "0123456789"
LETTERS = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ_"


@dataclass
class Token:
    kind: str
    text: str
    line: int
    col: int


class LexError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


def tokenize(source):
    tokens = []
    i = 0
    line = 1
    col = 1
    n = len(source)

    def advance(count):
        nonlocal i, line, col
        for _ in range(count):
            if source[i] == "\n":
                line += 1
                col = 1
            else:
                col += 1
            i += 1

    while i < n:
        ch = source[i]
        start_line, start_col = line, col
        if ch in " \t\r\n":
            advance(1)
        elif ch == "#":
            while i < n and source[i] != "\n":
                advance(1)
        elif ch in DIGITS:
            j = i
            while j < n and source[j] in DIGITS:
                j += 1
            tokens.append(Token("NUMBER", source[i:j], start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch in LETTERS:
            j = i
            while j < n and (source[j] in LETTERS or source[j] in DIGITS):
                j += 1
            word = source[i:j]
            kind = "KEYWORD" if word in KEYWORDS else "IDENT"
            tokens.append(Token(kind, word, start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch == '"':
            advance(1)
            chars = []
            while True:
                if i >= n or source[i] == "\n":
                    raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                c = source[i]
                if c == '"':
                    advance(1)
                    break
                if c == "\\":
                    if i + 1 >= n or source[i + 1] == "\n":
                        raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                    if source[i + 1] not in ESCAPES:
                        raise LexError("unknown escape", line, col)
                    chars.append(ESCAPES[source[i + 1]])
                    advance(2)
                else:
                    chars.append(c)
                    advance(1)
            tokens.append(Token("STRING", "".join(chars), start_line, start_col))
        elif source[i:i + 2] in TWO_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", source[i:i + 2], start_line, start_col))
            advance(2)
        elif ch in ONE_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", ch, start_line, start_col))
            advance(1)
        else:
            raise LexError(f"unexpected character {ch!r}", start_line, start_col)
    tokens.append(Token("EOF", "", line, col))
    return tokens

class ParseError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


COMPARE = ("==", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">=")
TYPES = ("int", "bool", "str")


class Parser:
    def __init__(self, tokens):
        self.tokens = tokens
        self.pos = 0

    def peek(self, ahead=0):
        return self.tokens[min(self.pos + ahead, len(self.tokens) - 1)]

    def at(self, *texts):
        tok = self.peek()
        return tok.kind in ("OP", "KEYWORD") and tok.text in texts

    def advance(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "EOF":
            self.pos += 1
        return tok

    def error(self, message):
        tok = self.peek()
        return ParseError(message, tok.line, tok.col)

    def expect(self, text):
        if not self.at(text):
            raise self.error(f"expected '{text}'")
        return self.advance()

    def expr(self):
        return self.or_expr()

    def or_expr(self):
        left = self.and_expr()
        while self.at("or"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.and_expr())
        return left

    def and_expr(self):
        left = self.not_expr()
        while self.at("and"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.not_expr())
        return left

    def not_expr(self):
        if self.at("not"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("not", self.not_expr())
        return self.compare()

    def compare(self):
        left = self.sum()
        if self.at(*COMPARE):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.sum())
            if self.at(*COMPARE):
                raise self.error("comparisons cannot be chained")
        return left

    def sum(self):
        left = self.product()
        while self.at("+", "-"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.product())
        return left

    def product(self):
        left = self.unary()
        while self.at("*", "/", "%"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.unary())
        return left

    def unary(self):
        if self.at("-"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("-", self.unary())
        return self.call()

    def call(self):
        expr = self.primary()
        while self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            args = []
            if not self.at(")"):
                args.append(self.expr())
                while self.at(","):
                    self.advance()
                    args.append(self.expr())
            self.expect(")")
            expr = Call(expr, args)
        return expr

    def primary(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind == "NUMBER":
            self.advance()
            return Num(int(tok.text))
        if tok.kind == "STRING":
            self.advance()
            return Str(tok.text)
        if tok.kind == "IDENT":
            self.advance()
            return Var(tok.text)
        if self.at("true", "false"):
            self.advance()
            return Bool(tok.text == "true")
        if self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            inner = self.expr()
            self.expect(")")
            return inner
        raise self.error("expected an expression")

    def program(self):
        stmts = []
        while self.peek().kind != "EOF":
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        return Program(stmts)

    def statement(self):
        if self.at("let"):
            return self.let_stmt()
        if self.at("print"):
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Print(value)
        if self.at("if"):
            return self.if_stmt()
        if self.at("while"):
            self.advance()
            cond = self.expr()
            return While(cond, self.block())
        if self.at("fn"):
            return self.fn_stmt()
        if self.at("return"):
            self.advance()
            value = None if self.at(";") else self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Return(value)
        nxt = self.peek(1)
        if self.peek().kind == "IDENT" and nxt.kind == "OP" and nxt.text == "=":
            name = self.advance().text
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Assign(name, value)
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return ExprStmt(value)

    def name(self):
        if self.peek().kind != "IDENT":
            raise self.error("expected a name")
        return self.advance().text

    def type_name(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "IDENT" or tok.text not in TYPES:
            raise self.error("expected a type")
        return self.advance().text

    def let_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        self.expect("=")
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return Let(name, type_, value)

    def if_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        cond = self.expr()
        then = self.block()
        else_ = None
        if self.at("else"):
            self.advance()
            else_ = self.if_stmt() if self.at("if") else self.block()
        return If(cond, then, else_)

    def block(self):
        self.expect("{")
        stmts = []
        while not self.at("}"):
            if self.peek().kind == "EOF":
                raise self.error("expected '}'")
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        self.advance()
        return Block(stmts)

    def param(self):
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        return (name, type_)

    def fn_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        self.expect("(")
        params = []
        if not self.at(")"):
            params.append(self.param())
            while self.at(","):
                self.advance()
                params.append(self.param())
        self.expect(")")
        ret = None
        if self.at("->"):
            self.advance()
            ret = self.type_name()
        return Fn(name, params, ret, self.block())


def parse_program(tokens):
    return Parser(tokens).program()


class CometError(Exception):
    pass


def comet_div(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q


def comet_mod(a, b):
    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)


class Interpreter:
    def __init__(self):
        self.env = {}
        self.output = []

    def run(self, program):
        for stmt in program.stmts:
            self.execute(stmt)

    def execute(self, stmt):
        raise CometError("execute is not written yet")

    def evaluate(self, expr):
        raise CometError("evaluate is not written yet")


def run_source(source):
    interp = Interpreter()
    try:
        interp.run(parse_program(tokenize(source)))
    except CometError as e:
        return interp.output, str(e)
    return interp.output, None

        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


COMPARE = ("==", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">=")
TYPES = ("int", "bool", "str")


class Parser:
    def __init__(self, tokens):
        self.tokens = tokens
        self.pos = 0

    def peek(self, ahead=0):
        return self.tokens[min(self.pos + ahead, len(self.tokens) - 1)]

    def at(self, *texts):
        tok = self.peek()
        return tok.kind in ("OP", "KEYWORD") and tok.text in texts

    def advance(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "EOF":
            self.pos += 1
        return tok

    def error(self, message):
        tok = self.peek()
        return ParseError(message, tok.line, tok.col)

    def expect(self, text):
        if not self.at(text):
            raise self.error(f"expected '{text}'")
        return self.advance()

    def expr(self):
        return self.or_expr()

    def or_expr(self):
        left = self.and_expr()
        while self.at("or"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.and_expr())
        return left

    def and_expr(self):
        left = self.not_expr()
        while self.at("and"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.not_expr())
        return left

    def not_expr(self):
        if self.at("not"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("not", self.not_expr())
        return self.compare()

    def compare(self):
        left = self.sum()
        if self.at(*COMPARE):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.sum())
            if self.at(*COMPARE):
                raise self.error("comparisons cannot be chained")
        return left

    def sum(self):
        left = self.product()
        while self.at("+", "-"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.product())
        return left

    def product(self):
        left = self.unary()
        while self.at("*", "/", "%"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.unary())
        return left

    def unary(self):
        if self.at("-"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("-", self.unary())
        return self.call()

    def call(self):
        expr = self.primary()
        while self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            args = []
            if not self.at(")"):
                args.append(self.expr())
                while self.at(","):
                    self.advance()
                    args.append(self.expr())
            self.expect(")")
            expr = Call(expr, args)
        return expr

    def primary(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind == "NUMBER":
            self.advance()
            return Num(int(tok.text))
        if tok.kind == "STRING":
            self.advance()
            return Str(tok.text)
        if tok.kind == "IDENT":
            self.advance()
            return Var(tok.text)
        if self.at("true", "false"):
            self.advance()
            return Bool(tok.text == "true")
        if self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            inner = self.expr()
            self.expect(")")
            return inner
        raise self.error("expected an expression")

    def program(self):
        stmts = []
        while self.peek().kind != "EOF":
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        return Program(stmts)

    def statement(self):
        if self.at("let"):
            return self.let_stmt()
        if self.at("print"):
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Print(value)
        if self.at("if"):
            return self.if_stmt()
        if self.at("while"):
            self.advance()
            cond = self.expr()
            return While(cond, self.block())
        if self.at("fn"):
            return self.fn_stmt()
        if self.at("return"):
            self.advance()
            value = None if self.at(";") else self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Return(value)
        nxt = self.peek(1)
        if self.peek().kind == "IDENT" and nxt.kind == "OP" and nxt.text == "=":
            name = self.advance().text
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Assign(name, value)
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return ExprStmt(value)

    def name(self):
        if self.peek().kind != "IDENT":
            raise self.error("expected a name")
        return self.advance().text

    def type_name(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "IDENT" or tok.text not in TYPES:
            raise self.error("expected a type")
        return self.advance().text

    def let_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        self.expect("=")
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return Let(name, type_, value)

    def if_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        cond = self.expr()
        then = self.block()
        else_ = None
        if self.at("else"):
            self.advance()
            else_ = self.if_stmt() if self.at("if") else self.block()
        return If(cond, then, else_)

    def block(self):
        self.expect("{")
        stmts = []
        while not self.at("}"):
            if self.peek().kind == "EOF":
                raise self.error("expected '}'")
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        self.advance()
        return Block(stmts)

    def param(self):
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        return (name, type_)

    def fn_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        self.expect("(")
        params = []
        if not self.at(")"):
            params.append(self.param())
            while self.at(","):
                self.advance()
                params.append(self.param())
        self.expect(")")
        ret = None
        if self.at("->"):
            self.advance()
            ret = self.type_name()
        return Fn(name, params, ret, self.block())


def parse_program(tokens):
    return Parser(tokens).program()


class CometError(Exception):
    pass


def comet_div(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q


def comet_mod(a, b):
    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)


def type_name(value):
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "bool"
    if isinstance(value, int):
        return "int"
    return "str"


def show(value):
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "true" if value else "false"
    return str(value)


class Interpreter:
    def __init__(self):
        self.env = {}
        self.output = []

    def run(self, program):
        for stmt in program.stmts:
            self.execute(stmt)

    def execute(self, stmt):
        if isinstance(stmt, Let):
            self.env[stmt.name] = self.evaluate(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Assign):
            if stmt.name not in self.env:
                raise CometError(f"assignment to undeclared variable {stmt.name}")
            self.env[stmt.name] = self.evaluate(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Print):
            self.output.append(show(self.evaluate(stmt.expr)))
        elif isinstance(stmt, ExprStmt):
            self.evaluate(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, If):
            if self.condition(stmt.cond):
                self.execute(stmt.then)
            elif stmt.else_ is not None:
                self.execute(stmt.else_)
        elif isinstance(stmt, While):
            while self.condition(stmt.cond):
                self.execute(stmt.body)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Block):
            for inner in stmt.stmts:
                self.execute(inner)
        else:
            raise CometError(f"{type(stmt).__name__} is not supported yet")

    def condition(self, expr):
        value = self.evaluate(expr)
        if not isinstance(value, bool):
            raise CometError(f"condition must be bool, not {type_name(value)}")
        return value

    def evaluate(self, expr):
        if isinstance(expr, (Num, Str, Bool)):
            return expr.value
        if isinstance(expr, Var):
            if expr.name not in self.env:
                raise CometError(f"undefined variable {expr.name}")
            return self.env[expr.name]
        if isinstance(expr, Unary):
            value = self.evaluate(expr.expr)
            if expr.op == "-":
                self.need("int", value, "-")
                return -value
            self.need("bool", value, "not")
            return not value
        if isinstance(expr, Binary):
            return self.binary(expr)
        raise CometError(f"{type(expr).__name__} is not supported yet")

    def need(self, wanted, value, op):
        if type_name(value) != wanted:
            raise CometError(f"'{op}' needs {wanted}, not {type_name(value)}")

    def binary(self, expr):
        op = expr.op
        left = self.evaluate(expr.left)
        if op in ("and", "or"):
            self.need("bool", left, op)
            if (op == "and" and not left) or (op == "or" and left):
                return left
            right = self.evaluate(expr.right)
            self.need("bool", right, op)
            return right
        right = self.evaluate(expr.right)
        if op in ("==", "!="):
            if type_name(left) != type_name(right):
                raise CometError(f"cannot compare {type_name(left)} with {type_name(right)}")
            return (left == right) == (op == "==")
        if op == "+" and type_name(left) == "str" and type_name(right) == "str":
            return left + right
        self.need("int", left, op)
        self.need("int", right, op)
        if op == "+":
            return left + right
        if op == "-":
            return left - right
        if op == "*":
            return left * right
        if op == "/":
            return comet_div(left, right)
        if op == "%":
            return comet_mod(left, right)
        if op == "<":
            return left < right
        if op == "<=":
            return left <= right
        if op == ">":
            return left > right
        return left >= right


def run_source(source):
    interp = Interpreter()
    try:
        interp.run(parse_program(tokenize(source)))
    except CometError as e:
        return interp.output, str(e)
    return interp.output, None
--- hint
Write two helpers first: `type_name(value)`, testing `bool` before `int`, and `show(value)` for printing. Then `execute` is one `isinstance` case per statement kind, and `evaluate` one case per expression kind; both end by raising `CometError` for anything else.
--- hint
For a `Binary` node, handle `and` and `or` before evaluating the right operand: evaluate the left, check it is a bool, and return it at once if it decides the answer. For every other operator, evaluate both sides, then check their types with `type_name` before computing: `==` and `!=` need equal type names, `+` accepts two ints or two strs, and the rest need two ints.
--- hint
For `If` and `While`, evaluate the condition through a small helper that raises `CometError` unless the value is a bool. `While` is a Python `while` loop around that helper and `self.execute(stmt.body)`.

+++ practice | A telemetry rule engine
--- task
A ground station raises alarms with rules written as Comet expressions, such as `temp > 80 and not venting`, checked against each reading. Write two functions (the starter gives the lexer, the expression AST classes, `parse_expr`, `CometError`, and Comet's division helpers):

- `evaluate(expr, env)`: the value of a Comet expression tree, where `env` is a dictionary from field names to values (`int`, `bool` or `str`). A `Var` looks its name up in `env`, and a missing field raises `CometError`. Everything else follows the lesson's rules exactly: the table of operators and types, short-circuit `and` and `or`, Comet's division, and `CometError` for any wrong type or a zero divisor. A `Call` raises `CometError`: rules cannot call functions.
- `rule_holds(source, reading)`: parse `source` with `parse_expr(tokenize(source))`, evaluate it with `reading` as the environment, and return the result, which must be a bool; raise `CometError` if it is not.

For example, `rule_holds("temp > 80 and not venting", {"temp": 91, "venting": False})` is `True`. Because of short-circuiting, `rule_holds("has_door and door_open", {"has_door": False})` is `False` without an error, although `door_open` is missing.
--- starter
from dataclasses import dataclass

KEYWORDS = {"let", "fn", "return", "if", "else", "while", "print",
            "true", "false", "and", "or", "not"}
TWO_CHAR = {"==", "!=", "<=", ">=", "->"}
ONE_CHAR = set("+-*/%<>=(){},;:")
ESCAPES = {'"': '"', "\\": "\\", "n": "\n"}
DIGITS = "0123456789"
LETTERS = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ_"


@dataclass
class Token:
    kind: str
    text: str
    line: int
    col: int


class LexError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


def tokenize(source):
    tokens = []
    i = 0
    line = 1
    col = 1
    n = len(source)

    def advance(count):
        nonlocal i, line, col
        for _ in range(count):
            if source[i] == "\n":
                line += 1
                col = 1
            else:
                col += 1
            i += 1

    while i < n:
        ch = source[i]
        start_line, start_col = line, col
        if ch in " \t\r\n":
            advance(1)
        elif ch == "#":
            while i < n and source[i] != "\n":
                advance(1)
        elif ch in DIGITS:
            j = i
            while j < n and source[j] in DIGITS:
                j += 1
            tokens.append(Token("NUMBER", source[i:j], start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch in LETTERS:
            j = i
            while j < n and (source[j] in LETTERS or source[j] in DIGITS):
                j += 1
            word = source[i:j]
            kind = "KEYWORD" if word in KEYWORDS else "IDENT"
            tokens.append(Token(kind, word, start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch == '"':
            advance(1)
            chars = []
            while True:
                if i >= n or source[i] == "\n":
                    raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                c = source[i]
                if c == '"':
                    advance(1)
                    break
                if c == "\\":
                    if i + 1 >= n or source[i + 1] == "\n":
                        raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                    if source[i + 1] not in ESCAPES:
                        raise LexError("unknown escape", line, col)
                    chars.append(ESCAPES[source[i + 1]])
                    advance(2)
                else:
                    chars.append(c)
                    advance(1)
            tokens.append(Token("STRING", "".join(chars), start_line, start_col))
        elif source[i:i + 2] in TWO_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", source[i:i + 2], start_line, start_col))
            advance(2)
        elif ch in ONE_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", ch, start_line, start_col))
            advance(1)
        else:
            raise LexError(f"unexpected character {ch!r}", start_line, start_col)
    tokens.append(Token("EOF", "", line, col))
    return tokens


from dataclasses import dataclass


@dataclass
class Num:
    value: int


@dataclass
class Str:
    value: str


@dataclass
class Bool:
    value: bool


@dataclass
class Var:
    name: str


@dataclass
class Unary:
    op: str
    expr: object


@dataclass
class Binary:
    op: str
    left: object
    right: object


@dataclass
class Call:
    callee: object
    args: list


class ParseError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


COMPARE = ("==", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">=")


class Parser:
    def __init__(self, tokens):
        self.tokens = tokens
        self.pos = 0

    def peek(self, ahead=0):
        return self.tokens[min(self.pos + ahead, len(self.tokens) - 1)]

    def at(self, *texts):
        tok = self.peek()
        return tok.kind in ("OP", "KEYWORD") and tok.text in texts

    def advance(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "EOF":
            self.pos += 1
        return tok

    def error(self, message):
        tok = self.peek()
        return ParseError(message, tok.line, tok.col)

    def expect(self, text):
        if not self.at(text):
            raise self.error(f"expected '{text}'")
        return self.advance()

    def expr(self):
        return self.or_expr()

    def or_expr(self):
        left = self.and_expr()
        while self.at("or"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.and_expr())
        return left

    def and_expr(self):
        left = self.not_expr()
        while self.at("and"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.not_expr())
        return left

    def not_expr(self):
        if self.at("not"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("not", self.not_expr())
        return self.compare()

    def compare(self):
        left = self.sum()
        if self.at(*COMPARE):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.sum())
            if self.at(*COMPARE):
                raise self.error("comparisons cannot be chained")
        return left

    def sum(self):
        left = self.product()
        while self.at("+", "-"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.product())
        return left

    def product(self):
        left = self.unary()
        while self.at("*", "/", "%"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.unary())
        return left

    def unary(self):
        if self.at("-"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("-", self.unary())
        return self.call()

    def call(self):
        expr = self.primary()
        while self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            args = []
            if not self.at(")"):
                args.append(self.expr())
                while self.at(","):
                    self.advance()
                    args.append(self.expr())
            self.expect(")")
            expr = Call(expr, args)
        return expr

    def primary(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind == "NUMBER":
            self.advance()
            return Num(int(tok.text))
        if tok.kind == "STRING":
            self.advance()
            return Str(tok.text)
        if tok.kind == "IDENT":
            self.advance()
            return Var(tok.text)
        if self.at("true", "false"):
            self.advance()
            return Bool(tok.text == "true")
        if self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            inner = self.expr()
            self.expect(")")
            return inner
        raise self.error("expected an expression")


def parse_expr(tokens):
    parser = Parser(tokens)
    tree = parser.expr()
    if parser.peek().kind != "EOF":
        raise parser.error("expected end of input")
    return tree

        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q


def comet_mod(a, b):
    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)


def evaluate(expr, env):
    return None


def rule_holds(source, reading):
    return False

    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col

class Parser:
    def __init__(self, tokens):
        self.tokens = tokens
        self.pos = 0

    def peek(self, ahead=0):
        return self.tokens[min(self.pos + ahead, len(self.tokens) - 1)]

    def at(self, *texts):
        tok = self.peek()
        return tok.kind in ("OP", "KEYWORD") and tok.text in texts

    def advance(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "EOF":
            self.pos += 1
        return tok

    def error(self, message):
        tok = self.peek()
        return ParseError(message, tok.line, tok.col)

    def expect(self, text):
        if not self.at(text):
            raise self.error(f"expected '{text}'")
        return self.advance()

    def expr(self):
        return self.or_expr()

    def or_expr(self):
        left = self.and_expr()
        while self.at("or"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.and_expr())
        return left

    def and_expr(self):
        left = self.not_expr()
        while self.at("and"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.not_expr())
        return left

    def not_expr(self):
        if self.at("not"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("not", self.not_expr())
        return self.compare()

    def compare(self):
        left = self.sum()
        if self.at(*COMPARE):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.sum())
            if self.at(*COMPARE):
                raise self.error("comparisons cannot be chained")
        return left

    def sum(self):
        left = self.product()
        while self.at("+", "-"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.product())
        return left

    def product(self):
        left = self.unary()
        while self.at("*", "/", "%"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.unary())
        return left

    def unary(self):
        if self.at("-"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("-", self.unary())
        return self.call()

    def call(self):
        expr = self.primary()
        while self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            args = []
            if not self.at(")"):
                args.append(self.expr())
                while self.at(","):
                    self.advance()
                    args.append(self.expr())
            self.expect(")")
            expr = Call(expr, args)
        return expr

    def primary(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind == "NUMBER":
            self.advance()
            return Num(int(tok.text))
        if tok.kind == "STRING":
            self.advance()
            return Str(tok.text)
        if tok.kind == "IDENT":
            self.advance()
            return Var(tok.text)
        if self.at("true", "false"):
            self.advance()
            return Bool(tok.text == "true")
        if self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            inner = self.expr()
            self.expect(")")
            return inner
        raise self.error("expected an expression")


def parse_expr(tokens):
    parser = Parser(tokens)
    tree = parser.expr()
    if parser.peek().kind != "EOF":
        raise parser.error("expected end of input")
    return tree


class CometError(Exception):
    pass


def comet_div(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q


def comet_mod(a, b):
    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)


def type_name(value):
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "bool"
    if isinstance(value, int):
        return "int"
    return "str"


def show(value):
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "true" if value else "false"
    return str(value)


def need(wanted, value, op):
    if type_name(value) != wanted:
        raise CometError(f"'{op}' needs {wanted}, not {type_name(value)}")


ARITHMETIC = {
    "-": lambda a, b: a - b,
    "*": lambda a, b: a * b,
    "/": comet_div,
    "%": comet_mod,
    "<": lambda a, b: a < b,
    "<=": lambda a, b: a <= b,
    ">": lambda a, b: a > b,
    ">=": lambda a, b: a >= b,
}


def evaluate(expr, env):
    if isinstance(expr, (Num, Str, Bool)):
        return expr.value
    if isinstance(expr, Var):
        if expr.name not in env:
            raise CometError(f"the reading has no field {expr.name}")
        return env[expr.name]
    if isinstance(expr, Unary):
        value = evaluate(expr.expr, env)
        if expr.op == "-":
            need("int", value, "-")
            return -value
        need("bool", value, "not")
        return not value
    if not isinstance(expr, Binary):
        raise CometError("rules cannot call functions")
    op = expr.op
    left = evaluate(expr.left, env)
    if op in ("and", "or"):
        need("bool", left, op)
        if (op == "and" and not left) or (op == "or" and left):
            return left
        right = evaluate(expr.right, env)
        need("bool", right, op)
        return right
    right = evaluate(expr.right, env)
    if op in ("==", "!="):
        if type_name(left) != type_name(right):
            raise CometError(f"cannot compare {type_name(left)} with {type_name(right)}")
        return (left == right) == (op == "==")
    if op == "+" and type_name(left) == "str" and type_name(right) == "str":
        return left + right
    need("int", left, op)
    need("int", right, op)
    if op == "+":
        return left + right
    return ARITHMETIC[op](left, right)


def rule_holds(source, reading):
    result = evaluate(parse_expr(tokenize(source)), reading)
    if type_name(result) != "bool":
        raise CometError("a rule must give a bool")
    return result
--- hint
This is the lesson's `evaluate` with the environment passed in as a parameter instead of stored on an object. Start with a `type_name` helper that tests `bool` before `int`, and check types before every operation.
--- hint
For `and` and `or`, evaluate and check the left operand, and return it straight away when it decides the answer; only then evaluate the right one. In `rule_holds`, check the final value's type with the same helper.
--- check case | The first example from the task
rule_holds("temp > 80 and not venting", {"temp": 91, "venting": False})
=> True
--- check case | Short-circuiting skips a missing field
(rule_holds("has_door and door_open", {"has_door": False}), rule_holds("safe or t / 0 > 1", {"safe": True, "t": 5}))
=> (False, True)
--- check case | Strings, equality and arithmetic in rules
(rule_holds('mode == "burn" and fuel * 2 >= limit', {"mode": "burn", "fuel": 30, "limit": 60}), rule_holds("-7 / 2 == -3 and -7 % 2 == -1", {}))
=> (True, True)
--- check case | evaluate returns values of every type
(evaluate(parse_expr(tokenize('"id-" + name')), {"name": "x7"}), evaluate(parse_expr(tokenize("a * (b + 1)")), {"a": 3, "b": 4}), evaluate(parse_expr(tokenize("not ok")), {"ok": True}))
=> ("id-x7", 15, False)
--- check test | Missing fields, wrong types and zero divisors raise CometError
all(raises(CometError, lambda s=s: rule_holds(s, {"t": 5, "on": True, "name": "a"})) for s in ["missing > 1", "t + on > 1", "on == 1", "name < \"b\"", "t / (t - 5) > 0", "not t", "on and t", "f(t)"])
--- check test | A rule must give a bool
raises(CometError, lambda: rule_holds("t + 1", {"t": 1})) and raises(CometError, lambda: rule_holds('"yes"', {}))

+++ practice | A fuel budget for scripts
--- task
A spacecraft must never let an uploaded script run forever. Its interpreter gives each run a **fuel** budget and stops the script when the fuel runs out, the way blockchains charge "gas" for every step. Write `run_with_fuel(source, fuel)` using the starter's working interpreter (the lesson's, complete), for example by subclassing `Interpreter`.

- Every statement that `execute` runs, except a `Block`, costs 1 unit, charged before the statement does anything.
- Every evaluation of a `while` loop's condition costs 1 unit, charged just before the condition is evaluated.
- If a charge would make the units used exceed `fuel`, raise `CometError("out of fuel")` instead, without charging.

Return a tuple `(output, used, error)`: the printed lines, the units used, and the `CometError`'s message (for running out of fuel or any other runtime error) or `None`.

For example, `let i = 0; while i < 3 { i = i + 1; }` costs 9 units: 1 for the `let`, 1 for the `while` statement, 4 condition checks (the last one is false) and 3 assignments. So `run_with_fuel` of it with fuel 9 is `([], 9, None)`, and with fuel 8 it is `([], 8, "out of fuel")`.
--- starter
from dataclasses import dataclass

KEYWORDS = {"let", "fn", "return", "if", "else", "while", "print",
            "true", "false", "and", "or", "not"}
TWO_CHAR = {"==", "!=", "<=", ">=", "->"}
ONE_CHAR = set("+-*/%<>=(){},;:")
ESCAPES = {'"': '"', "\\": "\\", "n": "\n"}
DIGITS = "0123456789"
LETTERS = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ_"


@dataclass
class Token:
    kind: str
    text: str
    line: int
    col: int


class LexError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


def tokenize(source):
    tokens = []
    i = 0
    line = 1
    col = 1
    n = len(source)

    def advance(count):
        nonlocal i, line, col
        for _ in range(count):
            if source[i] == "\n":
                line += 1
                col = 1
            else:
                col += 1
            i += 1

    while i < n:
        ch = source[i]
        start_line, start_col = line, col
        if ch in " \t\r\n":
            advance(1)
        elif ch == "#":
            while i < n and source[i] != "\n":
                advance(1)
        elif ch in DIGITS:
            j = i
            while j < n and source[j] in DIGITS:
                j += 1
            tokens.append(Token("NUMBER", source[i:j], start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch in LETTERS:
            j = i
            while j < n and (source[j] in LETTERS or source[j] in DIGITS):
                j += 1
            word = source[i:j]
            kind = "KEYWORD" if word in KEYWORDS else "IDENT"
            tokens.append(Token(kind, word, start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch == '"':
            advance(1)
            chars = []
            while True:
                if i >= n or source[i] == "\n":
                    raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                c = source[i]
                if c == '"':
                    advance(1)
                    break
                if c == "\\":
                    if i + 1 >= n or source[i + 1] == "\n":
                        raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                    if source[i + 1] not in ESCAPES:
                        raise LexError("unknown escape", line, col)
                    chars.append(ESCAPES[source[i + 1]])
                    advance(2)
                else:
                    chars.append(c)
                    advance(1)
            tokens.append(Token("STRING", "".join(chars), start_line, start_col))
        elif source[i:i + 2] in TWO_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", source[i:i + 2], start_line, start_col))
            advance(2)
        elif ch in ONE_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", ch, start_line, start_col))
            advance(1)
        else:
            raise LexError(f"unexpected character {ch!r}", start_line, start_col)
    tokens.append(Token("EOF", "", line, col))
    return tokens

class ParseError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


COMPARE = ("==", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">=")
TYPES = ("int", "bool", "str")


class Parser:
    def __init__(self, tokens):
        self.tokens = tokens
        self.pos = 0

    def peek(self, ahead=0):
        return self.tokens[min(self.pos + ahead, len(self.tokens) - 1)]

    def at(self, *texts):
        tok = self.peek()
        return tok.kind in ("OP", "KEYWORD") and tok.text in texts

    def advance(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "EOF":
            self.pos += 1
        return tok

    def error(self, message):
        tok = self.peek()
        return ParseError(message, tok.line, tok.col)

    def expect(self, text):
        if not self.at(text):
            raise self.error(f"expected '{text}'")
        return self.advance()

    def expr(self):
        return self.or_expr()

    def or_expr(self):
        left = self.and_expr()
        while self.at("or"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.and_expr())
        return left

    def and_expr(self):
        left = self.not_expr()
        while self.at("and"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.not_expr())
        return left

    def not_expr(self):
        if self.at("not"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("not", self.not_expr())
        return self.compare()

    def compare(self):
        left = self.sum()
        if self.at(*COMPARE):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.sum())
            if self.at(*COMPARE):
                raise self.error("comparisons cannot be chained")
        return left

    def sum(self):
        left = self.product()
        while self.at("+", "-"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.product())
        return left

    def product(self):
        left = self.unary()
        while self.at("*", "/", "%"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.unary())
        return left

    def unary(self):
        if self.at("-"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("-", self.unary())
        return self.call()

    def call(self):
        expr = self.primary()
        while self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            args = []
            if not self.at(")"):
                args.append(self.expr())
                while self.at(","):
                    self.advance()
                    args.append(self.expr())
            self.expect(")")
            expr = Call(expr, args)
        return expr

    def primary(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind == "NUMBER":
            self.advance()
            return Num(int(tok.text))
        if tok.kind == "STRING":
            self.advance()
            return Str(tok.text)
        if tok.kind == "IDENT":
            self.advance()
            return Var(tok.text)
        if self.at("true", "false"):
            self.advance()
            return Bool(tok.text == "true")
        if self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            inner = self.expr()
            self.expect(")")
            return inner
        raise self.error("expected an expression")

    def program(self):
        stmts = []
        while self.peek().kind != "EOF":
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        return Program(stmts)

    def statement(self):
        if self.at("let"):
            return self.let_stmt()
        if self.at("print"):
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Print(value)
        if self.at("if"):
            return self.if_stmt()
        if self.at("while"):
            self.advance()
            cond = self.expr()
            return While(cond, self.block())
        if self.at("fn"):
            return self.fn_stmt()
        if self.at("return"):
            self.advance()
            value = None if self.at(";") else self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Return(value)
        nxt = self.peek(1)
        if self.peek().kind == "IDENT" and nxt.kind == "OP" and nxt.text == "=":
            name = self.advance().text
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Assign(name, value)
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return ExprStmt(value)

    def name(self):
        if self.peek().kind != "IDENT":
            raise self.error("expected a name")
        return self.advance().text

    def type_name(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "IDENT" or tok.text not in TYPES:
            raise self.error("expected a type")
        return self.advance().text

    def let_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        self.expect("=")
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return Let(name, type_, value)

    def if_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        cond = self.expr()
        then = self.block()
        else_ = None
        if self.at("else"):
            self.advance()
            else_ = self.if_stmt() if self.at("if") else self.block()
        return If(cond, then, else_)

    def block(self):
        self.expect("{")
        stmts = []
        while not self.at("}"):
            if self.peek().kind == "EOF":
                raise self.error("expected '}'")
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        self.advance()
        return Block(stmts)

    def param(self):
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        return (name, type_)

    def fn_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        self.expect("(")
        params = []
        if not self.at(")"):
            params.append(self.param())
            while self.at(","):
                self.advance()
                params.append(self.param())
        self.expect(")")
        ret = None
        if self.at("->"):
            self.advance()
            ret = self.type_name()
        return Fn(name, params, ret, self.block())


def parse_program(tokens):
    return Parser(tokens).program()


class CometError(Exception):
    pass


def type_name(value):
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "bool"
    if isinstance(value, int):
        return "int"
    return "str"


def show(value):
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "true" if value else "false"
    return str(value)


def comet_div(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q


def comet_mod(a, b):
    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)


class Interpreter:
    def __init__(self):
        self.env = {}
        self.output = []

    def run(self, program):
        for stmt in program.stmts:
            self.execute(stmt)

    def execute(self, stmt):
        if isinstance(stmt, Let):
            self.env[stmt.name] = self.evaluate(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Assign):
            if stmt.name not in self.env:
                raise CometError(f"assignment to undeclared variable {stmt.name}")
            self.env[stmt.name] = self.evaluate(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Print):
            self.output.append(show(self.evaluate(stmt.expr)))
        elif isinstance(stmt, ExprStmt):
            self.evaluate(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, If):
            if self.condition(stmt.cond):
                self.execute(stmt.then)
            elif stmt.else_ is not None:
                self.execute(stmt.else_)
        elif isinstance(stmt, While):
            while self.condition(stmt.cond):
                self.execute(stmt.body)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Block):
            for inner in stmt.stmts:
                self.execute(inner)
        else:
            raise CometError(f"{type(stmt).__name__} is not supported yet")

    def condition(self, expr):
        value = self.evaluate(expr)
        if not isinstance(value, bool):
            raise CometError(f"condition must be bool, not {type_name(value)}")
        return value

    def evaluate(self, expr):
        if isinstance(expr, (Num, Str, Bool)):
            return expr.value
        if isinstance(expr, Var):
            if expr.name not in self.env:
                raise CometError(f"undefined variable {expr.name}")
            return self.env[expr.name]
        if isinstance(expr, Unary):
            value = self.evaluate(expr.expr)
            if expr.op == "-":
                self.need("int", value, "-")
                return -value
            self.need("bool", value, "not")
            return not value
        if isinstance(expr, Binary):
            return self.binary(expr)
        raise CometError(f"{type(expr).__name__} is not supported yet")

    def need(self, wanted, value, op):
        if type_name(value) != wanted:
            raise CometError(f"'{op}' needs {wanted}, not {type_name(value)}")

    def binary(self, expr):
        op = expr.op
        left = self.evaluate(expr.left)
        if op in ("and", "or"):
            self.need("bool", left, op)
            if (op == "and" and not left) or (op == "or" and left):
                return left
            right = self.evaluate(expr.right)
            self.need("bool", right, op)
            return right
        right = self.evaluate(expr.right)
        if op in ("==", "!="):
            if type_name(left) != type_name(right):
                raise CometError(f"cannot compare {type_name(left)} with {type_name(right)}")
            return (left == right) == (op == "==")
        if op == "+" and type_name(left) == "str" and type_name(right) == "str":
            return left + right
        self.need("int", left, op)
        self.need("int", right, op)
        if op == "+":
            return left + right
        if op == "-":
            return left - right
        if op == "*":
            return left * right
        if op == "/":
            return comet_div(left, right)
        if op == "%":
            return comet_mod(left, right)
        if op == "<":
            return left < right
        if op == "<=":
            return left <= right
        if op == ">":
            return left > right
        return left >= right


def run_with_fuel(source, fuel):
    return [], 0, None
