class ParseError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


COMPARE = ("==", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">=")
TYPES = ("int", "bool", "str")


class Parser:
    def __init__(self, tokens):
        self.tokens = tokens
        self.pos = 0

    def peek(self, ahead=0):
        return self.tokens[min(self.pos + ahead, len(self.tokens) - 1)]

    def at(self, *texts):
        tok = self.peek()
        return tok.kind in ("OP", "KEYWORD") and tok.text in texts

    def advance(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "EOF":
            self.pos += 1
        return tok

    def error(self, message):
        tok = self.peek()
        return ParseError(message, tok.line, tok.col)

    def expect(self, text):
        if not self.at(text):
            raise self.error(f"expected '{text}'")
        return self.advance()

    def expr(self):
        return self.or_expr()

    def or_expr(self):
        left = self.and_expr()
        while self.at("or"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.and_expr())
        return left

    def and_expr(self):
        left = self.not_expr()
        while self.at("and"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.not_expr())
        return left

    def not_expr(self):
        if self.at("not"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("not", self.not_expr())
        return self.compare()

    def compare(self):
        left = self.sum()
        if self.at(*COMPARE):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.sum())
            if self.at(*COMPARE):
                raise self.error("comparisons cannot be chained")
        return left

    def sum(self):
        left = self.product()
        while self.at("+", "-"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.product())
        return left

    def product(self):
        left = self.unary()
        while self.at("*", "/", "%"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.unary())
        return left

    def unary(self):
        if self.at("-"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("-", self.unary())
        return self.call()

    def call(self):
        expr = self.primary()
        while self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            args = []
            if not self.at(")"):
                args.append(self.expr())
                while self.at(","):
                    self.advance()
                    args.append(self.expr())
            self.expect(")")
            expr = Call(expr, args)
        return expr

    def primary(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind == "NUMBER":
            self.advance()
            return Num(int(tok.text))
        if tok.kind == "STRING":
            self.advance()
            return Str(tok.text)
        if tok.kind == "IDENT":
            self.advance()
            return Var(tok.text)
        if self.at("true", "false"):
            self.advance()
            return Bool(tok.text == "true")
        if self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            inner = self.expr()
            self.expect(")")
            return inner
        raise self.error("expected an expression")

    def program(self):
        stmts = []
        while self.peek().kind != "EOF":
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        return Program(stmts)

    def statement(self):
        if self.at("let"):
            return self.let_stmt()
        if self.at("print"):
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Print(value)
        if self.at("if"):
            return self.if_stmt()
        if self.at("while"):
            self.advance()
            cond = self.expr()
            return While(cond, self.block())
        if self.at("fn"):
            return self.fn_stmt()
        if self.at("return"):
            self.advance()
            value = None if self.at(";") else self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Return(value)
        nxt = self.peek(1)
        if self.peek().kind == "IDENT" and nxt.kind == "OP" and nxt.text == "=":
            name = self.advance().text
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Assign(name, value)
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return ExprStmt(value)

    def name(self):
        if self.peek().kind != "IDENT":
            raise self.error("expected a name")
        return self.advance().text

    def type_name(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "IDENT" or tok.text not in TYPES:
            raise self.error("expected a type")
        return self.advance().text

    def let_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        self.expect("=")
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return Let(name, type_, value)

    def if_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        cond = self.expr()
        then = self.block()
        else_ = None
        if self.at("else"):
            self.advance()
            else_ = self.if_stmt() if self.at("if") else self.block()
        return If(cond, then, else_)

    def block(self):
        self.expect("{")
        stmts = []
        while not self.at("}"):
            if self.peek().kind == "EOF":
                raise self.error("expected '}'")
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        self.advance()
        return Block(stmts)

    def param(self):
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        return (name, type_)

    def fn_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        self.expect("(")
        params = []
        if not self.at(")"):
            params.append(self.param())
            while self.at(","):
                self.advance()
                params.append(self.param())
        self.expect(")")
        ret = None
        if self.at("->"):
            self.advance()
            ret = self.type_name()
        return Fn(name, params, ret, self.block())


def parse_program(tokens):
    return Parser(tokens).program()


class CometError(Exception):
    pass


def type_name(value):
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "bool"
    if isinstance(value, int):
        return "int"
    return "str"


def show(value):
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "true" if value else "false"
    return str(value)


def comet_div(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q


def comet_mod(a, b):
    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)


class Interpreter:
    def __init__(self):
        self.env = {}
        self.output = []

    def run(self, program):
        for stmt in program.stmts:
            self.execute(stmt)

    def execute(self, stmt):
        if isinstance(stmt, Let):
            self.env[stmt.name] = self.evaluate(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Assign):
            if stmt.name not in self.env:
                raise CometError(f"assignment to undeclared variable {stmt.name}")
            self.env[stmt.name] = self.evaluate(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Print):
            self.output.append(show(self.evaluate(stmt.expr)))
        elif isinstance(stmt, ExprStmt):
            self.evaluate(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, If):
            if self.condition(stmt.cond):
                self.execute(stmt.then)
            elif stmt.else_ is not None:
                self.execute(stmt.else_)
        elif isinstance(stmt, While):
            while self.condition(stmt.cond):
                self.execute(stmt.body)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Block):
            for inner in stmt.stmts:
                self.execute(inner)
        else:
            raise CometError(f"{type(stmt).__name__} is not supported yet")

    def condition(self, expr):
        value = self.evaluate(expr)
        if not isinstance(value, bool):
            raise CometError(f"condition must be bool, not {type_name(value)}")
        return value

    def evaluate(self, expr):
        if isinstance(expr, (Num, Str, Bool)):
            return expr.value
        if isinstance(expr, Var):
            if expr.name not in self.env:
                raise CometError(f"undefined variable {expr.name}")
            return self.env[expr.name]
        if isinstance(expr, Unary):
            value = self.evaluate(expr.expr)
            if expr.op == "-":
                self.need("int", value, "-")
                return -value
            self.need("bool", value, "not")
            return not value
        if isinstance(expr, Binary):
            return self.binary(expr)
        raise CometError(f"{type(expr).__name__} is not supported yet")

    def need(self, wanted, value, op):
        if type_name(value) != wanted:
            raise CometError(f"'{op}' needs {wanted}, not {type_name(value)}")

    def binary(self, expr):
        op = expr.op
        left = self.evaluate(expr.left)
        if op in ("and", "or"):
            self.need("bool", left, op)
            if (op == "and" and not left) or (op == "or" and left):
                return left
            right = self.evaluate(expr.right)
            self.need("bool", right, op)
            return right
        right = self.evaluate(expr.right)
        if op in ("==", "!="):
            if type_name(left) != type_name(right):
                raise CometError(f"cannot compare {type_name(left)} with {type_name(right)}")
            return (left == right) == (op == "==")
        if op == "+" and type_name(left) == "str" and type_name(right) == "str":
            return left + right
        self.need("int", left, op)
        self.need("int", right, op)
        if op == "+":
            return left + right
        if op == "-":
            return left - right
        if op == "*":
            return left * right
        if op == "/":
            return comet_div(left, right)
        if op == "%":
            return comet_mod(left, right)
        if op == "<":
            return left < right
        if op == "<=":
            return left <= right
        if op == ">":
            return left > right
        return left >= right


def run_source(source):
    interp = Interpreter()
    try:
        interp.run(parse_program(tokenize(source)))
    except CometError as e:
        return interp.output, str(e)
    return interp.output, None
--- hint
Read `binary` from the top. At which moment is the right operand evaluated, and has the code looked at the left operand's value yet?
--- hint
For `and` and `or`, the right operand may only be evaluated after the left one has been checked and found not to decide the answer. Move the evaluation of the right operand so that it happens inside the `and`/`or` branch after that test, and, for every other operator, after that branch.
--- check case | The first example from the task
run_source("let n = 0; print n != 0 and 10 / n > 1;")
=> (["false"], None)
--- check case | The second example from the task
run_source("print true or missing;")
=> (["true"], None)
--- check case | The right operand still runs when it is needed
run_source("let n = 5; print n != 0 and 10 / n > 1; print false or n == 5;")
=> (["true", "true"], None)
--- check test | The right operand's type is still checked when it runs
run_source("print true and 1;")[1] is not None and run_source("print false or 0;")[1] is not None
--- check case | Other operators are unchanged
run_source('print 1 + 2 * 3; print "a" + "b"; print 3 == 3;')
=> (["7", "ab", "true"], None)

+++ practice | break and continue
--- task
Add `break;` and `continue;` to Comet. The starter already lexes the two new keywords and parses them into `Break()` and `Continue()` statement nodes. Its interpreter is the lesson's, complete, but it rejects the new nodes. Change the interpreter so that:

- `break;` ends the innermost `while` loop that is running; execution goes on with the statement after that loop.
- `continue;` ends the current pass of the innermost loop; execution goes on with the next check of that loop's condition.
- `break;` or `continue;` when no loop is running raises `CometError`, even inside an `if`.

These statements jump out of any number of nested blocks and `if`s at once, so an ordinary return value cannot carry them up. The usual technique is to raise a private Python exception (for example `class BreakSignal(Exception)`) where the statement runs, and catch it in the code that runs the loop. Keep a count of the loops that are running to detect the error case.

For example, `run_source("let i = 0; while i < 5 { i = i + 1; if i % 2 == 0 { continue; } print i; }")` is `(["1", "3", "5"], None)`.
--- starter
from dataclasses import dataclass

KEYWORDS = {"let", "fn", "return", "if", "else", "while", "print",
            "true", "false", "and", "or", "not"}
TWO_CHAR = {"==", "!=", "<=", ">=", "->"}
ONE_CHAR = set("+-*/%<>=(){},;:")
ESCAPES = {'"': '"', "\\": "\\", "n": "\n"}
DIGITS = "0123456789"
LETTERS = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ_"


@dataclass
class Token:
    kind: str
    text: str
    line: int
    col: int


class LexError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


def tokenize(source):
    tokens = []
    i = 0
    line = 1
    col = 1
    n = len(source)

    def advance(count):
        nonlocal i, line, col
        for _ in range(count):
            if source[i] == "\n":
                line += 1
                col = 1
            else:
                col += 1
            i += 1

    while i < n:
        ch = source[i]
        start_line, start_col = line, col
        if ch in " \t\r\n":
            advance(1)
        elif ch == "#":
            while i < n and source[i] != "\n":
                advance(1)
        elif ch in DIGITS:
            j = i
            while j < n and source[j] in DIGITS:
                j += 1
            tokens.append(Token("NUMBER", source[i:j], start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch in LETTERS:
            j = i
            while j < n and (source[j] in LETTERS or source[j] in DIGITS):
                j += 1
            word = source[i:j]
            kind = "KEYWORD" if word in KEYWORDS else "IDENT"
            tokens.append(Token(kind, word, start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch == '"':
            advance(1)
            chars = []
            while True:
                if i >= n or source[i] == "\n":
                    raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                c = source[i]
                if c == '"':
                    advance(1)
                    break
                if c == "\\":
                    if i + 1 >= n or source[i + 1] == "\n":
                        raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                    if source[i + 1] not in ESCAPES:
                        raise LexError("unknown escape", line, col)
                    chars.append(ESCAPES[source[i + 1]])
                    advance(2)
                else:
                    chars.append(c)
                    advance(1)
            tokens.append(Token("STRING", "".join(chars), start_line, start_col))
        elif source[i:i + 2] in TWO_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", source[i:i + 2], start_line, start_col))
            advance(2)
        elif ch in ONE_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", ch, start_line, start_col))
            advance(1)
        else:
            raise LexError(f"unexpected character {ch!r}", start_line, start_col)
    tokens.append(Token("EOF", "", line, col))
    return tokens


KEYWORDS.update({"break", "continue"})

class ParseError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


COMPARE = ("==", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">=")
TYPES = ("int", "bool", "str")


class Parser:
    def __init__(self, tokens):
        self.tokens = tokens
        self.pos = 0

    def peek(self, ahead=0):
        return self.tokens[min(self.pos + ahead, len(self.tokens) - 1)]

    def at(self, *texts):
        tok = self.peek()
        return tok.kind in ("OP", "KEYWORD") and tok.text in texts

    def advance(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "EOF":
            self.pos += 1
        return tok

    def error(self, message):
        tok = self.peek()
        return ParseError(message, tok.line, tok.col)

    def expect(self, text):
        if not self.at(text):
            raise self.error(f"expected '{text}'")
        return self.advance()

    def expr(self):
        return self.or_expr()

    def or_expr(self):
        left = self.and_expr()
        while self.at("or"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.and_expr())
        return left

    def and_expr(self):
        left = self.not_expr()
        while self.at("and"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.not_expr())
        return left

    def not_expr(self):
        if self.at("not"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("not", self.not_expr())
        return self.compare()

    def compare(self):
        left = self.sum()
        if self.at(*COMPARE):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.sum())
            if self.at(*COMPARE):
                raise self.error("comparisons cannot be chained")
        return left

    def sum(self):
        left = self.product()
        while self.at("+", "-"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.product())
        return left

    def product(self):
        left = self.unary()
        while self.at("*", "/", "%"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.unary())
        return left

    def unary(self):
        if self.at("-"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("-", self.unary())
        return self.call()

    def call(self):
        expr = self.primary()
        while self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            args = []
            if not self.at(")"):
                args.append(self.expr())
                while self.at(","):
                    self.advance()
                    args.append(self.expr())
            self.expect(")")
            expr = Call(expr, args)
        return expr

    def primary(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind == "NUMBER":
            self.advance()
            return Num(int(tok.text))
        if tok.kind == "STRING":
            self.advance()
            return Str(tok.text)
        if tok.kind == "IDENT":
            self.advance()
            return Var(tok.text)
        if self.at("true", "false"):
            self.advance()
            return Bool(tok.text == "true")
        if self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            inner = self.expr()
            self.expect(")")
            return inner
        raise self.error("expected an expression")

    def program(self):
        stmts = []
        while self.peek().kind != "EOF":
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        return Program(stmts)

    def statement(self):
        if self.at("let"):
            return self.let_stmt()
        if self.at("print"):
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Print(value)
        if self.at("if"):
            return self.if_stmt()
        if self.at("while"):
            self.advance()
            cond = self.expr()
            return While(cond, self.block())
        if self.at("fn"):
            return self.fn_stmt()
        if self.at("return"):
            self.advance()
            value = None if self.at(";") else self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Return(value)
        nxt = self.peek(1)
        if self.peek().kind == "IDENT" and nxt.kind == "OP" and nxt.text == "=":
            name = self.advance().text
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Assign(name, value)
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return ExprStmt(value)

    def name(self):
        if self.peek().kind != "IDENT":
            raise self.error("expected a name")
        return self.advance().text

    def type_name(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "IDENT" or tok.text not in TYPES:
            raise self.error("expected a type")
        return self.advance().text

    def let_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        self.expect("=")
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return Let(name, type_, value)

    def if_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        cond = self.expr()
        then = self.block()
        else_ = None
        if self.at("else"):
            self.advance()
            else_ = self.if_stmt() if self.at("if") else self.block()
        return If(cond, then, else_)

    def block(self):
        self.expect("{")
        stmts = []
        while not self.at("}"):
            if self.peek().kind == "EOF":
                raise self.error("expected '}'")
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        self.advance()
        return Block(stmts)

    def param(self):
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        return (name, type_)

    def fn_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        self.expect("(")
        params = []
        if not self.at(")"):
            params.append(self.param())
            while self.at(","):
                self.advance()
                params.append(self.param())
        self.expect(")")
        ret = None
        if self.at("->"):
            self.advance()
            ret = self.type_name()
        return Fn(name, params, ret, self.block())


def parse_program(tokens):
    return Parser(tokens).program()


class LoopParser(Parser):
    def statement(self):
        if self.at("break", "continue"):
            word = self.advance().text
            self.expect(";")
            return Break() if word == "break" else Continue()
        return super().statement()


def parse_program(tokens):
    return LoopParser(tokens).program()


class CometError(Exception):
    pass


def type_name(value):
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "bool"
    if isinstance(value, int):
        return "int"
    return "str"


def show(value):
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "true" if value else "false"
    return str(value)


def comet_div(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q


def comet_mod(a, b):
    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)


class Interpreter:
    def __init__(self):
        self.env = {}
        self.output = []

    def run(self, program):
        for stmt in program.stmts:
            self.execute(stmt)

    def execute(self, stmt):
        if isinstance(stmt, Let):
            self.env[stmt.name] = self.evaluate(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Assign):
            if stmt.name not in self.env:
                raise CometError(f"assignment to undeclared variable {stmt.name}")
            self.env[stmt.name] = self.evaluate(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Print):
            self.output.append(show(self.evaluate(stmt.expr)))
        elif isinstance(stmt, ExprStmt):
            self.evaluate(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, If):
            if self.condition(stmt.cond):
                self.execute(stmt.then)
            elif stmt.else_ is not None:
                self.execute(stmt.else_)
        elif isinstance(stmt, While):
            while self.condition(stmt.cond):
                self.execute(stmt.body)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Block):
            for inner in stmt.stmts:
                self.execute(inner)
        else:
            raise CometError(f"{type(stmt).__name__} is not supported yet")

    def condition(self, expr):
        value = self.evaluate(expr)
        if not isinstance(value, bool):
            raise CometError(f"condition must be bool, not {type_name(value)}")
        return value

    def evaluate(self, expr):
        if isinstance(expr, (Num, Str, Bool)):
            return expr.value
        if isinstance(expr, Var):
            if expr.name not in self.env:
                raise CometError(f"undefined variable {expr.name}")
            return self.env[expr.name]
        if isinstance(expr, Unary):
            value = self.evaluate(expr.expr)
            if expr.op == "-":
                self.need("int", value, "-")
                return -value
            self.need("bool", value, "not")
            return not value
        if isinstance(expr, Binary):
            return self.binary(expr)
        raise CometError(f"{type(expr).__name__} is not supported yet")

    def need(self, wanted, value, op):
        if type_name(value) != wanted:
            raise CometError(f"'{op}' needs {wanted}, not {type_name(value)}")

    def binary(self, expr):
        op = expr.op
        left = self.evaluate(expr.left)
        if op in ("and", "or"):
            self.need("bool", left, op)
            if (op == "and" and not left) or (op == "or" and left):
                return left
            right = self.evaluate(expr.right)
            self.need("bool", right, op)
            return right
        right = self.evaluate(expr.right)
        if op in ("==", "!="):
            if type_name(left) != type_name(right):
                raise CometError(f"cannot compare {type_name(left)} with {type_name(right)}")
            return (left == right) == (op == "==")
        if op == "+" and type_name(left) == "str" and type_name(right) == "str":
            return left + right
        self.need("int", left, op)
        self.need("int", right, op)
        if op == "+":
            return left + right
        if op == "-":
            return left - right
        if op == "*":
            return left * right
        if op == "/":
            return comet_div(left, right)
        if op == "%":
            return comet_mod(left, right)
        if op == "<":
            return left < right
        if op == "<=":
            return left <= right
        if op == ">":
            return left > right
        return left >= right


def run_source(source):
    interp = Interpreter()
    try:
        interp.run(parse_program(tokenize(source)))
    except CometError as e:
        return interp.output, str(e)
    return interp.output, None

from dataclasses import dataclass

KEYWORDS = {"let", "fn", "return", "if", "else", "while", "print",
            "true", "false", "and", "or", "not"}
TWO_CHAR = {"==", "!=", "<=", ">=", "->"}
ONE_CHAR = set("+-*/%<>=(){},;:")
ESCAPES = {'"': '"', "\\": "\\", "n": "\n"}
DIGITS = "0123456789"
LETTERS = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ_"


@dataclass
class Token:
    kind: str
    text: str
    line: int
    col: int


class LexError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


def tokenize(source):
    tokens = []
    i = 0
    line = 1
    col = 1
    n = len(source)

    def advance(count):
        nonlocal i, line, col
        for _ in range(count):
            if source[i] == "\n":
                line += 1
                col = 1
            else:
                col += 1
            i += 1

    while i < n:
        ch = source[i]
        start_line, start_col = line, col
        if ch in " \t\r\n":
            advance(1)
        elif ch == "#":
            while i < n and source[i] != "\n":
                advance(1)
        elif ch in DIGITS:
            j = i
            while j < n and source[j] in DIGITS:
                j += 1
            tokens.append(Token("NUMBER", source[i:j], start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch in LETTERS:
            j = i
            while j < n and (source[j] in LETTERS or source[j] in DIGITS):
                j += 1
            word = source[i:j]
            kind = "KEYWORD" if word in KEYWORDS else "IDENT"
            tokens.append(Token(kind, word, start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch == '"':
            advance(1)
            chars = []
            while True:
                if i >= n or source[i] == "\n":
                    raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                c = source[i]
                if c == '"':
                    advance(1)
                    break
                if c == "\\":
                    if i + 1 >= n or source[i + 1] == "\n":
                        raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                    if source[i + 1] not in ESCAPES:
                        raise LexError("unknown escape", line, col)
                    chars.append(ESCAPES[source[i + 1]])
                    advance(2)
                else:
                    chars.append(c)
                    advance(1)
            tokens.append(Token("STRING", "".join(chars), start_line, start_col))
        elif source[i:i + 2] in TWO_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", source[i:i + 2], start_line, start_col))
            advance(2)
        elif ch in ONE_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", ch, start_line, start_col))
            advance(1)
        else:
            raise LexError(f"unexpected character {ch!r}", start_line, start_col)
    tokens.append(Token("EOF", "", line, col))
    return tokens


KEYWORDS.update({"break", "continue"})

class ParseError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


COMPARE = ("==", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">=")
TYPES = ("int", "bool", "str")


class Parser:
    def __init__(self, tokens):
        self.tokens = tokens
        self.pos = 0

    def peek(self, ahead=0):
        return self.tokens[min(self.pos + ahead, len(self.tokens) - 1)]

    def at(self, *texts):
        tok = self.peek()
        return tok.kind in ("OP", "KEYWORD") and tok.text in texts

    def advance(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "EOF":
            self.pos += 1
        return tok

    def error(self, message):
        tok = self.peek()
        return ParseError(message, tok.line, tok.col)

    def expect(self, text):
        if not self.at(text):
            raise self.error(f"expected '{text}'")
        return self.advance()

    def expr(self):
        return self.or_expr()

    def or_expr(self):
        left = self.and_expr()
        while self.at("or"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.and_expr())
        return left

    def and_expr(self):
        left = self.not_expr()
        while self.at("and"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.not_expr())
        return left

    def not_expr(self):
        if self.at("not"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("not", self.not_expr())
        return self.compare()

    def compare(self):
        left = self.sum()
        if self.at(*COMPARE):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.sum())
            if self.at(*COMPARE):
                raise self.error("comparisons cannot be chained")
        return left

    def sum(self):
        left = self.product()
        while self.at("+", "-"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.product())
        return left

    def product(self):
        left = self.unary()
        while self.at("*", "/", "%"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.unary())
        return left

    def unary(self):
        if self.at("-"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("-", self.unary())
        return self.call()

    def call(self):
        expr = self.primary()
        while self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            args = []
            if not self.at(")"):
                args.append(self.expr())
                while self.at(","):
                    self.advance()
                    args.append(self.expr())
            self.expect(")")
            expr = Call(expr, args)
        return expr

    def primary(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind == "NUMBER":
            self.advance()
            return Num(int(tok.text))
        if tok.kind == "STRING":
            self.advance()
            return Str(tok.text)
        if tok.kind == "IDENT":
            self.advance()
            return Var(tok.text)
        if self.at("true", "false"):
            self.advance()
            return Bool(tok.text == "true")
        if self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            inner = self.expr()
            self.expect(")")
            return inner
        raise self.error("expected an expression")

    def program(self):
        stmts = []
        while self.peek().kind != "EOF":
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        return Program(stmts)

    def statement(self):
        if self.at("let"):
            return self.let_stmt()
        if self.at("print"):
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Print(value)
        if self.at("if"):
            return self.if_stmt()
        if self.at("while"):
            self.advance()
            cond = self.expr()
            return While(cond, self.block())
        if self.at("fn"):
            return self.fn_stmt()
        if self.at("return"):
            self.advance()
            value = None if self.at(";") else self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Return(value)
        nxt = self.peek(1)
        if self.peek().kind == "IDENT" and nxt.kind == "OP" and nxt.text == "=":
            name = self.advance().text
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Assign(name, value)
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return ExprStmt(value)

    def name(self):
        if self.peek().kind != "IDENT":
            raise self.error("expected a name")
        return self.advance().text

    def type_name(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "IDENT" or tok.text not in TYPES:
            raise self.error("expected a type")
        return self.advance().text

    def let_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        self.expect("=")
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return Let(name, type_, value)

    def if_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        cond = self.expr()
        then = self.block()
        else_ = None
        if self.at("else"):
            self.advance()
            else_ = self.if_stmt() if self.at("if") else self.block()
        return If(cond, then, else_)

    def block(self):
        self.expect("{")
        stmts = []
        while not self.at("}"):
            if self.peek().kind == "EOF":
                raise self.error("expected '}'")
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        self.advance()
        return Block(stmts)

    def param(self):
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        return (name, type_)

    def fn_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        self.expect("(")
        params = []
        if not self.at(")"):
            params.append(self.param())
            while self.at(","):
                self.advance()
                params.append(self.param())
        self.expect(")")
        ret = None
        if self.at("->"):
            self.advance()
            ret = self.type_name()
        return Fn(name, params, ret, self.block())


def parse_program(tokens):
    return Parser(tokens).program()


class LoopParser(Parser):
    def statement(self):
        if self.at("break", "continue"):
            word = self.advance().text
            self.expect(";")
            return Break() if word == "break" else Continue()
        return super().statement()


def parse_program(tokens):
    return LoopParser(tokens).program()


class CometError(Exception):
    pass


def type_name(value):
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "bool"
    if isinstance(value, int):
        return "int"
    return "str"


def show(value):
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "true" if value else "false"
    return str(value)


def comet_div(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q


def comet_mod(a, b):
    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)


class BreakSignal(Exception):
    pass


class ContinueSignal(Exception):
    pass


class Interpreter:
    def __init__(self):
        self.env = {}
        self.output = []
        self.loops = 0

    def run(self, program):
        for stmt in program.stmts:
            self.execute(stmt)

    def execute(self, stmt):
        if isinstance(stmt, Let):
            self.env[stmt.name] = self.evaluate(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Assign):
            if stmt.name not in self.env:
                raise CometError(f"assignment to undeclared variable {stmt.name}")
            self.env[stmt.name] = self.evaluate(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Print):
            self.output.append(show(self.evaluate(stmt.expr)))
        elif isinstance(stmt, ExprStmt):
            self.evaluate(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, If):
            if self.condition(stmt.cond):
                self.execute(stmt.then)
            elif stmt.else_ is not None:
                self.execute(stmt.else_)
        elif isinstance(stmt, While):
            self.loops += 1
            try:
                while self.condition(stmt.cond):
                    try:
                        self.execute(stmt.body)
                    except ContinueSignal:
                        pass
            except BreakSignal:
                pass
            finally:
                self.loops -= 1
        elif isinstance(stmt, (Break, Continue)):
            word = "break" if isinstance(stmt, Break) else "continue"
            if self.loops == 0:
                raise CometError(f"{word} outside a loop")
            raise BreakSignal() if word == "break" else ContinueSignal()
        elif isinstance(stmt, Block):
            for inner in stmt.stmts:
                self.execute(inner)
        else:
            raise CometError(f"{type(stmt).__name__} is not supported yet")

    def condition(self, expr):
        value = self.evaluate(expr)
        if not isinstance(value, bool):
            raise CometError(f"condition must be bool, not {type_name(value)}")
        return value

    def evaluate(self, expr):
        if isinstance(expr, (Num, Str, Bool)):
            return expr.value
        if isinstance(expr, Var):
            if expr.name not in self.env:
                raise CometError(f"undefined variable {expr.name}")
            return self.env[expr.name]
        if isinstance(expr, Unary):
            value = self.evaluate(expr.expr)
            if expr.op == "-":
                self.need("int", value, "-")
                return -value
            self.need("bool", value, "not")
            return not value
        if isinstance(expr, Binary):
            return self.binary(expr)
        raise CometError(f"{type(expr).__name__} is not supported yet")

    def need(self, wanted, value, op):
        if type_name(value) != wanted:
            raise CometError(f"'{op}' needs {wanted}, not {type_name(value)}")

    def binary(self, expr):
        op = expr.op
        left = self.evaluate(expr.left)
        if op in ("and", "or"):
            self.need("bool", left, op)
            if (op == "and" and not left) or (op == "or" and left):
                return left
            right = self.evaluate(expr.right)
            self.need("bool", right, op)
            return right
        right = self.evaluate(expr.right)
        if op in ("==", "!="):
            if type_name(left) != type_name(right):
                raise CometError(f"cannot compare {type_name(left)} with {type_name(right)}")
            return (left == right) == (op == "==")
        if op == "+" and type_name(left) == "str" and type_name(right) == "str":
            return left + right
        self.need("int", left, op)
        self.need("int", right, op)
        if op == "+":
            return left + right
        if op == "-":
            return left - right
        if op == "*":
            return left * right
        if op == "/":
            return comet_div(left, right)
        if op == "%":
            return comet_mod(left, right)
        if op == "<":
            return left < right
        if op == "<=":
            return left <= right
        if op == ">":
            return left > right
        return left >= right


def run_source(source):
    interp = Interpreter()
    try:
        interp.run(parse_program(tokenize(source)))
    except CometError as e:
        return interp.output, str(e)
    return interp.output, None
--- hint
Define two exception classes. In `execute`, a `Break` raises one and a `Continue` raises the other, unless the loop count is 0, in which case raise `CometError`.
--- hint
In the `While` case, add 1 to the loop count, and put the whole loop inside `try` / `except BreakSignal`. Inside the loop, run the body inside `try` / `except ContinueSignal`, so that a `continue` only abandons the current pass. Use `finally` to take 1 off the count however the loop ends.
--- check case | The example from the task
run_source("let i = 0; while i < 5 { i = i + 1; if i % 2 == 0 { continue; } print i; }")
=> (["1", "3", "5"], None)
--- check case | break ends an endless loop, and the program goes on
run_source("let i = 0; while true { i = i + 1; if i == 3 { break; } } print i; print \"after\";")
=> (["3", "after"], None)
--- check case | break leaves only the innermost loop
run_source("let a = 0; while a < 2 { a = a + 1; let b = 0; while true { b = b + 1; if b == 2 { break; } } print a * 10 + b; }")
=> (["12", "22"], None)
--- check case | continue skips the rest of the pass, even from nested blocks
run_source("let n = 0; let s = 0; while n < 10 { n = n + 1; if n > 3 { if n < 8 { continue; } } s = s + n; } print s;")
=> (["33"], None)

+++ question | Python's equality leaking in
--- ask
What happens when the lesson's interpreter runs `print true == 1;`?
--- choice
It prints `true`, because in Python `True == 1`.
--- choice
It prints `false`, because a bool is never equal to an int.
--- choice correct
It stops with a runtime error, because `==` needs two values of the same type.
--- choice
The parser rejects it, because `true` cannot be compared.
--- why
The program is grammatical, so the parser accepts it. Comet's `==` works on two values of the same type only, and `true` and `1` have different types, so it is a runtime error. An interpreter that simply used Python's `==` would print `true`, since Python's `bool` is a subclass of `int`.

+++ question | What a while loop means
--- ask
Which statement means exactly the same as `while c { b }`, according to the rules for `while`?
--- choice
`if c { b }`
--- choice correct
`if c { b; while c { b } }`
--- choice
`b; while c { b }`
--- choice
`while c { b } b;`
--- why
Rule 2 says a false condition does nothing, and rule 3 says a true condition runs the body once and then the whole loop again. That is exactly `if c { b; while c { b } }`. The third choice runs the body once even when c is false at the start.

+++ question | Predict the output
--- ask
What does this Comet program print?

```text
let a = 0;
let b = 5;
while b > 0 {
    a = a + b % 3;
    b = b - 2;
}
print a;
```
--- answer
3
--- why
The loop runs with b = 5, 3 and 1. The remainders are 5 % 3 = 2, 3 % 3 = 0 and 1 % 3 = 1, so a becomes 2, 2 and then 3. Then b is −1, the condition is false, and the program prints 3.

=== plc-07 | Scope: nested environments, shadowing and lexical scope
--- teach
Last lesson's interpreter keeps every variable in one dictionary for the whole program. That works for small scripts, but it means a helper variable inside a loop lives on after the loop, and two unrelated parts of a program cannot both use the name `i`. This lesson gives every block its own variables. It is the idea of **scope**, and it is the base that functions and closures stand on next lesson.

### What scope means

A **declaration** introduces a name: in Comet, `let x = …;` declares `x`. The **scope** of a declaration is the part of the program text where the name refers to that declaration. In everyday words: a block is a room, and a `let` pins a label on the wall of that room. Anyone in the room, or in a smaller room inside it, can read the label. Nobody outside the room can see it.

Comet's rule, stated precisely:

1. A `let` inside a block declares the name in that block. Its scope starts **just after the `let` statement** and ends at the block's closing `}`. It includes every block nested inside, unless one of them declares the same name again.
2. A name used somewhere refers to the **innermost** declaration whose scope contains that place.
3. The whole program is the outermost block, called the **global scope**.

This is **lexical scope**, also called static scope: you can tell which declaration a name refers to by reading the program's text, the way a [[lexer|lexical-word]] reads it, without running anything. Almost every modern language works this way.

### Shadowing

When an inner block declares a name that an outer block already declared, the inner declaration **shadows** the outer one: inside the inner block the name means the new variable, and the outer variable is untouched and comes back into view when the block ends.

```text
let level = 1;
if true {
    let level = 2;
    print level;
}
print level;
```

This prints `2`, then `1`. There are two different variables, both called `level`. Shadowing is different from assignment:

```text
let fuel = 100;
if true {
    fuel = fuel - 30;
}
print fuel;
```

This prints `70`. There is no `let` inside the block, so `fuel` refers to the outer variable, and the assignment changes it.

A `let` evaluates its right-hand side **before** the new name exists. So in `let level = level + 1;` inside a block, the `level` on the right is the outer one. The result is a new inner `level`, one bigger than the outer.

Declaring the same name twice **in the same block** is now an error: `let a = 1; let a = 2;` stops with "a is already declared in this scope". In lesson 6 the second `let` quietly replaced the first. Refusing it catches copy-paste mistakes, and it means that inside one block a name has exactly one meaning, which lesson 12 relies on when it checks names before the program runs. [[Languages differ here|redeclare]].

### Environments as a chain

The run-time picture of scope is a chain of **environments**. Each environment is one dictionary of names and values, the variables of one block, plus a link to the environment of the block around it, called its **parent**. The global environment has no parent.

- Entering a block creates a new, empty environment whose parent is the current one.
- `let x = e;` evaluates e, then adds x to the **current** environment, the innermost one.
- Reading `x` looks in the current environment; if x is not there, in its parent; and so on outwards. The first environment that has x wins. If the chain runs out, x is undefined.
- Assigning `x = e;` finds x the same way and changes it **in the environment where it was found**.
- Leaving a block throws its environment away and makes the parent current again.

Here is the lookup rule on a different structure: a stack of dictionaries in a Python list, innermost last.

```python
frames = [{"g": 9.8, "mass": 4}, {"mass": 7}, {"burn": 12}]

def find(name):
    for frame in reversed(frames):
        if name in frame:
            return frame[name]
    return None

print(find("burn"), find("mass"), find("g"), find("thrust"))   # 12 7 9.8 None
```

`mass` is found in the middle frame, which shadows the global one. The chain of parent links in this lesson does the same job without a list: each environment knows only its parent.

### The rules

Write the environment as a list of frames, innermost first: ρ = f₁ :: f₂ :: … :: fₙ, where fₙ is the global frame. The rules for blocks and declarations are:

1. **Block.** If running the statements s with ρ extended by an empty frame, {} :: ρ, ends in f′ :: ρ′, then running `{ s }` in ρ ends in ρ′. The block's own frame f′ is discarded, but changes made to outer frames are kept in ρ′.
2. **Let.** If ⟨e, ρ⟩ ⇓ v and x is not in f₁, then `let x = e;` turns f₁ :: rest into f₁[x ↦ v] :: rest.
3. **Lookup.** The value of x is fᵢ(x) for the smallest i with x in fᵢ; if there is none, x is undefined.
4. **Assign.** `x = e;` with ⟨e, ρ⟩ ⇓ v replaces x's value in that same fᵢ.

A loop body is a block, so rule 1 applies to every pass: each pass starts with a fresh, empty frame. That is why `while i < 3 { let square = i * i; … }` is not a redeclaration on the second pass.

### Keeping the chain right, even when things go wrong

The interpreter holds the current environment in `self.env`. To run a block it saves the old value, installs the new environment, runs the statements, and puts the old value back. The last step must happen **however** the block ends. A runtime error raises `CometError` from somewhere deep inside the block; if that skips the restore, `self.env` stays pointing at a dead inner environment. In a program that simply stops, nobody notices. In a read-eval-print loop, which keeps going after an error, every later line runs in the wrong scope. Next lesson, `return` will also leave blocks early through an exception. Python's [[try and finally|finally]] is exactly the tool: the `finally` part runs whether the `try` part finishes normally or by an exception.

```python
depth = 0

def nested(f):
    global depth
    depth += 1
    try:
        return f()
    finally:
        depth -= 1

def fails():
    raise ValueError("sensor offline")

try:
    nested(fails)
except ValueError:
    pass
print(depth)   # 0: restored although fails() raised
```

### Why it is correct

The claim is that the interpreter's lookup always finds the declaration that the lexical rule picks. The proof rests on an **invariant** about `self.env` during a run:

> When the interpreter is about to execute a statement s, the chain from `self.env` outwards has exactly one environment for each block that textually encloses s, innermost first, ending with the global one. Each of those environments holds exactly the names declared by `let` statements of that block that have already run in the current pass through the block.

- **At the start**, s is a top-level statement, the chain is just the global environment, and nothing has run.
- **Inside a block**, each statement keeps the invariant for the next: a `let` adds its name to the innermost environment, which is the statement's own block; nothing else adds names.
- **Entering a block** pushes one fresh environment, and that block is the one new block enclosing its statements.
- **Leaving a block**, normally or by an exception, restores the saved environment, thanks to `finally`, so the chain is again the one for the statements around the block.

Now take a use of x at s. The lets that have already run in the current pass of an enclosing block are exactly the declarations of that block that come textually **before** s, which by rule 1 are the ones whose scope contains s. Lookup walks the chain innermost first and stops at the first environment holding x, so it returns the innermost enclosing declaration whose scope contains s: rule 2 of the scope definition. The argument for assignment is the same.

### What it costs

- **Lookup and assignment** walk the chain: O(d), where d is the number of environments between the use and the declaration, at most the nesting depth of the program. Real programs rarely nest more than a handful of blocks, so d is small, but a global looked up from deep inside a loop pays the whole walk every time.
- **Declaring** is one average-O(1) dictionary insert. **Entering a block** allocates one small dictionary, O(1).
- **Space** is one entry per live variable, plus one environment per block currently being executed.

The walk can be removed. Because scope is lexical, the distance from each use to its declaration can be worked out once, before the program runs, and stored in the tree; lesson 12 does this. A compiler goes further and gives each local variable a fixed slot, so that reading it is one array access.

### Where it is used

- C, Java, C#, Rust, Go and JavaScript's `let` and `const` all give each block its own scope with these rules. Compilers keep the same chain at compile time in a [[symbol table|symtab]], to check names and pick storage.
- Python is different: a variable assigned anywhere in a function belongs to the **whole function**, not to a block. After `if True: y = 1`, the name y exists below the `if`. Python's rule is called [[LEGB|legb]].
- JavaScript's old `var` is function-scoped like Python's, which caused so many bugs that ES2015 added block-scoped `let`.
- Some languages use **dynamic scope** instead, where a name refers to the most recent binding **at run time**, whoever made it. The difference only shows up with functions, which is next lesson's subject. [[Where dynamic scope lives on|dynamic]].

**Watch out:**

- Restoring the environment only when a block finishes normally, not when it raises. Use `try` and `finally`.
- Restoring to the global environment instead of the saved one. Nested blocks then lose the variables of the blocks around them.
- Adding the name before evaluating the right-hand side of `let`. Then `let x = x + 1;` in an inner block reads the new, empty x instead of the outer one.
- Treating an assignment in an inner block as a new variable. Only `let` declares; `x = …` changes the nearest existing x.

::: context lexical-word Why it is called lexical
"Lexical" comes from the Greek for "word", and in compilers it means "about the program's text". The lexer of lesson 2 does lexical analysis, grouping characters into words. Lexical scope is scope you can see in the text: find the nearest enclosing block that declares the name. The opposite is anything that depends on the order things happen at run time, which you cannot know from the text alone.
:::

::: context redeclare Redeclaring in the same block
Languages disagree. Rust allows `let x = 5; let x = x * 2;` in one block and calls it shadowing: the second `let` makes a new variable. Java and C# forbid a local variable from even shadowing another local of an enclosing block in the same method. JavaScript's `let` forbids redeclaring in the same block, like Comet. Each choice is a trade: Rust's is convenient for transforming a value step by step, Java's catches more mistakes.
:::

::: context finally What finally guarantees
The `finally` part of a `try` runs when the `try` part ends normally, when it raises an exception, and even when it leaves by `return`, `break` or `continue`. After it runs, the exception, if there was one, carries on outwards. That makes it the standard place for clean-up that must always happen: closing a file, releasing a lock, or restoring a saved value. The `with` statement is built on the same mechanism.
:::

::: context symtab Symbol tables
A symbol table is a compiler's record of every declared name: its kind, its type, and where it will be stored. It is organised by scope, exactly like the environment chain, but it holds facts about names rather than run-time values. When the compiler enters a block it opens a new scope in the table; when it leaves, it closes it. Practice problem 2 builds a version whose lookup takes constant time.
:::

::: context legb Python's scope rule
Python looks a name up in four places, in order: the Local function, any Enclosing functions, the module's Global names, and the Built-ins, hence LEGB. Blocks such as `if`, `for` and `while` do not create scopes, so a loop variable is still defined after the loop. A name assigned anywhere in a function is local to the whole function, which is why reading a global and then assigning it in the same function raises UnboundLocalError.
:::

::: context dynamic Dynamic scope today
Early Lisps used dynamic scope, and Emacs Lisp kept it as the default until version 24 made lexical scope available. Bash's `local` variables are dynamically scoped: a function sees the local variables of whoever called it. Perl's `local` and Common Lisp's special variables work the same way, and some languages keep a dynamically scoped mechanism on purpose for settings like the current output stream or indentation level. Most code uses lexical scope because a reader can check it without tracing calls.
:::
--- task
The starter gives the lexer, the parser, `CometError`, Comet's division helpers, the helpers `type_name` and `show`, and the lesson 6 interpreter changed to use scopes. The interpreter keeps the global environment in `self.globals` and the current one in `self.env`, and it already calls the methods you write: `Let` calls `self.env.define`, `Var` calls `self.env.lookup`, `Assign` calls `self.env.assign`, and a `Block` calls `self.execute_block(stmt.stmts, Environment(self.env))`. Write:

- In `class Environment` (which keeps its variables in the dictionary `self.values` and its parent environment in `self.parent`, `None` for the global one):
  - `define(name, value)`: add the name to **this** environment. If this environment already has the name, raise `CometError` (for example "x is already declared in this scope").
  - `lookup(name)`: return the value from the nearest environment on the chain that has the name. Raise `CometError` (for example "undefined variable x") if none has it.
  - `assign(name, value)`: change the value in the nearest environment that has the name. Raise `CometError` (for example "assignment to undeclared variable x") if none has it.
- In `class Interpreter`, `execute_block(stmts, env)`: run the statements in order with `env` as the current environment, and put back the environment that was current before, **also** when a statement raises.

For example, `run_source("let t = 1; if true { let t = t + 5; print t; } print t;")` is `(["6", "1"], None)`.

from dataclasses import dataclass

KEYWORDS = {"let", "fn", "return", "if", "else", "while", "print",
            "true", "false", "and", "or", "not"}
TWO_CHAR = {"==", "!=", "<=", ">=", "->"}
ONE_CHAR = set("+-*/%<>=(){},;:")
ESCAPES = {'"': '"', "\\": "\\", "n": "\n"}
DIGITS = "0123456789"
LETTERS = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ_"


@dataclass
class Token:
    kind: str
    text: str
    line: int
    col: int


class LexError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


def tokenize(source):
    tokens = []
    i = 0
    line = 1
    col = 1
    n = len(source)

    def advance(count):
        nonlocal i, line, col
        for _ in range(count):
            if source[i] == "\n":
                line += 1
                col = 1
            else:
                col += 1
            i += 1

    while i < n:
        ch = source[i]
        start_line, start_col = line, col
        if ch in " \t\r\n":
            advance(1)
        elif ch == "#":
            while i < n and source[i] != "\n":
                advance(1)
        elif ch in DIGITS:
            j = i
            while j < n and source[j] in DIGITS:
                j += 1
            tokens.append(Token("NUMBER", source[i:j], start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch in LETTERS:
            j = i
            while j < n and (source[j] in LETTERS or source[j] in DIGITS):
                j += 1
            word = source[i:j]
            kind = "KEYWORD" if word in KEYWORDS else "IDENT"
            tokens.append(Token(kind, word, start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch == '"':
            advance(1)
            chars = []
            while True:
                if i >= n or source[i] == "\n":
                    raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                c = source[i]
                if c == '"':
                    advance(1)
                    break
                if c == "\\":
                    if i + 1 >= n or source[i + 1] == "\n":
                        raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                    if source[i + 1] not in ESCAPES:
                        raise LexError("unknown escape", line, col)
                    chars.append(ESCAPES[source[i + 1]])
                    advance(2)
                else:
                    chars.append(c)
                    advance(1)
            tokens.append(Token("STRING", "".join(chars), start_line, start_col))
        elif source[i:i + 2] in TWO_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", source[i:i + 2], start_line, start_col))
            advance(2)
        elif ch in ONE_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", ch, start_line, start_col))
            advance(1)
        else:
            raise LexError(f"unexpected character {ch!r}", start_line, start_col)
    tokens.append(Token("EOF", "", line, col))
    return tokens

class ParseError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


COMPARE = ("==", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">=")
TYPES = ("int", "bool", "str")


class Parser:
    def __init__(self, tokens):
        self.tokens = tokens
        self.pos = 0

    def peek(self, ahead=0):
        return self.tokens[min(self.pos + ahead, len(self.tokens) - 1)]

    def at(self, *texts):
        tok = self.peek()
        return tok.kind in ("OP", "KEYWORD") and tok.text in texts

    def advance(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "EOF":
            self.pos += 1
        return tok

    def error(self, message):
        tok = self.peek()
        return ParseError(message, tok.line, tok.col)

    def expect(self, text):
        if not self.at(text):
            raise self.error(f"expected '{text}'")
        return self.advance()

    def expr(self):
        return self.or_expr()

    def or_expr(self):
        left = self.and_expr()
        while self.at("or"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.and_expr())
        return left

    def and_expr(self):
        left = self.not_expr()
        while self.at("and"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.not_expr())
        return left

    def not_expr(self):
        if self.at("not"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("not", self.not_expr())
        return self.compare()

    def compare(self):
        left = self.sum()
        if self.at(*COMPARE):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.sum())
            if self.at(*COMPARE):
                raise self.error("comparisons cannot be chained")
        return left

    def sum(self):
        left = self.product()
        while self.at("+", "-"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.product())
        return left

    def product(self):
        left = self.unary()
        while self.at("*", "/", "%"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.unary())
        return left

    def unary(self):
        if self.at("-"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("-", self.unary())
        return self.call()

    def call(self):
        expr = self.primary()
        while self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            args = []
            if not self.at(")"):
                args.append(self.expr())
                while self.at(","):
                    self.advance()
                    args.append(self.expr())
            self.expect(")")
            expr = Call(expr, args)
        return expr

    def primary(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind == "NUMBER":
            self.advance()
            return Num(int(tok.text))
        if tok.kind == "STRING":
            self.advance()
            return Str(tok.text)
        if tok.kind == "IDENT":
            self.advance()
            return Var(tok.text)
        if self.at("true", "false"):
            self.advance()
            return Bool(tok.text == "true")
        if self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            inner = self.expr()
            self.expect(")")
            return inner
        raise self.error("expected an expression")

    def program(self):
        stmts = []
        while self.peek().kind != "EOF":
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        return Program(stmts)

    def statement(self):
        if self.at("let"):
            return self.let_stmt()
        if self.at("print"):
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Print(value)
        if self.at("if"):
            return self.if_stmt()
        if self.at("while"):
            self.advance()
            cond = self.expr()
            return While(cond, self.block())
        if self.at("fn"):
            return self.fn_stmt()
        if self.at("return"):
            self.advance()
            value = None if self.at(";") else self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Return(value)
        nxt = self.peek(1)
        if self.peek().kind == "IDENT" and nxt.kind == "OP" and nxt.text == "=":
            name = self.advance().text
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Assign(name, value)
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return ExprStmt(value)

    def name(self):
        if self.peek().kind != "IDENT":
            raise self.error("expected a name")
        return self.advance().text

    def type_name(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "IDENT" or tok.text not in TYPES:
            raise self.error("expected a type")
        return self.advance().text

    def let_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        self.expect("=")
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return Let(name, type_, value)

    def if_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        cond = self.expr()
        then = self.block()
        else_ = None
        if self.at("else"):
            self.advance()
            else_ = self.if_stmt() if self.at("if") else self.block()
        return If(cond, then, else_)

    def block(self):
        self.expect("{")
        stmts = []
        while not self.at("}"):
            if self.peek().kind == "EOF":
                raise self.error("expected '}'")
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        self.advance()
        return Block(stmts)

    def param(self):
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        return (name, type_)

    def fn_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        self.expect("(")
        params = []
        if not self.at(")"):
            params.append(self.param())
            while self.at(","):
                self.advance()
                params.append(self.param())
        self.expect(")")
        ret = None
        if self.at("->"):
            self.advance()
            ret = self.type_name()
        return Fn(name, params, ret, self.block())


def parse_program(tokens):
    return Parser(tokens).program()


class CometError(Exception):
    pass


def comet_div(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q


def comet_mod(a, b):
    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)


def type_name(value):
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "bool"
    if isinstance(value, int):
        return "int"
    return "str"


def show(value):
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "true" if value else "false"
    return str(value)


class Environment:
    def __init__(self, parent=None):
        self.values = {}
        self.parent = parent

    def define(self, name, value):
        raise CometError("define is not written yet")

    def lookup(self, name):
        raise CometError("lookup is not written yet")

    def assign(self, name, value):
        raise CometError("assign is not written yet")


class Interpreter:
    def __init__(self):
        self.globals = Environment()
        self.env = self.globals
        self.output = []

    def run(self, program):
        for stmt in program.stmts:
            self.execute(stmt)

    def execute_block(self, stmts, env):
        raise CometError("execute_block is not written yet")

    def execute(self, stmt):
        if isinstance(stmt, Let):
            self.env.define(stmt.name, self.evaluate(stmt.expr))
        elif isinstance(stmt, Assign):
            value = self.evaluate(stmt.expr)
            self.env.assign(stmt.name, value)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Print):
            self.output.append(show(self.evaluate(stmt.expr)))
        elif isinstance(stmt, ExprStmt):
            self.evaluate(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, If):
            if self.condition(stmt.cond):
                self.execute(stmt.then)
            elif stmt.else_ is not None:
                self.execute(stmt.else_)
        elif isinstance(stmt, While):
            while self.condition(stmt.cond):
                self.execute(stmt.body)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Block):
            self.execute_block(stmt.stmts, Environment(self.env))
        else:
            raise CometError(f"{type(stmt).__name__} is not supported yet")

    def condition(self, expr):
        value = self.evaluate(expr)
        if not isinstance(value, bool):
            raise CometError(f"condition must be bool, not {type_name(value)}")
        return value

    def evaluate(self, expr):
        if isinstance(expr, (Num, Str, Bool)):
            return expr.value
        if isinstance(expr, Var):
            return self.env.lookup(expr.name)
        if isinstance(expr, Unary):
            value = self.evaluate(expr.expr)
            if expr.op == "-":
                self.need("int", value, "-")
                return -value
            self.need("bool", value, "not")
            return not value
        if isinstance(expr, Binary):
            return self.binary(expr)
        raise CometError(f"{type(expr).__name__} is not supported yet")

    def need(self, wanted, value, op):
        if type_name(value) != wanted:
            raise CometError(f"'{op}' needs {wanted}, not {type_name(value)}")

    def binary(self, expr):
        op = expr.op
        left = self.evaluate(expr.left)
        if op in ("and", "or"):
            self.need("bool", left, op)
            if (op == "and" and not left) or (op == "or" and left):
                return left
            right = self.evaluate(expr.right)
            self.need("bool", right, op)
            return right
        right = self.evaluate(expr.right)
        if op in ("==", "!="):
            if type_name(left) != type_name(right):
                raise CometError(f"cannot compare {type_name(left)} with {type_name(right)}")
            return (left == right) == (op == "==")
        if op == "+" and type_name(left) == "str" and type_name(right) == "str":
            return left + right
        self.need("int", left, op)
        self.need("int", right, op)
        if op == "+":
            return left + right
        if op == "-":
            return left - right
        if op == "*":
            return left * right
        if op == "/":
            return comet_div(left, right)
        if op == "%":
            return comet_mod(left, right)
        if op == "<":
            return left < right
        if op == "<=":
            return left <= right
        if op == ">":
            return left > right
        return left >= right


def run_source(source):
    interp = Interpreter()
    try:
        interp.run(parse_program(tokenize(source)))
    except CometError as e:
        return interp.output, str(e)
    return interp.output, None

from dataclasses import dataclass

KEYWORDS = {"let", "fn", "return", "if", "else", "while", "print",
            "true", "false", "and", "or", "not"}
TWO_CHAR = {"==", "!=", "<=", ">=", "->"}
ONE_CHAR = set("+-*/%<>=(){},;:")
ESCAPES = {'"': '"', "\\": "\\", "n": "\n"}
DIGITS = "0123456789"
LETTERS = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ_"


@dataclass
class Token:
    kind: str
    text: str
    line: int
    col: int


class LexError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


def tokenize(source):
    tokens = []
    i = 0
    line = 1
    col = 1
    n = len(source)

    def advance(count):
        nonlocal i, line, col
        for _ in range(count):
            if source[i] == "\n":
                line += 1
                col = 1
            else:
                col += 1
            i += 1

    while i < n:
        ch = source[i]
        start_line, start_col = line, col
        if ch in " \t\r\n":
            advance(1)
        elif ch == "#":
            while i < n and source[i] != "\n":
                advance(1)
        elif ch in DIGITS:
            j = i
            while j < n and source[j] in DIGITS:
                j += 1
            tokens.append(Token("NUMBER", source[i:j], start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch in LETTERS:
            j = i
            while j < n and (source[j] in LETTERS or source[j] in DIGITS):
                j += 1
            word = source[i:j]
            kind = "KEYWORD" if word in KEYWORDS else "IDENT"
            tokens.append(Token(kind, word, start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch == '"':
            advance(1)
            chars = []
            while True:
                if i >= n or source[i] == "\n":
                    raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                c = source[i]
                if c == '"':
                    advance(1)
                    break
                if c == "\\":
                    if i + 1 >= n or source[i + 1] == "\n":
                        raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                    if source[i + 1] not in ESCAPES:
                        raise LexError("unknown escape", line, col)
                    chars.append(ESCAPES[source[i + 1]])
                    advance(2)
                else:
                    chars.append(c)
                    advance(1)
            tokens.append(Token("STRING", "".join(chars), start_line, start_col))
        elif source[i:i + 2] in TWO_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", source[i:i + 2], start_line, start_col))
            advance(2)
        elif ch in ONE_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", ch, start_line, start_col))
            advance(1)
        else:
            raise LexError(f"unexpected character {ch!r}", start_line, start_col)
    tokens.append(Token("EOF", "", line, col))
    return tokens
