class ParseError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


COMPARE = ("==", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">=")
TYPES = ("int", "bool", "str")


class Parser:
    def __init__(self, tokens):
        self.tokens = tokens
        self.pos = 0

    def peek(self, ahead=0):
        return self.tokens[min(self.pos + ahead, len(self.tokens) - 1)]

    def at(self, *texts):
        tok = self.peek()
        return tok.kind in ("OP", "KEYWORD") and tok.text in texts

    def advance(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "EOF":
            self.pos += 1
        return tok

    def error(self, message):
        tok = self.peek()
        return ParseError(message, tok.line, tok.col)

    def expect(self, text):
        if not self.at(text):
            raise self.error(f"expected '{text}'")
        return self.advance()

    def expr(self):
        return self.or_expr()

    def or_expr(self):
        left = self.and_expr()
        while self.at("or"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.and_expr())
        return left

    def and_expr(self):
        left = self.not_expr()
        while self.at("and"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.not_expr())
        return left

    def not_expr(self):
        if self.at("not"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("not", self.not_expr())
        return self.compare()

    def compare(self):
        left = self.sum()
        if self.at(*COMPARE):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.sum())
            if self.at(*COMPARE):
                raise self.error("comparisons cannot be chained")
        return left

    def sum(self):
        left = self.product()
        while self.at("+", "-"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.product())
        return left

    def product(self):
        left = self.unary()
        while self.at("*", "/", "%"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.unary())
        return left

    def unary(self):
        if self.at("-"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("-", self.unary())
        return self.call()

    def call(self):
        expr = self.primary()
        while self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            args = []
            if not self.at(")"):
                args.append(self.expr())
                while self.at(","):
                    self.advance()
                    args.append(self.expr())
            self.expect(")")
            expr = Call(expr, args)
        return expr

    def primary(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind == "NUMBER":
            self.advance()
            return Num(int(tok.text))
        if tok.kind == "STRING":
            self.advance()
            return Str(tok.text)
        if tok.kind == "IDENT":
            self.advance()
            return Var(tok.text)
        if self.at("true", "false"):
            self.advance()
            return Bool(tok.text == "true")
        if self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            inner = self.expr()
            self.expect(")")
            return inner
        raise self.error("expected an expression")

    def program(self):
        stmts = []
        while self.peek().kind != "EOF":
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        return Program(stmts)

    def statement(self):
        if self.at("let"):
            return self.let_stmt()
        if self.at("print"):
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Print(value)
        if self.at("if"):
            return self.if_stmt()
        if self.at("while"):
            self.advance()
            cond = self.expr()
            return While(cond, self.block())
        if self.at("fn"):
            return self.fn_stmt()
        if self.at("return"):
            self.advance()
            value = None if self.at(";") else self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Return(value)
        nxt = self.peek(1)
        if self.peek().kind == "IDENT" and nxt.kind == "OP" and nxt.text == "=":
            name = self.advance().text
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Assign(name, value)
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return ExprStmt(value)

    def name(self):
        if self.peek().kind != "IDENT":
            raise self.error("expected a name")
        return self.advance().text

    def type_name(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "IDENT" or tok.text not in TYPES:
            raise self.error("expected a type")
        return self.advance().text

    def let_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        self.expect("=")
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return Let(name, type_, value)

    def if_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        cond = self.expr()
        then = self.block()
        else_ = None
        if self.at("else"):
            self.advance()
            else_ = self.if_stmt() if self.at("if") else self.block()
        return If(cond, then, else_)

    def block(self):
        self.expect("{")
        stmts = []
        while not self.at("}"):
            if self.peek().kind == "EOF":
                raise self.error("expected '}'")
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        self.advance()
        return Block(stmts)

    def param(self):
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        return (name, type_)

    def fn_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        self.expect("(")
        params = []
        if not self.at(")"):
            params.append(self.param())
            while self.at(","):
                self.advance()
                params.append(self.param())
        self.expect(")")
        ret = None
        if self.at("->"):
            self.advance()
            ret = self.type_name()
        return Fn(name, params, ret, self.block())


def parse_program(tokens):
    return Parser(tokens).program()


class CometError(Exception):
    pass


def comet_div(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q


def comet_mod(a, b):
    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)


def type_name(value):
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "bool"
    if isinstance(value, int):
        return "int"
    return "str"


def show(value):
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "true" if value else "false"
    return str(value)


class Environment:
    def __init__(self, parent=None):
        self.values = {}
        self.parent = parent

    def define(self, name, value):
        if name in self.values:
            raise CometError(f"{name} is already declared in this scope")
        self.values[name] = value

    def find(self, name):
        env = self
        while env is not None:
            if name in env.values:
                return env
            env = env.parent
        return None

    def lookup(self, name):
        env = self.find(name)
        if env is None:
            raise CometError(f"undefined variable {name}")
        return env.values[name]

    def assign(self, name, value):
        env = self.find(name)
        if env is None:
            raise CometError(f"assignment to undeclared variable {name}")
        env.values[name] = value


class Interpreter:
    def __init__(self):
        self.globals = Environment()
        self.env = self.globals
        self.output = []

    def run(self, program):
        for stmt in program.stmts:
            self.execute(stmt)

    def execute_block(self, stmts, env):
        previous = self.env
        self.env = env
        try:
            for stmt in stmts:
                self.execute(stmt)
        finally:
            self.env = previous

    def execute(self, stmt):
        if isinstance(stmt, Let):
            self.env.define(stmt.name, self.evaluate(stmt.expr))
        elif isinstance(stmt, Assign):
            value = self.evaluate(stmt.expr)
            self.env.assign(stmt.name, value)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Print):
            self.output.append(show(self.evaluate(stmt.expr)))
        elif isinstance(stmt, ExprStmt):
            self.evaluate(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, If):
            if self.condition(stmt.cond):
                self.execute(stmt.then)
            elif stmt.else_ is not None:
                self.execute(stmt.else_)
        elif isinstance(stmt, While):
            while self.condition(stmt.cond):
                self.execute(stmt.body)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Block):
            self.execute_block(stmt.stmts, Environment(self.env))
        else:
            raise CometError(f"{type(stmt).__name__} is not supported yet")

    def condition(self, expr):
        value = self.evaluate(expr)
        if not isinstance(value, bool):
            raise CometError(f"condition must be bool, not {type_name(value)}")
        return value

    def evaluate(self, expr):
        if isinstance(expr, (Num, Str, Bool)):
            return expr.value
        if isinstance(expr, Var):
            return self.env.lookup(expr.name)
        if isinstance(expr, Unary):
            value = self.evaluate(expr.expr)
            if expr.op == "-":
                self.need("int", value, "-")
                return -value
            self.need("bool", value, "not")
            return not value
        if isinstance(expr, Binary):
            return self.binary(expr)
        raise CometError(f"{type(expr).__name__} is not supported yet")

    def need(self, wanted, value, op):
        if type_name(value) != wanted:
            raise CometError(f"'{op}' needs {wanted}, not {type_name(value)}")

    def binary(self, expr):
        op = expr.op
        left = self.evaluate(expr.left)
        if op in ("and", "or"):
            self.need("bool", left, op)
            if (op == "and" and not left) or (op == "or" and left):
                return left
            right = self.evaluate(expr.right)
            self.need("bool", right, op)
            return right
        right = self.evaluate(expr.right)
        if op in ("==", "!="):
            if type_name(left) != type_name(right):
                raise CometError(f"cannot compare {type_name(left)} with {type_name(right)}")
            return (left == right) == (op == "==")
        if op == "+" and type_name(left) == "str" and type_name(right) == "str":
            return left + right
        self.need("int", left, op)
        self.need("int", right, op)
        if op == "+":
            return left + right
        if op == "-":
            return left - right
        if op == "*":
            return left * right
        if op == "/":
            return comet_div(left, right)
        if op == "%":
            return comet_mod(left, right)
        if op == "<":
            return left < right
        if op == "<=":
            return left <= right
        if op == ">":
            return left > right
        return left >= right


def run_source(source):
    interp = Interpreter()
    try:
        interp.run(parse_program(tokenize(source)))
    except CometError as e:
        return interp.output, str(e)
    return interp.output, None


def let_names(program):
    names = []

    def walk(s):
        if isinstance(s, Let):
            names.append(s.name)
        elif isinstance(s, If):
            walk(s.then)
            if s.else_ is not None:
                walk(s.else_)
        elif isinstance(s, While):
            walk(s.body)
        elif isinstance(s, Block):
            for inner in s.stmts:
                walk(inner)

    for s in program.stmts:
        walk(s)
    return names


def same_output(source):
    program = parse_program(tokenize(source))
    before = Interpreter()
    before.run(program)
    after = Interpreter()
    after.run(rename(program))
    return before.output == after.output


def rename(program):
    taken = set()

    def collect_expr(e):
        if isinstance(e, Var):
            taken.add(e.name)
        elif isinstance(e, Unary):
            collect_expr(e.expr)
        elif isinstance(e, Binary):
            collect_expr(e.left)
            collect_expr(e.right)

    def collect(s):
        if isinstance(s, (Let, Assign)):
            taken.add(s.name)
            collect_expr(s.expr)
        elif isinstance(s, (Print, ExprStmt)):
            collect_expr(s.expr)
        elif isinstance(s, If):
            collect_expr(s.cond)
            collect(s.then)
            if s.else_ is not None:
                collect(s.else_)
        elif isinstance(s, While):
            collect_expr(s.cond)
            collect(s.body)
        elif isinstance(s, Block):
            for inner in s.stmts:
                collect(inner)

    for s in program.stmts:
        collect(s)

    declared = set()
    scopes = [{}]

    def fresh(name):
        if name not in declared:
            declared.add(name)
            return name
        k = 1
        while f"{name}_{k}" in taken or f"{name}_{k}" in declared:
            k += 1
        new = f"{name}_{k}"
        declared.add(new)
        return new

    def current(name):
        for scope in reversed(scopes):
            if name in scope:
                return scope[name]
        return name

    def expr(e):
        if isinstance(e, Var):
            return Var(current(e.name))
        if isinstance(e, Unary):
            return Unary(e.op, expr(e.expr))
        if isinstance(e, Binary):
            return Binary(e.op, expr(e.left), expr(e.right))
        return e

    def stmt(s):
        if isinstance(s, Let):
            value = expr(s.expr)
            new = fresh(s.name)
            scopes[-1][s.name] = new
            return Let(new, s.type, value)
        if isinstance(s, Assign):
            return Assign(current(s.name), expr(s.expr))
        if isinstance(s, Print):
            return Print(expr(s.expr))
        if isinstance(s, ExprStmt):
            return ExprStmt(expr(s.expr))
        if isinstance(s, If):
            else_ = None if s.else_ is None else stmt(s.else_)
            return If(expr(s.cond), stmt(s.then), else_)
        if isinstance(s, While):
            return While(expr(s.cond), stmt(s.body))
        if isinstance(s, Block):
            scopes.append({})
            body = [stmt(inner) for inner in s.stmts]
            scopes.pop()
            return Block(body)
        return s

    return Program([stmt(s) for s in program.stmts])
--- hint
Make two passes. First collect every name that appears anywhere in the program (in `Let`, `Assign` and `Var` nodes), so you know which `name_k` are taken. Then walk the tree again, building new nodes, with a stack of dictionaries from old name to new name, one per open block.
--- hint
For a `Let`, rename its right-hand side first, with the scopes as they are, then choose the fresh name and record it in the innermost dictionary. For a `Var` or an `Assign`, search the dictionaries from the innermost outwards; if the name is in none, keep it.

+++ question | What the block prints
--- ask
What does this Comet program print? Give the three printed values in order, separated by spaces.

```text
let x = 1;
let y = 10;
if x < y {
    let x = 5;
    y = y + x;
    let y = 0;
    print y;
}
print x;
print y;
```
--- answer
0 1 15
0, 1, 15
--- why
Inside the block, `let x = 5;` declares a new x that shadows the outer one. `y = y + x;` has no `let`, so it changes the outer y to 10 + 5 = 15. Then `let y = 0;` declares a new inner y, which is what `print y;` inside the block sees: 0. After the block, both inner variables are gone, so the program prints the outer x, 1, and the outer y, 15.

+++ question | Python's blocks
--- ask
In Python, `if True:` followed by an indented `z = 1`, and then `print(z)` after the `if`, prints 1. The Comet program `if true { let z = 1; } print z;` stops with "undefined variable z". Why the difference?
--- choice
Python evaluates `if True:` at compile time and removes it, but Comet does not.
--- choice correct
Python's scopes are whole functions or modules, so the `if` block creates no scope, while every Comet block has its own scope that ends at its `}`.
--- choice
Comet deletes variables as soon as they are no longer needed, to save memory.
--- choice
Python uses dynamic scope and Comet uses lexical scope.
--- why
Both languages are lexically scoped; they differ in what counts as a scope. In Python a variable assigned anywhere in a function or module belongs to the whole function or module, so z is still there after the `if`. In Comet, as in C, Java or JavaScript's `let`, the scope of a declaration ends at the closing brace of its block.

+++ question | Why finally
--- ask
`execute_block` restores the previous environment in a `finally` part. In which situation does that matter in this lesson's interpreter?
--- choice
When a block is empty, because the `for` loop over its statements never runs.
--- choice
When a block declares no variables, because its environment stays empty.
--- choice correct
When a statement inside the block raises `CometError` and the interpreter object is used again afterwards, as a read-eval-print loop does.
--- choice
Never: the program always stops at the first error, so the environment no longer matters.
--- why
Without `finally`, an exception leaves `self.env` pointing at the inner environment. A one-shot run stops anyway, but anything that keeps using the interpreter, such as a REPL or a test, then runs later code in the wrong scope. Next lesson `return` also leaves blocks by an exception, and then it matters for every program.
=== plc-08 | Functions and closures: first-class functions, the call stack, captured environments
--- teach
Last lesson gave every block its own environment, chained to the one around it. This lesson adds the feature everything else in a language is built from: **functions**. Comet functions are values, like numbers, and they remember the variables around the place where they were written. By the end the interpreter runs recursion, functions that take and return functions, and closures that keep private state.

### Declaring and calling

`fn area(w, h) { return w * h; }` declares a function named `area` with two **parameters**, `w` and `h`. `area(3, 4)` is a **call** with two **arguments**. Running a call takes five steps:

1. Evaluate the callee, the expression before the parentheses. Usually it is just a name, but it can be any expression whose value is a function.
2. Evaluate the arguments, left to right, in the **caller's** environment. Comet passes the resulting values, not the expressions: this is **call by value**, the rule of Python, Java and C. [[Other rules exist|passing]].
3. Check that the callee really is a function and that the number of arguments equals the number of parameters. Otherwise it is a runtime error.
4. Create a new environment, bind each parameter to its argument there, and run the body in it.
5. When the body runs `return e;`, the call's value is the value of e. If the body ends without `return`, or runs `return;`, the call returns nothing: `None` in the interpreter. Using nothing as a value, for example printing it, is an error.

### Functions are values

In Comet a function is a **first-class value**: it can be stored in a variable, passed as an argument, returned from another function, and compared with `==`. The `fn` statement is simply a declaration, like `let`, whose value is a function.

```text
fn half(n) { return n / 2; }
fn apply_twice(f, x) { return f(f(x)); }
let op = half;
print apply_twice(op, 40);
print op;
```

This prints `10`, then `<fn half>`. A function that takes or returns functions, like `apply_twice`, is called a **higher-order function**. [[First-class|first-class]] is a term with a history.

### Which environment does the body see?

This is the central question of the lesson. The body of a function mentions names that are not its parameters. Take this program:

```text
let unit = "m";
fn label(x) { return x + unit; }
fn report() {
    let unit = "km";
    return label("12");
}
print report();
```

When `label` runs, which `unit` does it see: the global one, `"m"`, which surrounds the place where `label` was **written**, or the one in `report`, `"km"`, which surrounds the place where it was **called**?

- **Lexical scope** answers "where it was written", and prints `12m`. This is Comet's rule, and lesson 7's rule: you can read it off the text.
- **Dynamic scope** answers "where it was called", and would print `12km`. The meaning of `label` would then change with every caller.

To get lexical scope, a function value must carry the environment of the place where it was defined. A function together with that environment is called a **closure**: it "closes over" the variables around it. So the `fn` statement creates `Closure(decl, env)`, where `decl` is the `Fn` node and `env` is the **current** environment at the moment the `fn` statement runs. A call then creates its new environment with the closure's `env` as its parent, **not** the caller's environment.

A name used in a function body that is not declared inside the function (not a parameter, not a local variable) is a **free variable** of the function. In `label`, `unit` is free and `x` is not. The closure's environment is exactly what gives free variables their meaning.

### Closures keep their environment alive

Because a closure holds a reference to its environment, that environment lives on after the function that created it has returned:

```text
fn make_clock(start) {
    let t = start;
    fn tick() {
        t = t + 60;
        return t;
    }
    return tick;
}
let a = make_clock(0);
let b = make_clock(1000);
print a();
print a();
print b();
```

This prints `60`, `120` and `1060`. Each call of `make_clock` creates a fresh environment with its own `t`, and the `tick` closure returned from it keeps that environment. `a` and `b` share nothing. This is how closures give **private state**: no other code can reach `t` except through `tick`.

So an environment cannot be thrown away just because its call returned: it can outlive the call. That is why this interpreter's environments are ordinary objects on the heap, and why languages with closures need a garbage collector, lesson 17's subject. The trouble this causes for stack-based implementations has a name: [[the funarg problem|funarg]].

Python closures work the same way. `nonlocal` tells Python that an assignment means the enclosing function's variable:

```python
def make_clock(start):
    t = start
    def tick():
        nonlocal t
        t += 60
        return t
    return tick

a = make_clock(0)
a()
print(a(), a.__code__.co_freevars)   # 120 ('t',)
```

`co_freevars` lists the free variables that Python found when it compiled `tick`.

### The call stack, and return as an exception

While a call runs, the caller is waiting in the middle of evaluating an expression. Each waiting call is one **frame** on the **call stack**, also called an [[activation record|frames]]. In this interpreter, Python's own call stack holds the waiting `evaluate` calls, and the interpreter keeps a list `self.frames` of the Comet functions currently running, innermost last. Recursion is simply a function whose frame appears more than once on the stack.

Every frame costs memory, so real languages limit the depth. Comet allows `MAX_DEPTH = 40` frames: a call when 40 are already running raises "stack overflow". Python's own limit is about 1,000 frames, and C's is set by the size of the stack, usually a few megabytes.

`return` can sit deep inside loops and `if` blocks. It must end all of them and the call at once. The neatest way in a tree-walker is an exception: `Return` raises `ReturnSignal(value)`, and the code that runs the call catches it. On its way out, the signal passes through every `execute_block` between the `return` and the call, and each one restores its saved environment in its `finally` part, exactly as last lesson prepared for. `return` at the top level, outside any function, is an error: the interpreter can tell because `self.frames` is empty.

### The rules

A closure is a pair ⟨fn f(x₁, …, xₙ) body, ρ_f⟩ of a declaration and an environment. With ρ the caller's environment:

1. **Declaration.** Running `fn f(…) body` in ρ = f₁ :: rest adds f ↦ ⟨fn f(…) body, ρ⟩ to f₁. The closure points to ρ itself, including the frame f₁ it is stored in, which is what makes recursion work: inside the body, the name f is found in that frame.
2. **Call.** If ⟨e, ρ⟩ ⇓ ⟨fn f(x₁, …, xₙ) body, ρ_f⟩, and ⟨eᵢ, ρ⟩ ⇓ vᵢ for i = 1 … n, and running body in {x₁ ↦ v₁, …, xₙ ↦ vₙ} :: ρ_f returns v, then ⟨e(e₁, …, eₙ), ρ⟩ ⇓ v.

The caller's environment ρ appears only in evaluating the callee and the arguments. The body runs in an extension of ρ_f. That single difference is lexical scope.

### Why it is correct

Lesson 7's invariant said: the environment chain at a statement has one environment per block that encloses the statement **in the text**. A function body is written inside the block where its `fn` statement stands. When the `fn` statement runs, the current environment is, by the invariant, the chain for exactly those enclosing blocks, and the closure saves it. A call puts one new environment, for the parameters and the body's own variables, in front of that saved chain. So while the body runs, the chain is again one environment per textually enclosing block, and the invariant holds inside function bodies too, whoever the caller is. The rest of lesson 7's argument then applies unchanged: every lookup finds the innermost enclosing declaration.

One subtlety remains. The saved chain is the **live** environment, not a copy, so the closure also sees declarations added to it **after** the `fn` statement ran: a function can call another function declared later in the same block. For functions at the top level, that is what makes two functions that call each other work. Lesson 12 examines when that is wanted.

### What it costs

- **Creating a closure** is O(1): it stores a pointer to the current environment and copies nothing, however many free variables there are.
- **A call** with n arguments costs O(n) to evaluate and bind them, plus one new environment, plus the body.
- **A free variable** costs a chain walk, O(d) for d environments between the use and the declaration; lesson 12 turns that into a precomputed distance.
- **Space:** each running call holds one environment and one frame, so the stack uses O(depth of recursion). Environments captured by closures stay alive as long as the closures do.

### Where it is used

- Callbacks and event handlers in JavaScript are closures: `button.onclick = () => count++` keeps `count` alive.
- Python's decorators, `functools.partial` and `sorted(key=lambda p: p[dist])` all rely on functions as values and on closures.
- Iterators and generators are closures in disguise: they keep private state between calls.
- C has function pointers but no closures, which is why C callback APIs such as `qsort_r` pass an extra `void *` context argument by hand. C++ lambdas and Rust closures build that context automatically.
- Flight software commonly registers handlers, closures over their configuration, to run when a telemetry value crosses a limit.

**Watch out:**

- Making the caller's environment the parent of the call's environment. Everything seems to work until a function uses a free variable that a caller also declares: that is dynamic scope, and the practice problems make you find it.
- Catching `ReturnSignal` without restoring the environment. The `finally` in `execute_block` handles it; do not bypass it.
- Forgetting to pop the frame when a call ends by an error. Use `finally` there too.
- Evaluating the arguments after switching to the new environment. They belong to the caller's scope: in `f(x)`, the `x` is the caller's.
- Comparing functions by what they compute. `==` on two closures is true only when they are the same closure object.

::: context passing How arguments are passed
Call by value copies each argument's value into the parameter, so assigning to a parameter never changes the caller's variable. Call by reference, which C++ offers with `int&`, makes the parameter another name for the caller's variable. Call by name, from Algol 60, re-evaluates the argument expression each time the parameter is used, and lazy languages like Haskell use a cached version called call by need. Python and Java pass values that are often references to objects, sometimes called call by sharing.
:::

::: context first-class Where "first-class" comes from
Christopher Strachey used the term in the 1960s: a first-class value can be passed as an argument, returned from a function, and stored in a variable, without restrictions. In early Fortran and C, functions were second-class: you could call them and pass pointers to them, but not create new ones at run time with their own captured variables. Lisp had first-class functions from 1958, and nearly every language designed since the 1990s does too.
:::

::: context funarg The funarg problem
In the 1960s, languages kept each call's variables in a frame on a stack and popped it on return. A function returned from another function, an "upward funarg", would then point to a popped frame. Peter Landin's closures of 1964 and Scheme's design in 1975 solved it by allocating environments on the heap and letting a garbage collector free them. Modern compilers keep variables on the stack when no closure captures them and move only the captured ones to the heap.
:::

::: context frames Activation records
An activation record, or stack frame, holds everything one running call needs: its parameters and local variables, the place in the caller to return to, and saved registers. Computer Organization's RISC-V calling convention builds them by moving the stack pointer. A debugger's backtrace is a list of these frames, and a stack overflow is what happens when too many are pushed, usually by recursion that never reaches its base case.
:::
--- task
The starter gives the lexer, the parser, lesson 7's `Environment`, and the interpreter from lesson 7 with a few additions: a class `Closure(decl, env)`, an exception `ReturnSignal(value)`, a list `self.frames` of the names of the functions currently running, the limit `MAX_DEPTH = 40`, and `type_name` and `show` updated so that a closure's type is `"fn"` and it prints as `<fn NAME>`. Write the four missing pieces:

- In `execute`, for `Fn`: define the function's name in the current environment as a `Closure` of the node and the current environment.
- In `execute`, for `Return`: raise `CometError` if no function is running (`self.frames` is empty); otherwise evaluate the expression, or use `None` for a bare `return;`, and raise `ReturnSignal` with it.
- In `evaluate`, for `Call`: evaluate the callee, then the arguments from left to right, and pass them to `self.call`.
- `call(callee, args)`: raise `CometError` if the callee is not a `Closure`, if the number of arguments differs from the number of parameters, or if `MAX_DEPTH` frames are already running (message "stack overflow"). Otherwise make a new `Environment` whose parent is the **closure's** environment, define each parameter in it, push the function's name onto `self.frames`, and run the body's statements in the new environment with `self.execute_block`. Return the value of a `ReturnSignal`, or `None` if the body ends without one. Pop the frame however the call ends.

For example, `run_source("fn sq(n) { return n * n; } print sq(sq(3));")` is `(["81"], None)`.
--- starter
from dataclasses import dataclass

KEYWORDS = {"let", "fn", "return", "if", "else", "while", "print",
            "true", "false", "and", "or", "not"}
TWO_CHAR = {"==", "!=", "<=", ">=", "->"}
ONE_CHAR = set("+-*/%<>=(){},;:")
ESCAPES = {'"': '"', "\\": "\\", "n": "\n"}
DIGITS = "0123456789"
LETTERS = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ_"


@dataclass
class Token:
    kind: str
    text: str
    line: int
    col: int


class LexError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


def tokenize(source):
    tokens = []
    i = 0
    line = 1
    col = 1
    n = len(source)

    def advance(count):
        nonlocal i, line, col
        for _ in range(count):
            if source[i] == "\n":
                line += 1
                col = 1
            else:
                col += 1
            i += 1

    while i < n:
        ch = source[i]
        start_line, start_col = line, col
        if ch in " \t\r\n":
            advance(1)
        elif ch == "#":
            while i < n and source[i] != "\n":
                advance(1)
        elif ch in DIGITS:
            j = i
            while j < n and source[j] in DIGITS:
                j += 1
            tokens.append(Token("NUMBER", source[i:j], start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch in LETTERS:
            j = i
            while j < n and (source[j] in LETTERS or source[j] in DIGITS):
                j += 1
            word = source[i:j]
            kind = "KEYWORD" if word in KEYWORDS else "IDENT"
            tokens.append(Token(kind, word, start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch == '"':
            advance(1)
            chars = []
            while True:
                if i >= n or source[i] == "\n":
                    raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                c = source[i]
                if c == '"':
                    advance(1)
                    break
                if c == "\\":
                    if i + 1 >= n or source[i + 1] == "\n":
                        raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                    if source[i + 1] not in ESCAPES:
                        raise LexError("unknown escape", line, col)
                    chars.append(ESCAPES[source[i + 1]])
                    advance(2)
                else:
                    chars.append(c)
                    advance(1)
            tokens.append(Token("STRING", "".join(chars), start_line, start_col))
        elif source[i:i + 2] in TWO_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", source[i:i + 2], start_line, start_col))
            advance(2)
        elif ch in ONE_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", ch, start_line, start_col))
            advance(1)
        else:
            raise LexError(f"unexpected character {ch!r}", start_line, start_col)
    tokens.append(Token("EOF", "", line, col))
    return tokens

class ParseError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


COMPARE = ("==", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">=")
TYPES = ("int", "bool", "str")


class Parser:
    def __init__(self, tokens):
        self.tokens = tokens
        self.pos = 0

    def peek(self, ahead=0):
        return self.tokens[min(self.pos + ahead, len(self.tokens) - 1)]

    def at(self, *texts):
        tok = self.peek()
        return tok.kind in ("OP", "KEYWORD") and tok.text in texts

    def advance(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "EOF":
            self.pos += 1
        return tok

    def error(self, message):
        tok = self.peek()
        return ParseError(message, tok.line, tok.col)

    def expect(self, text):
        if not self.at(text):
            raise self.error(f"expected '{text}'")
        return self.advance()

    def expr(self):
        return self.or_expr()

    def or_expr(self):
        left = self.and_expr()
        while self.at("or"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.and_expr())
        return left

    def and_expr(self):
        left = self.not_expr()
        while self.at("and"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.not_expr())
        return left

    def not_expr(self):
        if self.at("not"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("not", self.not_expr())
        return self.compare()

    def compare(self):
        left = self.sum()
        if self.at(*COMPARE):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.sum())
            if self.at(*COMPARE):
                raise self.error("comparisons cannot be chained")
        return left

    def sum(self):
        left = self.product()
        while self.at("+", "-"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.product())
        return left

    def product(self):
        left = self.unary()
        while self.at("*", "/", "%"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.unary())
        return left

    def unary(self):
        if self.at("-"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("-", self.unary())
        return self.call()

    def call(self):
        expr = self.primary()
        while self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            args = []
            if not self.at(")"):
                args.append(self.expr())
                while self.at(","):
                    self.advance()
                    args.append(self.expr())
            self.expect(")")
            expr = Call(expr, args)
        return expr

    def primary(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind == "NUMBER":
            self.advance()
            return Num(int(tok.text))
        if tok.kind == "STRING":
            self.advance()
            return Str(tok.text)
        if tok.kind == "IDENT":
            self.advance()
            return Var(tok.text)
        if self.at("true", "false"):
            self.advance()
            return Bool(tok.text == "true")
        if self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            inner = self.expr()
            self.expect(")")
            return inner
        raise self.error("expected an expression")

    def program(self):
        stmts = []
        while self.peek().kind != "EOF":
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        return Program(stmts)

    def statement(self):
        if self.at("let"):
            return self.let_stmt()
        if self.at("print"):
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Print(value)
        if self.at("if"):
            return self.if_stmt()
        if self.at("while"):
            self.advance()
            cond = self.expr()
            return While(cond, self.block())
        if self.at("fn"):
            return self.fn_stmt()
        if self.at("return"):
            self.advance()
            value = None if self.at(";") else self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Return(value)
        nxt = self.peek(1)
        if self.peek().kind == "IDENT" and nxt.kind == "OP" and nxt.text == "=":
            name = self.advance().text
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Assign(name, value)
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return ExprStmt(value)

    def name(self):
        if self.peek().kind != "IDENT":
            raise self.error("expected a name")
        return self.advance().text

    def type_name(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "IDENT" or tok.text not in TYPES:
            raise self.error("expected a type")
        return self.advance().text

    def let_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        self.expect("=")
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return Let(name, type_, value)

    def if_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        cond = self.expr()
        then = self.block()
        else_ = None
        if self.at("else"):
            self.advance()
            else_ = self.if_stmt() if self.at("if") else self.block()
        return If(cond, then, else_)

    def block(self):
        self.expect("{")
        stmts = []
        while not self.at("}"):
            if self.peek().kind == "EOF":
                raise self.error("expected '}'")
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        self.advance()
        return Block(stmts)

    def param(self):
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        return (name, type_)

    def fn_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        self.expect("(")
        params = []
        if not self.at(")"):
            params.append(self.param())
            while self.at(","):
                self.advance()
                params.append(self.param())
        self.expect(")")
        ret = None
        if self.at("->"):
            self.advance()
            ret = self.type_name()
        return Fn(name, params, ret, self.block())


def parse_program(tokens):
    return Parser(tokens).program()


class CometError(Exception):
    pass


def comet_div(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q


def comet_mod(a, b):
    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)


MAX_DEPTH = 40


class Closure:
    def __init__(self, decl, env):
        self.decl = decl
        self.env = env


class ReturnSignal(Exception):
    def __init__(self, value):
        super().__init__("return")
        self.value = value


def type_name(value):
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "bool"
    if isinstance(value, int):
        return "int"
    if isinstance(value, str):
        return "str"
    if isinstance(value, Closure):
        return "fn"

    return "nothing"


def show(value):
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "true" if value else "false"
    if isinstance(value, Closure):
        return f"<fn {value.decl.name}>"

    if value is None:
        raise CometError("cannot print nothing")
    return str(value)


class Environment:
    def __init__(self, parent=None):
        self.values = {}
        self.parent = parent

    def define(self, name, value):
        if name in self.values:
            raise CometError(f"{name} is already declared in this scope")
        self.values[name] = value

    def find(self, name):
        env = self
        while env is not None:
            if name in env.values:
                return env
            env = env.parent
        return None

    def lookup(self, name):
        env = self.find(name)
        if env is None:
            raise CometError(f"undefined variable {name}")
        return env.values[name]

    def assign(self, name, value):
        env = self.find(name)
        if env is None:
            raise CometError(f"assignment to undeclared variable {name}")
        env.values[name] = value


class Interpreter:
    def __init__(self):
        self.globals = Environment()
        self.env = self.globals
        self.output = []
        self.frames = []


    def run(self, program):
        for stmt in program.stmts:
            self.execute(stmt)

    def execute_block(self, stmts, env):
        previous = self.env
        self.env = env
        try:
            for stmt in stmts:
                self.execute(stmt)
        finally:
            self.env = previous

    def execute(self, stmt):
        if isinstance(stmt, Let):
            self.env.define(stmt.name, self.evaluate(stmt.expr))
        elif isinstance(stmt, Assign):
            value = self.evaluate(stmt.expr)
            self.env.assign(stmt.name, value)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Print):
            self.output.append(show(self.evaluate(stmt.expr)))
        elif isinstance(stmt, ExprStmt):
            self.evaluate(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, If):
            if self.condition(stmt.cond):
                self.execute(stmt.then)
            elif stmt.else_ is not None:
                self.execute(stmt.else_)
        elif isinstance(stmt, While):
            while self.condition(stmt.cond):
                self.execute(stmt.body)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Block):
            self.execute_block(stmt.stmts, Environment(self.env))
        elif isinstance(stmt, (Fn, Return)):
            raise CometError(f"{type(stmt).__name__} is not written yet")
        else:
            raise CometError(f"{type(stmt).__name__} is not supported yet")

    def condition(self, expr):
        value = self.evaluate(expr)
        if not isinstance(value, bool):
            raise CometError(f"condition must be bool, not {type_name(value)}")
        return value

    def evaluate(self, expr):
        if isinstance(expr, (Num, Str, Bool)):
            return expr.value
        if isinstance(expr, Var):
            return self.env.lookup(expr.name)
        if isinstance(expr, Unary):
            value = self.evaluate(expr.expr)
            if expr.op == "-":
                self.need("int", value, "-")
                return -value
            self.need("bool", value, "not")
            return not value
        if isinstance(expr, Binary):
            return self.binary(expr)
        if isinstance(expr, Call):
            raise CometError("Call is not written yet")
        raise CometError(f"{type(expr).__name__} is not supported yet")

    def call(self, callee, args):
        raise CometError("call is not written yet")

    def need(self, wanted, value, op):
        if type_name(value) != wanted:
            raise CometError(f"'{op}' needs {wanted}, not {type_name(value)}")

    def binary(self, expr):
        op = expr.op
        left = self.evaluate(expr.left)
        if op in ("and", "or"):
            self.need("bool", left, op)
            if (op == "and" and not left) or (op == "or" and left):
                return left
            right = self.evaluate(expr.right)
            self.need("bool", right, op)
            return right
        right = self.evaluate(expr.right)
        if op in ("==", "!="):
            if type_name(left) != type_name(right):
                raise CometError(f"cannot compare {type_name(left)} with {type_name(right)}")
            return (left is right if isinstance(left, Closure) else left == right) == (op == "==")
        if op == "+" and type_name(left) == "str" and type_name(right) == "str":
            return left + right
        self.need("int", left, op)
        self.need("int", right, op)
        if op == "+":
            return left + right
        if op == "-":
            return left - right
        if op == "*":
            return left * right
        if op == "/":
            return comet_div(left, right)
        if op == "%":
            return comet_mod(left, right)
        if op == "<":
            return left < right
        if op == "<=":
            return left <= right
        if op == ">":
            return left > right
        return left >= right


def run_source(source):
    interp = Interpreter()
    try:
        interp.run(parse_program(tokenize(source)))
    except CometError as e:
        return interp.output, str(e)
    return interp.output, None

from dataclasses import dataclass

KEYWORDS = {"let", "fn", "return", "if", "else", "while", "print",
            "true", "false", "and", "or", "not"}
TWO_CHAR = {"==", "!=", "<=", ">=", "->"}
ONE_CHAR = set("+-*/%<>=(){},;:")
ESCAPES = {'"': '"', "\\": "\\", "n": "\n"}
DIGITS = "0123456789"
LETTERS = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ_"


@dataclass
class Token:
    kind: str
    text: str
    line: int
    col: int


class LexError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


def tokenize(source):
    tokens = []
    i = 0
    line = 1
    col = 1
    n = len(source)

    def advance(count):
        nonlocal i, line, col
        for _ in range(count):
            if source[i] == "\n":
                line += 1
                col = 1
            else:
                col += 1
            i += 1

    while i < n:
        ch = source[i]
        start_line, start_col = line, col
        if ch in " \t\r\n":
            advance(1)
        elif ch == "#":
            while i < n and source[i] != "\n":
                advance(1)
        elif ch in DIGITS:
            j = i
            while j < n and source[j] in DIGITS:
                j += 1
            tokens.append(Token("NUMBER", source[i:j], start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch in LETTERS:
            j = i
            while j < n and (source[j] in LETTERS or source[j] in DIGITS):
                j += 1
            word = source[i:j]
            kind = "KEYWORD" if word in KEYWORDS else "IDENT"
            tokens.append(Token(kind, word, start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch == '"':
            advance(1)
            chars = []
            while True:
                if i >= n or source[i] == "\n":
                    raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                c = source[i]
                if c == '"':
                    advance(1)
                    break
                if c == "\\":
                    if i + 1 >= n or source[i + 1] == "\n":
                        raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                    if source[i + 1] not in ESCAPES:
                        raise LexError("unknown escape", line, col)
                    chars.append(ESCAPES[source[i + 1]])
                    advance(2)
                else:
                    chars.append(c)
                    advance(1)
            tokens.append(Token("STRING", "".join(chars), start_line, start_col))
        elif source[i:i + 2] in TWO_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", source[i:i + 2], start_line, start_col))
            advance(2)
        elif ch in ONE_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", ch, start_line, start_col))
            advance(1)
        else:
            raise LexError(f"unexpected character {ch!r}", start_line, start_col)
    tokens.append(Token("EOF", "", line, col))
    return tokens

    stmts: list


@dataclass
class Program:
    stmts: list


class ParseError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


COMPARE = ("==", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">=")
TYPES = ("int", "bool", "str")


class Parser:
    def __init__(self, tokens):
        self.tokens = tokens
        self.pos = 0

    def peek(self, ahead=0):
        return self.tokens[min(self.pos + ahead, len(self.tokens) - 1)]

    def at(self, *texts):
        tok = self.peek()
        return tok.kind in ("OP", "KEYWORD") and tok.text in texts

    def advance(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "EOF":
            self.pos += 1
        return tok

    def error(self, message):
        tok = self.peek()
        return ParseError(message, tok.line, tok.col)

    def expect(self, text):
        if not self.at(text):
            raise self.error(f"expected '{text}'")
        return self.advance()

    def expr(self):
        return self.or_expr()

    def or_expr(self):
        left = self.and_expr()
        while self.at("or"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.and_expr())
        return left

    def and_expr(self):
        left = self.not_expr()
        while self.at("and"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.not_expr())
        return left

    def not_expr(self):
        if self.at("not"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("not", self.not_expr())
        return self.compare()

    def compare(self):
        left = self.sum()
        if self.at(*COMPARE):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.sum())
            if self.at(*COMPARE):
                raise self.error("comparisons cannot be chained")
        return left

    def sum(self):
        left = self.product()
        while self.at("+", "-"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.product())
        return left

    def product(self):
        left = self.unary()
        while self.at("*", "/", "%"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.unary())
        return left

    def unary(self):
        if self.at("-"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("-", self.unary())
        return self.call()

    def call(self):
        expr = self.primary()
        while self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            args = []
            if not self.at(")"):
                args.append(self.expr())
                while self.at(","):
                    self.advance()
                    args.append(self.expr())
            self.expect(")")
            expr = Call(expr, args)
        return expr

    def primary(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind == "NUMBER":
            self.advance()
            return Num(int(tok.text))
        if tok.kind == "STRING":
            self.advance()
            return Str(tok.text)
        if tok.kind == "IDENT":
            self.advance()
            return Var(tok.text)
        if self.at("true", "false"):
            self.advance()
            return Bool(tok.text == "true")
        if self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            inner = self.expr()
            self.expect(")")
            return inner
        raise self.error("expected an expression")

    def program(self):
        stmts = []
        while self.peek().kind != "EOF":
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        return Program(stmts)

    def statement(self):
        if self.at("let"):
            return self.let_stmt()
        if self.at("print"):
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Print(value)
        if self.at("if"):
            return self.if_stmt()
        if self.at("while"):
            self.advance()
            cond = self.expr()
            return While(cond, self.block())
        if self.at("fn"):
            return self.fn_stmt()
        if self.at("return"):
            self.advance()
            value = None if self.at(";") else self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Return(value)
        nxt = self.peek(1)
        if self.peek().kind == "IDENT" and nxt.kind == "OP" and nxt.text == "=":
            name = self.advance().text
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Assign(name, value)
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return ExprStmt(value)

    def name(self):
        if self.peek().kind != "IDENT":
            raise self.error("expected a name")
        return self.advance().text

    def type_name(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "IDENT" or tok.text not in TYPES:
            raise self.error("expected a type")
        return self.advance().text

    def let_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        self.expect("=")
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return Let(name, type_, value)

    def if_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        cond = self.expr()
        then = self.block()
        else_ = None
        if self.at("else"):
            self.advance()
            else_ = self.if_stmt() if self.at("if") else self.block()
        return If(cond, then, else_)

    def block(self):
        self.expect("{")
        stmts = []
        while not self.at("}"):
            if self.peek().kind == "EOF":
                raise self.error("expected '}'")
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        self.advance()
        return Block(stmts)

    def param(self):
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        return (name, type_)

    def fn_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        self.expect("(")
        params = []
        if not self.at(")"):
            params.append(self.param())
            while self.at(","):
                self.advance()
                params.append(self.param())
        self.expect(")")
        ret = None
        if self.at("->"):
            self.advance()
            ret = self.type_name()
        return Fn(name, params, ret, self.block())


def parse_program(tokens):
    return Parser(tokens).program()


class CometError(Exception):
    pass


def comet_div(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q


def comet_mod(a, b):
    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)


MAX_DEPTH = 40


class Closure:
    def __init__(self, decl, env):
        self.decl = decl
        self.env = env


class ReturnSignal(Exception):
    def __init__(self, value):
        super().__init__("return")
        self.value = value


def type_name(value):
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "bool"
    if isinstance(value, int):
        return "int"
    if isinstance(value, str):
        return "str"
    if isinstance(value, Closure):
        return "fn"

    return "nothing"


def show(value):
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "true" if value else "false"
    if isinstance(value, Closure):
        return f"<fn {value.decl.name}>"

    if value is None:
        raise CometError("cannot print nothing")
    return str(value)


class Environment:
    def __init__(self, parent=None):
        self.values = {}
        self.parent = parent

    def define(self, name, value):
        if name in self.values:
            raise CometError(f"{name} is already declared in this scope")
        self.values[name] = value

    def find(self, name):
        env = self
        while env is not None:
            if name in env.values:
                return env
            env = env.parent
        return None

    def lookup(self, name):
        env = self.find(name)
        if env is None:
            raise CometError(f"undefined variable {name}")
        return env.values[name]

    def assign(self, name, value):
        env = self.find(name)
        if env is None:
            raise CometError(f"assignment to undeclared variable {name}")
        env.values[name] = value


class Interpreter:
    def __init__(self):
        self.globals = Environment()
        self.env = self.globals
        self.output = []
        self.frames = []


    def run(self, program):
        for stmt in program.stmts:
            self.execute(stmt)

    def execute_block(self, stmts, env):
        previous = self.env
        self.env = env
        try:
            for stmt in stmts:
                self.execute(stmt)
        finally:
            self.env = previous

    def execute(self, stmt):
        if isinstance(stmt, Let):
            self.env.define(stmt.name, self.evaluate(stmt.expr))
        elif isinstance(stmt, Assign):
            value = self.evaluate(stmt.expr)
            self.env.assign(stmt.name, value)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Print):
            self.output.append(show(self.evaluate(stmt.expr)))
        elif isinstance(stmt, ExprStmt):
            self.evaluate(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, If):
            if self.condition(stmt.cond):
                self.execute(stmt.then)
            elif stmt.else_ is not None:
                self.execute(stmt.else_)
        elif isinstance(stmt, While):
            while self.condition(stmt.cond):
                self.execute(stmt.body)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Block):
            self.execute_block(stmt.stmts, Environment(self.env))
        elif isinstance(stmt, Fn):
            self.env.define(stmt.name, Closure(stmt, self.env))
        elif isinstance(stmt, Return):
            if not self.frames:
                raise CometError("return outside a function")
            value = None if stmt.expr is None else self.evaluate(stmt.expr)
            raise ReturnSignal(value)
        else:
            raise CometError(f"{type(stmt).__name__} is not supported yet")

    def condition(self, expr):
        value = self.evaluate(expr)
        if not isinstance(value, bool):
            raise CometError(f"condition must be bool, not {type_name(value)}")
        return value

    def evaluate(self, expr):
        if isinstance(expr, (Num, Str, Bool)):
            return expr.value
        if isinstance(expr, Var):
            return self.env.lookup(expr.name)
        if isinstance(expr, Unary):
            value = self.evaluate(expr.expr)
            if expr.op == "-":
                self.need("int", value, "-")
                return -value
            self.need("bool", value, "not")
            return not value
        if isinstance(expr, Binary):
            return self.binary(expr)
        if isinstance(expr, Call):
            callee = self.evaluate(expr.callee)
            args = [self.evaluate(arg) for arg in expr.args]
            return self.call(callee, args)
        raise CometError(f"{type(expr).__name__} is not supported yet")

    def call(self, callee, args):
        if not isinstance(callee, Closure):
            raise CometError(f"cannot call a value of type {type_name(callee)}")
        decl = callee.decl
        if len(args) != len(decl.params):
            raise CometError(f"{decl.name} expects {len(decl.params)} arguments, got {len(args)}")
        if len(self.frames) >= MAX_DEPTH:
            raise CometError("stack overflow")
        env = Environment(callee.env)
        for (name, _), value in zip(decl.params, args):
            env.define(name, value)
        self.frames.append(decl.name)
        try:
            self.execute_block(decl.body.stmts, env)
        except ReturnSignal as signal:
            return signal.value
        finally:
            self.frames.pop()
        return None

    def need(self, wanted, value, op):
        if type_name(value) != wanted:
            raise CometError(f"'{op}' needs {wanted}, not {type_name(value)}")

    def binary(self, expr):
        op = expr.op
        left = self.evaluate(expr.left)
        if op in ("and", "or"):
            self.need("bool", left, op)
            if (op == "and" and not left) or (op == "or" and left):
                return left
            right = self.evaluate(expr.right)
            self.need("bool", right, op)
            return right
        right = self.evaluate(expr.right)
        if op in ("==", "!="):
            if type_name(left) != type_name(right):
                raise CometError(f"cannot compare {type_name(left)} with {type_name(right)}")
            return (left is right if isinstance(left, Closure) else left == right) == (op == "==")
        if op == "+" and type_name(left) == "str" and type_name(right) == "str":
            return left + right
        self.need("int", left, op)
        self.need("int", right, op)
        if op == "+":
            return left + right
        if op == "-":
            return left - right
        if op == "*":
            return left * right
        if op == "/":
            return comet_div(left, right)
        if op == "%":
            return comet_mod(left, right)
        if op == "<":
            return left < right
        if op == "<=":
            return left <= right
        if op == ">":
            return left > right
        return left >= right


def run_source(source):
    interp = Interpreter()
    try:
        interp.run(parse_program(tokenize(source)))
    except CometError as e:
        return interp.output, str(e)
    return interp.output, None
--- hint
The `Fn` case is one line: `self.env.define(stmt.name, Closure(stmt, self.env))`. The `Return` case checks `self.frames`, evaluates `stmt.expr` unless it is `None`, and raises `ReturnSignal`.
--- hint
In `call`, do the three checks first. Then build `env = Environment(callee.env)` and define each parameter: `decl.params` is a list of `(name, type)` pairs, so zip it with the arguments.
--- hint
Wrap the body in `try:` with `self.execute_block(decl.body.stmts, env)`, then `except ReturnSignal as signal: return signal.value`, and `finally: self.frames.pop()`. After the `try` statement, `return None`.

+++ practice | Closures written in Comet
--- task
This time you write Comet, not Python. The starter gives the lesson's finished interpreter and a Python string `PROGRAM`. Put three Comet function declarations in `PROGRAM`:

- `make_acc(start)` returns a function of one argument n. Each call of that function adds n to a running total, which starts at `start`, and returns the new total. Two accumulators made by separate calls of `make_acc` are independent.
- `compose(f, g)` returns a function of one argument x that returns `f(g(x))`.
- `repeat(f, n)` returns a function of one argument x that applies f to x n times and returns the result. With n = 0 it returns x unchanged.

The checks run `run_source(PROGRAM + more)`, where `more` is Comet code that calls your functions. For example, after `let a = make_acc(10);`, `print a(5); print a(-3);` prints `15` and `12`.
--- starter
from dataclasses import dataclass

KEYWORDS = {"let", "fn", "return", "if", "else", "while", "print",
            "true", "false", "and", "or", "not"}
TWO_CHAR = {"==", "!=", "<=", ">=", "->"}
ONE_CHAR = set("+-*/%<>=(){},;:")
ESCAPES = {'"': '"', "\\": "\\", "n": "\n"}
DIGITS = "0123456789"
LETTERS = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ_"


@dataclass
class Token:
    kind: str
    text: str
    line: int
    col: int


class LexError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


def tokenize(source):
    tokens = []
    i = 0
    line = 1
    col = 1
    n = len(source)

    def advance(count):
        nonlocal i, line, col
        for _ in range(count):
            if source[i] == "\n":
                line += 1
                col = 1
            else:
                col += 1
            i += 1

    while i < n:
        ch = source[i]
        start_line, start_col = line, col
        if ch in " \t\r\n":
            advance(1)
        elif ch == "#":
            while i < n and source[i] != "\n":
                advance(1)
        elif ch in DIGITS:
            j = i
            while j < n and source[j] in DIGITS:
                j += 1
            tokens.append(Token("NUMBER", source[i:j], start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch in LETTERS:
            j = i
            while j < n and (source[j] in LETTERS or source[j] in DIGITS):
                j += 1
            word = source[i:j]
            kind = "KEYWORD" if word in KEYWORDS else "IDENT"
            tokens.append(Token(kind, word, start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch == '"':
            advance(1)
            chars = []
            while True:
                if i >= n or source[i] == "\n":
                    raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                c = source[i]
                if c == '"':
                    advance(1)
                    break
                if c == "\\":
                    if i + 1 >= n or source[i + 1] == "\n":
                        raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                    if source[i + 1] not in ESCAPES:
                        raise LexError("unknown escape", line, col)
                    chars.append(ESCAPES[source[i + 1]])
                    advance(2)
                else:
                    chars.append(c)
                    advance(1)
            tokens.append(Token("STRING", "".join(chars), start_line, start_col))
        elif source[i:i + 2] in TWO_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", source[i:i + 2], start_line, start_col))
            advance(2)
        elif ch in ONE_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", ch, start_line, start_col))
            advance(1)
        else:
            raise LexError(f"unexpected character {ch!r}", start_line, start_col)
    tokens.append(Token("EOF", "", line, col))
    return tokens
