class ParseError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


COMPARE = ("==", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">=")
TYPES = ("int", "bool", "str")


class Parser:
    def __init__(self, tokens):
        self.tokens = tokens
        self.pos = 0

    def peek(self, ahead=0):
        return self.tokens[min(self.pos + ahead, len(self.tokens) - 1)]

    def at(self, *texts):
        tok = self.peek()
        return tok.kind in ("OP", "KEYWORD") and tok.text in texts

    def advance(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "EOF":
            self.pos += 1
        return tok

    def error(self, message):
        tok = self.peek()
        return ParseError(message, tok.line, tok.col)

    def expect(self, text):
        if not self.at(text):
            raise self.error(f"expected '{text}'")
        return self.advance()

    def expr(self):
        return self.or_expr()

    def or_expr(self):
        left = self.and_expr()
        while self.at("or"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.and_expr())
        return left

    def and_expr(self):
        left = self.not_expr()
        while self.at("and"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.not_expr())
        return left

    def not_expr(self):
        if self.at("not"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("not", self.not_expr())
        return self.compare()

    def compare(self):
        left = self.sum()
        if self.at(*COMPARE):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.sum())
            if self.at(*COMPARE):
                raise self.error("comparisons cannot be chained")
        return left

    def sum(self):
        left = self.product()
        while self.at("+", "-"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.product())
        return left

    def product(self):
        left = self.unary()
        while self.at("*", "/", "%"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.unary())
        return left

    def unary(self):
        if self.at("-"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("-", self.unary())
        return self.call()

    def call(self):
        expr = self.primary()
        while self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            args = []
            if not self.at(")"):
                args.append(self.expr())
                while self.at(","):
                    self.advance()
                    args.append(self.expr())
            self.expect(")")
            expr = Call(expr, args)
        return expr

    def primary(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind == "NUMBER":
            self.advance()
            return Num(int(tok.text))
        if tok.kind == "STRING":
            self.advance()
            return Str(tok.text)
        if tok.kind == "IDENT":
            self.advance()
            return Var(tok.text)
        if self.at("true", "false"):
            self.advance()
            return Bool(tok.text == "true")
        if self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            inner = self.expr()
            self.expect(")")
            return inner
        raise self.error("expected an expression")

    def program(self):
        stmts = []
        while self.peek().kind != "EOF":
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        return Program(stmts)

    def statement(self):
        if self.at("let"):
            return self.let_stmt()
        if self.at("print"):
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Print(value)
        if self.at("if"):
            return self.if_stmt()
        if self.at("while"):
            self.advance()
            cond = self.expr()
            return While(cond, self.block())
        if self.at("fn"):
            return self.fn_stmt()
        if self.at("return"):
            self.advance()
            value = None if self.at(";") else self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Return(value)
        nxt = self.peek(1)
        if self.peek().kind == "IDENT" and nxt.kind == "OP" and nxt.text == "=":
            name = self.advance().text
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Assign(name, value)
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return ExprStmt(value)

    def name(self):
        if self.peek().kind != "IDENT":
            raise self.error("expected a name")
        return self.advance().text

    def type_name(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "IDENT" or tok.text not in TYPES:
            raise self.error("expected a type")
        return self.advance().text

    def let_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        self.expect("=")
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return Let(name, type_, value)

    def if_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        cond = self.expr()
        then = self.block()
        else_ = None
        if self.at("else"):
            self.advance()
            else_ = self.if_stmt() if self.at("if") else self.block()
        return If(cond, then, else_)

    def block(self):
        self.expect("{")
        stmts = []
        while not self.at("}"):
            if self.peek().kind == "EOF":
                raise self.error("expected '}'")
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        self.advance()
        return Block(stmts)

    def param(self):
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        return (name, type_)

    def fn_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        self.expect("(")
        params = []
        if not self.at(")"):
            params.append(self.param())
            while self.at(","):
                self.advance()
                params.append(self.param())
        self.expect(")")
        ret = None
        if self.at("->"):
            self.advance()
            ret = self.type_name()
        return Fn(name, params, ret, self.block())


def parse_program(tokens):
    return Parser(tokens).program()

def comet_div(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q


def comet_mod(a, b):
    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FnType:
    params: tuple
    ret: object


def show_type(t):
    if isinstance(t, FnType):
        return "fn(" + ", ".join(show_type(p) for p in t.params) + ") -> " + show_type(t.ret)
    return t


class TypeCheckError(Exception):
    pass


ARITH = ("-", "*", "/", "%")
ORDER = ("<", "<=", ">", ">=")


class Checker:
    def __init__(self):
        self.scopes = [{}]
        self.returns = []

    def declare(self, name, t):
        if name in self.scopes[-1]:
            raise TypeCheckError(f"{name} is already declared in this scope")
        self.scopes[-1][name] = t

    def lookup(self, name):
        for scope in reversed(self.scopes):
            if name in scope:
                return scope[name]
        raise TypeCheckError(f"undefined variable {name}")

    def check_program(self, program):
        for stmt in program.stmts:
            self.check_stmt(stmt)

    def check_block(self, stmts):
        self.scopes.append({})
        try:
            for stmt in stmts:
                self.check_stmt(stmt)
        finally:
            self.scopes.pop()

    def value_type(self, expr):
        t = self.check_expr(expr)
        if t == "void":
            raise TypeCheckError("a call that returns nothing has no value")
        return t

    def check_stmt(self, stmt):
        if isinstance(stmt, Let):
            t = self.value_type(stmt.expr)
            if stmt.type is not None and stmt.type != t:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"{stmt.name} is declared {show_type(stmt.type)} but given {show_type(t)}")
            self.declare(stmt.name, t)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Assign):
            wanted = self.lookup(stmt.name)
            t = self.value_type(stmt.expr)
            if t != wanted:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"cannot assign {show_type(t)} to {stmt.name}, which is {show_type(wanted)}")
        elif isinstance(stmt, Print):
            self.value_type(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, ExprStmt):
            self.check_expr(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, If):
            self.condition(stmt.cond, "if")
            self.check_stmt(stmt.then)
            if stmt.else_ is not None:
                self.check_stmt(stmt.else_)
        elif isinstance(stmt, While):
            self.condition(stmt.cond, "while")
            self.check_stmt(stmt.body)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Block):
            self.check_block(stmt.stmts)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Fn):
            self.check_fn(stmt)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Return):
            self.check_return(stmt)

    def condition(self, expr, where):
        t = self.check_expr(expr)
        if t != "bool":
            raise TypeCheckError(f"the condition of {where} must be bool, not {show_type(t)}")

    def check_fn(self, stmt):
        for name, t in stmt.params:
            if t is None:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"parameter {name} of {stmt.name} needs a type")
        ret = stmt.ret if stmt.ret is not None else "void"
        self.declare(stmt.name, FnType(tuple(t for _, t in stmt.params), ret))
        self.scopes.append({})
        self.returns.append(ret)
        try:
            for name, t in stmt.params:
                self.declare(name, t)
            for inner in stmt.body.stmts:
                self.check_stmt(inner)
        finally:
            self.returns.pop()
            self.scopes.pop()
        if ret != "void" and not self.always_returns(stmt.body.stmts):
            raise TypeCheckError(f"{stmt.name} might end without returning a value of type {ret}")

    def check_return(self, stmt):
        if not self.returns:
            raise TypeCheckError("return outside a function")
        wanted = self.returns[-1]
        if stmt.expr is None:
            if wanted != "void":
                raise TypeCheckError(f"return needs a {wanted} value")
            return
        if wanted == "void":
            raise TypeCheckError("this function returns nothing, so return takes no value")
        t = self.value_type(stmt.expr)
        if t != wanted:
            raise TypeCheckError(f"return needs {wanted}, not {show_type(t)}")

    def always_returns(self, stmts):
        for stmt in stmts:
            if isinstance(stmt, Return):
                return True
            if isinstance(stmt, Block) and self.always_returns(stmt.stmts):
                return True
            if isinstance(stmt, If) and stmt.else_ is not None:
                if self.always_returns([stmt.then]) and self.always_returns([stmt.else_]):
                    return True
        return False

    def check_expr(self, expr):
        if isinstance(expr, Num):
            return "int"
        if isinstance(expr, Str):
            return "str"
        if isinstance(expr, Bool):
            return "bool"
        if isinstance(expr, Var):
            return self.lookup(expr.name)
        if isinstance(expr, Unary):
            t = self.check_expr(expr.expr)
            wanted = "int" if expr.op == "-" else "bool"
            if t != wanted:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"'{expr.op}' needs {wanted}, not {show_type(t)}")
            return wanted
        if isinstance(expr, Binary):
            return self.check_binary(expr)
        if isinstance(expr, Call):
            return self.check_call(expr)
        raise TypeCheckError(f"unknown expression {type(expr).__name__}")

    def check_binary(self, expr):
        left = self.check_expr(expr.left)
        right = self.check_expr(expr.right)
        return self.binary_type(expr.op, left, right)

    def binary_type(self, op, left, right):
        if "void" in (left, right):
            raise TypeCheckError("a call that returns nothing has no value")
        if op in ("and", "or"):
            if left != "bool" or right != "bool":
                raise TypeCheckError(f"'{op}' needs two bools, not {show_type(left)} and {show_type(right)}")
            return "bool"
        if op in ("==", "!="):
            if left != right:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"cannot compare {show_type(left)} with {show_type(right)}")
            return "bool"
        if op == "+" and left == right and left in ("int", "str"):
            return left
        if op in ARITH + ORDER + ("+",):
            if left != "int" or right != "int":
                raise TypeCheckError(f"'{op}' needs two ints, not {show_type(left)} and {show_type(right)}")
            return "bool" if op in ORDER else "int"
        raise TypeCheckError(f"unknown operator {op}")

    def check_call(self, expr):
        callee = self.check_expr(expr.callee)
        if not isinstance(callee, FnType):
            raise TypeCheckError(f"cannot call a value of type {show_type(callee)}")
        if len(expr.args) != len(callee.params):
            raise TypeCheckError(f"expected {len(callee.params)} arguments, got {len(expr.args)}")
        for arg, wanted in zip(expr.args, callee.params):
            t = self.check_expr(arg)
            if t != wanted:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"argument needs {show_type(wanted)}, not {show_type(t)}")
        return callee.ret


def check_source(source):
    try:
        Checker().check_program(parse_program(tokenize(source)))
    except TypeCheckError as e:
        return str(e)
    return None
--- hint
Start with `check_expr`: literals, `Var` through `self.lookup`, `Unary`, `Binary` (compute both operand types first, then apply the rule for the operator), and `Call` (the callee's type must be an `FnType`; compare the argument count and each argument's type with its parameter type, and return `ret`).
--- hint
In `check_stmt`, a small helper that checks an expression and refuses `"void"` serves `Let`, `Assign`, `Print` and `Return`. For `If` and `While`, check the condition is `"bool"` and pass the branches back to `check_stmt`: a `Block` goes to `self.check_block`.
--- hint
For `Fn`: raise if some parameter's type is `None`; compute `ret` (`"void"` when `stmt.ret` is `None`); `self.declare(stmt.name, FnType(tuple(types), ret))`; then append a new scope and `ret`, declare the parameters, check each body statement, and pop both in a `finally`. `always_returns` loops over the statements and returns `True` as soon as one is a `Return`, a `Block` that always returns, or an `If` with an `else` whose two branches both always return.

+++ practice | Typing telemetry rules
--- task
Ground controllers write alarm rules as Comet expressions over the fields of a telemetry reading, such as `temp > 80 and not venting`. A rule with a type error should be refused when it is uploaded, not when it first fires. Write two functions (the starter gives the lexer and parser, and `TypeCheckError`):

- `expr_type(source, fields)`: parse the expression with `parse_program(tokenize(source + ";")).stmts[0].expr`, and return its type, `"int"`, `"bool"` or `"str"`, by the lesson's rules. `fields` is a dictionary from field name to type. A name that is not a field raises `TypeCheckError`, and so does any rule that does not fit, and any call: rules cannot call functions.
- `valid_rules(rules, fields)`: the list of the rules (source strings) that type check **and** have type `"bool"`, in their original order, since an alarm rule must be true or false.

For example, with `fields = {"temp": "int", "venting": "bool", "mode": "str"}`, `expr_type("temp > 80 and not venting", fields)` is `"bool"`.
--- starter
from dataclasses import dataclass

KEYWORDS = {"let", "fn", "return", "if", "else", "while", "print",
            "true", "false", "and", "or", "not"}
TWO_CHAR = {"==", "!=", "<=", ">=", "->"}
ONE_CHAR = set("+-*/%<>=(){},;:")
ESCAPES = {'"': '"', "\\": "\\", "n": "\n"}
DIGITS = "0123456789"
LETTERS = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ_"


@dataclass
class Token:
    kind: str
    text: str
    line: int
    col: int


class LexError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


def tokenize(source):
    tokens = []
    i = 0
    line = 1
    col = 1
    n = len(source)

    def advance(count):
        nonlocal i, line, col
        for _ in range(count):
            if source[i] == "\n":
                line += 1
                col = 1
            else:
                col += 1
            i += 1

    while i < n:
        ch = source[i]
        start_line, start_col = line, col
        if ch in " \t\r\n":
            advance(1)
        elif ch == "#":
            while i < n and source[i] != "\n":
                advance(1)
        elif ch in DIGITS:
            j = i
            while j < n and source[j] in DIGITS:
                j += 1
            tokens.append(Token("NUMBER", source[i:j], start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch in LETTERS:
            j = i
            while j < n and (source[j] in LETTERS or source[j] in DIGITS):
                j += 1
            word = source[i:j]
            kind = "KEYWORD" if word in KEYWORDS else "IDENT"
            tokens.append(Token(kind, word, start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch == '"':
            advance(1)
            chars = []
            while True:
                if i >= n or source[i] == "\n":
                    raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                c = source[i]
                if c == '"':
                    advance(1)
                    break
                if c == "\\":
                    if i + 1 >= n or source[i + 1] == "\n":
                        raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                    if source[i + 1] not in ESCAPES:
                        raise LexError("unknown escape", line, col)
                    chars.append(ESCAPES[source[i + 1]])
                    advance(2)
                else:
                    chars.append(c)
                    advance(1)
            tokens.append(Token("STRING", "".join(chars), start_line, start_col))
        elif source[i:i + 2] in TWO_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", source[i:i + 2], start_line, start_col))
            advance(2)
        elif ch in ONE_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", ch, start_line, start_col))
            advance(1)
        else:
            raise LexError(f"unexpected character {ch!r}", start_line, start_col)
    tokens.append(Token("EOF", "", line, col))
    return tokens


@dataclass
class Num:

@dataclass

@dataclass

    callee: object
    args: list


@dataclass
class Let:
    name: str

@dataclass

    name: str
    expr: object


@dataclass

    expr: object

    then: object
    else_: object


@dataclass

    name: str
    params: list
    ret: object
    body: object


@dataclass
class Return:

@dataclass

@dataclass

@dataclass
class Program:
    stmts: list


class ParseError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


COMPARE = ("==", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">=")
TYPES = ("int", "bool", "str")


class Parser:
    def __init__(self, tokens):
        self.tokens = tokens
        self.pos = 0

    def peek(self, ahead=0):
        return self.tokens[min(self.pos + ahead, len(self.tokens) - 1)]

    def at(self, *texts):
        tok = self.peek()
        return tok.kind in ("OP", "KEYWORD") and tok.text in texts

    def advance(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "EOF":
            self.pos += 1
        return tok

    def error(self, message):
        tok = self.peek()
        return ParseError(message, tok.line, tok.col)

    def expect(self, text):
        if not self.at(text):
            raise self.error(f"expected '{text}'")
        return self.advance()

    def expr(self):
        return self.or_expr()

    def or_expr(self):
        left = self.and_expr()
        while self.at("or"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.and_expr())
        return left

    def and_expr(self):
        left = self.not_expr()
        while self.at("and"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.not_expr())
        return left

    def not_expr(self):
        if self.at("not"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("not", self.not_expr())
        return self.compare()

    def compare(self):
        left = self.sum()
        if self.at(*COMPARE):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.sum())
            if self.at(*COMPARE):
                raise self.error("comparisons cannot be chained")
        return left

    def sum(self):
        left = self.product()
        while self.at("+", "-"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.product())
        return left

    def product(self):
        left = self.unary()
        while self.at("*", "/", "%"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.unary())
        return left

    def unary(self):
        if self.at("-"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("-", self.unary())
        return self.call()

    def call(self):
        expr = self.primary()
        while self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            args = []
            if not self.at(")"):
                args.append(self.expr())
                while self.at(","):
                    self.advance()
                    args.append(self.expr())
            self.expect(")")
            expr = Call(expr, args)
        return expr

    def primary(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind == "NUMBER":
            self.advance()
            return Num(int(tok.text))
        if tok.kind == "STRING":
            self.advance()
            return Str(tok.text)
        if tok.kind == "IDENT":
            self.advance()
            return Var(tok.text)
        if self.at("true", "false"):
            self.advance()
            return Bool(tok.text == "true")
        if self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            inner = self.expr()
            self.expect(")")
            return inner
        raise self.error("expected an expression")

    def program(self):
        stmts = []
        while self.peek().kind != "EOF":
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        return Program(stmts)

    def statement(self):
        if self.at("let"):
            return self.let_stmt()
        if self.at("print"):
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Print(value)
        if self.at("if"):
            return self.if_stmt()
        if self.at("while"):
            self.advance()
            cond = self.expr()
            return While(cond, self.block())
        if self.at("fn"):
            return self.fn_stmt()
        if self.at("return"):
            self.advance()
            value = None if self.at(";") else self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Return(value)
        nxt = self.peek(1)
        if self.peek().kind == "IDENT" and nxt.kind == "OP" and nxt.text == "=":
            name = self.advance().text
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Assign(name, value)
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return ExprStmt(value)

    def name(self):
        if self.peek().kind != "IDENT":
            raise self.error("expected a name")
        return self.advance().text

    def type_name(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "IDENT" or tok.text not in TYPES:
            raise self.error("expected a type")
        return self.advance().text

    def let_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        self.expect("=")
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return Let(name, type_, value)

    def if_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        cond = self.expr()
        then = self.block()
        else_ = None
        if self.at("else"):
            self.advance()
            else_ = self.if_stmt() if self.at("if") else self.block()
        return If(cond, then, else_)

    def block(self):
        self.expect("{")
        stmts = []
        while not self.at("}"):
            if self.peek().kind == "EOF":
                raise self.error("expected '}'")
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        self.advance()
        return Block(stmts)

    def param(self):
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        return (name, type_)

    def fn_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        self.expect("(")
        params = []
        if not self.at(")"):
            params.append(self.param())
            while self.at(","):
                self.advance()
                params.append(self.param())
        self.expect(")")
        ret = None
        if self.at("->"):
            self.advance()
            ret = self.type_name()
        return Fn(name, params, ret, self.block())


def parse_program(tokens):
    return Parser(tokens).program()


class CometError(Exception):
    pass


def comet_div(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q


def comet_mod(a, b):
    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)


class TypeCheckError(Exception):
    pass

    raise TypeCheckError("expr_type is not written yet")

    raise TypeCheckError("valid_rules is not written yet")

from dataclasses import dataclass

KEYWORDS = {"let", "fn", "return", "if", "else", "while", "print",
            "true", "false", "and", "or", "not"}
TWO_CHAR = {"==", "!=", "<=", ">=", "->"}
ONE_CHAR = set("+-*/%<>=(){},;:")
ESCAPES = {'"': '"', "\\": "\\", "n": "\n"}
DIGITS = "0123456789"
LETTERS = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ_"


@dataclass
class Token:
    kind: str
    text: str
    line: int
    col: int


class LexError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


def tokenize(source):
    tokens = []
    i = 0
    line = 1
    col = 1
    n = len(source)

    def advance(count):
        nonlocal i, line, col
        for _ in range(count):
            if source[i] == "\n":
                line += 1
                col = 1
            else:
                col += 1
            i += 1

    while i < n:
        ch = source[i]
        start_line, start_col = line, col
        if ch in " \t\r\n":
            advance(1)
        elif ch == "#":
            while i < n and source[i] != "\n":
                advance(1)
        elif ch in DIGITS:
            j = i
            while j < n and source[j] in DIGITS:
                j += 1
            tokens.append(Token("NUMBER", source[i:j], start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch in LETTERS:
            j = i
            while j < n and (source[j] in LETTERS or source[j] in DIGITS):
                j += 1
            word = source[i:j]
            kind = "KEYWORD" if word in KEYWORDS else "IDENT"
            tokens.append(Token(kind, word, start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch == '"':
            advance(1)
            chars = []
            while True:
                if i >= n or source[i] == "\n":
                    raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                c = source[i]
                if c == '"':
                    advance(1)
                    break
                if c == "\\":
                    if i + 1 >= n or source[i + 1] == "\n":
                        raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                    if source[i + 1] not in ESCAPES:
                        raise LexError("unknown escape", line, col)
                    chars.append(ESCAPES[source[i + 1]])
                    advance(2)
                else:
                    chars.append(c)
                    advance(1)
            tokens.append(Token("STRING", "".join(chars), start_line, start_col))
        elif source[i:i + 2] in TWO_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", source[i:i + 2], start_line, start_col))
            advance(2)
        elif ch in ONE_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", ch, start_line, start_col))
            advance(1)
        else:
            raise LexError(f"unexpected character {ch!r}", start_line, start_col)
    tokens.append(Token("EOF", "", line, col))
    return tokens

class ParseError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


COMPARE = ("==", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">=")
TYPES = ("int", "bool", "str")


class Parser:
    def __init__(self, tokens):
        self.tokens = tokens
        self.pos = 0

    def peek(self, ahead=0):
        return self.tokens[min(self.pos + ahead, len(self.tokens) - 1)]

    def at(self, *texts):
        tok = self.peek()
        return tok.kind in ("OP", "KEYWORD") and tok.text in texts

    def advance(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "EOF":
            self.pos += 1
        return tok

    def error(self, message):
        tok = self.peek()
        return ParseError(message, tok.line, tok.col)

    def expect(self, text):
        if not self.at(text):
            raise self.error(f"expected '{text}'")
        return self.advance()

    def expr(self):
        return self.or_expr()

    def or_expr(self):
        left = self.and_expr()
        while self.at("or"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.and_expr())
        return left

    def and_expr(self):
        left = self.not_expr()
        while self.at("and"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.not_expr())
        return left

    def not_expr(self):
        if self.at("not"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("not", self.not_expr())
        return self.compare()

    def compare(self):
        left = self.sum()
        if self.at(*COMPARE):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.sum())
            if self.at(*COMPARE):
                raise self.error("comparisons cannot be chained")
        return left

    def sum(self):
        left = self.product()
        while self.at("+", "-"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.product())
        return left

    def product(self):
        left = self.unary()
        while self.at("*", "/", "%"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.unary())
        return left

    def unary(self):
        if self.at("-"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("-", self.unary())
        return self.call()

    def call(self):
        expr = self.primary()
        while self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            args = []
            if not self.at(")"):
                args.append(self.expr())
                while self.at(","):
                    self.advance()
                    args.append(self.expr())
            self.expect(")")
            expr = Call(expr, args)
        return expr

    def primary(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind == "NUMBER":
            self.advance()
            return Num(int(tok.text))
        if tok.kind == "STRING":
            self.advance()
            return Str(tok.text)
        if tok.kind == "IDENT":
            self.advance()
            return Var(tok.text)
        if self.at("true", "false"):
            self.advance()
            return Bool(tok.text == "true")
        if self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            inner = self.expr()
            self.expect(")")
            return inner
        raise self.error("expected an expression")

    def program(self):
        stmts = []
        while self.peek().kind != "EOF":
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        return Program(stmts)

    def statement(self):
        if self.at("let"):
            return self.let_stmt()
        if self.at("print"):
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Print(value)
        if self.at("if"):
            return self.if_stmt()
        if self.at("while"):
            self.advance()
            cond = self.expr()
            return While(cond, self.block())
        if self.at("fn"):
            return self.fn_stmt()
        if self.at("return"):
            self.advance()
            value = None if self.at(";") else self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Return(value)
        nxt = self.peek(1)
        if self.peek().kind == "IDENT" and nxt.kind == "OP" and nxt.text == "=":
            name = self.advance().text
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Assign(name, value)
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return ExprStmt(value)

    def name(self):
        if self.peek().kind != "IDENT":
            raise self.error("expected a name")
        return self.advance().text

    def type_name(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "IDENT" or tok.text not in TYPES:
            raise self.error("expected a type")
        return self.advance().text

    def let_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        self.expect("=")
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return Let(name, type_, value)

    def if_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        cond = self.expr()
        then = self.block()
        else_ = None
        if self.at("else"):
            self.advance()
            else_ = self.if_stmt() if self.at("if") else self.block()
        return If(cond, then, else_)

    def block(self):
        self.expect("{")
        stmts = []
        while not self.at("}"):
            if self.peek().kind == "EOF":
                raise self.error("expected '}'")
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        self.advance()
        return Block(stmts)

    def param(self):
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        return (name, type_)

    def fn_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        self.expect("(")
        params = []
        if not self.at(")"):
            params.append(self.param())
            while self.at(","):
                self.advance()
                params.append(self.param())
        self.expect(")")
        ret = None
        if self.at("->"):
            self.advance()
            ret = self.type_name()
        return Fn(name, params, ret, self.block())


def parse_program(tokens):
    return Parser(tokens).program()


class CometError(Exception):
    pass


def comet_div(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q


def comet_mod(a, b):
    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)


class TypeCheckError(Exception):
    pass


def type_of(expr, fields):
    if isinstance(expr, Num):
        return "int"
    if isinstance(expr, Str):
        return "str"
    if isinstance(expr, Bool):
        return "bool"
    if isinstance(expr, Var):
        if expr.name not in fields:
            raise TypeCheckError(f"unknown field {expr.name}")
        return fields[expr.name]
    if isinstance(expr, Unary):
        t = type_of(expr.expr, fields)
        wanted = "int" if expr.op == "-" else "bool"
        if t != wanted:
            raise TypeCheckError(f"'{expr.op}' needs {wanted}, not {t}")
        return wanted
    if isinstance(expr, Binary):
        left = type_of(expr.left, fields)
        right = type_of(expr.right, fields)
        op = expr.op
        if op in ("and", "or"):
            if left != "bool" or right != "bool":
                raise TypeCheckError(f"'{op}' needs two bools")
            return "bool"
        if op in ("==", "!="):
            if left != right:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"cannot compare {left} with {right}")
            return "bool"
        if op == "+" and left == right == "str":
            return "str"
        if left != "int" or right != "int":
            raise TypeCheckError(f"'{op}' needs two ints, not {left} and {right}")
        return "bool" if op in ("<", "<=", ">", ">=") else "int"
    raise TypeCheckError("rules cannot call functions")


def expr_type(source, fields):
    expr = parse_program(tokenize(source + ";")).stmts[0].expr
    return type_of(expr, fields)


def valid_rules(rules, fields):
    good = []
    for rule in rules:
        try:
            if expr_type(rule, fields) == "bool":
                good.append(rule)
        except TypeCheckError:
            pass
    return good
--- hint
Write a recursive `type_of(expr, fields)` with one case per node kind: `Num`, `Str`, `Bool`, `Var` (look it up in `fields`), `Unary` and `Binary`, and raise `TypeCheckError` for anything else, which includes `Call`.
--- hint
For `Binary`, find both operand types first. `and` and `or` need two bools; `==` and `!=` need equal types; `+` accepts two strs; everything else needs two ints and gives `bool` for the four comparisons and `int` otherwise. `valid_rules` calls `expr_type` inside `try` and keeps the rule only when no error is raised and the type is `"bool"`.
--- check test | The example from the task, and the other types
(lambda f: expr_type("temp > 80 and not venting", f) == "bool" and expr_type('mode + "!"', f) == "str" and expr_type("-temp * 2 % 3", f) == "int" and expr_type("venting == false", f) == "bool")({"temp": "int", "venting": "bool", "mode": "str"})
--- check test | Type errors raise
(lambda f: all(raises(TypeCheckError, lambda s=s: expr_type(s, f)) for s in ["temp + venting", "mode < mode", "not temp", "venting or 1", "mode == 3", "-mode", 'mode - "a"']))({"temp": "int", "venting": "bool", "mode": "str"})
--- check test | Unknown fields and calls raise
(lambda f: raises(TypeCheckError, lambda: expr_type("pressure > 1", f)) and raises(TypeCheckError, lambda: expr_type("check(temp)", f)))({"temp": "int"})
--- check case | Only well-typed bool rules survive, in order
valid_rules(["temp > 80", "temp + 1", "mode == 3", "venting or temp", 'mode != "safe" and venting', "pressure > 1", "temp / 0 == 0"], {"temp": "int", "venting": "bool", "mode": "str"})
=> ["temp > 80", 'mode != "safe" and venting', "temp / 0 == 0"]
--- check case | No rules
valid_rules([], {"temp": "int"})
=> []

+++ practice | Choosing the operation from the types
--- task
In Comet, `+` means two different operations: adding ints and joining strings. The interpreter decides at run time, each time. A compiler decides once, from the types, and emits a different instruction for each; the JVM, for example, has `iadd` for ints. Recording that choice is called **elaboration**. The starter gives the lesson's finished checker. Write `typed_ops(source)`: type check the program and return the list of operation names for every operator in it, in the order the checker finishes them (an operator comes after its operands). Raise `TypeCheckError` if the program does not type check.

The names:

- `+` is `"iadd"` on ints and `"concat"` on strings; `-` `*` `/` `%` are `"isub"`, `"imul"`, `"idiv"`, `"irem"`.
- `<` `<=` `>` `>=` are `"ilt"`, `"ile"`, `"igt"`, `"ige"`.
- `==` is `"eq_"` and `!=` is `"ne_"` followed by the operands' type: `int`, `bool`, `str`, or `fn` for any function type.
- `and` and `or` are `"and"` and `"or"`; `not` is `"not"`; `-` in front is `"ineg"`.

For example, `typed_ops('print "a" + "b" == "ab";')` is `["concat", "eq_str"]`.
--- starter
from dataclasses import dataclass

KEYWORDS = {"let", "fn", "return", "if", "else", "while", "print",
            "true", "false", "and", "or", "not"}
TWO_CHAR = {"==", "!=", "<=", ">=", "->"}
ONE_CHAR = set("+-*/%<>=(){},;:")
ESCAPES = {'"': '"', "\\": "\\", "n": "\n"}
DIGITS = "0123456789"
LETTERS = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ_"


@dataclass
class Token:
    kind: str
    text: str
    line: int
    col: int


class LexError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


def tokenize(source):
    tokens = []
    i = 0
    line = 1
    col = 1
    n = len(source)

    def advance(count):
        nonlocal i, line, col
        for _ in range(count):
            if source[i] == "\n":
                line += 1
                col = 1
            else:
                col += 1
            i += 1

    while i < n:
        ch = source[i]
        start_line, start_col = line, col
        if ch in " \t\r\n":
            advance(1)
        elif ch == "#":
            while i < n and source[i] != "\n":
                advance(1)
        elif ch in DIGITS:
            j = i
            while j < n and source[j] in DIGITS:
                j += 1
            tokens.append(Token("NUMBER", source[i:j], start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch in LETTERS:
            j = i
            while j < n and (source[j] in LETTERS or source[j] in DIGITS):
                j += 1
            word = source[i:j]
            kind = "KEYWORD" if word in KEYWORDS else "IDENT"
            tokens.append(Token(kind, word, start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch == '"':
            advance(1)
            chars = []
            while True:
                if i >= n or source[i] == "\n":
                    raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                c = source[i]
                if c == '"':
                    advance(1)
                    break
                if c == "\\":
                    if i + 1 >= n or source[i + 1] == "\n":
                        raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                    if source[i + 1] not in ESCAPES:
                        raise LexError("unknown escape", line, col)
                    chars.append(ESCAPES[source[i + 1]])
                    advance(2)
                else:
                    chars.append(c)
                    advance(1)
            tokens.append(Token("STRING", "".join(chars), start_line, start_col))
        elif source[i:i + 2] in TWO_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", source[i:i + 2], start_line, start_col))
            advance(2)
        elif ch in ONE_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", ch, start_line, start_col))
            advance(1)
        else:
            raise LexError(f"unexpected character {ch!r}", start_line, start_col)
    tokens.append(Token("EOF", "", line, col))
    return tokens

class ParseError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


COMPARE = ("==", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">=")
TYPES = ("int", "bool", "str")


class Parser:
    def __init__(self, tokens):
        self.tokens = tokens
        self.pos = 0

    def peek(self, ahead=0):
        return self.tokens[min(self.pos + ahead, len(self.tokens) - 1)]

    def at(self, *texts):
        tok = self.peek()
        return tok.kind in ("OP", "KEYWORD") and tok.text in texts

    def advance(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "EOF":
            self.pos += 1
        return tok

    def error(self, message):
        tok = self.peek()
        return ParseError(message, tok.line, tok.col)

    def expect(self, text):
        if not self.at(text):
            raise self.error(f"expected '{text}'")
        return self.advance()

    def expr(self):
        return self.or_expr()

    def or_expr(self):
        left = self.and_expr()
        while self.at("or"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.and_expr())
        return left

    def and_expr(self):
        left = self.not_expr()
        while self.at("and"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.not_expr())
        return left

    def not_expr(self):
        if self.at("not"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("not", self.not_expr())
        return self.compare()

    def compare(self):
        left = self.sum()
        if self.at(*COMPARE):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.sum())
            if self.at(*COMPARE):
                raise self.error("comparisons cannot be chained")
        return left

    def sum(self):
        left = self.product()
        while self.at("+", "-"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.product())
        return left

    def product(self):
        left = self.unary()
        while self.at("*", "/", "%"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.unary())
        return left

    def unary(self):
        if self.at("-"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("-", self.unary())
        return self.call()

    def call(self):
        expr = self.primary()
        while self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            args = []
            if not self.at(")"):
                args.append(self.expr())
                while self.at(","):
                    self.advance()
                    args.append(self.expr())
            self.expect(")")
            expr = Call(expr, args)
        return expr

    def primary(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind == "NUMBER":
            self.advance()
            return Num(int(tok.text))
        if tok.kind == "STRING":
            self.advance()
            return Str(tok.text)
        if tok.kind == "IDENT":
            self.advance()
            return Var(tok.text)
        if self.at("true", "false"):
            self.advance()
            return Bool(tok.text == "true")
        if self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            inner = self.expr()
            self.expect(")")
            return inner
        raise self.error("expected an expression")

    def program(self):
        stmts = []
        while self.peek().kind != "EOF":
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        return Program(stmts)

    def statement(self):
        if self.at("let"):
            return self.let_stmt()
        if self.at("print"):
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Print(value)
        if self.at("if"):
            return self.if_stmt()
        if self.at("while"):
            self.advance()
            cond = self.expr()
            return While(cond, self.block())
        if self.at("fn"):
            return self.fn_stmt()
        if self.at("return"):
            self.advance()
            value = None if self.at(";") else self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Return(value)
        nxt = self.peek(1)
        if self.peek().kind == "IDENT" and nxt.kind == "OP" and nxt.text == "=":
            name = self.advance().text
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Assign(name, value)
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return ExprStmt(value)

    def name(self):
        if self.peek().kind != "IDENT":
            raise self.error("expected a name")
        return self.advance().text

    def type_name(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "IDENT" or tok.text not in TYPES:
            raise self.error("expected a type")
        return self.advance().text

    def let_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        self.expect("=")
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return Let(name, type_, value)

    def if_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        cond = self.expr()
        then = self.block()
        else_ = None
        if self.at("else"):
            self.advance()
            else_ = self.if_stmt() if self.at("if") else self.block()
        return If(cond, then, else_)

    def block(self):
        self.expect("{")
        stmts = []
        while not self.at("}"):
            if self.peek().kind == "EOF":
                raise self.error("expected '}'")
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        self.advance()
        return Block(stmts)

    def param(self):
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        return (name, type_)

    def fn_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        self.expect("(")
        params = []
        if not self.at(")"):
            params.append(self.param())
            while self.at(","):
                self.advance()
                params.append(self.param())
        self.expect(")")
        ret = None
        if self.at("->"):
            self.advance()
            ret = self.type_name()
        return Fn(name, params, ret, self.block())


def parse_program(tokens):
    return Parser(tokens).program()


class CometError(Exception):
    pass


def comet_div(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q


def comet_mod(a, b):
    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FnType:
    params: tuple
    ret: object


def show_type(t):
    if isinstance(t, FnType):
        return "fn(" + ", ".join(show_type(p) for p in t.params) + ") -> " + show_type(t.ret)
    return t


class TypeCheckError(Exception):
    pass


ARITH = ("-", "*", "/", "%")
ORDER = ("<", "<=", ">", ">=")


class Checker:
    def __init__(self):
        self.scopes = [{}]
        self.returns = []

    def declare(self, name, t):
        if name in self.scopes[-1]:
            raise TypeCheckError(f"{name} is already declared in this scope")
        self.scopes[-1][name] = t

    def lookup(self, name):
        for scope in reversed(self.scopes):
            if name in scope:
                return scope[name]
        raise TypeCheckError(f"undefined variable {name}")

    def check_program(self, program):
        for stmt in program.stmts:
            self.check_stmt(stmt)

    def check_block(self, stmts):
        self.scopes.append({})
        try:
            for stmt in stmts:
                self.check_stmt(stmt)
        finally:
            self.scopes.pop()

    def value_type(self, expr):
        t = self.check_expr(expr)
        if t == "void":
            raise TypeCheckError("a call that returns nothing has no value")
        return t

    def check_stmt(self, stmt):
        if isinstance(stmt, Let):
            t = self.value_type(stmt.expr)
            if stmt.type is not None and stmt.type != t:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"{stmt.name} is declared {show_type(stmt.type)} but given {show_type(t)}")
            self.declare(stmt.name, t)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Assign):
            wanted = self.lookup(stmt.name)
            t = self.value_type(stmt.expr)
            if t != wanted:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"cannot assign {show_type(t)} to {stmt.name}, which is {show_type(wanted)}")
        elif isinstance(stmt, Print):
            self.value_type(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, ExprStmt):
            self.check_expr(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, If):
            self.condition(stmt.cond, "if")
            self.check_stmt(stmt.then)
            if stmt.else_ is not None:
                self.check_stmt(stmt.else_)
        elif isinstance(stmt, While):
            self.condition(stmt.cond, "while")
            self.check_stmt(stmt.body)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Block):
            self.check_block(stmt.stmts)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Fn):
            self.check_fn(stmt)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Return):
            self.check_return(stmt)

    def condition(self, expr, where):
        t = self.check_expr(expr)
        if t != "bool":
            raise TypeCheckError(f"the condition of {where} must be bool, not {show_type(t)}")

    def check_fn(self, stmt):
        for name, t in stmt.params:
            if t is None:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"parameter {name} of {stmt.name} needs a type")
        ret = stmt.ret if stmt.ret is not None else "void"
        self.declare(stmt.name, FnType(tuple(t for _, t in stmt.params), ret))
        self.scopes.append({})
        self.returns.append(ret)
        try:
            for name, t in stmt.params:
                self.declare(name, t)
            for inner in stmt.body.stmts:
                self.check_stmt(inner)
        finally:
            self.returns.pop()
            self.scopes.pop()
        if ret != "void" and not self.always_returns(stmt.body.stmts):
            raise TypeCheckError(f"{stmt.name} might end without returning a value of type {ret}")

    def check_return(self, stmt):
        if not self.returns:
            raise TypeCheckError("return outside a function")
        wanted = self.returns[-1]
        if stmt.expr is None:
            if wanted != "void":
                raise TypeCheckError(f"return needs a {wanted} value")
            return
        if wanted == "void":
            raise TypeCheckError("this function returns nothing, so return takes no value")
        t = self.value_type(stmt.expr)
        if t != wanted:
            raise TypeCheckError(f"return needs {wanted}, not {show_type(t)}")

    def always_returns(self, stmts):
        for stmt in stmts:
            if isinstance(stmt, Return):
                return True
            if isinstance(stmt, Block) and self.always_returns(stmt.stmts):
                return True
            if isinstance(stmt, If) and stmt.else_ is not None:
                if self.always_returns([stmt.then]) and self.always_returns([stmt.else_]):
                    return True
        return False

    def check_expr(self, expr):
        if isinstance(expr, Num):
            return "int"
        if isinstance(expr, Str):
            return "str"
        if isinstance(expr, Bool):
            return "bool"
        if isinstance(expr, Var):
            return self.lookup(expr.name)
        if isinstance(expr, Unary):
            t = self.check_expr(expr.expr)
            wanted = "int" if expr.op == "-" else "bool"
            if t != wanted:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"'{expr.op}' needs {wanted}, not {show_type(t)}")
            return wanted
        if isinstance(expr, Binary):
            return self.check_binary(expr)
        if isinstance(expr, Call):
            return self.check_call(expr)
        raise TypeCheckError(f"unknown expression {type(expr).__name__}")

    def check_binary(self, expr):
        left = self.check_expr(expr.left)
        right = self.check_expr(expr.right)
        return self.binary_type(expr.op, left, right)

    def binary_type(self, op, left, right):
        if "void" in (left, right):
            raise TypeCheckError("a call that returns nothing has no value")
        if op in ("and", "or"):
            if left != "bool" or right != "bool":
                raise TypeCheckError(f"'{op}' needs two bools, not {show_type(left)} and {show_type(right)}")
            return "bool"
        if op in ("==", "!="):
            if left != right:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"cannot compare {show_type(left)} with {show_type(right)}")
            return "bool"
        if op == "+" and left == right and left in ("int", "str"):
            return left
        if op in ARITH + ORDER + ("+",):
            if left != "int" or right != "int":
                raise TypeCheckError(f"'{op}' needs two ints, not {show_type(left)} and {show_type(right)}")
            return "bool" if op in ORDER else "int"
        raise TypeCheckError(f"unknown operator {op}")

    def check_call(self, expr):
        callee = self.check_expr(expr.callee)
        if not isinstance(callee, FnType):
            raise TypeCheckError(f"cannot call a value of type {show_type(callee)}")
        if len(expr.args) != len(callee.params):
            raise TypeCheckError(f"expected {len(callee.params)} arguments, got {len(expr.args)}")
        for arg, wanted in zip(expr.args, callee.params):
            t = self.check_expr(arg)
            if t != wanted:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"argument needs {show_type(wanted)}, not {show_type(t)}")
        return callee.ret


def check_source(source):
    try:
        Checker().check_program(parse_program(tokenize(source)))
    except TypeCheckError as e:
        return str(e)
    return None


def typed_ops(source):
    raise TypeCheckError("typed_ops is not written yet")

from dataclasses import dataclass

KEYWORDS = {"let", "fn", "return", "if", "else", "while", "print",
            "true", "false", "and", "or", "not"}
TWO_CHAR = {"==", "!=", "<=", ">=", "->"}
ONE_CHAR = set("+-*/%<>=(){},;:")
ESCAPES = {'"': '"', "\\": "\\", "n": "\n"}
DIGITS = "0123456789"
LETTERS = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ_"


@dataclass
class Token:
    kind: str
    text: str
    line: int
    col: int


class LexError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


def tokenize(source):
    tokens = []
    i = 0
    line = 1
    col = 1
    n = len(source)

    def advance(count):
        nonlocal i, line, col
        for _ in range(count):
            if source[i] == "\n":
                line += 1
                col = 1
            else:
                col += 1
            i += 1

    while i < n:
        ch = source[i]
        start_line, start_col = line, col
        if ch in " \t\r\n":
            advance(1)
        elif ch == "#":
            while i < n and source[i] != "\n":
                advance(1)
        elif ch in DIGITS:
            j = i
            while j < n and source[j] in DIGITS:
                j += 1
            tokens.append(Token("NUMBER", source[i:j], start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch in LETTERS:
            j = i
            while j < n and (source[j] in LETTERS or source[j] in DIGITS):
                j += 1
            word = source[i:j]
            kind = "KEYWORD" if word in KEYWORDS else "IDENT"
            tokens.append(Token(kind, word, start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch == '"':
            advance(1)
            chars = []
            while True:
                if i >= n or source[i] == "\n":
                    raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                c = source[i]
                if c == '"':
                    advance(1)
                    break
                if c == "\\":
                    if i + 1 >= n or source[i + 1] == "\n":
                        raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                    if source[i + 1] not in ESCAPES:
                        raise LexError("unknown escape", line, col)
                    chars.append(ESCAPES[source[i + 1]])
                    advance(2)
                else:
                    chars.append(c)
                    advance(1)
            tokens.append(Token("STRING", "".join(chars), start_line, start_col))
        elif source[i:i + 2] in TWO_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", source[i:i + 2], start_line, start_col))
            advance(2)
        elif ch in ONE_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", ch, start_line, start_col))
            advance(1)
        else:
            raise LexError(f"unexpected character {ch!r}", start_line, start_col)
    tokens.append(Token("EOF", "", line, col))
    return tokens

class ParseError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


COMPARE = ("==", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">=")
TYPES = ("int", "bool", "str")


class Parser:
    def __init__(self, tokens):
        self.tokens = tokens
        self.pos = 0

    def peek(self, ahead=0):
        return self.tokens[min(self.pos + ahead, len(self.tokens) - 1)]

    def at(self, *texts):
        tok = self.peek()
        return tok.kind in ("OP", "KEYWORD") and tok.text in texts

    def advance(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "EOF":
            self.pos += 1
        return tok

    def error(self, message):
        tok = self.peek()
        return ParseError(message, tok.line, tok.col)

    def expect(self, text):
        if not self.at(text):
            raise self.error(f"expected '{text}'")
        return self.advance()

    def expr(self):
        return self.or_expr()

    def or_expr(self):
        left = self.and_expr()
        while self.at("or"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.and_expr())
        return left

    def and_expr(self):
        left = self.not_expr()
        while self.at("and"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.not_expr())
        return left

    def not_expr(self):
        if self.at("not"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("not", self.not_expr())
        return self.compare()

    def compare(self):
        left = self.sum()
        if self.at(*COMPARE):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.sum())
            if self.at(*COMPARE):
                raise self.error("comparisons cannot be chained")
        return left

    def sum(self):
        left = self.product()
        while self.at("+", "-"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.product())
        return left

    def product(self):
        left = self.unary()
        while self.at("*", "/", "%"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.unary())
        return left

    def unary(self):
        if self.at("-"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("-", self.unary())
        return self.call()

    def call(self):
        expr = self.primary()
        while self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            args = []
            if not self.at(")"):
                args.append(self.expr())
                while self.at(","):
                    self.advance()
                    args.append(self.expr())
            self.expect(")")
            expr = Call(expr, args)
        return expr

    def primary(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind == "NUMBER":
            self.advance()
            return Num(int(tok.text))
        if tok.kind == "STRING":
            self.advance()
            return Str(tok.text)
        if tok.kind == "IDENT":
            self.advance()
            return Var(tok.text)
        if self.at("true", "false"):
            self.advance()
            return Bool(tok.text == "true")
        if self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            inner = self.expr()
            self.expect(")")
            return inner
        raise self.error("expected an expression")

    def program(self):
        stmts = []
        while self.peek().kind != "EOF":
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        return Program(stmts)

    def statement(self):
        if self.at("let"):
            return self.let_stmt()
        if self.at("print"):
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Print(value)
        if self.at("if"):
            return self.if_stmt()
        if self.at("while"):
            self.advance()
            cond = self.expr()
            return While(cond, self.block())
        if self.at("fn"):
            return self.fn_stmt()
        if self.at("return"):
            self.advance()
            value = None if self.at(";") else self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Return(value)
        nxt = self.peek(1)
        if self.peek().kind == "IDENT" and nxt.kind == "OP" and nxt.text == "=":
            name = self.advance().text
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Assign(name, value)
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return ExprStmt(value)

    def name(self):
        if self.peek().kind != "IDENT":
            raise self.error("expected a name")
        return self.advance().text

    def type_name(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "IDENT" or tok.text not in TYPES:
            raise self.error("expected a type")
        return self.advance().text

    def let_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        self.expect("=")
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return Let(name, type_, value)

    def if_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        cond = self.expr()
        then = self.block()
        else_ = None
        if self.at("else"):
            self.advance()
            else_ = self.if_stmt() if self.at("if") else self.block()
        return If(cond, then, else_)

    def block(self):
        self.expect("{")
        stmts = []
        while not self.at("}"):
            if self.peek().kind == "EOF":
                raise self.error("expected '}'")
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        self.advance()
        return Block(stmts)

    def param(self):
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        return (name, type_)

    def fn_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        self.expect("(")
        params = []
        if not self.at(")"):
            params.append(self.param())
            while self.at(","):
                self.advance()
                params.append(self.param())
        self.expect(")")
        ret = None
        if self.at("->"):
            self.advance()
            ret = self.type_name()
        return Fn(name, params, ret, self.block())


def parse_program(tokens):
    return Parser(tokens).program()

class TypeCheckError(Exception):
    pass
