ORDER = ("<", "<=", ">", ">=")


class Checker:
    def __init__(self):
        self.scopes = [{}]
        self.returns = []

    def declare(self, name, t):
        if name in self.scopes[-1]:
            raise TypeCheckError(f"{name} is already declared in this scope")
        self.scopes[-1][name] = t

    def lookup(self, name):
        for scope in reversed(self.scopes):
            if name in scope:
                return scope[name]
        raise TypeCheckError(f"undefined variable {name}")

    def check_program(self, program):
        for stmt in program.stmts:
            self.check_stmt(stmt)

    def check_block(self, stmts):
        self.scopes.append({})
        try:
            for stmt in stmts:
                self.check_stmt(stmt)
        finally:
            self.scopes.pop()

    def value_type(self, expr):
        t = self.check_expr(expr)
        if t == "void":
            raise TypeCheckError("a call that returns nothing has no value")
        return t

    def check_stmt(self, stmt):
        if isinstance(stmt, Let):
            t = self.value_type(stmt.expr)
            if stmt.type is not None and stmt.type != t:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"{stmt.name} is declared {show_type(stmt.type)} but given {show_type(t)}")
            self.declare(stmt.name, t)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Assign):
            wanted = self.lookup(stmt.name)
            t = self.value_type(stmt.expr)
            if t != wanted:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"cannot assign {show_type(t)} to {stmt.name}, which is {show_type(wanted)}")
        elif isinstance(stmt, Print):
            self.value_type(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, ExprStmt):
            self.check_expr(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, If):
            self.condition(stmt.cond, "if")
            self.check_stmt(stmt.then)
            if stmt.else_ is not None:
                self.check_stmt(stmt.else_)
        elif isinstance(stmt, While):
            self.condition(stmt.cond, "while")
            self.check_stmt(stmt.body)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Block):
            self.check_block(stmt.stmts)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Fn):
            self.check_fn(stmt)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Return):
            self.check_return(stmt)

    def condition(self, expr, where):
        t = self.check_expr(expr)
        if t != "bool":
            raise TypeCheckError(f"the condition of {where} must be bool, not {show_type(t)}")

    def check_fn(self, stmt):
        for name, t in stmt.params:
            if t is None:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"parameter {name} of {stmt.name} needs a type")
        ret = stmt.ret if stmt.ret is not None else "void"
        self.declare(stmt.name, FnType(tuple(t for _, t in stmt.params), ret))
        self.scopes.append({})
        self.returns.append(ret)
        try:
            for name, t in stmt.params:
                self.declare(name, t)
            for inner in stmt.body.stmts:
                self.check_stmt(inner)
        finally:
            self.returns.pop()
            self.scopes.pop()
        if ret != "void" and not self.always_returns(stmt.body.stmts):
            raise TypeCheckError(f"{stmt.name} might end without returning a value of type {ret}")

    def check_return(self, stmt):
        if not self.returns:
            raise TypeCheckError("return outside a function")
        wanted = self.returns[-1]
        if stmt.expr is None:
            if wanted != "void":
                raise TypeCheckError(f"return needs a {wanted} value")
            return
        if wanted == "void":
            raise TypeCheckError("this function returns nothing, so return takes no value")
        t = self.value_type(stmt.expr)
        if t != wanted:
            raise TypeCheckError(f"return needs {wanted}, not {show_type(t)}")

    def always_returns(self, stmts):
        for stmt in stmts:
            if isinstance(stmt, Return):
                return True
            if isinstance(stmt, Block) and self.always_returns(stmt.stmts):
                return True
            if isinstance(stmt, If) and stmt.else_ is not None:
                if self.always_returns([stmt.then]) and self.always_returns([stmt.else_]):
                    return True
        return False

    def check_expr(self, expr):
        if isinstance(expr, Num):
            return "int"
        if isinstance(expr, Str):
            return "str"
        if isinstance(expr, Bool):
            return "bool"
        if isinstance(expr, Var):
            return self.lookup(expr.name)
        if isinstance(expr, Unary):
            t = self.check_expr(expr.expr)
            wanted = "int" if expr.op == "-" else "bool"
            if t != wanted:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"'{expr.op}' needs {wanted}, not {show_type(t)}")
            return wanted
        if isinstance(expr, Binary):
            return self.check_binary(expr)
        if isinstance(expr, Call):
            return self.check_call(expr)
        raise TypeCheckError(f"unknown expression {type(expr).__name__}")

    def check_binary(self, expr):
        left = self.check_expr(expr.left)
        right = self.check_expr(expr.right)
        return self.binary_type(expr.op, left, right)

    def binary_type(self, op, left, right):
        if "void" in (left, right):
            raise TypeCheckError("a call that returns nothing has no value")
        if op in ("and", "or"):
            if left != "bool" or right != "bool":
                raise TypeCheckError(f"'{op}' needs two bools, not {show_type(left)} and {show_type(right)}")
            return "bool"
        if op in ("==", "!="):
            if left != right:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"cannot compare {show_type(left)} with {show_type(right)}")
            return "bool"
        if op == "+" and left == right and left in ("int", "str"):
            return left
        if op in ARITH + ORDER + ("+",):
            if left != "int" or right != "int":
                raise TypeCheckError(f"'{op}' needs two ints, not {show_type(left)} and {show_type(right)}")
            return "bool" if op in ORDER else "int"
        raise TypeCheckError(f"unknown operator {op}")

    def check_call(self, expr):
        callee = self.check_expr(expr.callee)
        if not isinstance(callee, FnType):
            raise TypeCheckError(f"cannot call a value of type {show_type(callee)}")
        if len(expr.args) != len(callee.params):
            raise TypeCheckError(f"expected {len(callee.params)} arguments, got {len(expr.args)}")
        for arg, wanted in zip(expr.args, callee.params):
            t = self.check_expr(arg)
            if t != wanted:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"argument needs {show_type(wanted)}, not {show_type(t)}")
        return callee.ret


def check_source(source):
    try:
        Checker().check_program(parse_program(tokenize(source)))
    except TypeCheckError as e:
        return str(e)
    return None


OP_NAMES = {"-": "isub", "*": "imul", "/": "idiv", "%": "irem",
            "<": "ilt", "<=": "ile", ">": "igt", ">=": "ige"}


class OpChecker(Checker):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.ops = []

    def check_expr(self, expr):
        t = super().check_expr(expr)
        if isinstance(expr, Unary):
            self.ops.append("ineg" if expr.op == "-" else "not")
        return t

    def check_binary(self, expr):
        left = self.check_expr(expr.left)
        right = self.check_expr(expr.right)
        t = self.binary_type(expr.op, left, right)
        op = expr.op
        if op in ("and", "or"):
            self.ops.append(op)
        elif op in ("==", "!="):
            kind = "fn" if isinstance(left, FnType) else left
            self.ops.append(("eq_" if op == "==" else "ne_") + kind)
        elif op == "+":
            self.ops.append("iadd" if t == "int" else "concat")
        else:
            self.ops.append(OP_NAMES[op])
        return t


def typed_ops(source):
    checker = OpChecker()
    checker.check_program(parse_program(tokenize(source)))
    return checker.ops
--- hint
Make a subclass of `Checker` with a list `self.ops`. Override `check_binary`: compute the operand types with `self.check_expr`, get the result type from `self.binary_type`, then append the name. Appending after the operands are checked gives the right order.
--- hint
For `==` and `!=` you need the operand type, which is `left`; use `"fn"` when it is an `FnType`. Override `check_expr` too, calling `super().check_expr(expr)` and appending `"ineg"` or `"not"` afterwards when the node is a `Unary`.
--- check case | The example from the task
typed_ops('print "a" + "b" == "ab";')
=> ["concat", "eq_str"]
--- check case | Nested expressions come out operands first
typed_ops('let s = "a" + "b"; print 1 + 2 * 3 == 7; print s == "x" and not (1 < 2); print -(4 % 3) != 1 - 1;')
=> ["concat", "imul", "iadd", "eq_int", "eq_str", "ilt", "not", "and", "irem", "ineg", "isub", "ne_int"]
--- check case | Inside functions, and equality on functions and bools
typed_ops("fn f(n: int) -> int { return n / 2; } print f == f; print f(4) >= 2 or true == false;")
=> ["idiv", "eq_fn", "ige", "eq_bool", "or"]
--- check case | A program without operators
typed_ops("let x = 1; print x;")
=> []
--- check test | Ill-typed programs raise
raises(TypeCheckError, lambda: typed_ops('print 1 + "a";')) and raises(TypeCheckError, lambda: typed_ops("print 1 == true;"))

+++ practice | Function types in annotations
--- task
Comet's annotations can only name `int`, `bool` and `str`, so a function that takes a function, like `fn apply(f, x) { return f(x); }`, cannot be checked: `f` has no type to write down. Extend the language with **function types** in annotations: `fn(T₁, …, Tₙ) -> R`, and `fn(T₁, …, Tₙ)` without an arrow for a function returning `void`. They may nest: `fn(int) -> fn(int) -> int` is a function returning a function, because the arrow's right side is itself a type.

The starter gives the lesson's finished checker. Change the parser's `type_name` method so that, when the next token is the keyword `fn`, it reads a function type and returns the matching `FnType` (with a tuple of parameter types). The checker then works unchanged, because it already compares types with `==`.

For example, `check_source("fn apply(f: fn(int) -> int, x: int) -> int { return f(x); } fn inc(n: int) -> int { return n + 1; } print apply(inc, 2);")` must be `None`.
--- starter
from dataclasses import dataclass

KEYWORDS = {"let", "fn", "return", "if", "else", "while", "print",
            "true", "false", "and", "or", "not"}
TWO_CHAR = {"==", "!=", "<=", ">=", "->"}
ONE_CHAR = set("+-*/%<>=(){},;:")
ESCAPES = {'"': '"', "\\": "\\", "n": "\n"}
DIGITS = "0123456789"
LETTERS = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ_"


@dataclass
class Token:
    kind: str
    text: str
    line: int
    col: int


class LexError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


def tokenize(source):
    tokens = []
    i = 0
    line = 1
    col = 1
    n = len(source)

    def advance(count):
        nonlocal i, line, col
        for _ in range(count):
            if source[i] == "\n":
                line += 1
                col = 1
            else:
                col += 1
            i += 1

    while i < n:
        ch = source[i]
        start_line, start_col = line, col
        if ch in " \t\r\n":
            advance(1)
        elif ch == "#":
            while i < n and source[i] != "\n":
                advance(1)
        elif ch in DIGITS:
            j = i
            while j < n and source[j] in DIGITS:
                j += 1
            tokens.append(Token("NUMBER", source[i:j], start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch in LETTERS:
            j = i
            while j < n and (source[j] in LETTERS or source[j] in DIGITS):
                j += 1
            word = source[i:j]
            kind = "KEYWORD" if word in KEYWORDS else "IDENT"
            tokens.append(Token(kind, word, start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch == '"':
            advance(1)
            chars = []
            while True:
                if i >= n or source[i] == "\n":
                    raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                c = source[i]
                if c == '"':
                    advance(1)
                    break
                if c == "\\":
                    if i + 1 >= n or source[i + 1] == "\n":
                        raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                    if source[i + 1] not in ESCAPES:
                        raise LexError("unknown escape", line, col)
                    chars.append(ESCAPES[source[i + 1]])
                    advance(2)
                else:
                    chars.append(c)
                    advance(1)
            tokens.append(Token("STRING", "".join(chars), start_line, start_col))
        elif source[i:i + 2] in TWO_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", source[i:i + 2], start_line, start_col))
            advance(2)
        elif ch in ONE_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", ch, start_line, start_col))
            advance(1)
        else:
            raise LexError(f"unexpected character {ch!r}", start_line, start_col)
    tokens.append(Token("EOF", "", line, col))
    return tokens

class ParseError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


COMPARE = ("==", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">=")
TYPES = ("int", "bool", "str")


class Parser:
    def __init__(self, tokens):
        self.tokens = tokens
        self.pos = 0

    def peek(self, ahead=0):
        return self.tokens[min(self.pos + ahead, len(self.tokens) - 1)]

    def at(self, *texts):
        tok = self.peek()
        return tok.kind in ("OP", "KEYWORD") and tok.text in texts

    def advance(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "EOF":
            self.pos += 1
        return tok

    def error(self, message):
        tok = self.peek()
        return ParseError(message, tok.line, tok.col)

    def expect(self, text):
        if not self.at(text):
            raise self.error(f"expected '{text}'")
        return self.advance()

    def expr(self):
        return self.or_expr()

    def or_expr(self):
        left = self.and_expr()
        while self.at("or"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.and_expr())
        return left

    def and_expr(self):
        left = self.not_expr()
        while self.at("and"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.not_expr())
        return left

    def not_expr(self):
        if self.at("not"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("not", self.not_expr())
        return self.compare()

    def compare(self):
        left = self.sum()
        if self.at(*COMPARE):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.sum())
            if self.at(*COMPARE):
                raise self.error("comparisons cannot be chained")
        return left

    def sum(self):
        left = self.product()
        while self.at("+", "-"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.product())
        return left

    def product(self):
        left = self.unary()
        while self.at("*", "/", "%"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.unary())
        return left

    def unary(self):
        if self.at("-"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("-", self.unary())
        return self.call()

    def call(self):
        expr = self.primary()
        while self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            args = []
            if not self.at(")"):
                args.append(self.expr())
                while self.at(","):
                    self.advance()
                    args.append(self.expr())
            self.expect(")")
            expr = Call(expr, args)
        return expr

    def primary(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind == "NUMBER":
            self.advance()
            return Num(int(tok.text))
        if tok.kind == "STRING":
            self.advance()
            return Str(tok.text)
        if tok.kind == "IDENT":
            self.advance()
            return Var(tok.text)
        if self.at("true", "false"):
            self.advance()
            return Bool(tok.text == "true")
        if self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            inner = self.expr()
            self.expect(")")
            return inner
        raise self.error("expected an expression")

    def program(self):
        stmts = []
        while self.peek().kind != "EOF":
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        return Program(stmts)

    def statement(self):
        if self.at("let"):
            return self.let_stmt()
        if self.at("print"):
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Print(value)
        if self.at("if"):
            return self.if_stmt()
        if self.at("while"):
            self.advance()
            cond = self.expr()
            return While(cond, self.block())
        if self.at("fn"):
            return self.fn_stmt()
        if self.at("return"):
            self.advance()
            value = None if self.at(";") else self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Return(value)
        nxt = self.peek(1)
        if self.peek().kind == "IDENT" and nxt.kind == "OP" and nxt.text == "=":
            name = self.advance().text
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Assign(name, value)
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return ExprStmt(value)

    def name(self):
        if self.peek().kind != "IDENT":
            raise self.error("expected a name")
        return self.advance().text

    def type_name(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "IDENT" or tok.text not in TYPES:
            raise self.error("expected a type")
        return self.advance().text

    def let_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        self.expect("=")
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return Let(name, type_, value)

    def if_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        cond = self.expr()
        then = self.block()
        else_ = None
        if self.at("else"):
            self.advance()
            else_ = self.if_stmt() if self.at("if") else self.block()
        return If(cond, then, else_)

    def block(self):
        self.expect("{")
        stmts = []
        while not self.at("}"):
            if self.peek().kind == "EOF":
                raise self.error("expected '}'")
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        self.advance()
        return Block(stmts)

    def param(self):
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        return (name, type_)

    def fn_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        self.expect("(")
        params = []
        if not self.at(")"):
            params.append(self.param())
            while self.at(","):
                self.advance()
                params.append(self.param())
        self.expect(")")
        ret = None
        if self.at("->"):
            self.advance()
            ret = self.type_name()
        return Fn(name, params, ret, self.block())


def parse_program(tokens):
    return Parser(tokens).program()


class CometError(Exception):
    pass


def comet_div(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q


def comet_mod(a, b):
    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FnType:
    params: tuple
    ret: object


def show_type(t):
    if isinstance(t, FnType):
        return "fn(" + ", ".join(show_type(p) for p in t.params) + ") -> " + show_type(t.ret)
    return t


class TypeCheckError(Exception):
    pass


ARITH = ("-", "*", "/", "%")
ORDER = ("<", "<=", ">", ">=")


class Checker:
    def __init__(self):
        self.scopes = [{}]
        self.returns = []

    def declare(self, name, t):
        if name in self.scopes[-1]:
            raise TypeCheckError(f"{name} is already declared in this scope")
        self.scopes[-1][name] = t

    def lookup(self, name):
        for scope in reversed(self.scopes):
            if name in scope:
                return scope[name]
        raise TypeCheckError(f"undefined variable {name}")

    def check_program(self, program):
        for stmt in program.stmts:
            self.check_stmt(stmt)

    def check_block(self, stmts):
        self.scopes.append({})
        try:
            for stmt in stmts:
                self.check_stmt(stmt)
        finally:
            self.scopes.pop()

    def value_type(self, expr):
        t = self.check_expr(expr)
        if t == "void":
            raise TypeCheckError("a call that returns nothing has no value")
        return t

    def check_stmt(self, stmt):
        if isinstance(stmt, Let):
            t = self.value_type(stmt.expr)
            if stmt.type is not None and stmt.type != t:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"{stmt.name} is declared {show_type(stmt.type)} but given {show_type(t)}")
            self.declare(stmt.name, t)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Assign):
            wanted = self.lookup(stmt.name)
            t = self.value_type(stmt.expr)
            if t != wanted:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"cannot assign {show_type(t)} to {stmt.name}, which is {show_type(wanted)}")
        elif isinstance(stmt, Print):
            self.value_type(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, ExprStmt):
            self.check_expr(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, If):
            self.condition(stmt.cond, "if")
            self.check_stmt(stmt.then)
            if stmt.else_ is not None:
                self.check_stmt(stmt.else_)
        elif isinstance(stmt, While):
            self.condition(stmt.cond, "while")
            self.check_stmt(stmt.body)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Block):
            self.check_block(stmt.stmts)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Fn):
            self.check_fn(stmt)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Return):
            self.check_return(stmt)

    def condition(self, expr, where):
        t = self.check_expr(expr)
        if t != "bool":
            raise TypeCheckError(f"the condition of {where} must be bool, not {show_type(t)}")

    def check_fn(self, stmt):
        for name, t in stmt.params:
            if t is None:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"parameter {name} of {stmt.name} needs a type")
        ret = stmt.ret if stmt.ret is not None else "void"
        self.declare(stmt.name, FnType(tuple(t for _, t in stmt.params), ret))
        self.scopes.append({})
        self.returns.append(ret)
        try:
            for name, t in stmt.params:
                self.declare(name, t)
            for inner in stmt.body.stmts:
                self.check_stmt(inner)
        finally:
            self.returns.pop()
            self.scopes.pop()
        if ret != "void" and not self.always_returns(stmt.body.stmts):
            raise TypeCheckError(f"{stmt.name} might end without returning a value of type {ret}")

    def check_return(self, stmt):
        if not self.returns:
            raise TypeCheckError("return outside a function")
        wanted = self.returns[-1]
        if stmt.expr is None:
            if wanted != "void":
                raise TypeCheckError(f"return needs a {wanted} value")
            return
        if wanted == "void":
            raise TypeCheckError("this function returns nothing, so return takes no value")
        t = self.value_type(stmt.expr)
        if t != wanted:
            raise TypeCheckError(f"return needs {wanted}, not {show_type(t)}")

    def always_returns(self, stmts):
        for stmt in stmts:
            if isinstance(stmt, Return):
                return True
            if isinstance(stmt, Block) and self.always_returns(stmt.stmts):
                return True
            if isinstance(stmt, If) and stmt.else_ is not None:
                if self.always_returns([stmt.then]) and self.always_returns([stmt.else_]):
                    return True
        return False

    def check_expr(self, expr):
        if isinstance(expr, Num):
            return "int"
        if isinstance(expr, Str):
            return "str"
        if isinstance(expr, Bool):
            return "bool"
        if isinstance(expr, Var):
            return self.lookup(expr.name)
        if isinstance(expr, Unary):
            t = self.check_expr(expr.expr)
            wanted = "int" if expr.op == "-" else "bool"
            if t != wanted:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"'{expr.op}' needs {wanted}, not {show_type(t)}")
            return wanted
        if isinstance(expr, Binary):
            return self.check_binary(expr)
        if isinstance(expr, Call):
            return self.check_call(expr)
        raise TypeCheckError(f"unknown expression {type(expr).__name__}")

    def check_binary(self, expr):
        left = self.check_expr(expr.left)
        right = self.check_expr(expr.right)
        return self.binary_type(expr.op, left, right)

    def binary_type(self, op, left, right):
        if "void" in (left, right):
            raise TypeCheckError("a call that returns nothing has no value")
        if op in ("and", "or"):
            if left != "bool" or right != "bool":
                raise TypeCheckError(f"'{op}' needs two bools, not {show_type(left)} and {show_type(right)}")
            return "bool"
        if op in ("==", "!="):
            if left != right:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"cannot compare {show_type(left)} with {show_type(right)}")
            return "bool"
        if op == "+" and left == right and left in ("int", "str"):
            return left
        if op in ARITH + ORDER + ("+",):
            if left != "int" or right != "int":
                raise TypeCheckError(f"'{op}' needs two ints, not {show_type(left)} and {show_type(right)}")
            return "bool" if op in ORDER else "int"
        raise TypeCheckError(f"unknown operator {op}")

    def check_call(self, expr):
        callee = self.check_expr(expr.callee)
        if not isinstance(callee, FnType):
            raise TypeCheckError(f"cannot call a value of type {show_type(callee)}")
        if len(expr.args) != len(callee.params):
            raise TypeCheckError(f"expected {len(callee.params)} arguments, got {len(expr.args)}")
        for arg, wanted in zip(expr.args, callee.params):
            t = self.check_expr(arg)
            if t != wanted:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"argument needs {show_type(wanted)}, not {show_type(t)}")
        return callee.ret


def check_source(source):
    try:
        Checker().check_program(parse_program(tokenize(source)))
    except TypeCheckError as e:
        return str(e)
    return None
--- solution
from dataclasses import dataclass

KEYWORDS = {"let", "fn", "return", "if", "else", "while", "print",
            "true", "false", "and", "or", "not"}
TWO_CHAR = {"==", "!=", "<=", ">=", "->"}
ONE_CHAR = set("+-*/%<>=(){},;:")
ESCAPES = {'"': '"', "\\": "\\", "n": "\n"}
DIGITS = "0123456789"
LETTERS = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ_"


@dataclass
class Token:
    kind: str
    text: str
    line: int
    col: int


class LexError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


def tokenize(source):
    tokens = []
    i = 0
    line = 1
    col = 1
    n = len(source)

    def advance(count):
        nonlocal i, line, col
        for _ in range(count):
            if source[i] == "\n":
                line += 1
                col = 1
            else:
                col += 1
            i += 1

    while i < n:
        ch = source[i]
        start_line, start_col = line, col
        if ch in " \t\r\n":
            advance(1)
        elif ch == "#":
            while i < n and source[i] != "\n":
                advance(1)
        elif ch in DIGITS:
            j = i
            while j < n and source[j] in DIGITS:
                j += 1
            tokens.append(Token("NUMBER", source[i:j], start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch in LETTERS:
            j = i
            while j < n and (source[j] in LETTERS or source[j] in DIGITS):
                j += 1
            word = source[i:j]
            kind = "KEYWORD" if word in KEYWORDS else "IDENT"
            tokens.append(Token(kind, word, start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch == '"':
            advance(1)
            chars = []
            while True:
                if i >= n or source[i] == "\n":
                    raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                c = source[i]
                if c == '"':
                    advance(1)
                    break
                if c == "\\":
                    if i + 1 >= n or source[i + 1] == "\n":
                        raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                    if source[i + 1] not in ESCAPES:
                        raise LexError("unknown escape", line, col)
                    chars.append(ESCAPES[source[i + 1]])
                    advance(2)
                else:
                    chars.append(c)
                    advance(1)
            tokens.append(Token("STRING", "".join(chars), start_line, start_col))
        elif source[i:i + 2] in TWO_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", source[i:i + 2], start_line, start_col))
            advance(2)
        elif ch in ONE_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", ch, start_line, start_col))
            advance(1)
        else:
            raise LexError(f"unexpected character {ch!r}", start_line, start_col)
    tokens.append(Token("EOF", "", line, col))
    return tokens

class ParseError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


COMPARE = ("==", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">=")
TYPES = ("int", "bool", "str")


class Parser:
    def __init__(self, tokens):
        self.tokens = tokens
        self.pos = 0

    def peek(self, ahead=0):
        return self.tokens[min(self.pos + ahead, len(self.tokens) - 1)]

    def at(self, *texts):
        tok = self.peek()
        return tok.kind in ("OP", "KEYWORD") and tok.text in texts

    def advance(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "EOF":
            self.pos += 1
        return tok

    def error(self, message):
        tok = self.peek()
        return ParseError(message, tok.line, tok.col)

    def expect(self, text):
        if not self.at(text):
            raise self.error(f"expected '{text}'")
        return self.advance()

    def expr(self):
        return self.or_expr()

    def or_expr(self):
        left = self.and_expr()
        while self.at("or"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.and_expr())
        return left

    def and_expr(self):
        left = self.not_expr()
        while self.at("and"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.not_expr())
        return left

    def not_expr(self):
        if self.at("not"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("not", self.not_expr())
        return self.compare()

    def compare(self):
        left = self.sum()
        if self.at(*COMPARE):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.sum())
            if self.at(*COMPARE):
                raise self.error("comparisons cannot be chained")
        return left

    def sum(self):
        left = self.product()
        while self.at("+", "-"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.product())
        return left

    def product(self):
        left = self.unary()
        while self.at("*", "/", "%"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.unary())
        return left

    def unary(self):
        if self.at("-"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("-", self.unary())
        return self.call()

    def call(self):
        expr = self.primary()
        while self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            args = []
            if not self.at(")"):
                args.append(self.expr())
                while self.at(","):
                    self.advance()
                    args.append(self.expr())
            self.expect(")")
            expr = Call(expr, args)
        return expr

    def primary(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind == "NUMBER":
            self.advance()
            return Num(int(tok.text))
        if tok.kind == "STRING":
            self.advance()
            return Str(tok.text)
        if tok.kind == "IDENT":
            self.advance()
            return Var(tok.text)
        if self.at("true", "false"):
            self.advance()
            return Bool(tok.text == "true")
        if self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            inner = self.expr()
            self.expect(")")
            return inner
        raise self.error("expected an expression")

    def program(self):
        stmts = []
        while self.peek().kind != "EOF":
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        return Program(stmts)

    def statement(self):
        if self.at("let"):
            return self.let_stmt()
        if self.at("print"):
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Print(value)
        if self.at("if"):
            return self.if_stmt()
        if self.at("while"):
            self.advance()
            cond = self.expr()
            return While(cond, self.block())
        if self.at("fn"):
            return self.fn_stmt()
        if self.at("return"):
            self.advance()
            value = None if self.at(";") else self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Return(value)
        nxt = self.peek(1)
        if self.peek().kind == "IDENT" and nxt.kind == "OP" and nxt.text == "=":
            name = self.advance().text
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Assign(name, value)
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return ExprStmt(value)

    def name(self):
        if self.peek().kind != "IDENT":
            raise self.error("expected a name")
        return self.advance().text

    def type_name(self):
        if self.at("fn"):
            self.advance()
            self.expect("(")
            params = []
            if not self.at(")"):
                params.append(self.type_name())
                while self.at(","):
                    self.advance()
                    params.append(self.type_name())
            self.expect(")")
            ret = "void"
            if self.at("->"):
                self.advance()
                ret = self.type_name()
            return FnType(tuple(params), ret)
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "IDENT" or tok.text not in TYPES:
            raise self.error("expected a type")
        return self.advance().text

    def let_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        self.expect("=")
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return Let(name, type_, value)

    def if_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        cond = self.expr()
        then = self.block()
        else_ = None
        if self.at("else"):
            self.advance()
            else_ = self.if_stmt() if self.at("if") else self.block()
        return If(cond, then, else_)

    def block(self):
        self.expect("{")
        stmts = []
        while not self.at("}"):
            if self.peek().kind == "EOF":
                raise self.error("expected '}'")
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        self.advance()
        return Block(stmts)

    def param(self):
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        return (name, type_)

    def fn_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        self.expect("(")
        params = []
        if not self.at(")"):
            params.append(self.param())
            while self.at(","):
                self.advance()
                params.append(self.param())
        self.expect(")")
        ret = None
        if self.at("->"):
            self.advance()
            ret = self.type_name()
        return Fn(name, params, ret, self.block())


def parse_program(tokens):
    return Parser(tokens).program()


class CometError(Exception):
    pass


def comet_div(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q


def comet_mod(a, b):
    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FnType:
    params: tuple
    ret: object


def show_type(t):
    if isinstance(t, FnType):
        return "fn(" + ", ".join(show_type(p) for p in t.params) + ") -> " + show_type(t.ret)
    return t


class TypeCheckError(Exception):
    pass


ARITH = ("-", "*", "/", "%")
ORDER = ("<", "<=", ">", ">=")


class Checker:
    def __init__(self):
        self.scopes = [{}]
        self.returns = []

    def declare(self, name, t):
        if name in self.scopes[-1]:
            raise TypeCheckError(f"{name} is already declared in this scope")
        self.scopes[-1][name] = t

    def lookup(self, name):
        for scope in reversed(self.scopes):
            if name in scope:
                return scope[name]
        raise TypeCheckError(f"undefined variable {name}")

    def check_program(self, program):
        for stmt in program.stmts:
            self.check_stmt(stmt)

    def check_block(self, stmts):
        self.scopes.append({})
        try:
            for stmt in stmts:
                self.check_stmt(stmt)
        finally:
            self.scopes.pop()

    def value_type(self, expr):
        t = self.check_expr(expr)
        if t == "void":
            raise TypeCheckError("a call that returns nothing has no value")
        return t

    def check_stmt(self, stmt):
        if isinstance(stmt, Let):
            t = self.value_type(stmt.expr)
            if stmt.type is not None and stmt.type != t:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"{stmt.name} is declared {show_type(stmt.type)} but given {show_type(t)}")
            self.declare(stmt.name, t)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Assign):
            wanted = self.lookup(stmt.name)
            t = self.value_type(stmt.expr)
            if t != wanted:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"cannot assign {show_type(t)} to {stmt.name}, which is {show_type(wanted)}")
        elif isinstance(stmt, Print):
            self.value_type(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, ExprStmt):
            self.check_expr(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, If):
            self.condition(stmt.cond, "if")
            self.check_stmt(stmt.then)
            if stmt.else_ is not None:
                self.check_stmt(stmt.else_)
        elif isinstance(stmt, While):
            self.condition(stmt.cond, "while")
            self.check_stmt(stmt.body)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Block):
            self.check_block(stmt.stmts)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Fn):
            self.check_fn(stmt)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Return):
            self.check_return(stmt)

    def condition(self, expr, where):
        t = self.check_expr(expr)
        if t != "bool":
            raise TypeCheckError(f"the condition of {where} must be bool, not {show_type(t)}")

    def check_fn(self, stmt):
        for name, t in stmt.params:
            if t is None:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"parameter {name} of {stmt.name} needs a type")
        ret = stmt.ret if stmt.ret is not None else "void"
        self.declare(stmt.name, FnType(tuple(t for _, t in stmt.params), ret))
        self.scopes.append({})
        self.returns.append(ret)
        try:
            for name, t in stmt.params:
                self.declare(name, t)
            for inner in stmt.body.stmts:
                self.check_stmt(inner)
        finally:
            self.returns.pop()
            self.scopes.pop()
        if ret != "void" and not self.always_returns(stmt.body.stmts):
            raise TypeCheckError(f"{stmt.name} might end without returning a value of type {ret}")

    def check_return(self, stmt):
        if not self.returns:
            raise TypeCheckError("return outside a function")
        wanted = self.returns[-1]
        if stmt.expr is None:
            if wanted != "void":
                raise TypeCheckError(f"return needs a {wanted} value")
            return
        if wanted == "void":
            raise TypeCheckError("this function returns nothing, so return takes no value")
        t = self.value_type(stmt.expr)
        if t != wanted:
            raise TypeCheckError(f"return needs {wanted}, not {show_type(t)}")

    def always_returns(self, stmts):
        for stmt in stmts:
            if isinstance(stmt, Return):
                return True
            if isinstance(stmt, Block) and self.always_returns(stmt.stmts):
                return True
            if isinstance(stmt, If) and stmt.else_ is not None:
                if self.always_returns([stmt.then]) and self.always_returns([stmt.else_]):
                    return True
        return False

    def check_expr(self, expr):
        if isinstance(expr, Num):
            return "int"
        if isinstance(expr, Str):
            return "str"
        if isinstance(expr, Bool):
            return "bool"
        if isinstance(expr, Var):
            return self.lookup(expr.name)
        if isinstance(expr, Unary):
            t = self.check_expr(expr.expr)
            wanted = "int" if expr.op == "-" else "bool"
            if t != wanted:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"'{expr.op}' needs {wanted}, not {show_type(t)}")
            return wanted
        if isinstance(expr, Binary):
            return self.check_binary(expr)
        if isinstance(expr, Call):
            return self.check_call(expr)
        raise TypeCheckError(f"unknown expression {type(expr).__name__}")

    def check_binary(self, expr):
        left = self.check_expr(expr.left)
        right = self.check_expr(expr.right)
        return self.binary_type(expr.op, left, right)

    def binary_type(self, op, left, right):
        if "void" in (left, right):
            raise TypeCheckError("a call that returns nothing has no value")
        if op in ("and", "or"):
            if left != "bool" or right != "bool":
                raise TypeCheckError(f"'{op}' needs two bools, not {show_type(left)} and {show_type(right)}")
            return "bool"
        if op in ("==", "!="):
            if left != right:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"cannot compare {show_type(left)} with {show_type(right)}")
            return "bool"
        if op == "+" and left == right and left in ("int", "str"):
            return left
        if op in ARITH + ORDER + ("+",):
            if left != "int" or right != "int":
                raise TypeCheckError(f"'{op}' needs two ints, not {show_type(left)} and {show_type(right)}")
            return "bool" if op in ORDER else "int"
        raise TypeCheckError(f"unknown operator {op}")

    def check_call(self, expr):
        callee = self.check_expr(expr.callee)
        if not isinstance(callee, FnType):
            raise TypeCheckError(f"cannot call a value of type {show_type(callee)}")
        if len(expr.args) != len(callee.params):
            raise TypeCheckError(f"expected {len(callee.params)} arguments, got {len(expr.args)}")
        for arg, wanted in zip(expr.args, callee.params):
            t = self.check_expr(arg)
            if t != wanted:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"argument needs {show_type(wanted)}, not {show_type(t)}")
        return callee.ret


def check_source(source):
    try:
        Checker().check_program(parse_program(tokenize(source)))
    except TypeCheckError as e:
        return str(e)
    return None
--- hint
Inside `type_name`, check `self.at("fn")` first. Then `self.advance()`, `self.expect("(")`, read zero or more types separated by commas by calling `self.type_name()` recursively, and `self.expect(")")`.
--- hint
After the `)`, the return type is `"void"` unless `self.at("->")`: then advance and read it with `self.type_name()`, which also handles a function type there. Return `FnType(tuple(params), ret)`. Keep the old code for simple types below.
--- check test | The example from the task
check_source("fn apply(f: fn(int) -> int, x: int) -> int { return f(x); } fn inc(n: int) -> int { return n + 1; } print apply(inc, 2);") is None
--- check test | The wrong kind of function is rejected
check_source("fn apply(f: fn(int) -> int, x: int) -> int { return f(x); } fn neg(b: bool) -> bool { return not b; } print apply(neg, 2);") is not None and check_source("fn call2(f: fn(int, int) -> int) -> int { return f(1); }") is not None
--- check test | A function type without an arrow returns void
check_source("fn run(cb: fn()) { cb(); } fn hi() { print 1; } run(hi);") is None and check_source("fn run(cb: fn()) { print cb(); }") is not None
--- check test | Returning functions, and nested function types
check_source("fn compose(f: fn(int) -> int, g: fn(int) -> int) -> fn(int) -> int { fn h(x: int) -> int { return f(g(x)); } return h; }") is None and check_source("fn k(f: fn(int) -> fn(int) -> int) -> int { return f(1)(2); }") is None
--- check test | Function types on let, and their messages
check_source("fn inc(n: int) -> int { return n + 1; } let g: fn(int) -> int = inc; print g(1);") is None and check_source("let g: fn(int, str) -> bool = 3;") == "g is declared fn(int, str) -> bool but given int"
--- check test | Bad type syntax is a parse error
raises(ParseError, lambda: parse_program(tokenize("let f: fn(int -> int = 1;"))) and raises(ParseError, lambda: parse_program(tokenize("let f: fn(float) = 1;")))

+++ practice | Statements that can never run
--- task
Java refuses to compile a statement that can never run, such as a line after a `return`: it is almost always a mistake. Write `unreachable(source)`, which parses a program (it need not type check) and reports unreachable statements inside function bodies.

- In every list of statements that belongs to a function (the body itself, and the statement lists of the blocks inside it), find the first statement that always returns, by the lesson's definition. If any statement follows it in the same list, the one right after it is unreachable. Report only that first unreachable statement of each list.
- Look into every list, including lists inside unreachable code and inside nested functions. A statement inside a nested function belongs to the nested function.
- Report each as a pair `(function name, class name of the statement)`, such as `("f", "Print")`, in the order the statements appear in the text. Top-level code, outside any function, is never reported.

The starter gives the lesson's finished checker, whose `always_returns` you may use. For example, `unreachable("fn f(n: int) -> int { return n; print n; let x = 1; }")` is `[("f", "Print")]`.
--- starter
from dataclasses import dataclass

KEYWORDS = {"let", "fn", "return", "if", "else", "while", "print",
            "true", "false", "and", "or", "not"}
TWO_CHAR = {"==", "!=", "<=", ">=", "->"}
ONE_CHAR = set("+-*/%<>=(){},;:")
ESCAPES = {'"': '"', "\\": "\\", "n": "\n"}
DIGITS = "0123456789"
LETTERS = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ_"


@dataclass
class Token:
    kind: str
    text: str
    line: int
    col: int


class LexError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


def tokenize(source):
    tokens = []
    i = 0
    line = 1
    col = 1
    n = len(source)

    def advance(count):
        nonlocal i, line, col
        for _ in range(count):
            if source[i] == "\n":
                line += 1
                col = 1
            else:
                col += 1
            i += 1

    while i < n:
        ch = source[i]
        start_line, start_col = line, col
        if ch in " \t\r\n":
            advance(1)
        elif ch == "#":
            while i < n and source[i] != "\n":
                advance(1)
        elif ch in DIGITS:
            j = i
            while j < n and source[j] in DIGITS:
                j += 1
            tokens.append(Token("NUMBER", source[i:j], start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch in LETTERS:
            j = i
            while j < n and (source[j] in LETTERS or source[j] in DIGITS):
                j += 1
            word = source[i:j]
            kind = "KEYWORD" if word in KEYWORDS else "IDENT"
            tokens.append(Token(kind, word, start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch == '"':
            advance(1)
            chars = []
            while True:
                if i >= n or source[i] == "\n":
                    raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                c = source[i]
                if c == '"':
                    advance(1)
                    break
                if c == "\\":
                    if i + 1 >= n or source[i + 1] == "\n":
                        raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                    if source[i + 1] not in ESCAPES:
                        raise LexError("unknown escape", line, col)
                    chars.append(ESCAPES[source[i + 1]])
                    advance(2)
                else:
                    chars.append(c)
                    advance(1)
            tokens.append(Token("STRING", "".join(chars), start_line, start_col))
        elif source[i:i + 2] in TWO_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", source[i:i + 2], start_line, start_col))
            advance(2)
        elif ch in ONE_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", ch, start_line, start_col))
            advance(1)
        else:
            raise LexError(f"unexpected character {ch!r}", start_line, start_col)
    tokens.append(Token("EOF", "", line, col))
    return tokens

    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


COMPARE = ("==", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">=")
TYPES = ("int", "bool", "str")


class Parser:
    def __init__(self, tokens):
        self.tokens = tokens
        self.pos = 0

    def peek(self, ahead=0):
        return self.tokens[min(self.pos + ahead, len(self.tokens) - 1)]

    def at(self, *texts):
        tok = self.peek()
        return tok.kind in ("OP", "KEYWORD") and tok.text in texts

    def advance(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "EOF":
            self.pos += 1
        return tok

    def error(self, message):
        tok = self.peek()
        return ParseError(message, tok.line, tok.col)

    def expect(self, text):
        if not self.at(text):
            raise self.error(f"expected '{text}'")
        return self.advance()

    def expr(self):
        return self.or_expr()

    def or_expr(self):
        left = self.and_expr()
        while self.at("or"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.and_expr())
        return left

    def and_expr(self):
        left = self.not_expr()
        while self.at("and"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.not_expr())
        return left

    def not_expr(self):
        if self.at("not"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("not", self.not_expr())
        return self.compare()

    def compare(self):
        left = self.sum()
        if self.at(*COMPARE):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.sum())
            if self.at(*COMPARE):
                raise self.error("comparisons cannot be chained")
        return left

    def sum(self):
        left = self.product()
        while self.at("+", "-"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.product())
        return left

    def product(self):
        left = self.unary()
        while self.at("*", "/", "%"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.unary())
        return left

    def unary(self):
        if self.at("-"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("-", self.unary())
        return self.call()

    def call(self):
        expr = self.primary()
        while self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            args = []
            if not self.at(")"):
                args.append(self.expr())
                while self.at(","):
                    self.advance()
                    args.append(self.expr())
            self.expect(")")
            expr = Call(expr, args)
        return expr

    def primary(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind == "NUMBER":
            self.advance()
            return Num(int(tok.text))
        if tok.kind == "STRING":
            self.advance()
            return Str(tok.text)
        if tok.kind == "IDENT":
            self.advance()
            return Var(tok.text)
        if self.at("true", "false"):
            self.advance()
            return Bool(tok.text == "true")
        if self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            inner = self.expr()
            self.expect(")")
            return inner
        raise self.error("expected an expression")

    def program(self):
        stmts = []
        while self.peek().kind != "EOF":
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        return Program(stmts)

    def statement(self):
        if self.at("let"):
            return self.let_stmt()
        if self.at("print"):
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Print(value)
        if self.at("if"):
            return self.if_stmt()
        if self.at("while"):
            self.advance()
            cond = self.expr()
            return While(cond, self.block())
        if self.at("fn"):
            return self.fn_stmt()
        if self.at("return"):
            self.advance()
            value = None if self.at(";") else self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Return(value)
        nxt = self.peek(1)
        if self.peek().kind == "IDENT" and nxt.kind == "OP" and nxt.text == "=":
            name = self.advance().text
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Assign(name, value)
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return ExprStmt(value)

    def name(self):
        if self.peek().kind != "IDENT":
            raise self.error("expected a name")
        return self.advance().text

    def type_name(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "IDENT" or tok.text not in TYPES:
            raise self.error("expected a type")
        return self.advance().text

    def let_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        self.expect("=")
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return Let(name, type_, value)

    def if_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        cond = self.expr()
        then = self.block()
        else_ = None
        if self.at("else"):
            self.advance()
            else_ = self.if_stmt() if self.at("if") else self.block()
        return If(cond, then, else_)

    def block(self):
        self.expect("{")
        stmts = []
        while not self.at("}"):
            if self.peek().kind == "EOF":
                raise self.error("expected '}'")
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        self.advance()
        return Block(stmts)

    def param(self):
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        return (name, type_)

    def fn_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        self.expect("(")
        params = []
        if not self.at(")"):
            params.append(self.param())
            while self.at(","):
                self.advance()
                params.append(self.param())
        self.expect(")")
        ret = None
        if self.at("->"):
            self.advance()
            ret = self.type_name()
        return Fn(name, params, ret, self.block())


def parse_program(tokens):
    return Parser(tokens).program()


class CometError(Exception):
    pass


def comet_div(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q


def comet_mod(a, b):
    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FnType:
    params: tuple
    ret: object


def show_type(t):
    if isinstance(t, FnType):
        return "fn(" + ", ".join(show_type(p) for p in t.params) + ") -> " + show_type(t.ret)
    return t


class TypeCheckError(Exception):
    pass


ARITH = ("-", "*", "/", "%")
ORDER = ("<", "<=", ">", ">=")


class Checker:
    def __init__(self):
        self.scopes = [{}]
        self.returns = []

    def declare(self, name, t):
        if name in self.scopes[-1]:
            raise TypeCheckError(f"{name} is already declared in this scope")
        self.scopes[-1][name] = t

    def lookup(self, name):
        for scope in reversed(self.scopes):
            if name in scope:
                return scope[name]
        raise TypeCheckError(f"undefined variable {name}")

    def check_program(self, program):
        for stmt in program.stmts:
            self.check_stmt(stmt)

    def check_block(self, stmts):
        self.scopes.append({})
        try:
            for stmt in stmts:
                self.check_stmt(stmt)
        finally:
            self.scopes.pop()

    def value_type(self, expr):
        t = self.check_expr(expr)
        if t == "void":
            raise TypeCheckError("a call that returns nothing has no value")
        return t

    def check_stmt(self, stmt):
        if isinstance(stmt, Let):
            t = self.value_type(stmt.expr)
            if stmt.type is not None and stmt.type != t:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"{stmt.name} is declared {show_type(stmt.type)} but given {show_type(t)}")
            self.declare(stmt.name, t)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Assign):
            wanted = self.lookup(stmt.name)
            t = self.value_type(stmt.expr)
            if t != wanted:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"cannot assign {show_type(t)} to {stmt.name}, which is {show_type(wanted)}")
        elif isinstance(stmt, Print):
            self.value_type(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, ExprStmt):
            self.check_expr(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, If):
            self.condition(stmt.cond, "if")
            self.check_stmt(stmt.then)
            if stmt.else_ is not None:
                self.check_stmt(stmt.else_)
        elif isinstance(stmt, While):
            self.condition(stmt.cond, "while")
            self.check_stmt(stmt.body)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Block):
            self.check_block(stmt.stmts)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Fn):
            self.check_fn(stmt)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Return):
            self.check_return(stmt)

    def condition(self, expr, where):
        t = self.check_expr(expr)
        if t != "bool":
            raise TypeCheckError(f"the condition of {where} must be bool, not {show_type(t)}")

    def check_fn(self, stmt):
        for name, t in stmt.params:
            if t is None:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"parameter {name} of {stmt.name} needs a type")
        ret = stmt.ret if stmt.ret is not None else "void"
        self.declare(stmt.name, FnType(tuple(t for _, t in stmt.params), ret))
        self.scopes.append({})
        self.returns.append(ret)
        try:
            for name, t in stmt.params:
                self.declare(name, t)
            for inner in stmt.body.stmts:
                self.check_stmt(inner)
        finally:
            self.returns.pop()
            self.scopes.pop()
        if ret != "void" and not self.always_returns(stmt.body.stmts):
            raise TypeCheckError(f"{stmt.name} might end without returning a value of type {ret}")

    def check_return(self, stmt):
        if not self.returns:
            raise TypeCheckError("return outside a function")
        wanted = self.returns[-1]
        if stmt.expr is None:
            if wanted != "void":
                raise TypeCheckError(f"return needs a {wanted} value")
            return
        if wanted == "void":
            raise TypeCheckError("this function returns nothing, so return takes no value")
        t = self.value_type(stmt.expr)
        if t != wanted:
            raise TypeCheckError(f"return needs {wanted}, not {show_type(t)}")

    def always_returns(self, stmts):
        for stmt in stmts:
            if isinstance(stmt, Return):
                return True
            if isinstance(stmt, Block) and self.always_returns(stmt.stmts):
                return True
            if isinstance(stmt, If) and stmt.else_ is not None:
                if self.always_returns([stmt.then]) and self.always_returns([stmt.else_]):
                    return True
        return False

    def check_expr(self, expr):
        if isinstance(expr, Num):
            return "int"
        if isinstance(expr, Str):
            return "str"
        if isinstance(expr, Bool):
            return "bool"
        if isinstance(expr, Var):
            return self.lookup(expr.name)
        if isinstance(expr, Unary):
            t = self.check_expr(expr.expr)
            wanted = "int" if expr.op == "-" else "bool"
            if t != wanted:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"'{expr.op}' needs {wanted}, not {show_type(t)}")
            return wanted
        if isinstance(expr, Binary):
            return self.check_binary(expr)
        if isinstance(expr, Call):
            return self.check_call(expr)
        raise TypeCheckError(f"unknown expression {type(expr).__name__}")

    def check_binary(self, expr):
        left = self.check_expr(expr.left)
        right = self.check_expr(expr.right)
        return self.binary_type(expr.op, left, right)

    def binary_type(self, op, left, right):
        if "void" in (left, right):
            raise TypeCheckError("a call that returns nothing has no value")
        if op in ("and", "or"):
            if left != "bool" or right != "bool":
                raise TypeCheckError(f"'{op}' needs two bools, not {show_type(left)} and {show_type(right)}")
            return "bool"
        if op in ("==", "!="):
            if left != right:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"cannot compare {show_type(left)} with {show_type(right)}")
            return "bool"
        if op == "+" and left == right and left in ("int", "str"):
            return left
        if op in ARITH + ORDER + ("+",):
            if left != "int" or right != "int":
                raise TypeCheckError(f"'{op}' needs two ints, not {show_type(left)} and {show_type(right)}")
            return "bool" if op in ORDER else "int"
        raise TypeCheckError(f"unknown operator {op}")

    def check_call(self, expr):
        callee = self.check_expr(expr.callee)
        if not isinstance(callee, FnType):
            raise TypeCheckError(f"cannot call a value of type {show_type(callee)}")
        if len(expr.args) != len(callee.params):
            raise TypeCheckError(f"expected {len(callee.params)} arguments, got {len(expr.args)}")
        for arg, wanted in zip(expr.args, callee.params):
            t = self.check_expr(arg)
            if t != wanted:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"argument needs {show_type(wanted)}, not {show_type(t)}")
        return callee.ret


def check_source(source):
    try:
        Checker().check_program(parse_program(tokenize(source)))
    except TypeCheckError as e:
        return str(e)
    return None


def unreachable(source):
    raise NotImplementedError("unreachable is not written yet")

from dataclasses import dataclass

KEYWORDS = {"let", "fn", "return", "if", "else", "while", "print",
            "true", "false", "and", "or", "not"}
TWO_CHAR = {"==", "!=", "<=", ">=", "->"}
ONE_CHAR = set("+-*/%<>=(){},;:")
ESCAPES = {'"': '"', "\\": "\\", "n": "\n"}
DIGITS = "0123456789"
LETTERS = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ_"


@dataclass
class Token:
    kind: str
    text: str
    line: int
    col: int


class LexError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


def tokenize(source):
    tokens = []
    i = 0
    line = 1
    col = 1
    n = len(source)

    def advance(count):
        nonlocal i, line, col
        for _ in range(count):
            if source[i] == "\n":
                line += 1
                col = 1
            else:
                col += 1
            i += 1

    while i < n:
        ch = source[i]
        start_line, start_col = line, col
        if ch in " \t\r\n":
            advance(1)
        elif ch == "#":
            while i < n and source[i] != "\n":
                advance(1)
        elif ch in DIGITS:
            j = i
            while j < n and source[j] in DIGITS:
                j += 1
            tokens.append(Token("NUMBER", source[i:j], start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch in LETTERS:
            j = i
            while j < n and (source[j] in LETTERS or source[j] in DIGITS):
                j += 1
            word = source[i:j]
            kind = "KEYWORD" if word in KEYWORDS else "IDENT"
            tokens.append(Token(kind, word, start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch == '"':
            advance(1)
            chars = []
            while True:
                if i >= n or source[i] == "\n":
                    raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                c = source[i]
                if c == '"':
                    advance(1)
                    break
                if c == "\\":
                    if i + 1 >= n or source[i + 1] == "\n":
                        raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                    if source[i + 1] not in ESCAPES:
                        raise LexError("unknown escape", line, col)
                    chars.append(ESCAPES[source[i + 1]])
                    advance(2)
                else:
                    chars.append(c)
                    advance(1)
            tokens.append(Token("STRING", "".join(chars), start_line, start_col))
        elif source[i:i + 2] in TWO_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", source[i:i + 2], start_line, start_col))
            advance(2)
        elif ch in ONE_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", ch, start_line, start_col))
            advance(1)
        else:
            raise LexError(f"unexpected character {ch!r}", start_line, start_col)
    tokens.append(Token("EOF", "", line, col))
    return tokens

class ParseError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


COMPARE = ("==", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">=")
TYPES = ("int", "bool", "str")


class Parser:
    def __init__(self, tokens):
        self.tokens = tokens
        self.pos = 0

    def peek(self, ahead=0):
        return self.tokens[min(self.pos + ahead, len(self.tokens) - 1)]

    def at(self, *texts):
        tok = self.peek()
        return tok.kind in ("OP", "KEYWORD") and tok.text in texts

    def advance(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "EOF":
            self.pos += 1
        return tok

    def error(self, message):
        tok = self.peek()
        return ParseError(message, tok.line, tok.col)

    def expect(self, text):
        if not self.at(text):
            raise self.error(f"expected '{text}'")
        return self.advance()

    def expr(self):
        return self.or_expr()

    def or_expr(self):
        left = self.and_expr()
        while self.at("or"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.and_expr())
        return left

    def and_expr(self):
        left = self.not_expr()
        while self.at("and"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.not_expr())
        return left

    def not_expr(self):
        if self.at("not"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("not", self.not_expr())
        return self.compare()

    def compare(self):
        left = self.sum()
        if self.at(*COMPARE):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.sum())
            if self.at(*COMPARE):
                raise self.error("comparisons cannot be chained")
        return left

    def sum(self):
        left = self.product()
        while self.at("+", "-"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.product())
        return left

    def product(self):
        left = self.unary()
        while self.at("*", "/", "%"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.unary())
        return left

    def unary(self):
        if self.at("-"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("-", self.unary())
        return self.call()

    def call(self):
        expr = self.primary()
        while self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            args = []
            if not self.at(")"):
                args.append(self.expr())
                while self.at(","):
                    self.advance()
                    args.append(self.expr())
            self.expect(")")
            expr = Call(expr, args)
        return expr

    def primary(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind == "NUMBER":
            self.advance()
            return Num(int(tok.text))
        if tok.kind == "STRING":
            self.advance()
            return Str(tok.text)
        if tok.kind == "IDENT":
            self.advance()
            return Var(tok.text)
        if self.at("true", "false"):
            self.advance()
            return Bool(tok.text == "true")
        if self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            inner = self.expr()
            self.expect(")")
            return inner
        raise self.error("expected an expression")

    def program(self):
        stmts = []
        while self.peek().kind != "EOF":
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        return Program(stmts)

    def statement(self):
        if self.at("let"):
            return self.let_stmt()
        if self.at("print"):
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Print(value)
        if self.at("if"):
            return self.if_stmt()
        if self.at("while"):
            self.advance()
            cond = self.expr()
            return While(cond, self.block())
        if self.at("fn"):
            return self.fn_stmt()
        if self.at("return"):
            self.advance()
            value = None if self.at(";") else self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Return(value)
        nxt = self.peek(1)
        if self.peek().kind == "IDENT" and nxt.kind == "OP" and nxt.text == "=":
            name = self.advance().text
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Assign(name, value)
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return ExprStmt(value)

    def name(self):
        if self.peek().kind != "IDENT":
            raise self.error("expected a name")
        return self.advance().text

    def type_name(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "IDENT" or tok.text not in TYPES:
            raise self.error("expected a type")
        return self.advance().text

    def let_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        self.expect("=")
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return Let(name, type_, value)

    def if_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        cond = self.expr()
        then = self.block()
        else_ = None
        if self.at("else"):
            self.advance()
            else_ = self.if_stmt() if self.at("if") else self.block()
        return If(cond, then, else_)

    def block(self):
        self.expect("{")
        stmts = []
        while not self.at("}"):
            if self.peek().kind == "EOF":
                raise self.error("expected '}'")
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        self.advance()
        return Block(stmts)

    def param(self):
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        return (name, type_)

    def fn_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        self.expect("(")
        params = []
        if not self.at(")"):
            params.append(self.param())
            while self.at(","):
                self.advance()
                params.append(self.param())
        self.expect(")")
        ret = None
        if self.at("->"):
            self.advance()
            ret = self.type_name()
        return Fn(name, params, ret, self.block())


def parse_program(tokens):
    return Parser(tokens).program()


class CometError(Exception):
