def comet_div(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q


def comet_mod(a, b):
    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FnType:
    params: tuple
    ret: object


def show_type(t):
    if isinstance(t, FnType):
        return "fn(" + ", ".join(show_type(p) for p in t.params) + ") -> " + show_type(t.ret)
    return t


class TypeCheckError(Exception):
    pass


ARITH = ("-", "*", "/", "%")
ORDER = ("<", "<=", ">", ">=")


class Checker:
    def __init__(self):
        self.scopes = [{}]
        self.returns = []

    def declare(self, name, t):
        if name in self.scopes[-1]:
            raise TypeCheckError(f"{name} is already declared in this scope")
        self.scopes[-1][name] = t

    def lookup(self, name):
        for scope in reversed(self.scopes):
            if name in scope:
                return scope[name]
        raise TypeCheckError(f"undefined variable {name}")

    def check_program(self, program):
        for stmt in program.stmts:
            self.check_stmt(stmt)

    def check_block(self, stmts):
        self.scopes.append({})
        try:
            for stmt in stmts:
                self.check_stmt(stmt)
        finally:
            self.scopes.pop()

    def value_type(self, expr):
        t = self.check_expr(expr)
        if t == "void":
            raise TypeCheckError("a call that returns nothing has no value")
        return t

    def check_stmt(self, stmt):
        if isinstance(stmt, Let):
            t = self.value_type(stmt.expr)
            if stmt.type is not None and stmt.type != t:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"{stmt.name} is declared {show_type(stmt.type)} but given {show_type(t)}")
            self.declare(stmt.name, t)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Assign):
            wanted = self.lookup(stmt.name)
            t = self.value_type(stmt.expr)
            if t != wanted:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"cannot assign {show_type(t)} to {stmt.name}, which is {show_type(wanted)}")
        elif isinstance(stmt, Print):
            self.value_type(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, ExprStmt):
            self.check_expr(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, If):
            self.condition(stmt.cond, "if")
            self.check_stmt(stmt.then)
            if stmt.else_ is not None:
                self.check_stmt(stmt.else_)
        elif isinstance(stmt, While):
            self.condition(stmt.cond, "while")
            self.check_stmt(stmt.body)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Block):
            self.check_block(stmt.stmts)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Fn):
            self.check_fn(stmt)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Return):
            self.check_return(stmt)

    def condition(self, expr, where):
        t = self.check_expr(expr)
        if t != "bool":
            raise TypeCheckError(f"the condition of {where} must be bool, not {show_type(t)}")

    def check_fn(self, stmt):
        for name, t in stmt.params:
            if t is None:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"parameter {name} of {stmt.name} needs a type")
        ret = stmt.ret if stmt.ret is not None else "void"
        self.declare(stmt.name, FnType(tuple(t for _, t in stmt.params), ret))
        self.scopes.append({})
        self.returns.append(ret)
        try:
            for name, t in stmt.params:
                self.declare(name, t)
            for inner in stmt.body.stmts:
                self.check_stmt(inner)
        finally:
            self.returns.pop()
            self.scopes.pop()
        if ret != "void" and not self.always_returns(stmt.body.stmts):
            raise TypeCheckError(f"{stmt.name} might end without returning a value of type {ret}")

    def check_return(self, stmt):
        if not self.returns:
            raise TypeCheckError("return outside a function")
        wanted = self.returns[-1]
        if stmt.expr is None:
            if wanted != "void":
                raise TypeCheckError(f"return needs a {wanted} value")
            return
        if wanted == "void":
            raise TypeCheckError("this function returns nothing, so return takes no value")
        t = self.value_type(stmt.expr)
        if t != wanted:
            raise TypeCheckError(f"return needs {wanted}, not {show_type(t)}")

    def always_returns(self, stmts):
        for stmt in stmts:
            if isinstance(stmt, Return):
                return True
            if isinstance(stmt, Block) and self.always_returns(stmt.stmts):
                return True
            if isinstance(stmt, If) and stmt.else_ is not None:
                if self.always_returns([stmt.then]) and self.always_returns([stmt.else_]):
                    return True
        return False

    def check_expr(self, expr):
        if isinstance(expr, Num):
            return "int"
        if isinstance(expr, Str):
            return "str"
        if isinstance(expr, Bool):
            return "bool"
        if isinstance(expr, Var):
            return self.lookup(expr.name)
        if isinstance(expr, Unary):
            t = self.check_expr(expr.expr)
            wanted = "int" if expr.op == "-" else "bool"
            if t != wanted:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"'{expr.op}' needs {wanted}, not {show_type(t)}")
            return wanted
        if isinstance(expr, Binary):
            return self.check_binary(expr)
        if isinstance(expr, Call):
            return self.check_call(expr)
        raise TypeCheckError(f"unknown expression {type(expr).__name__}")

    def check_binary(self, expr):
        left = self.check_expr(expr.left)
        right = self.check_expr(expr.right)
        return self.binary_type(expr.op, left, right)

    def binary_type(self, op, left, right):
        if "void" in (left, right):
            raise TypeCheckError("a call that returns nothing has no value")
        if op in ("and", "or"):
            if left != "bool" or right != "bool":
                raise TypeCheckError(f"'{op}' needs two bools, not {show_type(left)} and {show_type(right)}")
            return "bool"
        if op in ("==", "!="):
            if left != right:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"cannot compare {show_type(left)} with {show_type(right)}")
            return "bool"
        if op == "+" and left == right and left in ("int", "str"):
            return left
        if op in ARITH + ORDER + ("+",):
            if left != "int" or right != "int":
                raise TypeCheckError(f"'{op}' needs two ints, not {show_type(left)} and {show_type(right)}")
            return "bool" if op in ORDER else "int"
        raise TypeCheckError(f"unknown operator {op}")

    def check_call(self, expr):
        callee = self.check_expr(expr.callee)
        if not isinstance(callee, FnType):
            raise TypeCheckError(f"cannot call a value of type {show_type(callee)}")
        if len(expr.args) != len(callee.params):
            raise TypeCheckError(f"expected {len(callee.params)} arguments, got {len(expr.args)}")
        for arg, wanted in zip(expr.args, callee.params):
            t = self.check_expr(arg)
            if t != wanted:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"argument needs {show_type(wanted)}, not {show_type(t)}")
        return callee.ret


def check_source(source):
    try:
        Checker().check_program(parse_program(tokenize(source)))
    except TypeCheckError as e:
        return str(e)
    return None


def unreachable(source):
    program = parse_program(tokenize(source))
    checker = Checker()
    found = []

    def statements(stmts, fn_name):
        first = None
        if fn_name is not None:
            for i in range(len(stmts) - 1):
                if checker.always_returns([stmts[i]]):
                    first = i + 1
                    break
        for i, stmt in enumerate(stmts):
            if i == first:
                found.append((fn_name, type(stmt).__name__))
            nested(stmt, fn_name)

    def nested(stmt, fn_name):
        if isinstance(stmt, Block):
            statements(stmt.stmts, fn_name)
        elif isinstance(stmt, If):
            nested(stmt.then, fn_name)
            if stmt.else_ is not None:
                nested(stmt.else_, fn_name)
        elif isinstance(stmt, While):
            nested(stmt.body, fn_name)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Fn):
            statements(stmt.body.stmts, stmt.name)

    statements(program.stmts, None)
    return found
--- hint
Write a function that handles one list of statements and the name of the function it belongs to (or `None` at the top level). It finds the index of the first statement for which `Checker().always_returns([stmt])` is true, and walks the list; when it reaches the statement right after that index it records it, and for every statement it looks inside.
--- hint
Looking inside: a `Block` is a new list for the same function; an `If` looks inside its `then` and `else_`; a `While` inside its body; an `Fn` is a new list with the nested function's name. Record the unreachable statement before looking inside it, so the pairs come out in text order.
--- check case | The example from the task
unreachable("fn f(n: int) -> int { return n; print n; let x = 1; }")
=> [("f", "Print")]
--- check case | An if with an else that returns on both sides
unreachable("fn f(n: int) -> int { if n > 0 { return 1; } else { return 2; } print 3; }")
=> [("f", "Print")]
--- check case | Without an else, or with a loop, the code after is reachable
unreachable("fn f(n: int) -> int { if n > 0 { return 1; } print 3; return 2; } fn g(n: int) -> int { while true { return 1; } print 2; return 3; }")
=> []
--- check case | Nested functions, in text order
unreachable("fn f() { fn g() -> int { return 1; print 5; } print 6; return; fn h() { } }")
=> [("g", "Print"), ("f", "Fn")]
--- check case | else if chains ending in else
unreachable("fn f(n: int) -> int { if n > 0 { return 1; } else if n < 0 { return -1; } else { return 0; } n = 1; }")
=> [("f", "Assign")]
--- check case | Inside blocks, and inside unreachable code
unreachable("fn f() { return; if true { return; print 1; } } fn g(n: int) -> int { if true { return 1; print 1; } return 2; }")
=> [("f", "If"), ("f", "Print"), ("g", "Print")]
--- check case | Top-level code is not reported
unreachable("print 1; if true { print 2; }")
=> []

+++ practice | Debug: recursion that is refused
--- task
The starter's checker accepts most programs correctly, but it refuses every recursive function. `fn fact(n: int) -> int { if n <= 1 { return 1; } return n * fact(n - 1); }` is rejected with "undefined variable fact", although it is well typed. Find the bug in `check_fn` and fix it, without breaking anything else: a function's own parameters and local variables must still be invisible after its declaration, and the function's name must be visible after it.
--- starter
from dataclasses import dataclass

KEYWORDS = {"let", "fn", "return", "if", "else", "while", "print",
            "true", "false", "and", "or", "not"}
TWO_CHAR = {"==", "!=", "<=", ">=", "->"}
ONE_CHAR = set("+-*/%<>=(){},;:")
ESCAPES = {'"': '"', "\\": "\\", "n": "\n"}
DIGITS = "0123456789"
LETTERS = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ_"


@dataclass
class Token:
    kind: str
    text: str
    line: int
    col: int


class LexError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


def tokenize(source):
    tokens = []
    i = 0
    line = 1
    col = 1
    n = len(source)

    def advance(count):
        nonlocal i, line, col
        for _ in range(count):
            if source[i] == "\n":
                line += 1
                col = 1
            else:
                col += 1
            i += 1

    while i < n:
        ch = source[i]
        start_line, start_col = line, col
        if ch in " \t\r\n":
            advance(1)
        elif ch == "#":
            while i < n and source[i] != "\n":
                advance(1)
        elif ch in DIGITS:
            j = i
            while j < n and source[j] in DIGITS:
                j += 1
            tokens.append(Token("NUMBER", source[i:j], start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch in LETTERS:
            j = i
            while j < n and (source[j] in LETTERS or source[j] in DIGITS):
                j += 1
            word = source[i:j]
            kind = "KEYWORD" if word in KEYWORDS else "IDENT"
            tokens.append(Token(kind, word, start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch == '"':
            advance(1)
            chars = []
            while True:
                if i >= n or source[i] == "\n":
                    raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                c = source[i]
                if c == '"':
                    advance(1)
                    break
                if c == "\\":
                    if i + 1 >= n or source[i + 1] == "\n":
                        raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                    if source[i + 1] not in ESCAPES:
                        raise LexError("unknown escape", line, col)
                    chars.append(ESCAPES[source[i + 1]])
                    advance(2)
                else:
                    chars.append(c)
                    advance(1)
            tokens.append(Token("STRING", "".join(chars), start_line, start_col))
        elif source[i:i + 2] in TWO_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", source[i:i + 2], start_line, start_col))
            advance(2)
        elif ch in ONE_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", ch, start_line, start_col))
            advance(1)
        else:
            raise LexError(f"unexpected character {ch!r}", start_line, start_col)
    tokens.append(Token("EOF", "", line, col))
    return tokens

class ParseError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


COMPARE = ("==", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">=")
TYPES = ("int", "bool", "str")


class Parser:
    def __init__(self, tokens):
        self.tokens = tokens
        self.pos = 0

    def peek(self, ahead=0):
        return self.tokens[min(self.pos + ahead, len(self.tokens) - 1)]

    def at(self, *texts):
        tok = self.peek()
        return tok.kind in ("OP", "KEYWORD") and tok.text in texts

    def advance(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "EOF":
            self.pos += 1
        return tok

    def error(self, message):
        tok = self.peek()
        return ParseError(message, tok.line, tok.col)

    def expect(self, text):
        if not self.at(text):
            raise self.error(f"expected '{text}'")
        return self.advance()

    def expr(self):
        return self.or_expr()

    def or_expr(self):
        left = self.and_expr()
        while self.at("or"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.and_expr())
        return left

    def and_expr(self):
        left = self.not_expr()
        while self.at("and"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.not_expr())
        return left

    def not_expr(self):
        if self.at("not"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("not", self.not_expr())
        return self.compare()

    def compare(self):
        left = self.sum()
        if self.at(*COMPARE):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.sum())
            if self.at(*COMPARE):
                raise self.error("comparisons cannot be chained")
        return left

    def sum(self):
        left = self.product()
        while self.at("+", "-"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.product())
        return left

    def product(self):
        left = self.unary()
        while self.at("*", "/", "%"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.unary())
        return left

    def unary(self):
        if self.at("-"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("-", self.unary())
        return self.call()

    def call(self):
        expr = self.primary()
        while self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            args = []
            if not self.at(")"):
                args.append(self.expr())
                while self.at(","):
                    self.advance()
                    args.append(self.expr())
            self.expect(")")
            expr = Call(expr, args)
        return expr

    def primary(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind == "NUMBER":
            self.advance()
            return Num(int(tok.text))
        if tok.kind == "STRING":
            self.advance()
            return Str(tok.text)
        if tok.kind == "IDENT":
            self.advance()
            return Var(tok.text)
        if self.at("true", "false"):
            self.advance()
            return Bool(tok.text == "true")
        if self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            inner = self.expr()
            self.expect(")")
            return inner
        raise self.error("expected an expression")

    def program(self):
        stmts = []
        while self.peek().kind != "EOF":
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        return Program(stmts)

    def statement(self):
        if self.at("let"):
            return self.let_stmt()
        if self.at("print"):
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Print(value)
        if self.at("if"):
            return self.if_stmt()
        if self.at("while"):
            self.advance()
            cond = self.expr()
            return While(cond, self.block())
        if self.at("fn"):
            return self.fn_stmt()
        if self.at("return"):
            self.advance()
            value = None if self.at(";") else self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Return(value)
        nxt = self.peek(1)
        if self.peek().kind == "IDENT" and nxt.kind == "OP" and nxt.text == "=":
            name = self.advance().text
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Assign(name, value)
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return ExprStmt(value)

    def name(self):
        if self.peek().kind != "IDENT":
            raise self.error("expected a name")
        return self.advance().text

    def type_name(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "IDENT" or tok.text not in TYPES:
            raise self.error("expected a type")
        return self.advance().text

    def let_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        self.expect("=")
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return Let(name, type_, value)

    def if_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        cond = self.expr()
        then = self.block()
        else_ = None
        if self.at("else"):
            self.advance()
            else_ = self.if_stmt() if self.at("if") else self.block()
        return If(cond, then, else_)

    def block(self):
        self.expect("{")
        stmts = []
        while not self.at("}"):
            if self.peek().kind == "EOF":
                raise self.error("expected '}'")
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        self.advance()
        return Block(stmts)

    def param(self):
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        return (name, type_)

    def fn_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        self.expect("(")
        params = []
        if not self.at(")"):
            params.append(self.param())
            while self.at(","):
                self.advance()
                params.append(self.param())
        self.expect(")")
        ret = None
        if self.at("->"):
            self.advance()
            ret = self.type_name()
        return Fn(name, params, ret, self.block())


def parse_program(tokens):
    return Parser(tokens).program()


class CometError(Exception):
    pass


def comet_div(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q


def comet_mod(a, b):
    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FnType:
    params: tuple
    ret: object


def show_type(t):
    if isinstance(t, FnType):
        return "fn(" + ", ".join(show_type(p) for p in t.params) + ") -> " + show_type(t.ret)
    return t


class TypeCheckError(Exception):
    pass


ARITH = ("-", "*", "/", "%")
ORDER = ("<", "<=", ">", ">=")


class Checker:
    def __init__(self):
        self.scopes = [{}]
        self.returns = []

    def declare(self, name, t):
        if name in self.scopes[-1]:
            raise TypeCheckError(f"{name} is already declared in this scope")
        self.scopes[-1][name] = t

    def lookup(self, name):
        for scope in reversed(self.scopes):
            if name in scope:
                return scope[name]
        raise TypeCheckError(f"undefined variable {name}")

    def check_program(self, program):
        for stmt in program.stmts:
            self.check_stmt(stmt)

    def check_block(self, stmts):
        self.scopes.append({})
        try:
            for stmt in stmts:
                self.check_stmt(stmt)
        finally:
            self.scopes.pop()

    def value_type(self, expr):
        t = self.check_expr(expr)
        if t == "void":
            raise TypeCheckError("a call that returns nothing has no value")
        return t

    def check_stmt(self, stmt):
        if isinstance(stmt, Let):
            t = self.value_type(stmt.expr)
            if stmt.type is not None and stmt.type != t:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"{stmt.name} is declared {show_type(stmt.type)} but given {show_type(t)}")
            self.declare(stmt.name, t)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Assign):
            wanted = self.lookup(stmt.name)
            t = self.value_type(stmt.expr)
            if t != wanted:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"cannot assign {show_type(t)} to {stmt.name}, which is {show_type(wanted)}")
        elif isinstance(stmt, Print):
            self.value_type(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, ExprStmt):
            self.check_expr(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, If):
            self.condition(stmt.cond, "if")
            self.check_stmt(stmt.then)
            if stmt.else_ is not None:
                self.check_stmt(stmt.else_)
        elif isinstance(stmt, While):
            self.condition(stmt.cond, "while")
            self.check_stmt(stmt.body)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Block):
            self.check_block(stmt.stmts)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Fn):
            self.check_fn(stmt)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Return):
            self.check_return(stmt)

    def condition(self, expr, where):
        t = self.check_expr(expr)
        if t != "bool":
            raise TypeCheckError(f"the condition of {where} must be bool, not {show_type(t)}")

    def check_fn(self, stmt):
        for name, t in stmt.params:
            if t is None:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"parameter {name} of {stmt.name} needs a type")
        ret = stmt.ret if stmt.ret is not None else "void"
        self.scopes.append({})
        self.returns.append(ret)
        try:
            for name, t in stmt.params:
                self.declare(name, t)
            for inner in stmt.body.stmts:
                self.check_stmt(inner)
        finally:
            self.returns.pop()
            self.scopes.pop()
        self.declare(stmt.name, FnType(tuple(t for _, t in stmt.params), ret))
        if ret != "void" and not self.always_returns(stmt.body.stmts):
            raise TypeCheckError(f"{stmt.name} might end without returning a value of type {ret}")

    def check_return(self, stmt):
        if not self.returns:
            raise TypeCheckError("return outside a function")
        wanted = self.returns[-1]
        if stmt.expr is None:
            if wanted != "void":
                raise TypeCheckError(f"return needs a {wanted} value")
            return
        if wanted == "void":
            raise TypeCheckError("this function returns nothing, so return takes no value")
        t = self.value_type(stmt.expr)
        if t != wanted:
            raise TypeCheckError(f"return needs {wanted}, not {show_type(t)}")

    def always_returns(self, stmts):
        for stmt in stmts:
            if isinstance(stmt, Return):
                return True
            if isinstance(stmt, Block) and self.always_returns(stmt.stmts):
                return True
            if isinstance(stmt, If) and stmt.else_ is not None:
                if self.always_returns([stmt.then]) and self.always_returns([stmt.else_]):
                    return True
        return False

    def check_expr(self, expr):
        if isinstance(expr, Num):
            return "int"
        if isinstance(expr, Str):
            return "str"
        if isinstance(expr, Bool):
            return "bool"
        if isinstance(expr, Var):
            return self.lookup(expr.name)
        if isinstance(expr, Unary):
            t = self.check_expr(expr.expr)
            wanted = "int" if expr.op == "-" else "bool"
            if t != wanted:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"'{expr.op}' needs {wanted}, not {show_type(t)}")
            return wanted
        if isinstance(expr, Binary):
            return self.check_binary(expr)
        if isinstance(expr, Call):
            return self.check_call(expr)
        raise TypeCheckError(f"unknown expression {type(expr).__name__}")

    def check_binary(self, expr):
        left = self.check_expr(expr.left)
        right = self.check_expr(expr.right)
        return self.binary_type(expr.op, left, right)

    def binary_type(self, op, left, right):
        if "void" in (left, right):
            raise TypeCheckError("a call that returns nothing has no value")
        if op in ("and", "or"):
            if left != "bool" or right != "bool":
                raise TypeCheckError(f"'{op}' needs two bools, not {show_type(left)} and {show_type(right)}")
            return "bool"
        if op in ("==", "!="):
            if left != right:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"cannot compare {show_type(left)} with {show_type(right)}")
            return "bool"
        if op == "+" and left == right and left in ("int", "str"):
            return left
        if op in ARITH + ORDER + ("+",):
            if left != "int" or right != "int":
                raise TypeCheckError(f"'{op}' needs two ints, not {show_type(left)} and {show_type(right)}")
            return "bool" if op in ORDER else "int"
        raise TypeCheckError(f"unknown operator {op}")

    def check_call(self, expr):
        callee = self.check_expr(expr.callee)
        if not isinstance(callee, FnType):
            raise TypeCheckError(f"cannot call a value of type {show_type(callee)}")
        if len(expr.args) != len(callee.params):
            raise TypeCheckError(f"expected {len(callee.params)} arguments, got {len(expr.args)}")
        for arg, wanted in zip(expr.args, callee.params):
            t = self.check_expr(arg)
            if t != wanted:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"argument needs {show_type(wanted)}, not {show_type(t)}")
        return callee.ret


def check_source(source):
    try:
        Checker().check_program(parse_program(tokenize(source)))
    except TypeCheckError as e:
        return str(e)
    return None

from dataclasses import dataclass

KEYWORDS = {"let", "fn", "return", "if", "else", "while", "print",
            "true", "false", "and", "or", "not"}
TWO_CHAR = {"==", "!=", "<=", ">=", "->"}
ONE_CHAR = set("+-*/%<>=(){},;:")
ESCAPES = {'"': '"', "\\": "\\", "n": "\n"}
DIGITS = "0123456789"
LETTERS = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ_"


@dataclass
class Token:
    kind: str
    text: str
    line: int
    col: int


class LexError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


def tokenize(source):
    tokens = []
    i = 0
    line = 1
    col = 1
    n = len(source)

    def advance(count):
        nonlocal i, line, col
        for _ in range(count):
            if source[i] == "\n":
                line += 1
                col = 1
            else:
                col += 1
            i += 1

    while i < n:
        ch = source[i]
        start_line, start_col = line, col
        if ch in " \t\r\n":
            advance(1)
        elif ch == "#":
            while i < n and source[i] != "\n":
                advance(1)
        elif ch in DIGITS:
            j = i
            while j < n and source[j] in DIGITS:
                j += 1
            tokens.append(Token("NUMBER", source[i:j], start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch in LETTERS:
            j = i
            while j < n and (source[j] in LETTERS or source[j] in DIGITS):
                j += 1
            word = source[i:j]
            kind = "KEYWORD" if word in KEYWORDS else "IDENT"
            tokens.append(Token(kind, word, start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch == '"':
            advance(1)
            chars = []
            while True:
                if i >= n or source[i] == "\n":
                    raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                c = source[i]
                if c == '"':
                    advance(1)
                    break
                if c == "\\":
                    if i + 1 >= n or source[i + 1] == "\n":
                        raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                    if source[i + 1] not in ESCAPES:
                        raise LexError("unknown escape", line, col)
                    chars.append(ESCAPES[source[i + 1]])
                    advance(2)
                else:
                    chars.append(c)
                    advance(1)
            tokens.append(Token("STRING", "".join(chars), start_line, start_col))
        elif source[i:i + 2] in TWO_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", source[i:i + 2], start_line, start_col))
            advance(2)
        elif ch in ONE_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", ch, start_line, start_col))
            advance(1)
        else:
            raise LexError(f"unexpected character {ch!r}", start_line, start_col)
    tokens.append(Token("EOF", "", line, col))
    return tokens

class ParseError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


COMPARE = ("==", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">=")
TYPES = ("int", "bool", "str")


class Parser:
    def __init__(self, tokens):
        self.tokens = tokens
        self.pos = 0

    def peek(self, ahead=0):
        return self.tokens[min(self.pos + ahead, len(self.tokens) - 1)]

    def at(self, *texts):
        tok = self.peek()
        return tok.kind in ("OP", "KEYWORD") and tok.text in texts

    def advance(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "EOF":
            self.pos += 1
        return tok

    def error(self, message):
        tok = self.peek()
        return ParseError(message, tok.line, tok.col)

    def expect(self, text):
        if not self.at(text):
            raise self.error(f"expected '{text}'")
        return self.advance()

    def expr(self):
        return self.or_expr()

    def or_expr(self):
        left = self.and_expr()
        while self.at("or"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.and_expr())
        return left

    def and_expr(self):
        left = self.not_expr()
        while self.at("and"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.not_expr())
        return left

    def not_expr(self):
        if self.at("not"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("not", self.not_expr())
        return self.compare()

    def compare(self):
        left = self.sum()
        if self.at(*COMPARE):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.sum())
            if self.at(*COMPARE):
                raise self.error("comparisons cannot be chained")
        return left

    def sum(self):
        left = self.product()
        while self.at("+", "-"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.product())
        return left

    def product(self):
        left = self.unary()
        while self.at("*", "/", "%"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.unary())
        return left

    def unary(self):
        if self.at("-"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("-", self.unary())
        return self.call()

    def call(self):
        expr = self.primary()
        while self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            args = []
            if not self.at(")"):
                args.append(self.expr())
                while self.at(","):
                    self.advance()
                    args.append(self.expr())
            self.expect(")")
            expr = Call(expr, args)
        return expr

    def primary(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind == "NUMBER":
            self.advance()
            return Num(int(tok.text))
        if tok.kind == "STRING":
            self.advance()
            return Str(tok.text)
        if tok.kind == "IDENT":
            self.advance()
            return Var(tok.text)
        if self.at("true", "false"):
            self.advance()
            return Bool(tok.text == "true")
        if self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            inner = self.expr()
            self.expect(")")
            return inner
        raise self.error("expected an expression")

    def program(self):
        stmts = []
        while self.peek().kind != "EOF":
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        return Program(stmts)

    def statement(self):
        if self.at("let"):
            return self.let_stmt()
        if self.at("print"):
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Print(value)
        if self.at("if"):
            return self.if_stmt()
        if self.at("while"):
            self.advance()
            cond = self.expr()
            return While(cond, self.block())
        if self.at("fn"):
            return self.fn_stmt()
        if self.at("return"):
            self.advance()
            value = None if self.at(";") else self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Return(value)
        nxt = self.peek(1)
        if self.peek().kind == "IDENT" and nxt.kind == "OP" and nxt.text == "=":
            name = self.advance().text
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Assign(name, value)
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return ExprStmt(value)

    def name(self):
        if self.peek().kind != "IDENT":
            raise self.error("expected a name")
        return self.advance().text

    def type_name(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "IDENT" or tok.text not in TYPES:
            raise self.error("expected a type")
        return self.advance().text

    def let_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        self.expect("=")
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return Let(name, type_, value)

    def if_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        cond = self.expr()
        then = self.block()
        else_ = None
        if self.at("else"):
            self.advance()
            else_ = self.if_stmt() if self.at("if") else self.block()
        return If(cond, then, else_)

    def block(self):
        self.expect("{")
        stmts = []
        while not self.at("}"):
            if self.peek().kind == "EOF":
                raise self.error("expected '}'")
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        self.advance()
        return Block(stmts)

    def param(self):
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        return (name, type_)

    def fn_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        self.expect("(")
        params = []
        if not self.at(")"):
            params.append(self.param())
            while self.at(","):
                self.advance()
                params.append(self.param())
        self.expect(")")
        ret = None
        if self.at("->"):
            self.advance()
            ret = self.type_name()
        return Fn(name, params, ret, self.block())


def parse_program(tokens):
    return Parser(tokens).program()


class CometError(Exception):
    pass


def comet_div(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q


def comet_mod(a, b):
    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FnType:
    params: tuple
    ret: object


def show_type(t):
    if isinstance(t, FnType):
        return "fn(" + ", ".join(show_type(p) for p in t.params) + ") -> " + show_type(t.ret)
    return t


class TypeCheckError(Exception):
    pass


ARITH = ("-", "*", "/", "%")
ORDER = ("<", "<=", ">", ">=")


class Checker:
    def __init__(self):
        self.scopes = [{}]
        self.returns = []

    def declare(self, name, t):
        if name in self.scopes[-1]:
            raise TypeCheckError(f"{name} is already declared in this scope")
        self.scopes[-1][name] = t

    def lookup(self, name):
        for scope in reversed(self.scopes):
            if name in scope:
                return scope[name]
        raise TypeCheckError(f"undefined variable {name}")

    def check_program(self, program):
        for stmt in program.stmts:
            self.check_stmt(stmt)

    def check_block(self, stmts):
        self.scopes.append({})
        try:
            for stmt in stmts:
                self.check_stmt(stmt)
        finally:
            self.scopes.pop()

    def value_type(self, expr):
        t = self.check_expr(expr)
        if t == "void":
            raise TypeCheckError("a call that returns nothing has no value")
        return t

    def check_stmt(self, stmt):
        if isinstance(stmt, Let):
            t = self.value_type(stmt.expr)
            if stmt.type is not None and stmt.type != t:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"{stmt.name} is declared {show_type(stmt.type)} but given {show_type(t)}")
            self.declare(stmt.name, t)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Assign):
            wanted = self.lookup(stmt.name)
            t = self.value_type(stmt.expr)
            if t != wanted:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"cannot assign {show_type(t)} to {stmt.name}, which is {show_type(wanted)}")
        elif isinstance(stmt, Print):
            self.value_type(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, ExprStmt):
            self.check_expr(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, If):
            self.condition(stmt.cond, "if")
            self.check_stmt(stmt.then)
            if stmt.else_ is not None:
                self.check_stmt(stmt.else_)
        elif isinstance(stmt, While):
            self.condition(stmt.cond, "while")
            self.check_stmt(stmt.body)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Block):
            self.check_block(stmt.stmts)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Fn):
            self.check_fn(stmt)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Return):
            self.check_return(stmt)

    def condition(self, expr, where):
        t = self.check_expr(expr)
        if t != "bool":
            raise TypeCheckError(f"the condition of {where} must be bool, not {show_type(t)}")

    def check_fn(self, stmt):
        for name, t in stmt.params:
            if t is None:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"parameter {name} of {stmt.name} needs a type")
        ret = stmt.ret if stmt.ret is not None else "void"
        self.declare(stmt.name, FnType(tuple(t for _, t in stmt.params), ret))
        self.scopes.append({})
        self.returns.append(ret)
        try:
            for name, t in stmt.params:
                self.declare(name, t)
            for inner in stmt.body.stmts:
                self.check_stmt(inner)
        finally:
            self.returns.pop()
            self.scopes.pop()
        if ret != "void" and not self.always_returns(stmt.body.stmts):
            raise TypeCheckError(f"{stmt.name} might end without returning a value of type {ret}")

    def check_return(self, stmt):
        if not self.returns:
            raise TypeCheckError("return outside a function")
        wanted = self.returns[-1]
        if stmt.expr is None:
            if wanted != "void":
                raise TypeCheckError(f"return needs a {wanted} value")
            return
        if wanted == "void":
            raise TypeCheckError("this function returns nothing, so return takes no value")
        t = self.value_type(stmt.expr)
        if t != wanted:
            raise TypeCheckError(f"return needs {wanted}, not {show_type(t)}")

    def always_returns(self, stmts):
        for stmt in stmts:
            if isinstance(stmt, Return):
                return True
            if isinstance(stmt, Block) and self.always_returns(stmt.stmts):
                return True
            if isinstance(stmt, If) and stmt.else_ is not None:
                if self.always_returns([stmt.then]) and self.always_returns([stmt.else_]):
                    return True
        return False

    def check_expr(self, expr):
        if isinstance(expr, Num):
            return "int"
        if isinstance(expr, Str):
            return "str"
        if isinstance(expr, Bool):
            return "bool"
        if isinstance(expr, Var):
            return self.lookup(expr.name)
        if isinstance(expr, Unary):
            t = self.check_expr(expr.expr)
            wanted = "int" if expr.op == "-" else "bool"
            if t != wanted:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"'{expr.op}' needs {wanted}, not {show_type(t)}")
            return wanted
        if isinstance(expr, Binary):
            return self.check_binary(expr)
        if isinstance(expr, Call):
            return self.check_call(expr)
        raise TypeCheckError(f"unknown expression {type(expr).__name__}")

    def check_binary(self, expr):
        left = self.check_expr(expr.left)
        right = self.check_expr(expr.right)
        return self.binary_type(expr.op, left, right)

    def binary_type(self, op, left, right):
        if "void" in (left, right):
            raise TypeCheckError("a call that returns nothing has no value")
        if op in ("and", "or"):
            if left != "bool" or right != "bool":
                raise TypeCheckError(f"'{op}' needs two bools, not {show_type(left)} and {show_type(right)}")
            return "bool"
        if op in ("==", "!="):
            if left != right:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"cannot compare {show_type(left)} with {show_type(right)}")
            return "bool"
        if op == "+" and left == right and left in ("int", "str"):
            return left
        if op in ARITH + ORDER + ("+",):
            if left != "int" or right != "int":
                raise TypeCheckError(f"'{op}' needs two ints, not {show_type(left)} and {show_type(right)}")
            return "bool" if op in ORDER else "int"
        raise TypeCheckError(f"unknown operator {op}")

    def check_call(self, expr):
        callee = self.check_expr(expr.callee)
        if not isinstance(callee, FnType):
            raise TypeCheckError(f"cannot call a value of type {show_type(callee)}")
        if len(expr.args) != len(callee.params):
            raise TypeCheckError(f"expected {len(callee.params)} arguments, got {len(expr.args)}")
        for arg, wanted in zip(expr.args, callee.params):
            t = self.check_expr(arg)
            if t != wanted:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"argument needs {show_type(wanted)}, not {show_type(t)}")
        return callee.ret


def check_source(source):
    try:
        Checker().check_program(parse_program(tokenize(source)))
    except TypeCheckError as e:
        return str(e)
    return None

+++ practice | A type system for units
--- task
In 1999 the Mars Climate Orbiter was lost because one program produced thrust figures in pound-seconds and another read them as newton-seconds. A type system that tracks **units** catches that before launch. Write `units_of(source, env)` for Comet expressions over physical quantities (the starter gives the lexer, the parser and `UnitError`). Parse with `parse_program(tokenize(source + ";")).stmts[0].expr`.

`env` maps each variable to its units, a dictionary from base unit to a non-zero integer power: speed in metres per second is `{"m": 1, "s": -1}`. The rules:

- A number is dimensionless (no units). `true` and `false` are booleans. A string, a call, or a variable not in `env` raises `UnitError`.
- `*` adds the powers of the two sides and `/` subtracts them; powers that become 0 disappear.
- `+`, `-` and `%` need both sides to have the same units, which the result keeps. `-` in front keeps the units.
- `==` `!=` `<` `<=` `>` `>=` need the same units on both sides and give a boolean. `and`, `or` and `not` need booleans. Using a boolean as a quantity raises `UnitError`.

Return `"bool"` for a boolean, and otherwise the units as text: the units with positive powers in alphabetical order, joined by `*`, each written `u^k` if its power k is above 1, or `"1"` if there are none; then, if there are negative powers, a `/` followed by the units with negative powers written the same way (with the power's size), in alphabetical order, in parentheses and joined by `*` if there is more than one. So `{"m": 1, "s": -2}` is `m/s^2`, `{"m": 1, "kg": -1, "s": -1}` is `m/(kg*s)`, `{"s": -1}` is `1/s`, and no units is `1`.

For example, with speed `v` in `{"m": 1, "s": -1}` and time `t` in `{"s": 1}`, `units_of("v / t", env)` is `"m/s^2"`.
--- starter
from dataclasses import dataclass

KEYWORDS = {"let", "fn", "return", "if", "else", "while", "print",
            "true", "false", "and", "or", "not"}
TWO_CHAR = {"==", "!=", "<=", ">=", "->"}
ONE_CHAR = set("+-*/%<>=(){},;:")
ESCAPES = {'"': '"', "\\": "\\", "n": "\n"}
DIGITS = "0123456789"
LETTERS = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ_"


@dataclass
class Token:
    kind: str
    text: str
    line: int
    col: int


class LexError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


def tokenize(source):
    tokens = []
    i = 0
    line = 1
    col = 1
    n = len(source)

    def advance(count):
        nonlocal i, line, col
        for _ in range(count):
            if source[i] == "\n":
                line += 1
                col = 1
            else:
                col += 1
            i += 1

    while i < n:
        ch = source[i]
        start_line, start_col = line, col
        if ch in " \t\r\n":
            advance(1)
        elif ch == "#":
            while i < n and source[i] != "\n":
                advance(1)
        elif ch in DIGITS:
            j = i
            while j < n and source[j] in DIGITS:
                j += 1
            tokens.append(Token("NUMBER", source[i:j], start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch in LETTERS:
            j = i
            while j < n and (source[j] in LETTERS or source[j] in DIGITS):
                j += 1
            word = source[i:j]
            kind = "KEYWORD" if word in KEYWORDS else "IDENT"
            tokens.append(Token(kind, word, start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch == '"':
            advance(1)
            chars = []
            while True:
                if i >= n or source[i] == "\n":
                    raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                c = source[i]
                if c == '"':
                    advance(1)
                    break
                if c == "\\":
                    if i + 1 >= n or source[i + 1] == "\n":
                        raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                    if source[i + 1] not in ESCAPES:
                        raise LexError("unknown escape", line, col)
                    chars.append(ESCAPES[source[i + 1]])
                    advance(2)
                else:
                    chars.append(c)
                    advance(1)
            tokens.append(Token("STRING", "".join(chars), start_line, start_col))
        elif source[i:i + 2] in TWO_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", source[i:i + 2], start_line, start_col))
            advance(2)
        elif ch in ONE_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", ch, start_line, start_col))
            advance(1)
        else:
            raise LexError(f"unexpected character {ch!r}", start_line, start_col)
    tokens.append(Token("EOF", "", line, col))
    return tokens

class ParseError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


COMPARE = ("==", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">=")
TYPES = ("int", "bool", "str")


class Parser:
    def __init__(self, tokens):
        self.tokens = tokens
        self.pos = 0

    def peek(self, ahead=0):
        return self.tokens[min(self.pos + ahead, len(self.tokens) - 1)]

    def at(self, *texts):
        tok = self.peek()
        return tok.kind in ("OP", "KEYWORD") and tok.text in texts

    def advance(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "EOF":
            self.pos += 1
        return tok

    def error(self, message):
        tok = self.peek()
        return ParseError(message, tok.line, tok.col)

    def expect(self, text):
        if not self.at(text):
            raise self.error(f"expected '{text}'")
        return self.advance()

    def expr(self):
        return self.or_expr()

    def or_expr(self):
        left = self.and_expr()
        while self.at("or"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.and_expr())
        return left

    def and_expr(self):
        left = self.not_expr()
        while self.at("and"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.not_expr())
        return left

    def not_expr(self):
        if self.at("not"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("not", self.not_expr())
        return self.compare()

    def compare(self):
        left = self.sum()
        if self.at(*COMPARE):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.sum())
            if self.at(*COMPARE):
                raise self.error("comparisons cannot be chained")
        return left

    def sum(self):
        left = self.product()
        while self.at("+", "-"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.product())
        return left

    def product(self):
        left = self.unary()
        while self.at("*", "/", "%"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.unary())
        return left

    def unary(self):
        if self.at("-"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("-", self.unary())
        return self.call()

    def call(self):
        expr = self.primary()
        while self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            args = []
            if not self.at(")"):
                args.append(self.expr())
                while self.at(","):
                    self.advance()
                    args.append(self.expr())
            self.expect(")")
            expr = Call(expr, args)
        return expr

    def primary(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind == "NUMBER":
            self.advance()
            return Num(int(tok.text))
        if tok.kind == "STRING":
            self.advance()
            return Str(tok.text)
        if tok.kind == "IDENT":
            self.advance()
            return Var(tok.text)
        if self.at("true", "false"):
            self.advance()
            return Bool(tok.text == "true")
        if self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            inner = self.expr()
            self.expect(")")
            return inner
        raise self.error("expected an expression")

    def program(self):
        stmts = []
        while self.peek().kind != "EOF":
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        return Program(stmts)

    def statement(self):
        if self.at("let"):
            return self.let_stmt()
        if self.at("print"):
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Print(value)
        if self.at("if"):
            return self.if_stmt()
        if self.at("while"):
            self.advance()
            cond = self.expr()
            return While(cond, self.block())
        if self.at("fn"):
            return self.fn_stmt()
        if self.at("return"):
            self.advance()
            value = None if self.at(";") else self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Return(value)
        nxt = self.peek(1)
        if self.peek().kind == "IDENT" and nxt.kind == "OP" and nxt.text == "=":
            name = self.advance().text
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Assign(name, value)
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return ExprStmt(value)

    def name(self):
        if self.peek().kind != "IDENT":
            raise self.error("expected a name")
        return self.advance().text

    def type_name(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "IDENT" or tok.text not in TYPES:
            raise self.error("expected a type")
        return self.advance().text

    def let_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        self.expect("=")
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return Let(name, type_, value)

    def if_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        cond = self.expr()
        then = self.block()
        else_ = None
        if self.at("else"):
            self.advance()
            else_ = self.if_stmt() if self.at("if") else self.block()
        return If(cond, then, else_)

    def block(self):
        self.expect("{")
        stmts = []
        while not self.at("}"):
            if self.peek().kind == "EOF":
                raise self.error("expected '}'")
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        self.advance()
        return Block(stmts)

    def param(self):
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        return (name, type_)

    def fn_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        self.expect("(")
        params = []
        if not self.at(")"):
            params.append(self.param())
            while self.at(","):
                self.advance()
                params.append(self.param())
        self.expect(")")
        ret = None
        if self.at("->"):
            self.advance()
            ret = self.type_name()
        return Fn(name, params, ret, self.block())


def parse_program(tokens):
    return Parser(tokens).program()

    pass


def comet_div(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q


def comet_mod(a, b):
    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)

        self.pos = 0

        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "EOF":
            self.pos += 1
        return tok

    def error(self, message):
        tok = self.peek()
        return ParseError(message, tok.line, tok.col)

    def expect(self, text):
        if not self.at(text):
            raise self.error(f"expected '{text}'")
        return self.advance()

    def expr(self):
        return self.or_expr()

    def or_expr(self):

            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.and_expr())
        return left

    def and_expr(self):

            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.not_expr())
        return left

    def not_expr(self):
        if self.at("not"):
            self.advance()

        return self.compare()

    def compare(self):

            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.sum())
            if self.at(*COMPARE):
                raise self.error("comparisons cannot be chained")
        return left

            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.product())
        return left

    def product(self):
        left = self.unary()
        while self.at("*", "/", "%"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.unary())
        return left

    def unary(self):
        if self.at("-"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("-", self.unary())
        return self.call()

    def call(self):
        expr = self.primary()

            self.advance()
            args = []
            if not self.at(")"):
                args.append(self.expr())
                while self.at(","):
                    self.advance()
                    args.append(self.expr())
            self.expect(")")
            expr = Call(expr, args)
        return expr

    def primary(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind == "NUMBER":
            self.advance()
            return Num(int(tok.text))
        if tok.kind == "STRING":
            self.advance()
            return Str(tok.text)
        if tok.kind == "IDENT":
            self.advance()
            return Var(tok.text)

            cond = self.expr()

            return self.fn_stmt()

            return Assign(name, value)

        self.expect(";")
        return ExprStmt(value)

    def name(self):
        if self.peek().kind != "IDENT":
            raise self.error("expected a name")
        return self.advance().text

    def type_name(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "IDENT" or tok.text not in TYPES:
            raise self.error("expected a type")

    def let_stmt(self):

            self.advance()

    def if_stmt(self):

        cond = self.expr()
        then = self.block()
        else_ = None
        if self.at("else"):
            self.advance()
            else_ = self.if_stmt() if self.at("if") else self.block()
        return If(cond, then, else_)

    def block(self):

def comet_div(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q

class UnitError(Exception):
    pass


def combine(a, b, sign):
    result = dict(a)
    for unit, power in b.items():
        result[unit] = result.get(unit, 0) + sign * power
        if result[unit] == 0:
            del result[unit]
    return result


def unit_text(units):
    top = [u if units[u] == 1 else f"{u}^{units[u]}" for u in sorted(units) if units[u] > 0]
    bottom = [u if units[u] == -1 else f"{u}^{-units[u]}" for u in sorted(units) if units[u] < 0]
    text = "*".join(top) if top else "1"
    if len(bottom) == 1:
        text += "/" + bottom[0]
    elif bottom:
        text += "/(" + "*".join(bottom) + ")"
    return text


def units(expr, env):
    if isinstance(expr, Num):
        return {}
    if isinstance(expr, Bool):
        return "bool"
    if isinstance(expr, Var):
        if expr.name not in env:
            raise UnitError(f"unknown quantity {expr.name}")
        return dict(env[expr.name])
    if isinstance(expr, Unary):
        inner = units(expr.expr, env)
        if expr.op == "not":
            if inner != "bool":
                raise UnitError("'not' needs a bool")
            return "bool"
        if inner == "bool":
            raise UnitError("cannot negate a bool")
        return inner
    if isinstance(expr, Binary):
        left = units(expr.left, env)
        right = units(expr.right, env)
        op = expr.op
        if op in ("and", "or"):
            if left != "bool" or right != "bool":
                raise UnitError(f"'{op}' needs two bools")
            return "bool"
        if left == "bool" or right == "bool":
            raise UnitError(f"'{op}' needs quantities, not bools")
        if op == "*":
            return combine(left, right, 1)
        if op == "/":
            return combine(left, right, -1)
        if left != right:
            raise UnitError(f"'{op}' needs equal units, not {unit_text(left)} and {unit_text(right)}")
        if op in ("+", "-", "%"):
            return left
        return "bool"
    raise UnitError(f"{type(expr).__name__} has no units")


def units_of(source, env):
    expr = parse_program(tokenize(source + ";")).stmts[0].expr
    result = units(expr, env)
    return result if result == "bool" else unit_text(result)

units_of("v / t", {"v": {"m": 1, "s": -1}, "t": {"s": 1}}) == "m/s^2"

(lambda env: [units_of(s, env) for s in ["dist / t / t", "mass * a", "dist / (t * mass)", "hz", "mass * mass * dist / (t * t * hz)", "dist / dist", "3"]] == ["m/s^2", "kg*m/s^2", "m/(kg*s)", "1/s", "kg^2*m/s", "1", "1"])({"dist": {"m": 1}, "t": {"s": 1}, "mass": {"kg": 1}, "a": {"m": 1, "s": -2}, "hz": {"s": -1}})
--- check test | Adding needs equal units
(lambda env: units_of("f / mass - a", env) == "m/s^2" and units_of("2 * dist + dist", env) == "m" and units_of("-v", env) == "m/s" and raises(UnitError, lambda: units_of("dist + t", env)) and raises(UnitError, lambda: units_of("v - dist", env)))({"dist": {"m": 1}, "t": {"s": 1}, "v": {"m": 1, "s": -1}, "mass": {"kg": 1}, "a": {"m": 1, "s": -2}, "f": {"kg": 1, "m": 1, "s": -2}})
--- check test | Comparisons give booleans
(lambda env: units_of("v * t == dist", env) == "bool" and units_of("t * hz > 1 and true", env) == "bool" and raises(UnitError, lambda: units_of("v == dist", env)) and raises(UnitError, lambda: units_of("t > 1", env)))({"dist": {"m": 1}, "t": {"s": 1}, "v": {"m": 1, "s": -1}, "hz": {"s": -1}})
--- check test | Booleans are not quantities, and unknown names fail
(lambda env: all(raises(UnitError, lambda s=s: units_of(s, env)) for s in ["not dist", "dist and true", "-true", "true + 1", "x + 1", '"s"', "f(dist)"]))({"dist": {"m": 1}})
--- check test | The environment is not changed
(lambda env: (units_of("v * v * v", env), env == {"v": {"m": 1, "s": -1}})[-1])({"v": {"m": 1, "s": -1}})

+++ practice | Breaking an unsound checker
--- task
A type checker is sound only if every rule keeps the lesson's invariant. The starter gives the lesson's checker, the lesson 8 interpreter (`run_source`), and a second checker, `lax_check_source`, which is the same except for one rule: for an assignment `x = e;`, it only checks that x is declared and that e has a type other than `void`, not that the two types are equal.

Prove that `lax_check_source` is unsound by finding a counterexample: set `COUNTEREXAMPLE` to a Comet program that

- `lax_check_source` accepts (returns `None`),
- the real `check_source` rejects, and
- stops with a **runtime type error** when run with `run_source`: an error other than "division by zero" or "stack overflow".
--- starter
from dataclasses import dataclass

KEYWORDS = {"let", "fn", "return", "if", "else", "while", "print",
            "true", "false", "and", "or", "not"}
TWO_CHAR = {"==", "!=", "<=", ">=", "->"}
ONE_CHAR = set("+-*/%<>=(){},;:")
ESCAPES = {'"': '"', "\\": "\\", "n": "\n"}
DIGITS = "0123456789"
LETTERS = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ_"


@dataclass
class Token:
    kind: str
    text: str
    line: int
    col: int


class LexError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


def tokenize(source):
    tokens = []
    i = 0
    line = 1
    col = 1
    n = len(source)

    def advance(count):
        nonlocal i, line, col
        for _ in range(count):
            if source[i] == "\n":
                line += 1
                col = 1
            else:
                col += 1
            i += 1

    while i < n:
        ch = source[i]
        start_line, start_col = line, col
        if ch in " \t\r\n":
            advance(1)
        elif ch == "#":
            while i < n and source[i] != "\n":
                advance(1)
        elif ch in DIGITS:
            j = i
            while j < n and source[j] in DIGITS:
                j += 1
            tokens.append(Token("NUMBER", source[i:j], start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch in LETTERS:
            j = i
            while j < n and (source[j] in LETTERS or source[j] in DIGITS):
                j += 1
            word = source[i:j]
            kind = "KEYWORD" if word in KEYWORDS else "IDENT"
            tokens.append(Token(kind, word, start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch == '"':
            advance(1)
            chars = []
            while True:
                if i >= n or source[i] == "\n":
                    raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                c = source[i]
                if c == '"':
                    advance(1)
                    break
                if c == "\\":
                    if i + 1 >= n or source[i + 1] == "\n":
                        raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                    if source[i + 1] not in ESCAPES:
                        raise LexError("unknown escape", line, col)
                    chars.append(ESCAPES[source[i + 1]])
                    advance(2)
                else:
                    chars.append(c)
                    advance(1)
            tokens.append(Token("STRING", "".join(chars), start_line, start_col))
        elif source[i:i + 2] in TWO_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", source[i:i + 2], start_line, start_col))
            advance(2)
        elif ch in ONE_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", ch, start_line, start_col))
            advance(1)
        else:
            raise LexError(f"unexpected character {ch!r}", start_line, start_col)
    tokens.append(Token("EOF", "", line, col))
    return tokens
