class ParseError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


COMPARE = ("==", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">=")
TYPES = ("int", "bool", "str")


class Parser:
    def __init__(self, tokens):
        self.tokens = tokens
        self.pos = 0

    def peek(self, ahead=0):
        return self.tokens[min(self.pos + ahead, len(self.tokens) - 1)]

    def at(self, *texts):
        tok = self.peek()
        return tok.kind in ("OP", "KEYWORD") and tok.text in texts

    def advance(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "EOF":
            self.pos += 1
        return tok

    def error(self, message):
        tok = self.peek()
        return ParseError(message, tok.line, tok.col)

    def expect(self, text):
        if not self.at(text):
            raise self.error(f"expected '{text}'")
        return self.advance()

    def expr(self):
        return self.or_expr()

    def or_expr(self):
        left = self.and_expr()
        while self.at("or"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.and_expr())
        return left

    def and_expr(self):
        left = self.not_expr()
        while self.at("and"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.not_expr())
        return left

    def not_expr(self):
        if self.at("not"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("not", self.not_expr())
        return self.compare()

    def compare(self):
        left = self.sum()
        if self.at(*COMPARE):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.sum())
            if self.at(*COMPARE):
                raise self.error("comparisons cannot be chained")
        return left

    def sum(self):
        left = self.product()
        while self.at("+", "-"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.product())
        return left

    def product(self):
        left = self.unary()
        while self.at("*", "/", "%"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.unary())
        return left

    def unary(self):
        if self.at("-"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("-", self.unary())
        return self.call()

    def call(self):
        expr = self.primary()
        while self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            args = []
            if not self.at(")"):
                args.append(self.expr())
                while self.at(","):
                    self.advance()
                    args.append(self.expr())
            self.expect(")")
            expr = Call(expr, args)
        return expr

    def primary(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind == "NUMBER":
            self.advance()
            return Num(int(tok.text))
        if tok.kind == "STRING":
            self.advance()
            return Str(tok.text)
        if tok.kind == "IDENT":
            self.advance()
            return Var(tok.text)
        if self.at("true", "false"):
            self.advance()
            return Bool(tok.text == "true")
        if self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            inner = self.expr()
            self.expect(")")
            return inner
        raise self.error("expected an expression")

    def program(self):
        stmts = []
        while self.peek().kind != "EOF":
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        return Program(stmts)

    def statement(self):
        if self.at("let"):
            return self.let_stmt()
        if self.at("print"):
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Print(value)
        if self.at("if"):
            return self.if_stmt()
        if self.at("while"):
            self.advance()
            cond = self.expr()
            return While(cond, self.block())
        if self.at("fn"):
            return self.fn_stmt()
        if self.at("return"):
            self.advance()
            value = None if self.at(";") else self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Return(value)
        nxt = self.peek(1)
        if self.peek().kind == "IDENT" and nxt.kind == "OP" and nxt.text == "=":
            name = self.advance().text
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Assign(name, value)
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return ExprStmt(value)

    def name(self):
        if self.peek().kind != "IDENT":
            raise self.error("expected a name")
        return self.advance().text

    def type_name(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "IDENT" or tok.text not in TYPES:
            raise self.error("expected a type")
        return self.advance().text

    def let_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        self.expect("=")
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return Let(name, type_, value)

    def if_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        cond = self.expr()
        then = self.block()
        else_ = None
        if self.at("else"):
            self.advance()
            else_ = self.if_stmt() if self.at("if") else self.block()
        return If(cond, then, else_)

    def block(self):
        self.expect("{")
        stmts = []
        while not self.at("}"):
            if self.peek().kind == "EOF":
                raise self.error("expected '}'")
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        self.advance()
        return Block(stmts)

    def param(self):
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        return (name, type_)

    def fn_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        self.expect("(")
        params = []
        if not self.at(")"):
            params.append(self.param())
            while self.at(","):
                self.advance()
                params.append(self.param())
        self.expect(")")
        ret = None
        if self.at("->"):
            self.advance()
            ret = self.type_name()
        return Fn(name, params, ret, self.block())


def parse_program(tokens):
    return Parser(tokens).program()


class CometError(Exception):
    pass


def comet_div(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q


def comet_mod(a, b):
    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FnType:
    params: tuple
    ret: object


def show_type(t):
    if isinstance(t, FnType):
        return "fn(" + ", ".join(show_type(p) for p in t.params) + ") -> " + show_type(t.ret)
    return t


class TypeCheckError(Exception):
    pass


ARITH = ("-", "*", "/", "%")
ORDER = ("<", "<=", ">", ">=")


class Checker:
    def __init__(self):
        self.scopes = [{}]
        self.returns = []

    def declare(self, name, t):
        if name in self.scopes[-1]:
            raise TypeCheckError(f"{name} is already declared in this scope")
        self.scopes[-1][name] = t

    def lookup(self, name):
        for scope in reversed(self.scopes):
            if name in scope:
                return scope[name]
        raise TypeCheckError(f"undefined variable {name}")

    def check_program(self, program):
        for stmt in program.stmts:
            self.check_stmt(stmt)

    def check_block(self, stmts):
        self.scopes.append({})
        try:
            for stmt in stmts:
                self.check_stmt(stmt)
        finally:
            self.scopes.pop()

    def value_type(self, expr):
        t = self.check_expr(expr)
        if t == "void":
            raise TypeCheckError("a call that returns nothing has no value")
        return t

    def check_stmt(self, stmt):
        if isinstance(stmt, Let):
            t = self.value_type(stmt.expr)
            if stmt.type is not None and stmt.type != t:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"{stmt.name} is declared {show_type(stmt.type)} but given {show_type(t)}")
            self.declare(stmt.name, t)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Assign):
            wanted = self.lookup(stmt.name)
            t = self.value_type(stmt.expr)
            if t != wanted:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"cannot assign {show_type(t)} to {stmt.name}, which is {show_type(wanted)}")
        elif isinstance(stmt, Print):
            self.value_type(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, ExprStmt):
            self.check_expr(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, If):
            self.condition(stmt.cond, "if")
            self.check_stmt(stmt.then)
            if stmt.else_ is not None:
                self.check_stmt(stmt.else_)
        elif isinstance(stmt, While):
            self.condition(stmt.cond, "while")
            self.check_stmt(stmt.body)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Block):
            self.check_block(stmt.stmts)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Fn):
            self.check_fn(stmt)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Return):
            self.check_return(stmt)

    def condition(self, expr, where):
        t = self.check_expr(expr)
        if t != "bool":
            raise TypeCheckError(f"the condition of {where} must be bool, not {show_type(t)}")

    def check_fn(self, stmt):
        for name, t in stmt.params:
            if t is None:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"parameter {name} of {stmt.name} needs a type")
        ret = stmt.ret if stmt.ret is not None else "void"
        self.declare(stmt.name, FnType(tuple(t for _, t in stmt.params), ret))
        self.scopes.append({})
        self.returns.append(ret)
        try:
            for name, t in stmt.params:
                self.declare(name, t)
            for inner in stmt.body.stmts:
                self.check_stmt(inner)
        finally:
            self.returns.pop()
            self.scopes.pop()
        if ret != "void" and not self.always_returns(stmt.body.stmts):
            raise TypeCheckError(f"{stmt.name} might end without returning a value of type {ret}")

    def check_return(self, stmt):
        if not self.returns:
            raise TypeCheckError("return outside a function")
        wanted = self.returns[-1]
        if stmt.expr is None:
            if wanted != "void":
                raise TypeCheckError(f"return needs a {wanted} value")
            return
        if wanted == "void":
            raise TypeCheckError("this function returns nothing, so return takes no value")
        t = self.value_type(stmt.expr)
        if t != wanted:
            raise TypeCheckError(f"return needs {wanted}, not {show_type(t)}")

    def always_returns(self, stmts):
        for stmt in stmts:
            if isinstance(stmt, Return):
                return True
            if isinstance(stmt, Block) and self.always_returns(stmt.stmts):
                return True
            if isinstance(stmt, If) and stmt.else_ is not None:
                if self.always_returns([stmt.then]) and self.always_returns([stmt.else_]):
                    return True
        return False

    def check_expr(self, expr):
        if isinstance(expr, Num):
            return "int"
        if isinstance(expr, Str):
            return "str"
        if isinstance(expr, Bool):
            return "bool"
        if isinstance(expr, Var):
            return self.lookup(expr.name)
        if isinstance(expr, Unary):
            t = self.check_expr(expr.expr)
            wanted = "int" if expr.op == "-" else "bool"
            if t != wanted:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"'{expr.op}' needs {wanted}, not {show_type(t)}")
            return wanted
        if isinstance(expr, Binary):
            return self.check_binary(expr)
        if isinstance(expr, Call):
            return self.check_call(expr)
        raise TypeCheckError(f"unknown expression {type(expr).__name__}")

    def check_binary(self, expr):
        left = self.check_expr(expr.left)
        right = self.check_expr(expr.right)
        return self.binary_type(expr.op, left, right)

    def binary_type(self, op, left, right):
        if "void" in (left, right):
            raise TypeCheckError("a call that returns nothing has no value")
        if op in ("and", "or"):
            if left != "bool" or right != "bool":
                raise TypeCheckError(f"'{op}' needs two bools, not {show_type(left)} and {show_type(right)}")
            return "bool"
        if op in ("==", "!="):
            if left != right:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"cannot compare {show_type(left)} with {show_type(right)}")
            return "bool"
        if op == "+" and left == right and left in ("int", "str"):
            return left
        if op in ARITH + ORDER + ("+",):
            if left != "int" or right != "int":
                raise TypeCheckError(f"'{op}' needs two ints, not {show_type(left)} and {show_type(right)}")
            return "bool" if op in ORDER else "int"
        raise TypeCheckError(f"unknown operator {op}")

    def check_call(self, expr):
        callee = self.check_expr(expr.callee)
        if not isinstance(callee, FnType):
            raise TypeCheckError(f"cannot call a value of type {show_type(callee)}")
        if len(expr.args) != len(callee.params):
            raise TypeCheckError(f"expected {len(callee.params)} arguments, got {len(expr.args)}")
        for arg, wanted in zip(expr.args, callee.params):
            t = self.check_expr(arg)
            if t != wanted:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"argument needs {show_type(wanted)}, not {show_type(t)}")
        return callee.ret


def check_source(source):
    try:
        Checker().check_program(parse_program(tokenize(source)))
    except TypeCheckError as e:
        return str(e)
    return None


class LaxChecker(Checker):
    def check_stmt(self, stmt):
        if isinstance(stmt, Assign):
            self.lookup(stmt.name)
            self.value_type(stmt.expr)
            return
        super().check_stmt(stmt)


def lax_check_source(source):
    try:
        LaxChecker().check_program(parse_program(tokenize(source)))
    except TypeCheckError as e:
        return str(e)
    return None


MAX_DEPTH = 40


class Closure:
    def __init__(self, decl, env):
        self.decl = decl
        self.env = env


class ReturnSignal(Exception):
    def __init__(self, value):
        super().__init__("return")
        self.value = value


def type_name(value):
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "bool"
    if isinstance(value, int):
        return "int"
    if isinstance(value, str):
        return "str"
    if isinstance(value, Closure):
        return "fn"

    return "nothing"


def show(value):
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "true" if value else "false"
    if isinstance(value, Closure):
        return f"<fn {value.decl.name}>"

    if value is None:
        raise CometError("cannot print nothing")
    return str(value)


class Environment:
    def __init__(self, parent=None):
        self.values = {}
        self.parent = parent

    def define(self, name, value):
        if name in self.values:
            raise CometError(f"{name} is already declared in this scope")
        self.values[name] = value

    def find(self, name):
        env = self
        while env is not None:
            if name in env.values:
                return env
            env = env.parent
        return None

    def lookup(self, name):
        env = self.find(name)
        if env is None:
            raise CometError(f"undefined variable {name}")
        return env.values[name]

    def assign(self, name, value):
        env = self.find(name)
        if env is None:
            raise CometError(f"assignment to undeclared variable {name}")
        env.values[name] = value


class Interpreter:
    def __init__(self):
        self.globals = Environment()
        self.env = self.globals
        self.output = []
        self.frames = []


    def run(self, program):
        for stmt in program.stmts:
            self.execute(stmt)

    def execute_block(self, stmts, env):
        previous = self.env
        self.env = env
        try:
            for stmt in stmts:
                self.execute(stmt)
        finally:
            self.env = previous

    def execute(self, stmt):
        if isinstance(stmt, Let):
            self.env.define(stmt.name, self.evaluate(stmt.expr))
        elif isinstance(stmt, Assign):
            value = self.evaluate(stmt.expr)
            self.env.assign(stmt.name, value)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Print):
            self.output.append(show(self.evaluate(stmt.expr)))
        elif isinstance(stmt, ExprStmt):
            self.evaluate(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, If):
            if self.condition(stmt.cond):
                self.execute(stmt.then)
            elif stmt.else_ is not None:
                self.execute(stmt.else_)
        elif isinstance(stmt, While):
            while self.condition(stmt.cond):
                self.execute(stmt.body)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Block):
            self.execute_block(stmt.stmts, Environment(self.env))
        elif isinstance(stmt, Fn):
            self.env.define(stmt.name, Closure(stmt, self.env))
        elif isinstance(stmt, Return):
            if not self.frames:
                raise CometError("return outside a function")
            value = None if stmt.expr is None else self.evaluate(stmt.expr)
            raise ReturnSignal(value)
        else:
            raise CometError(f"{type(stmt).__name__} is not supported yet")

    def condition(self, expr):
        value = self.evaluate(expr)
        if not isinstance(value, bool):
            raise CometError(f"condition must be bool, not {type_name(value)}")
        return value

    def evaluate(self, expr):
        if isinstance(expr, (Num, Str, Bool)):
            return expr.value
        if isinstance(expr, Var):
            return self.env.lookup(expr.name)
        if isinstance(expr, Unary):
            value = self.evaluate(expr.expr)
            if expr.op == "-":
                self.need("int", value, "-")
                return -value
            self.need("bool", value, "not")
            return not value
        if isinstance(expr, Binary):
            return self.binary(expr)
        if isinstance(expr, Call):
            callee = self.evaluate(expr.callee)
            args = [self.evaluate(arg) for arg in expr.args]
            return self.call(callee, args)
        raise CometError(f"{type(expr).__name__} is not supported yet")

    def call(self, callee, args):
        if not isinstance(callee, Closure):
            raise CometError(f"cannot call a value of type {type_name(callee)}")
        decl = callee.decl
        if len(args) != len(decl.params):
            raise CometError(f"{decl.name} expects {len(decl.params)} arguments, got {len(args)}")
        if len(self.frames) >= MAX_DEPTH:
            raise CometError("stack overflow")
        env = Environment(callee.env)
        for (name, _), value in zip(decl.params, args):
            env.define(name, value)
        self.frames.append(decl.name)
        try:
            self.execute_block(decl.body.stmts, env)
        except ReturnSignal as signal:
            return signal.value
        finally:
            self.frames.pop()
        return None

    def need(self, wanted, value, op):
        if type_name(value) != wanted:
            raise CometError(f"'{op}' needs {wanted}, not {type_name(value)}")

    def binary(self, expr):
        op = expr.op
        left = self.evaluate(expr.left)
        if op in ("and", "or"):
            self.need("bool", left, op)
            if (op == "and" and not left) or (op == "or" and left):
                return left
            right = self.evaluate(expr.right)
            self.need("bool", right, op)
            return right
        right = self.evaluate(expr.right)
        if op in ("==", "!="):
            if type_name(left) != type_name(right):
                raise CometError(f"cannot compare {type_name(left)} with {type_name(right)}")
            return (left is right if isinstance(left, Closure) else left == right) == (op == "==")
        if op == "+" and type_name(left) == "str" and type_name(right) == "str":
            return left + right
        self.need("int", left, op)
        self.need("int", right, op)
        if op == "+":
            return left + right
        if op == "-":
            return left - right
        if op == "*":
            return left * right
        if op == "/":
            return comet_div(left, right)
        if op == "%":
            return comet_mod(left, right)
        if op == "<":
            return left < right
        if op == "<=":
            return left <= right
        if op == ">":
            return left > right
        return left >= right


def run_source(source):
    interp = Interpreter()
    try:
        interp.run(parse_program(tokenize(source)))
    except CometError as e:
        return interp.output, str(e)
    return interp.output, None

let reading = 1;
print reading;

from dataclasses import dataclass

KEYWORDS = {"let", "fn", "return", "if", "else", "while", "print",
            "true", "false", "and", "or", "not"}
TWO_CHAR = {"==", "!=", "<=", ">=", "->"}
ONE_CHAR = set("+-*/%<>=(){},;:")
ESCAPES = {'"': '"', "\\": "\\", "n": "\n"}
DIGITS = "0123456789"
LETTERS = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ_"


@dataclass
class Token:
    kind: str
    text: str
    line: int
    col: int


class LexError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


def tokenize(source):
    tokens = []
    i = 0
    line = 1
    col = 1
    n = len(source)

    def advance(count):
        nonlocal i, line, col
        for _ in range(count):
            if source[i] == "\n":
                line += 1
                col = 1
            else:
                col += 1
            i += 1

    while i < n:
        ch = source[i]
        start_line, start_col = line, col
        if ch in " \t\r\n":
            advance(1)
        elif ch == "#":
            while i < n and source[i] != "\n":
                advance(1)
        elif ch in DIGITS:
            j = i
            while j < n and source[j] in DIGITS:
                j += 1
            tokens.append(Token("NUMBER", source[i:j], start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch in LETTERS:
            j = i
            while j < n and (source[j] in LETTERS or source[j] in DIGITS):
                j += 1
            word = source[i:j]
            kind = "KEYWORD" if word in KEYWORDS else "IDENT"
            tokens.append(Token(kind, word, start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch == '"':
            advance(1)
            chars = []
            while True:
                if i >= n or source[i] == "\n":
                    raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                c = source[i]
                if c == '"':
                    advance(1)
                    break
                if c == "\\":
                    if i + 1 >= n or source[i + 1] == "\n":
                        raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                    if source[i + 1] not in ESCAPES:
                        raise LexError("unknown escape", line, col)
                    chars.append(ESCAPES[source[i + 1]])
                    advance(2)
                else:
                    chars.append(c)
                    advance(1)
            tokens.append(Token("STRING", "".join(chars), start_line, start_col))
        elif source[i:i + 2] in TWO_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", source[i:i + 2], start_line, start_col))
            advance(2)
        elif ch in ONE_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", ch, start_line, start_col))
            advance(1)
        else:
            raise LexError(f"unexpected character {ch!r}", start_line, start_col)
    tokens.append(Token("EOF", "", line, col))
    return tokens

class ParseError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


COMPARE = ("==", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">=")
TYPES = ("int", "bool", "str")


class Parser:
    def __init__(self, tokens):
        self.tokens = tokens
        self.pos = 0

    def peek(self, ahead=0):
        return self.tokens[min(self.pos + ahead, len(self.tokens) - 1)]

    def at(self, *texts):
        tok = self.peek()
        return tok.kind in ("OP", "KEYWORD") and tok.text in texts

    def advance(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "EOF":
            self.pos += 1
        return tok

    def error(self, message):
        tok = self.peek()
        return ParseError(message, tok.line, tok.col)

    def expect(self, text):
        if not self.at(text):
            raise self.error(f"expected '{text}'")
        return self.advance()

    def expr(self):
        return self.or_expr()

    def or_expr(self):
        left = self.and_expr()
        while self.at("or"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.and_expr())
        return left

    def and_expr(self):
        left = self.not_expr()
        while self.at("and"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.not_expr())
        return left

    def not_expr(self):
        if self.at("not"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("not", self.not_expr())
        return self.compare()

    def compare(self):
        left = self.sum()
        if self.at(*COMPARE):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.sum())
            if self.at(*COMPARE):
                raise self.error("comparisons cannot be chained")
        return left

    def sum(self):
        left = self.product()
        while self.at("+", "-"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.product())
        return left

    def product(self):
        left = self.unary()
        while self.at("*", "/", "%"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.unary())
        return left

    def unary(self):
        if self.at("-"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("-", self.unary())
        return self.call()

    def call(self):
        expr = self.primary()
        while self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            args = []
            if not self.at(")"):
                args.append(self.expr())
                while self.at(","):
                    self.advance()
                    args.append(self.expr())
            self.expect(")")
            expr = Call(expr, args)
        return expr

    def primary(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind == "NUMBER":
            self.advance()
            return Num(int(tok.text))
        if tok.kind == "STRING":
            self.advance()
            return Str(tok.text)
        if tok.kind == "IDENT":
            self.advance()
            return Var(tok.text)
        if self.at("true", "false"):
            self.advance()
            return Bool(tok.text == "true")
        if self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            inner = self.expr()
            self.expect(")")
            return inner
        raise self.error("expected an expression")

    def program(self):
        stmts = []
        while self.peek().kind != "EOF":
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        return Program(stmts)

    def statement(self):
        if self.at("let"):
            return self.let_stmt()
        if self.at("print"):
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Print(value)
        if self.at("if"):
            return self.if_stmt()
        if self.at("while"):
            self.advance()
            cond = self.expr()
            return While(cond, self.block())
        if self.at("fn"):
            return self.fn_stmt()
        if self.at("return"):
            self.advance()
            value = None if self.at(";") else self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Return(value)
        nxt = self.peek(1)
        if self.peek().kind == "IDENT" and nxt.kind == "OP" and nxt.text == "=":
            name = self.advance().text
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Assign(name, value)
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return ExprStmt(value)

    def name(self):
        if self.peek().kind != "IDENT":
            raise self.error("expected a name")
        return self.advance().text

    def type_name(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "IDENT" or tok.text not in TYPES:
            raise self.error("expected a type")
        return self.advance().text

    def let_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        self.expect("=")
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return Let(name, type_, value)

    def if_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        cond = self.expr()
        then = self.block()
        else_ = None
        if self.at("else"):
            self.advance()
            else_ = self.if_stmt() if self.at("if") else self.block()
        return If(cond, then, else_)

    def block(self):
        self.expect("{")
        stmts = []
        while not self.at("}"):
            if self.peek().kind == "EOF":
                raise self.error("expected '}'")
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        self.advance()
        return Block(stmts)

    def param(self):
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        return (name, type_)

    def fn_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        self.expect("(")
        params = []
        if not self.at(")"):
            params.append(self.param())
            while self.at(","):
                self.advance()
                params.append(self.param())
        self.expect(")")
        ret = None
        if self.at("->"):
            self.advance()
            ret = self.type_name()
        return Fn(name, params, ret, self.block())


def parse_program(tokens):
    return Parser(tokens).program()


class CometError(Exception):
    pass


def comet_div(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q


def comet_mod(a, b):
    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FnType:
    params: tuple
    ret: object


def show_type(t):
    if isinstance(t, FnType):
        return "fn(" + ", ".join(show_type(p) for p in t.params) + ") -> " + show_type(t.ret)
    return t


class TypeCheckError(Exception):
    pass


ARITH = ("-", "*", "/", "%")
ORDER = ("<", "<=", ">", ">=")


class Checker:
    def __init__(self):
        self.scopes = [{}]
        self.returns = []

    def declare(self, name, t):
        if name in self.scopes[-1]:
            raise TypeCheckError(f"{name} is already declared in this scope")
        self.scopes[-1][name] = t

    def lookup(self, name):
        for scope in reversed(self.scopes):
            if name in scope:
                return scope[name]
        raise TypeCheckError(f"undefined variable {name}")

    def check_program(self, program):
        for stmt in program.stmts:
            self.check_stmt(stmt)

    def check_block(self, stmts):
        self.scopes.append({})
        try:
            for stmt in stmts:
                self.check_stmt(stmt)
        finally:
            self.scopes.pop()

    def value_type(self, expr):
        t = self.check_expr(expr)
        if t == "void":
            raise TypeCheckError("a call that returns nothing has no value")
        return t

    def check_stmt(self, stmt):
        if isinstance(stmt, Let):
            t = self.value_type(stmt.expr)
            if stmt.type is not None and stmt.type != t:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"{stmt.name} is declared {show_type(stmt.type)} but given {show_type(t)}")
            self.declare(stmt.name, t)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Assign):
            wanted = self.lookup(stmt.name)
            t = self.value_type(stmt.expr)
            if t != wanted:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"cannot assign {show_type(t)} to {stmt.name}, which is {show_type(wanted)}")
        elif isinstance(stmt, Print):
            self.value_type(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, ExprStmt):
            self.check_expr(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, If):
            self.condition(stmt.cond, "if")
            self.check_stmt(stmt.then)
            if stmt.else_ is not None:
                self.check_stmt(stmt.else_)
        elif isinstance(stmt, While):
            self.condition(stmt.cond, "while")
            self.check_stmt(stmt.body)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Block):
            self.check_block(stmt.stmts)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Fn):
            self.check_fn(stmt)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Return):
            self.check_return(stmt)

    def condition(self, expr, where):
        t = self.check_expr(expr)
        if t != "bool":
            raise TypeCheckError(f"the condition of {where} must be bool, not {show_type(t)}")

    def check_fn(self, stmt):
        for name, t in stmt.params:
            if t is None:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"parameter {name} of {stmt.name} needs a type")
        ret = stmt.ret if stmt.ret is not None else "void"
        self.declare(stmt.name, FnType(tuple(t for _, t in stmt.params), ret))
        self.scopes.append({})
        self.returns.append(ret)
        try:
            for name, t in stmt.params:
                self.declare(name, t)
            for inner in stmt.body.stmts:
                self.check_stmt(inner)
        finally:
            self.returns.pop()
            self.scopes.pop()
        if ret != "void" and not self.always_returns(stmt.body.stmts):
            raise TypeCheckError(f"{stmt.name} might end without returning a value of type {ret}")

    def check_return(self, stmt):
        if not self.returns:
            raise TypeCheckError("return outside a function")
        wanted = self.returns[-1]
        if stmt.expr is None:
            if wanted != "void":
                raise TypeCheckError(f"return needs a {wanted} value")
            return
        if wanted == "void":
            raise TypeCheckError("this function returns nothing, so return takes no value")
        t = self.value_type(stmt.expr)
        if t != wanted:
            raise TypeCheckError(f"return needs {wanted}, not {show_type(t)}")

    def always_returns(self, stmts):
        for stmt in stmts:
            if isinstance(stmt, Return):
                return True
            if isinstance(stmt, Block) and self.always_returns(stmt.stmts):
                return True
            if isinstance(stmt, If) and stmt.else_ is not None:
                if self.always_returns([stmt.then]) and self.always_returns([stmt.else_]):
                    return True
        return False

    def check_expr(self, expr):
        if isinstance(expr, Num):
            return "int"
        if isinstance(expr, Str):
            return "str"
        if isinstance(expr, Bool):
            return "bool"
        if isinstance(expr, Var):
            return self.lookup(expr.name)
        if isinstance(expr, Unary):
            t = self.check_expr(expr.expr)
            wanted = "int" if expr.op == "-" else "bool"
            if t != wanted:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"'{expr.op}' needs {wanted}, not {show_type(t)}")
            return wanted
        if isinstance(expr, Binary):
            return self.check_binary(expr)
        if isinstance(expr, Call):
            return self.check_call(expr)
        raise TypeCheckError(f"unknown expression {type(expr).__name__}")

    def check_binary(self, expr):
        left = self.check_expr(expr.left)
        right = self.check_expr(expr.right)
        return self.binary_type(expr.op, left, right)

    def binary_type(self, op, left, right):
        if "void" in (left, right):
            raise TypeCheckError("a call that returns nothing has no value")
        if op in ("and", "or"):
            if left != "bool" or right != "bool":
                raise TypeCheckError(f"'{op}' needs two bools, not {show_type(left)} and {show_type(right)}")
            return "bool"
        if op in ("==", "!="):
            if left != right:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"cannot compare {show_type(left)} with {show_type(right)}")
            return "bool"
        if op == "+" and left == right and left in ("int", "str"):
            return left
        if op in ARITH + ORDER + ("+",):
            if left != "int" or right != "int":
                raise TypeCheckError(f"'{op}' needs two ints, not {show_type(left)} and {show_type(right)}")
            return "bool" if op in ORDER else "int"
        raise TypeCheckError(f"unknown operator {op}")

    def check_call(self, expr):
        callee = self.check_expr(expr.callee)
        if not isinstance(callee, FnType):
            raise TypeCheckError(f"cannot call a value of type {show_type(callee)}")
        if len(expr.args) != len(callee.params):
            raise TypeCheckError(f"expected {len(callee.params)} arguments, got {len(expr.args)}")
        for arg, wanted in zip(expr.args, callee.params):
            t = self.check_expr(arg)
            if t != wanted:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"argument needs {show_type(wanted)}, not {show_type(t)}")
        return callee.ret


def check_source(source):
    try:
        Checker().check_program(parse_program(tokenize(source)))
    except TypeCheckError as e:
        return str(e)
    return None


class LaxChecker(Checker):
    def check_stmt(self, stmt):
        if isinstance(stmt, Assign):
            self.lookup(stmt.name)
            self.value_type(stmt.expr)
            return
        super().check_stmt(stmt)


def lax_check_source(source):
    try:
        LaxChecker().check_program(parse_program(tokenize(source)))
    except TypeCheckError as e:
        return str(e)
    return None


MAX_DEPTH = 40


class Closure:
    def __init__(self, decl, env):
        self.decl = decl
        self.env = env


class ReturnSignal(Exception):
    def __init__(self, value):
        super().__init__("return")
        self.value = value


def type_name(value):
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "bool"
    if isinstance(value, int):
        return "int"
    if isinstance(value, str):
        return "str"
    if isinstance(value, Closure):
        return "fn"

    return "nothing"


def show(value):
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "true" if value else "false"
    if isinstance(value, Closure):
        return f"<fn {value.decl.name}>"

    if value is None:
        raise CometError("cannot print nothing")
    return str(value)


class Environment:
    def __init__(self, parent=None):
        self.values = {}
        self.parent = parent

    def define(self, name, value):
        if name in self.values:
            raise CometError(f"{name} is already declared in this scope")
        self.values[name] = value

    def find(self, name):
        env = self
        while env is not None:
            if name in env.values:
                return env
            env = env.parent
        return None

    def lookup(self, name):
        env = self.find(name)
        if env is None:
            raise CometError(f"undefined variable {name}")
        return env.values[name]

    def assign(self, name, value):
        env = self.find(name)
        if env is None:
            raise CometError(f"assignment to undeclared variable {name}")
        env.values[name] = value


class Interpreter:
    def __init__(self):
        self.globals = Environment()
        self.env = self.globals
        self.output = []
        self.frames = []


    def run(self, program):
        for stmt in program.stmts:
            self.execute(stmt)

    def execute_block(self, stmts, env):
        previous = self.env
        self.env = env
        try:
            for stmt in stmts:
                self.execute(stmt)
        finally:
            self.env = previous

    def execute(self, stmt):
        if isinstance(stmt, Let):
            self.env.define(stmt.name, self.evaluate(stmt.expr))
        elif isinstance(stmt, Assign):
            value = self.evaluate(stmt.expr)
            self.env.assign(stmt.name, value)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Print):
            self.output.append(show(self.evaluate(stmt.expr)))
        elif isinstance(stmt, ExprStmt):
            self.evaluate(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, If):
            if self.condition(stmt.cond):
                self.execute(stmt.then)
            elif stmt.else_ is not None:
                self.execute(stmt.else_)
        elif isinstance(stmt, While):
            while self.condition(stmt.cond):
                self.execute(stmt.body)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Block):
            self.execute_block(stmt.stmts, Environment(self.env))
        elif isinstance(stmt, Fn):
            self.env.define(stmt.name, Closure(stmt, self.env))
        elif isinstance(stmt, Return):
            if not self.frames:
                raise CometError("return outside a function")
            value = None if stmt.expr is None else self.evaluate(stmt.expr)
            raise ReturnSignal(value)
        else:
            raise CometError(f"{type(stmt).__name__} is not supported yet")

    def condition(self, expr):
        value = self.evaluate(expr)
        if not isinstance(value, bool):
            raise CometError(f"condition must be bool, not {type_name(value)}")
        return value

    def evaluate(self, expr):
        if isinstance(expr, (Num, Str, Bool)):
            return expr.value
        if isinstance(expr, Var):
            return self.env.lookup(expr.name)
        if isinstance(expr, Unary):
            value = self.evaluate(expr.expr)
            if expr.op == "-":
                self.need("int", value, "-")
                return -value
            self.need("bool", value, "not")
            return not value
        if isinstance(expr, Binary):
            return self.binary(expr)
        if isinstance(expr, Call):
            callee = self.evaluate(expr.callee)
            args = [self.evaluate(arg) for arg in expr.args]
            return self.call(callee, args)
        raise CometError(f"{type(expr).__name__} is not supported yet")

    def call(self, callee, args):
        if not isinstance(callee, Closure):
            raise CometError(f"cannot call a value of type {type_name(callee)}")
        decl = callee.decl
        if len(args) != len(decl.params):
            raise CometError(f"{decl.name} expects {len(decl.params)} arguments, got {len(args)}")
        if len(self.frames) >= MAX_DEPTH:
            raise CometError("stack overflow")
        env = Environment(callee.env)
        for (name, _), value in zip(decl.params, args):
            env.define(name, value)
        self.frames.append(decl.name)
        try:
            self.execute_block(decl.body.stmts, env)
        except ReturnSignal as signal:
            return signal.value
        finally:
            self.frames.pop()
        return None

    def need(self, wanted, value, op):
        if type_name(value) != wanted:
            raise CometError(f"'{op}' needs {wanted}, not {type_name(value)}")

    def binary(self, expr):
        op = expr.op
        left = self.evaluate(expr.left)
        if op in ("and", "or"):
            self.need("bool", left, op)
            if (op == "and" and not left) or (op == "or" and left):
                return left
            right = self.evaluate(expr.right)
            self.need("bool", right, op)
            return right
        right = self.evaluate(expr.right)
        if op in ("==", "!="):
            if type_name(left) != type_name(right):
                raise CometError(f"cannot compare {type_name(left)} with {type_name(right)}")
            return (left is right if isinstance(left, Closure) else left == right) == (op == "==")
        if op == "+" and type_name(left) == "str" and type_name(right) == "str":
            return left + right
        self.need("int", left, op)
        self.need("int", right, op)
        if op == "+":
            return left + right
        if op == "-":
            return left - right
        if op == "*":
            return left * right
        if op == "/":
            return comet_div(left, right)
        if op == "%":
            return comet_mod(left, right)
        if op == "<":
            return left < right
        if op == "<=":
            return left <= right
        if op == ">":
            return left > right
        return left >= right


def run_source(source):
    interp = Interpreter()
    try:
        interp.run(parse_program(tokenize(source)))
    except CometError as e:
        return interp.output, str(e)
    return interp.output, None

let reading = 1;
reading = "offline";
print reading + 1;
"""

+++ question | Which step of the soundness proof
--- ask
The lesson's soundness proof keeps the invariant "every variable holds a value of its static type". Suppose the rule for `let x: T = e;` were changed to skip comparing e's type with T when an annotation is given. Which case of the proof would then fail?
--- choice
The case for literals, because a literal could get the wrong type.
--- choice correct
The case for `let` and assignment, because x could then hold a value whose type differs from its static type T.
--- choice
The case for calls, because the argument count would no longer be checked.
--- choice
None: the interpreter still checks types at run time, so the program stays safe.
--- why
The `let` case of the proof relies on the value stored having the variable's static type. Without the comparison, `let x: int = "a";` gives x the static type int while it holds a string, so the "variable" case of the proof fails for every later use of x, and `x + 1` would pass the checker and fail at run time. The interpreter's own checks catching it is exactly the failure a sound checker promises to prevent.

+++ question | Rejected but harmless
--- ask
The checker rejects `fn f() -> int { while true { return 1; } }`, although every call of f returns 1. Why is that acceptable for a sound checker?
--- choice
It is a bug: a correct checker must accept every program that never goes wrong.
--- choice correct
Soundness only promises that accepted programs never go wrong. A decidable, sound checker must reject some harmless programs, and treating loops conservatively is one of those cases.
--- choice
Because `while true` is not allowed in Comet.
--- choice
Because the function has no parameters.
--- why
Whether a loop always runs, or ever ends, is undecidable in general, so the checker uses a rule it can decide: loops never count as always returning. That can only err by rejecting, never by accepting a bad program. Java adds a special case for `while (true)` without `break`; Comet keeps the simpler rule.

+++ question | The type of a function value
--- ask
In this checker, what is the type of `pick` after `fn pick(a: int, b: bool) -> str { return "x"; }`? Type it the way `show_type` writes it.
--- answer
fn(int, bool) -> str
--- why
A function's type lists its parameter types in order and its return type: fn(int, bool) -> str. `show_type` writes an `FnType` exactly that way, and two functions with the same parameter and return types have equal types, whatever their names.
=== plc-10 | Type inference: unification and Hindley-Milner in the small
--- teach
Last lesson's checker needs a type on every parameter, and it cannot type `fn apply(f, x) { return f(x); }` at all, because nothing says what `f` is. Yet a person reading that function knows: `f` takes whatever `x` is and returns something, and `apply` returns that same something. This lesson teaches the checker to work that out alone. It is **type inference**, and the method, called **Hindley-Milner**, is the one behind ML, OCaml, Haskell and F#.

### Unknowns become type variables

The idea is algebra. When a type is not written down, give it a name, a **type variable**, and collect what the program says about it as **equations** between types. Then solve the equations.

In `fn apply(f, x) { return f(x); }`:

1. `f` gets a fresh variable t1, `x` gets t2, and the return type gets t3.
2. The call `f(x)` needs f to be a function taking x's type: t1 = fn(t2) -> t4, where t4 is a fresh variable for the call's result.
3. `return f(x);` says the return type is the call's type: t3 = t4.

Solving gives t1 = fn(t2) -> t4 and t3 = t4. So `apply` has type fn(fn(t2) -> t4, t2) -> t4, written `(('a) -> 'b, 'a) -> 'b` with the variables renamed in order of appearance, as ML prints them. Nothing about t2 and t4 is known, and nothing needs to be: `apply` works for **every** choice of them. That is **parametric polymorphism**: one function, one piece of code, many types.

Some terms, precisely:

- A **substitution** maps type variables to types. Applying it replaces each variable in a type with what it maps to.
- A **unifier** of two types is a substitution that makes them equal. The **most general unifier** (mgu) is one from which every other unifier can be obtained by substituting further.
- The **principal type** of a function is its most general type: every other type the function could have is an instance of it.

### Unification

**Unification** finds the most general unifier of two types, or reports that there is none. It was invented by [[J. A. Robinson|robinson]] in 1965 for automated theorem proving. First replace any variable that is already bound by what it is bound to, then:

1. If the two types are identical, there is nothing to do.
2. If one side is a variable α, bind α to the other side, **unless α occurs inside the other side**, which is an error.
3. If both are function types with the same number of parameters, unify the parameters pairwise, then the return types.
4. Anything else, such as `int` against `bool`, or a function against `str`, or functions with different numbers of parameters, is a type error.

A worked example: unify `(t1, int) -> t2` with `(bool, t3) -> t1`. The parameters give t1 := bool and then t3 := int; the return types give t2 against t1, and t1 is already bool, so t2 := bool. The mgu is {t1 ↦ bool, t3 ↦ int, t2 ↦ bool}.

### The occurs check

Rule 2's exception is called the **occurs check**. Consider `fn self_apply(x) { return x(x); }`. With x : t1, the call needs t1 = fn(t1) -> t2. Binding t1 to a type that contains t1 would describe an infinite type, fn(fn(fn(…) -> t2) -> t2) -> t2, which no finite type expresses. So the program is rejected. Without the check, the binding is made, and the next attempt to resolve t1 replaces it forever, until Python's recursion limit.

### Inference rules with variables

Lesson 9's rules still apply. Where a rule demanded a type, the inferencer now **unifies** with it:

- `-e` unifies e's type with `int`; `not e` and both sides of `and` and `or` with `bool`; `if` and `while` conditions with `bool`.
- `e₁ == e₂` unifies the two operand types and gives `bool`.
- A call `f(e₁, …, eₙ)` makes a fresh result variable r and unifies f's type with fn(T₁, …, Tₙ) -> r, where Tᵢ is eᵢ's type.
- `return e;` unifies e's type with the function's return type. A function whose body might end without `return` unifies its return type with `void`.

Annotations are still allowed, and are simply more equations: `fn f(n: int)` gives n the type `int` instead of a variable. A function written without `-> T` no longer means `void`: its return type is a fresh variable like any other unknown, so it is inferred from the `return` statements, and becomes `void` only when the body can end without returning or has only bare `return;` statements.

One operator does not fit: `+` works on two ints or two strings. Hindley-Milner has no type for "int or str", so Comet uses a rule of its own: `+` unifies its two operands, and if, at the end of the enclosing function, their type is still unknown, it becomes `int`. Haskell resolves such cases by a similar [[default|overloading]]; OCaml avoids them by using a different operator, `^`, for strings.

### Polymorphism: generalize, then instantiate

Solving equations is not enough for this program:

```text
fn id(x) { return x; }
print id(1);
print id(true);
```

`id` has type fn(t1) -> t1. If that t1 were one unknown shared by the whole program, `id(1)` would fix it to `int`, and `id(true)` would fail. Instead, when the inferencer finishes a `fn` declaration, it **generalizes**: every type variable that nothing else in scope mentions becomes a parameter of the type. The result is a **type scheme**, written ∀a. (a) -> a, "for all a". Each **use** of the name then **instantiates** the scheme with fresh variables, so `id(1)` works on (t5) -> t5 and `id(true)` on (t6) -> t6, independently.

The side condition "that nothing else in scope mentions" matters. In

```text
fn keep(v) {
    fn get() { return v; }
    return get;
}
```

`get` has type () -> t1, where t1 is v's type. t1 also appears in the scope, as the type of `v`, so it must **not** be generalized: `get` returns v's type, not anything at all. The correct type of `keep` is `('a) -> () -> 'a`. Generalizing t1 anyway would claim `get` returns every type, and a program could add its result to 1 and to `"s"`, which the practice problems will show going wrong.

### Where Comet does not generalize

- **Variables declared with `let` stay monomorphic.** In `let g = id;`, g gets one instance of id's type, fixed by its first use. This is ML's [[value restriction|value-restriction]], and Comet needs it because variables can be assigned. If g were ∀a. (a) -> a, then `g = inc;` (inc takes an int) would fit one instance, and `g(true)` another, and the program would add 1 to `true` at run time. For the same reason, assigning to a polymorphic function's name is an error.
- **A function is monomorphic inside its own body.** While `fn f` is being inferred, f has its not-yet-generalized type, so recursive calls must all use it at the same type. Allowing [[polymorphic recursion|polyrec]] makes inference undecidable.

### Why it is correct

Two facts carry the proof, both about unification.

**Unification terminates.** Each binding removes one variable for good: it is replaced everywhere and never bound again. Each decomposition of function types replaces one equation by several strictly smaller ones. Order the pair (number of unbound variables, total size of the remaining equations) lexicographically: every step makes it smaller, and such pairs cannot decrease forever.

**Unification finds a most general unifier when one exists.** Every step keeps the set of unifiers the same. Decomposing fn(A) -> B = fn(C) -> D into A = C and B = D does, since two function types are equal exactly when their parts are. Binding α := T, when α does not occur in T, does too: every unifier must map α to the same type as T, so substituting T for α everywhere changes no solution. And the steps that fail do so only when no unifier exists: `int` never equals `bool`, and α never equals a larger type containing α. When the equations are all solved, the bindings made are exactly the ones every unifier is forced to agree with, and nothing more, so they form a most general unifier.

From these, Damas and Milner proved in 1982 that the whole algorithm, called Algorithm W, is sound with respect to the typing rules and finds the **principal** type of every program that has a type. Sound, as in lesson 9, means an accepted program has no run-time type errors; principal means no type the program could have is lost by choosing too early.

### What it costs

- A step of unification costs time proportional to the sizes of the types involved. With a plain dictionary substitution, long chains of variables bound to variables can make a sequence of unifications quadratic. Representing the classes of equal variables with **union-find**, from DSA I, makes unification nearly linear: O(n α(n)). Practice problem 6 measures the difference.
- Over a whole program, Hindley-Milner runs in close to linear time on real code. Its worst case is exponential: nested `let` declarations can double the size of a type at each level, a result of [[Mairson and Kanellakis|exponential]] from 1990. That case never shows up in practice.
- Space: the substitution holds one entry per bound variable, plus the schemes in scope.

### Where it is used

- ML, OCaml, Haskell, F# and Elm infer the types of entire programs with Hindley-Milner, extended with records, type classes or modules.
- Rust, Swift, Kotlin, Scala and TypeScript infer the types of local variables and closures with the same unification idea, but ask for annotations on function signatures, trading completeness for clearer error messages.
- C++'s `auto` and Java's `var` take the type from the right-hand side only, which is not Hindley-Milner: there are no type variables and nothing flows backwards.
- The same unification algorithm is the engine of Prolog and of automated theorem provers.

**Watch out:**

- Leaving out the occurs check. `x(x)` is then accepted, and resolving the type loops.
- Comparing types without first resolving bound variables. t1 bound to `int` and `int` itself are the same type, but not equal as objects.
- Generalizing type variables that are still free in the scope. It produces types that promise too much, and the checker stops being sound.
- Instantiating a monomorphic variable with fresh type variables, or forgetting to instantiate a polymorphic one: both break the rules above.
- Treating `void` as an ordinary type. Comet has no value of type `void`, but a type variable can later turn out to be `void`: `fn show(h) { print h(); }` passes, and calling `show` with a function that returns nothing then prints nothing at run time. ML avoids the problem by making "nothing" a real value, called unit, that can be printed and stored.

::: context robinson Unification's origin
John Alan Robinson introduced unification in 1965 in his paper on the resolution principle, as the step that matches two logical formulas with variables. It made automated theorem proving practical and became the core of the Prolog language in 1972. Roger Hindley in 1969 and Robin Milner in 1978 independently used it to find the principal types of programs, which is why the method carries both their names.
:::

::: context overloading Overloaded operators and inference
An overloaded operator, like Comet's `+` on ints and strings, has no single most general type in plain Hindley-Milner. Haskell solves it with type classes: `+` has type `Num a => a -> a -> a`, meaning "for every a that is a number", and a defaulting rule picks a type when nothing else decides. OCaml avoids the question with separate operators: `+` for ints, `+.` for floats and `^` for strings.
:::

::: context value-restriction The value restriction
Early ML generalized every `let`, and in 1990 it was found unsound with mutable references: a reference to an empty list could be generalized to "a list of anything", then filled with an int and read back as a string. Standard ML fixed it in 1997 with Andrew Wright's value restriction: only a `let` whose right side is a syntactic value, such as a function, is generalized. OCaml uses a relaxed version of the same rule.
:::

::: context polyrec Polymorphic recursion
Polymorphic recursion means a function calling itself at a different type than the one it was called at. It is useful for some nested data types. With it, type inference becomes undecidable, which Fritz Henglein and, independently, Kfoury, Tiuryn and Urzyczyn proved in 1993. Haskell allows polymorphic recursion only when the function has a written type signature, so the inferencer never has to guess.
:::

::: context exponential The exponential worst case
In 1990 Harry Mairson, and Kanellakis and Mitchell, showed that deciding whether an ML program has a type is complete for deterministic exponential time. The bad programs nest `let` declarations so that each one pairs the previous function with itself, doubling its type's size. Real programs never do that, and ML compilers handle millions of lines comfortably.
:::
--- task
The starter gives the lexer and parser and a Hindley-Milner inferencer for Comet, with everything except four methods. Types are frozen dataclasses: `TVar(name)`, `TCon(name)` for `int`, `bool`, `str` and `void` (the constants `INT`, `BOOL`, `STR`, `VOID`), and `TFun(params, ret)` with a tuple of parameter types. A `Scheme(vars, type)` is a type with the tuple `vars` of variable names it is general over. The `Inferencer` keeps the substitution in `self.subst`, a dictionary from variable name to type, and gives `fresh()`, `resolve(t)` (applies the substitution all the way down), `env_vars()` (the set of variable names free in the current scopes), and the module-level `type_vars(t)` (the variable names in t, in order of first appearance). `infer_source(source)` returns a dictionary from each top-level name to its type as text, and `type_error(source)` returns the error message or `None`. Write:

- `occurs(name, t)`: whether the variable called `name` appears in t, after resolving.
- `unify(a, b)`: make a and b equal by extending `self.subst`, following the lesson's four rules, with the occurs check. Raise `TypeCheckError` when they cannot be made equal.
- `generalize(t)`: resolve t and return a `Scheme` over every variable in it that is not in `self.env_vars()`, in order of first appearance.
- `instantiate(scheme)`: resolve the scheme's type and return a copy in which each of the scheme's `vars` is replaced by a fresh variable. Other variables stay as they are.

For example, `infer_source("fn apply(f, x) { return f(x); }")` is `{"apply": "(('a) -> 'b, 'a) -> 'b"}`.
--- starter
from dataclasses import dataclass

KEYWORDS = {"let", "fn", "return", "if", "else", "while", "print",
            "true", "false", "and", "or", "not"}
TWO_CHAR = {"==", "!=", "<=", ">=", "->"}
ONE_CHAR = set("+-*/%<>=(){},;:")
ESCAPES = {'"': '"', "\\": "\\", "n": "\n"}
DIGITS = "0123456789"
LETTERS = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ_"


@dataclass
class Token:
    kind: str
    text: str
    line: int
    col: int


class LexError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


def tokenize(source):
    tokens = []
    i = 0
    line = 1
    col = 1
    n = len(source)

    def advance(count):
        nonlocal i, line, col
        for _ in range(count):
            if source[i] == "\n":
                line += 1
                col = 1
            else:
                col += 1
            i += 1

    while i < n:
        ch = source[i]
        start_line, start_col = line, col
        if ch in " \t\r\n":
            advance(1)
        elif ch == "#":
            while i < n and source[i] != "\n":
                advance(1)
        elif ch in DIGITS:
            j = i
            while j < n and source[j] in DIGITS:
                j += 1
            tokens.append(Token("NUMBER", source[i:j], start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch in LETTERS:
            j = i
            while j < n and (source[j] in LETTERS or source[j] in DIGITS):
                j += 1
            word = source[i:j]
            kind = "KEYWORD" if word in KEYWORDS else "IDENT"
            tokens.append(Token(kind, word, start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch == '"':
            advance(1)
            chars = []
            while True:
                if i >= n or source[i] == "\n":
                    raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                c = source[i]
                if c == '"':
                    advance(1)
                    break
                if c == "\\":
                    if i + 1 >= n or source[i + 1] == "\n":
                        raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                    if source[i + 1] not in ESCAPES:
                        raise LexError("unknown escape", line, col)
                    chars.append(ESCAPES[source[i + 1]])
                    advance(2)
                else:
                    chars.append(c)
                    advance(1)
            tokens.append(Token("STRING", "".join(chars), start_line, start_col))
        elif source[i:i + 2] in TWO_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", source[i:i + 2], start_line, start_col))
            advance(2)
        elif ch in ONE_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", ch, start_line, start_col))
            advance(1)
        else:
            raise LexError(f"unexpected character {ch!r}", start_line, start_col)
    tokens.append(Token("EOF", "", line, col))
    return tokens
