class ParseError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


COMPARE = ("==", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">=")
TYPES = ("int", "bool", "str")


class Parser:
    def __init__(self, tokens):
        self.tokens = tokens
        self.pos = 0

    def peek(self, ahead=0):
        return self.tokens[min(self.pos + ahead, len(self.tokens) - 1)]

    def at(self, *texts):
        tok = self.peek()
        return tok.kind in ("OP", "KEYWORD") and tok.text in texts

    def advance(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "EOF":
            self.pos += 1
        return tok

    def error(self, message):
        tok = self.peek()
        return ParseError(message, tok.line, tok.col)

    def expect(self, text):
        if not self.at(text):
            raise self.error(f"expected '{text}'")
        return self.advance()

    def expr(self):
        return self.or_expr()

    def or_expr(self):
        left = self.and_expr()
        while self.at("or"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.and_expr())
        return left

    def and_expr(self):
        left = self.not_expr()
        while self.at("and"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.not_expr())
        return left

    def not_expr(self):
        if self.at("not"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("not", self.not_expr())
        return self.compare()

    def compare(self):
        left = self.sum()
        if self.at(*COMPARE):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.sum())
            if self.at(*COMPARE):
                raise self.error("comparisons cannot be chained")
        return left

    def sum(self):
        left = self.product()
        while self.at("+", "-"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.product())
        return left

    def product(self):
        left = self.unary()
        while self.at("*", "/", "%"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.unary())
        return left

    def unary(self):
        if self.at("-"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("-", self.unary())
        return self.call()

    def call(self):
        expr = self.primary()
        while self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            args = []
            if not self.at(")"):
                args.append(self.expr())
                while self.at(","):
                    self.advance()
                    args.append(self.expr())
            self.expect(")")
            expr = Call(expr, args)
        return expr

    def primary(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind == "NUMBER":
            self.advance()
            return Num(int(tok.text))
        if tok.kind == "STRING":
            self.advance()
            return Str(tok.text)
        if tok.kind == "IDENT":
            self.advance()
            return Var(tok.text)
        if self.at("true", "false"):
            self.advance()
            return Bool(tok.text == "true")
        if self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            inner = self.expr()
            self.expect(")")
            return inner
        raise self.error("expected an expression")

    def program(self):
        stmts = []
        while self.peek().kind != "EOF":
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        return Program(stmts)

    def statement(self):
        if self.at("let"):
            return self.let_stmt()
        if self.at("print"):
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Print(value)
        if self.at("if"):
            return self.if_stmt()
        if self.at("while"):
            self.advance()
            cond = self.expr()
            return While(cond, self.block())
        if self.at("fn"):
            return self.fn_stmt()
        if self.at("return"):
            self.advance()
            value = None if self.at(";") else self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Return(value)
        nxt = self.peek(1)
        if self.peek().kind == "IDENT" and nxt.kind == "OP" and nxt.text == "=":
            name = self.advance().text
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Assign(name, value)
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return ExprStmt(value)

    def name(self):
        if self.peek().kind != "IDENT":
            raise self.error("expected a name")
        return self.advance().text

    def type_name(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "IDENT" or tok.text not in TYPES:
            raise self.error("expected a type")
        return self.advance().text

    def let_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        self.expect("=")
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return Let(name, type_, value)

    def if_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        cond = self.expr()
        then = self.block()
        else_ = None
        if self.at("else"):
            self.advance()
            else_ = self.if_stmt() if self.at("if") else self.block()
        return If(cond, then, else_)

    def block(self):
        self.expect("{")
        stmts = []
        while not self.at("}"):
            if self.peek().kind == "EOF":
                raise self.error("expected '}'")
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        self.advance()
        return Block(stmts)

    def param(self):
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        return (name, type_)

    def fn_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        self.expect("(")
        params = []
        if not self.at(")"):
            params.append(self.param())
            while self.at(","):
                self.advance()
                params.append(self.param())
        self.expect(")")
        ret = None
        if self.at("->"):
            self.advance()
            ret = self.type_name()
        return Fn(name, params, ret, self.block())


def parse_program(tokens):
    return Parser(tokens).program()


class CometError(Exception):
    pass


def comet_div(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q


def comet_mod(a, b):
    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TVar:
    name: str


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TCon:
    name: str


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TFun:
    params: tuple
    ret: object


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Scheme:
    vars: tuple
    type: object


INT, BOOL, STR, VOID = TCon("int"), TCon("bool"), TCon("str"), TCon("void")


class TypeCheckError(Exception):
    pass


def type_vars(t, found=None):
    """The names of the type variables in t, in order of first appearance."""
    if found is None:
        found = []
    if isinstance(t, TVar):
        if t.name not in found:
            found.append(t.name)
    elif isinstance(t, TFun):
        for p in t.params:
            type_vars(p, found)
        type_vars(t.ret, found)

    return found


def show_type(t, names=None):
    if names is None:
        names = {v: "'" + chr(ord("a") + i) for i, v in enumerate(type_vars(t))}
    if isinstance(t, TVar):
        return names.get(t.name, t.name)
    if isinstance(t, TFun):
        params = ", ".join(show_type(p, names) for p in t.params)
        return f"({params}) -> {show_type(t.ret, names)}"

    return t.name


def always_returns(stmts):
    for stmt in stmts:
        if isinstance(stmt, Return):
            return True
        if isinstance(stmt, Block) and always_returns(stmt.stmts):
            return True
        if isinstance(stmt, If) and stmt.else_ is not None:
            if always_returns([stmt.then]) and always_returns([stmt.else_]):
                return True
    return False


class Inferencer:
    def __init__(self):
        self.subst = {}
        self.count = 0
        self.scopes = [{}]
        self.returns = []
        self.pending = []


    def fresh(self):
        self.count += 1
        return TVar(f"t{self.count}")

    def resolve(self, t):
        """t with every bound type variable replaced by what it is bound to, all the way down."""
        if isinstance(t, TVar):
            if t.name in self.subst:
                return self.resolve(self.subst[t.name])
            return t
        if isinstance(t, TFun):
            return TFun(tuple(self.resolve(p) for p in t.params), self.resolve(t.ret))

        return t

    def env_vars(self):
        """The type variables that are free somewhere in the current scopes."""
        found = set()
        for scope in self.scopes:
            for scheme in scope.values():
                found.update(v for v in type_vars(self.resolve(scheme.type)) if v not in scheme.vars)
        return found

    def occurs(self, name, t):
        raise TypeCheckError("occurs is not written yet")

    def unify(self, a, b):
        raise TypeCheckError("unify is not written yet")

    def generalize(self, t):
        raise TypeCheckError("generalize is not written yet")

    def instantiate(self, scheme):
        raise TypeCheckError("instantiate is not written yet")

    # ---- the walk over the program, given ----

    def declare(self, name, scheme):
        if name in self.scopes[-1]:
            raise TypeCheckError(f"{name} is already declared in this scope")
        self.scopes[-1][name] = scheme

    def lookup(self, name):
        for scope in reversed(self.scopes):
            if name in scope:
                return scope[name]
        raise TypeCheckError(f"undefined variable {name}")

    def infer_program(self, program):
        for stmt in program.stmts:
            self.infer_stmt(stmt)
        self.settle_plus()

    def settle_plus(self):
        """Each '+' whose operand type is still unknown adds ints, like a default."""
        for t in self.pending:
            if isinstance(self.resolve(t), TVar):
                self.unify(t, INT)
        self.pending = []

    def infer_block(self, stmts):
        self.scopes.append({})
        try:
            for stmt in stmts:
                self.infer_stmt(stmt)
        finally:
            self.scopes.pop()

    def value(self, expr):
        t = self.infer_expr(expr)
        if self.resolve(t) == VOID:
            raise TypeCheckError("a call that returns nothing has no value")
        return t

    def infer_stmt(self, stmt):
        if isinstance(stmt, Let):
            t = self.value(stmt.expr)
            if stmt.type is not None:
                self.unify(t, TCon(stmt.type))
            self.declare(stmt.name, Scheme((), t))
        elif isinstance(stmt, Assign):
            scheme = self.lookup(stmt.name)
            if scheme.vars:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"cannot assign to the polymorphic function {stmt.name}")
            self.unify(scheme.type, self.value(stmt.expr))
        elif isinstance(stmt, Print):
            self.value(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, ExprStmt):
            self.infer_expr(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, If):
            self.unify(self.infer_expr(stmt.cond), BOOL)
            self.infer_stmt(stmt.then)
            if stmt.else_ is not None:
                self.infer_stmt(stmt.else_)
        elif isinstance(stmt, While):
            self.unify(self.infer_expr(stmt.cond), BOOL)
            self.infer_stmt(stmt.body)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Block):
            self.infer_block(stmt.stmts)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Return):
            if not self.returns:
                raise TypeCheckError("return outside a function")
            t = VOID if stmt.expr is None else self.value(stmt.expr)
            self.unify(t, self.returns[-1])
        elif isinstance(stmt, Fn):
            self.infer_fn(stmt)

    def infer_fn(self, stmt):
        params = [TCon(t) if t is not None else self.fresh() for _, t in stmt.params]
        ret = TCon(stmt.ret) if stmt.ret is not None else self.fresh()
        fn_type = TFun(tuple(params), ret)
        self.declare(stmt.name, Scheme((), fn_type))
        self.scopes.append({})
        self.returns.append(ret)
        try:
            for (name, _), t in zip(stmt.params, params):
                self.declare(name, Scheme((), t))
            for inner in stmt.body.stmts:
                self.infer_stmt(inner)
        finally:
            self.returns.pop()
            self.scopes.pop()
        if not always_returns(stmt.body.stmts):
            self.unify(ret, VOID)
        self.settle_plus()
        del self.scopes[-1][stmt.name]
        self.scopes[-1][stmt.name] = self.generalize(fn_type)

    def infer_expr(self, expr):
        if isinstance(expr, Num):
            return INT
        if isinstance(expr, Str):
            return STR
        if isinstance(expr, Bool):
            return BOOL
        if isinstance(expr, Var):
            return self.instantiate(self.lookup(expr.name))
        if isinstance(expr, Unary):
            wanted = INT if expr.op == "-" else BOOL
            self.unify(self.infer_expr(expr.expr), wanted)
            return wanted
        if isinstance(expr, Binary):
            return self.infer_binary(expr)
        if isinstance(expr, Call):
            callee = self.infer_expr(expr.callee)
            args = tuple(self.value(arg) for arg in expr.args)
            result = self.fresh()
            self.unify(callee, TFun(args, result))
            return result
        raise TypeCheckError(f"unknown expression {type(expr).__name__}")

    def infer_binary(self, expr):
        op = expr.op
        left = self.value(expr.left)
        right = self.value(expr.right)
        if op in ("and", "or"):
            self.unify(left, BOOL)
            self.unify(right, BOOL)
            return BOOL
        if op in ("==", "!="):
            self.unify(left, right)
            return BOOL
        if op == "+":
            self.unify(left, right)
            t = self.resolve(left)
            if isinstance(t, TVar):
                self.pending.append(t)
            elif t not in (INT, STR):
                raise TypeCheckError(f"'+' needs two ints or two strs, not {show_type(t)}")
            return t
        self.unify(left, INT)
        self.unify(right, INT)
        return BOOL if op in ("<", "<=", ">", ">=") else INT


def infer_source(source):
    """The inferred type of every top-level name, as text."""
    inf = Inferencer()
    inf.infer_program(parse_program(tokenize(source)))
    return {name: show_type(inf.resolve(s.type)) for name, s in inf.scopes[-1].items()}


def type_error(source):
    try:
        infer_source(source)
    except TypeCheckError as e:
        return str(e)
    return None

from dataclasses import dataclass

KEYWORDS = {"let", "fn", "return", "if", "else", "while", "print",
            "true", "false", "and", "or", "not"}
TWO_CHAR = {"==", "!=", "<=", ">=", "->"}
ONE_CHAR = set("+-*/%<>=(){},;:")
ESCAPES = {'"': '"', "\\": "\\", "n": "\n"}
DIGITS = "0123456789"
LETTERS = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ_"


@dataclass
class Token:
    kind: str
    text: str
    line: int
    col: int


class LexError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


def tokenize(source):
    tokens = []
    i = 0
    line = 1
    col = 1
    n = len(source)

    def advance(count):
        nonlocal i, line, col
        for _ in range(count):
            if source[i] == "\n":
                line += 1
                col = 1
            else:
                col += 1
            i += 1

    while i < n:
        ch = source[i]
        start_line, start_col = line, col
        if ch in " \t\r\n":
            advance(1)
        elif ch == "#":
            while i < n and source[i] != "\n":
                advance(1)
        elif ch in DIGITS:
            j = i
            while j < n and source[j] in DIGITS:
                j += 1
            tokens.append(Token("NUMBER", source[i:j], start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch in LETTERS:
            j = i
            while j < n and (source[j] in LETTERS or source[j] in DIGITS):
                j += 1
            word = source[i:j]
            kind = "KEYWORD" if word in KEYWORDS else "IDENT"
            tokens.append(Token(kind, word, start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch == '"':
            advance(1)
            chars = []
            while True:
                if i >= n or source[i] == "\n":
                    raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                c = source[i]
                if c == '"':
                    advance(1)
                    break
                if c == "\\":
                    if i + 1 >= n or source[i + 1] == "\n":
                        raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                    if source[i + 1] not in ESCAPES:
                        raise LexError("unknown escape", line, col)
                    chars.append(ESCAPES[source[i + 1]])
                    advance(2)
                else:
                    chars.append(c)
                    advance(1)
            tokens.append(Token("STRING", "".join(chars), start_line, start_col))
        elif source[i:i + 2] in TWO_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", source[i:i + 2], start_line, start_col))
            advance(2)
        elif ch in ONE_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", ch, start_line, start_col))
            advance(1)
        else:
            raise LexError(f"unexpected character {ch!r}", start_line, start_col)
    tokens.append(Token("EOF", "", line, col))
    return tokens

class ParseError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


COMPARE = ("==", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">=")
TYPES = ("int", "bool", "str")


class Parser:
    def __init__(self, tokens):
        self.tokens = tokens
        self.pos = 0

    def peek(self, ahead=0):
        return self.tokens[min(self.pos + ahead, len(self.tokens) - 1)]

    def at(self, *texts):
        tok = self.peek()
        return tok.kind in ("OP", "KEYWORD") and tok.text in texts

    def advance(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "EOF":
            self.pos += 1
        return tok

    def error(self, message):
        tok = self.peek()
        return ParseError(message, tok.line, tok.col)

    def expect(self, text):
        if not self.at(text):
            raise self.error(f"expected '{text}'")
        return self.advance()

    def expr(self):
        return self.or_expr()

    def or_expr(self):
        left = self.and_expr()
        while self.at("or"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.and_expr())
        return left

    def and_expr(self):
        left = self.not_expr()
        while self.at("and"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.not_expr())
        return left

    def not_expr(self):
        if self.at("not"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("not", self.not_expr())
        return self.compare()

    def compare(self):
        left = self.sum()
        if self.at(*COMPARE):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.sum())
            if self.at(*COMPARE):
                raise self.error("comparisons cannot be chained")
        return left

    def sum(self):
        left = self.product()
        while self.at("+", "-"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.product())
        return left

    def product(self):
        left = self.unary()
        while self.at("*", "/", "%"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.unary())
        return left

    def unary(self):
        if self.at("-"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("-", self.unary())
        return self.call()

    def call(self):
        expr = self.primary()
        while self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            args = []
            if not self.at(")"):
                args.append(self.expr())
                while self.at(","):
                    self.advance()
                    args.append(self.expr())
            self.expect(")")
            expr = Call(expr, args)
        return expr

    def primary(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind == "NUMBER":
            self.advance()
            return Num(int(tok.text))
        if tok.kind == "STRING":
            self.advance()
            return Str(tok.text)
        if tok.kind == "IDENT":
            self.advance()
            return Var(tok.text)
        if self.at("true", "false"):
            self.advance()
            return Bool(tok.text == "true")
        if self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            inner = self.expr()
            self.expect(")")
            return inner
        raise self.error("expected an expression")

    def program(self):
        stmts = []
        while self.peek().kind != "EOF":
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        return Program(stmts)

    def statement(self):
        if self.at("let"):
            return self.let_stmt()
        if self.at("print"):
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Print(value)
        if self.at("if"):
            return self.if_stmt()
        if self.at("while"):
            self.advance()
            cond = self.expr()
            return While(cond, self.block())
        if self.at("fn"):
            return self.fn_stmt()
        if self.at("return"):
            self.advance()
            value = None if self.at(";") else self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Return(value)
        nxt = self.peek(1)
        if self.peek().kind == "IDENT" and nxt.kind == "OP" and nxt.text == "=":
            name = self.advance().text
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Assign(name, value)
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return ExprStmt(value)

    def name(self):
        if self.peek().kind != "IDENT":
            raise self.error("expected a name")
        return self.advance().text

    def type_name(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "IDENT" or tok.text not in TYPES:
            raise self.error("expected a type")
        return self.advance().text

    def let_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        self.expect("=")
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return Let(name, type_, value)

    def if_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        cond = self.expr()
        then = self.block()
        else_ = None
        if self.at("else"):
            self.advance()
            else_ = self.if_stmt() if self.at("if") else self.block()
        return If(cond, then, else_)

    def block(self):
        self.expect("{")
        stmts = []
        while not self.at("}"):
            if self.peek().kind == "EOF":
                raise self.error("expected '}'")
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        self.advance()
        return Block(stmts)

    def param(self):
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        return (name, type_)

    def fn_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        self.expect("(")
        params = []
        if not self.at(")"):
            params.append(self.param())
            while self.at(","):
                self.advance()
                params.append(self.param())
        self.expect(")")
        ret = None
        if self.at("->"):
            self.advance()
            ret = self.type_name()
        return Fn(name, params, ret, self.block())


def parse_program(tokens):
    return Parser(tokens).program()

    if b == 0:

    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q


def comet_mod(a, b):
    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)

class Inferencer:
    def __init__(self):
        self.subst = {}
        self.count = 0
        self.scopes = [{}]
        self.returns = []
        self.pending = []


    def fresh(self):
        self.count += 1
        return TVar(f"t{self.count}")

    def resolve(self, t):
        """t with every bound type variable replaced by what it is bound to, all the way down."""
        if isinstance(t, TVar):
            if t.name in self.subst:
                return self.resolve(self.subst[t.name])
            return t
        if isinstance(t, TFun):
            return TFun(tuple(self.resolve(p) for p in t.params), self.resolve(t.ret))

        return t

    def env_vars(self):
        """The type variables that are free somewhere in the current scopes."""
        found = set()
        for scope in self.scopes:
            for scheme in scope.values():
                found.update(v for v in type_vars(self.resolve(scheme.type)) if v not in scheme.vars)
        return found

    def occurs(self, name, t):
        return name in type_vars(self.resolve(t))

    def unify(self, a, b):
        a = self.resolve(a)
        b = self.resolve(b)
        if a == b:
            return
        if isinstance(a, TVar):
            if self.occurs(a.name, b):
                raise TypeCheckError(f"infinite type: {show_type(a)} would contain itself")
            self.subst[a.name] = b
            return
        if isinstance(b, TVar):
            self.unify(b, a)
            return
        if isinstance(a, TFun) and isinstance(b, TFun):
            if len(a.params) != len(b.params):
                raise TypeCheckError(f"a function of {len(a.params)} arguments is not one of {len(b.params)}")
            for p, q in zip(a.params, b.params):
                self.unify(p, q)
            self.unify(a.ret, b.ret)
            return
        raise TypeCheckError(f"type mismatch: {show_type(a)} and {show_type(b)}")

    def generalize(self, t):
        t = self.resolve(t)
        env = self.env_vars()
        return Scheme(tuple(v for v in type_vars(t) if v not in env), t)

    def instantiate(self, scheme):
        mapping = {v: self.fresh() for v in scheme.vars}
        return self.replace(self.resolve(scheme.type), mapping)

    def replace(self, t, mapping):
        if isinstance(t, TVar):
            return mapping.get(t.name, t)
        if isinstance(t, TFun):
            return TFun(tuple(self.replace(p, mapping) for p in t.params), self.replace(t.ret, mapping))
        return t

    # ---- the walk over the program, given ----

    def declare(self, name, scheme):
        if name in self.scopes[-1]:
            raise TypeCheckError(f"{name} is already declared in this scope")
        self.scopes[-1][name] = scheme

    def lookup(self, name):
        for scope in reversed(self.scopes):
            if name in scope:
                return scope[name]
        raise TypeCheckError(f"undefined variable {name}")

    def infer_program(self, program):
        for stmt in program.stmts:
            self.infer_stmt(stmt)
        self.settle_plus()

    def settle_plus(self):
        """Each '+' whose operand type is still unknown adds ints, like a default."""
        for t in self.pending:
            if isinstance(self.resolve(t), TVar):
                self.unify(t, INT)
        self.pending = []

    def infer_block(self, stmts):
        self.scopes.append({})
        try:
            for stmt in stmts:
                self.infer_stmt(stmt)
        finally:
            self.scopes.pop()

    def value(self, expr):
        t = self.infer_expr(expr)
        if self.resolve(t) == VOID:
            raise TypeCheckError("a call that returns nothing has no value")
        return t

    def infer_stmt(self, stmt):
        if isinstance(stmt, Let):
            t = self.value(stmt.expr)
            if stmt.type is not None:
                self.unify(t, TCon(stmt.type))
            self.declare(stmt.name, Scheme((), t))
        elif isinstance(stmt, Assign):
            scheme = self.lookup(stmt.name)
            if scheme.vars:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"cannot assign to the polymorphic function {stmt.name}")
            self.unify(scheme.type, self.value(stmt.expr))
        elif isinstance(stmt, Print):
            self.value(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, ExprStmt):
            self.infer_expr(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, If):
            self.unify(self.infer_expr(stmt.cond), BOOL)
            self.infer_stmt(stmt.then)
            if stmt.else_ is not None:
                self.infer_stmt(stmt.else_)
        elif isinstance(stmt, While):
            self.unify(self.infer_expr(stmt.cond), BOOL)
            self.infer_stmt(stmt.body)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Block):
            self.infer_block(stmt.stmts)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Return):
            if not self.returns:
                raise TypeCheckError("return outside a function")
            t = VOID if stmt.expr is None else self.value(stmt.expr)
            self.unify(t, self.returns[-1])
        elif isinstance(stmt, Fn):
            self.infer_fn(stmt)

    def infer_fn(self, stmt):
        params = [TCon(t) if t is not None else self.fresh() for _, t in stmt.params]
        ret = TCon(stmt.ret) if stmt.ret is not None else self.fresh()
        fn_type = TFun(tuple(params), ret)
        self.declare(stmt.name, Scheme((), fn_type))
        self.scopes.append({})
        self.returns.append(ret)
        try:
            for (name, _), t in zip(stmt.params, params):
                self.declare(name, Scheme((), t))
            for inner in stmt.body.stmts:
                self.infer_stmt(inner)
        finally:
            self.returns.pop()
            self.scopes.pop()
        if not always_returns(stmt.body.stmts):
            self.unify(ret, VOID)
        self.settle_plus()
        del self.scopes[-1][stmt.name]
        self.scopes[-1][stmt.name] = self.generalize(fn_type)

    def infer_expr(self, expr):
        if isinstance(expr, Num):
            return INT
        if isinstance(expr, Str):
            return STR
        if isinstance(expr, Bool):
            return BOOL
        if isinstance(expr, Var):
            return self.instantiate(self.lookup(expr.name))
        if isinstance(expr, Unary):
            wanted = INT if expr.op == "-" else BOOL
            self.unify(self.infer_expr(expr.expr), wanted)
            return wanted
        if isinstance(expr, Binary):
            return self.infer_binary(expr)
        if isinstance(expr, Call):
            callee = self.infer_expr(expr.callee)
            args = tuple(self.value(arg) for arg in expr.args)
            result = self.fresh()
            self.unify(callee, TFun(args, result))
            return result
        raise TypeCheckError(f"unknown expression {type(expr).__name__}")

    def infer_binary(self, expr):
        op = expr.op
        left = self.value(expr.left)
        right = self.value(expr.right)
        if op in ("and", "or"):
            self.unify(left, BOOL)
            self.unify(right, BOOL)
            return BOOL
        if op in ("==", "!="):
            self.unify(left, right)
            return BOOL
        if op == "+":
            self.unify(left, right)
            t = self.resolve(left)
            if isinstance(t, TVar):
                self.pending.append(t)
            elif t not in (INT, STR):
                raise TypeCheckError(f"'+' needs two ints or two strs, not {show_type(t)}")
            return t
        self.unify(left, INT)
        self.unify(right, INT)
        return BOOL if op in ("<", "<=", ">", ">=") else INT


def infer_source(source):
    """The inferred type of every top-level name, as text."""
    inf = Inferencer()
    inf.infer_program(parse_program(tokenize(source)))
    return {name: show_type(inf.resolve(s.type)) for name, s in inf.scopes[-1].items()}


def type_error(source):
    try:
        infer_source(source)
    except TypeCheckError as e:
        return str(e)
    return None
--- hint
`occurs` is one line with `type_vars` and `self.resolve`. In `unify`, resolve both sides first and return at once if they are equal. Then handle a `TVar` on the left, a `TVar` on the right (swap and call again), two `TFun`s, and raise for everything else.
--- hint
Binding a variable is `self.subst[a.name] = b`, but only after `self.occurs(a.name, b)` is false. For two functions, compare the numbers of parameters, then unify each pair of parameters and the two return types.
--- hint
`generalize`: `t = self.resolve(t)`, then keep the names from `type_vars(t)` that are not in `self.env_vars()`. `instantiate`: build a dictionary from each of `scheme.vars` to `self.fresh()`, then rebuild the resolved type with a small recursive helper that swaps those variables and copies everything else.

+++ practice | The most general unifier
--- task
Unification works on any representation of types. Here types are plain Python values: `"int"`, `"bool"`, `"str"` and `"void"` are constants; a string that starts with a quote, such as `"'a"`, is a type variable; and a function type is a tuple `("fn", params, ret)`, where `params` is a tuple of types. So `('a) -> int` is `("fn", ("'a",), "int")`.

Write `mgu(a, b)`: the most general unifier of the two types, as a dictionary from each variable that had to be bound to its type with every bound variable inside it replaced (fully resolved). Return `None` if the types cannot be unified, including when the occurs check fails. Two equal types give `{}`.

For example, `mgu(("fn", ("'a", "int"), "'b"), ("fn", ("bool", "'c"), "'a"))` is `{"'a": "bool", "'c": "int", "'b": "bool"}`.
--- starter
def mgu(a, b):
    raise NotImplementedError("mgu is not written yet")
--- solution
def is_var(t):
    return isinstance(t, str) and t.startswith("'")


def walk(t, subst):
    while is_var(t) and t in subst:
        t = subst[t]
    return t


def resolve(t, subst):
    t = walk(t, subst)
    if isinstance(t, tuple):
        return ("fn", tuple(resolve(p, subst) for p in t[1]), resolve(t[2], subst))
    return t


def occurs(v, t, subst):
    t = walk(t, subst)
    if t == v:
        return True
    if isinstance(t, tuple):
        return any(occurs(v, p, subst) for p in t[1]) or occurs(v, t[2], subst)
    return False


def unify(a, b, subst):
    a = walk(a, subst)
    b = walk(b, subst)
    if a == b:
        return True
    if is_var(a):
        if occurs(a, b, subst):
            return False
        subst[a] = b
        return True
    if is_var(b):
        return unify(b, a, subst)
    if isinstance(a, tuple) and isinstance(b, tuple) and len(a[1]) == len(b[1]):
        return all(unify(p, q, subst) for p, q in zip(a[1], b[1])) and unify(a[2], b[2], subst)
    return False


def mgu(a, b):
    subst = {}
    if not unify(a, b, subst):
        return None
    return {v: resolve(t, subst) for v, t in subst.items()}
--- hint
Keep a dictionary `subst`. A helper `walk(t, subst)` follows bindings while t is a bound variable; `unify(a, b, subst)` walks both sides and then applies the lesson's four rules, returning `True` or `False`.
--- hint
The occurs check walks through the other type, looking through bound variables too. At the end, build the answer by resolving each bound variable's type all the way down, replacing bound variables inside function types as well.
--- check case | The example from the task
mgu(("fn", ("'a", "int"), "'b"), ("fn", ("bool", "'c"), "'a"))
=> {"'a": "bool", "'c": "int", "'b": "bool"}
--- check case | A variable against a function type
mgu("'f", ("fn", ("int",), "'r"))
=> {"'f": ("fn", ("int",), "'r")}
--- check case | Bindings are fully resolved
mgu(("fn", ("'a",), "'a"), ("fn", ("'b",), ("fn", (), "'c")))
=> {"'a": ("fn", (), "'c"), "'b": ("fn", (), "'c")}
--- check test | Equal types need nothing
mgu("'a", "'a") == {} and mgu(("fn", ("int",), "str"), ("fn", ("int",), "str")) == {}
--- check test | No unifier
mgu("int", "str") is None and mgu(("fn", ("int",), "int"), ("fn", ("int", "int"), "int")) is None and mgu(("fn", (), "int"), "int") is None
--- check test | The occurs check
mgu("'a", ("fn", ("'a",), "int")) is None and mgu(("fn", ("'a",), "'b"), ("fn", ("'b",), ("fn", ("'a",), "int"))) is None

+++ practice | Signatures for an editor
--- task
Editors for languages with type inference show the inferred types next to the code. Write `signatures(source)`, which infers the types of a program with the lesson's inferencer (given in the starter, finished) and returns one line for each `fn` declaration, in the order they appear in the text (an inner function comes after the function it is in), such as:

```text
fn compose(f: ('a) -> 'b, g: ('c) -> 'a) -> ('c) -> 'b
```

Each line is `fn NAME(PARAM: TYPE, ...) -> TYPE`. The types are the ones known at the **end** of inferring the whole program, and in each line the type variables are named `'a`, `'b`, … in the order they first appear in that line's function type. A function without parameters has `()`. If the program has a type error, raise `TypeCheckError`.
--- starter
from dataclasses import dataclass

KEYWORDS = {"let", "fn", "return", "if", "else", "while", "print",
            "true", "false", "and", "or", "not"}
TWO_CHAR = {"==", "!=", "<=", ">=", "->"}
ONE_CHAR = set("+-*/%<>=(){},;:")
ESCAPES = {'"': '"', "\\": "\\", "n": "\n"}
DIGITS = "0123456789"
LETTERS = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ_"


@dataclass
class Token:
    kind: str
    text: str
    line: int
    col: int


class LexError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


def tokenize(source):
    tokens = []
    i = 0
    line = 1
    col = 1
    n = len(source)

    def advance(count):
        nonlocal i, line, col
        for _ in range(count):
            if source[i] == "\n":
                line += 1
                col = 1
            else:
                col += 1
            i += 1

    while i < n:
        ch = source[i]
        start_line, start_col = line, col
        if ch in " \t\r\n":
            advance(1)
        elif ch == "#":
            while i < n and source[i] != "\n":
                advance(1)
        elif ch in DIGITS:
            j = i
            while j < n and source[j] in DIGITS:
                j += 1
            tokens.append(Token("NUMBER", source[i:j], start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch in LETTERS:
            j = i
            while j < n and (source[j] in LETTERS or source[j] in DIGITS):
                j += 1
            word = source[i:j]
            kind = "KEYWORD" if word in KEYWORDS else "IDENT"
            tokens.append(Token(kind, word, start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch == '"':
            advance(1)
            chars = []
            while True:
                if i >= n or source[i] == "\n":
                    raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                c = source[i]
                if c == '"':
                    advance(1)
                    break
                if c == "\\":
                    if i + 1 >= n or source[i + 1] == "\n":
                        raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                    if source[i + 1] not in ESCAPES:
                        raise LexError("unknown escape", line, col)
                    chars.append(ESCAPES[source[i + 1]])
                    advance(2)
                else:
                    chars.append(c)
                    advance(1)
            tokens.append(Token("STRING", "".join(chars), start_line, start_col))
        elif source[i:i + 2] in TWO_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", source[i:i + 2], start_line, start_col))
            advance(2)
        elif ch in ONE_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", ch, start_line, start_col))
            advance(1)
        else:
            raise LexError(f"unexpected character {ch!r}", start_line, start_col)
    tokens.append(Token("EOF", "", line, col))
    return tokens


@dataclass
class Num:

class ParseError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


COMPARE = ("==", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">=")
TYPES = ("int", "bool", "str")


class Parser:
    def __init__(self, tokens):
        self.tokens = tokens
        self.pos = 0

    def peek(self, ahead=0):
        return self.tokens[min(self.pos + ahead, len(self.tokens) - 1)]

    def at(self, *texts):
        tok = self.peek()
        return tok.kind in ("OP", "KEYWORD") and tok.text in texts

    def advance(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "EOF":
            self.pos += 1
        return tok

    def error(self, message):
        tok = self.peek()
        return ParseError(message, tok.line, tok.col)

    def expect(self, text):
        if not self.at(text):
            raise self.error(f"expected '{text}'")
        return self.advance()

    def expr(self):
        return self.or_expr()

    def or_expr(self):
        left = self.and_expr()
        while self.at("or"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.and_expr())
        return left

    def and_expr(self):
        left = self.not_expr()
        while self.at("and"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.not_expr())
        return left

    def not_expr(self):
        if self.at("not"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("not", self.not_expr())
        return self.compare()

    def compare(self):
        left = self.sum()
        if self.at(*COMPARE):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.sum())
            if self.at(*COMPARE):
                raise self.error("comparisons cannot be chained")
        return left

    def sum(self):
        left = self.product()
        while self.at("+", "-"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.product())
        return left

    def product(self):
        left = self.unary()
        while self.at("*", "/", "%"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.unary())
        return left

    def unary(self):
        if self.at("-"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("-", self.unary())
        return self.call()

    def call(self):
        expr = self.primary()
        while self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            args = []
            if not self.at(")"):
                args.append(self.expr())
                while self.at(","):
                    self.advance()
                    args.append(self.expr())
            self.expect(")")
            expr = Call(expr, args)
        return expr

    def primary(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind == "NUMBER":
            self.advance()
            return Num(int(tok.text))
        if tok.kind == "STRING":
            self.advance()
            return Str(tok.text)
        if tok.kind == "IDENT":
            self.advance()
            return Var(tok.text)
        if self.at("true", "false"):
            self.advance()
            return Bool(tok.text == "true")
        if self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            inner = self.expr()
            self.expect(")")
            return inner
        raise self.error("expected an expression")

    def program(self):
        stmts = []
        while self.peek().kind != "EOF":
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        return Program(stmts)

    def statement(self):
        if self.at("let"):
            return self.let_stmt()
        if self.at("print"):
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Print(value)
        if self.at("if"):
            return self.if_stmt()
        if self.at("while"):
            self.advance()
            cond = self.expr()
            return While(cond, self.block())
        if self.at("fn"):
            return self.fn_stmt()
        if self.at("return"):
            self.advance()
            value = None if self.at(";") else self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Return(value)
        nxt = self.peek(1)
        if self.peek().kind == "IDENT" and nxt.kind == "OP" and nxt.text == "=":
            name = self.advance().text
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Assign(name, value)
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return ExprStmt(value)

    def name(self):
        if self.peek().kind != "IDENT":
            raise self.error("expected a name")
        return self.advance().text

    def type_name(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "IDENT" or tok.text not in TYPES:
            raise self.error("expected a type")
        return self.advance().text

    def let_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        self.expect("=")
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return Let(name, type_, value)

    def if_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        cond = self.expr()
        then = self.block()
        else_ = None
        if self.at("else"):
            self.advance()
            else_ = self.if_stmt() if self.at("if") else self.block()
        return If(cond, then, else_)

    def block(self):
        self.expect("{")
        stmts = []
        while not self.at("}"):
            if self.peek().kind == "EOF":
                raise self.error("expected '}'")
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        self.advance()
        return Block(stmts)

    def param(self):
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        return (name, type_)

    def fn_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        self.expect("(")
        params = []
        if not self.at(")"):
            params.append(self.param())
            while self.at(","):
                self.advance()
                params.append(self.param())
        self.expect(")")
        ret = None
        if self.at("->"):
            self.advance()
            ret = self.type_name()
        return Fn(name, params, ret, self.block())


def parse_program(tokens):
    return Parser(tokens).program()


class CometError(Exception):
    pass


def comet_div(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q


def comet_mod(a, b):
    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TVar:
    name: str


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TCon:
    name: str


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TFun:
    params: tuple
    ret: object


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Scheme:
    vars: tuple
    type: object


INT, BOOL, STR, VOID = TCon("int"), TCon("bool"), TCon("str"), TCon("void")


class TypeCheckError(Exception):
    pass


def type_vars(t, found=None):
    """The names of the type variables in t, in order of first appearance."""
    if found is None:
        found = []
    if isinstance(t, TVar):
        if t.name not in found:
            found.append(t.name)
    elif isinstance(t, TFun):
        for p in t.params:
            type_vars(p, found)
        type_vars(t.ret, found)

    return found


def show_type(t, names=None):
    if names is None:
        names = {v: "'" + chr(ord("a") + i) for i, v in enumerate(type_vars(t))}
    if isinstance(t, TVar):
        return names.get(t.name, t.name)
    if isinstance(t, TFun):
        params = ", ".join(show_type(p, names) for p in t.params)
        return f"({params}) -> {show_type(t.ret, names)}"

    return t.name


def always_returns(stmts):
    for stmt in stmts:
        if isinstance(stmt, Return):
            return True
        if isinstance(stmt, Block) and always_returns(stmt.stmts):
            return True
        if isinstance(stmt, If) and stmt.else_ is not None:
            if always_returns([stmt.then]) and always_returns([stmt.else_]):
                return True
    return False


class Inferencer:
    def __init__(self):
        self.subst = {}
        self.count = 0
        self.scopes = [{}]
        self.returns = []
        self.pending = []


    def fresh(self):
        self.count += 1
        return TVar(f"t{self.count}")

    def resolve(self, t):
        """t with every bound type variable replaced by what it is bound to, all the way down."""
        if isinstance(t, TVar):
            if t.name in self.subst:
                return self.resolve(self.subst[t.name])
            return t
        if isinstance(t, TFun):
            return TFun(tuple(self.resolve(p) for p in t.params), self.resolve(t.ret))

        return t

    def env_vars(self):
        """The type variables that are free somewhere in the current scopes."""
        found = set()
        for scope in self.scopes:
            for scheme in scope.values():
                found.update(v for v in type_vars(self.resolve(scheme.type)) if v not in scheme.vars)
        return found

    def occurs(self, name, t):
        return name in type_vars(self.resolve(t))

    def unify(self, a, b):
        a = self.resolve(a)
        b = self.resolve(b)
        if a == b:
            return
        if isinstance(a, TVar):
            if self.occurs(a.name, b):
                raise TypeCheckError(f"infinite type: {show_type(a)} would contain itself")
            self.subst[a.name] = b
            return
        if isinstance(b, TVar):
            self.unify(b, a)
            return
        if isinstance(a, TFun) and isinstance(b, TFun):
            if len(a.params) != len(b.params):
                raise TypeCheckError(f"a function of {len(a.params)} arguments is not one of {len(b.params)}")
            for p, q in zip(a.params, b.params):
                self.unify(p, q)
            self.unify(a.ret, b.ret)
            return
        raise TypeCheckError(f"type mismatch: {show_type(a)} and {show_type(b)}")

    def generalize(self, t):
        t = self.resolve(t)
        env = self.env_vars()
        return Scheme(tuple(v for v in type_vars(t) if v not in env), t)

    def instantiate(self, scheme):
        mapping = {v: self.fresh() for v in scheme.vars}
        return self.replace(self.resolve(scheme.type), mapping)

    def replace(self, t, mapping):
        if isinstance(t, TVar):
            return mapping.get(t.name, t)
        if isinstance(t, TFun):
            return TFun(tuple(self.replace(p, mapping) for p in t.params), self.replace(t.ret, mapping))
        return t

    # ---- the walk over the program, given ----

    def declare(self, name, scheme):
        if name in self.scopes[-1]:
            raise TypeCheckError(f"{name} is already declared in this scope")
        self.scopes[-1][name] = scheme

    def lookup(self, name):
        for scope in reversed(self.scopes):
            if name in scope:
                return scope[name]
        raise TypeCheckError(f"undefined variable {name}")

    def infer_program(self, program):
        for stmt in program.stmts:
            self.infer_stmt(stmt)
        self.settle_plus()

    def settle_plus(self):
        """Each '+' whose operand type is still unknown adds ints, like a default."""
        for t in self.pending:
            if isinstance(self.resolve(t), TVar):
                self.unify(t, INT)
        self.pending = []

    def infer_block(self, stmts):
        self.scopes.append({})
        try:
            for stmt in stmts:
                self.infer_stmt(stmt)
        finally:
            self.scopes.pop()

    def value(self, expr):
        t = self.infer_expr(expr)
        if self.resolve(t) == VOID:
            raise TypeCheckError("a call that returns nothing has no value")
        return t

    def infer_stmt(self, stmt):
        if isinstance(stmt, Let):
            t = self.value(stmt.expr)
            if stmt.type is not None:
                self.unify(t, TCon(stmt.type))
            self.declare(stmt.name, Scheme((), t))
        elif isinstance(stmt, Assign):
            scheme = self.lookup(stmt.name)
            if scheme.vars:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"cannot assign to the polymorphic function {stmt.name}")
            self.unify(scheme.type, self.value(stmt.expr))
        elif isinstance(stmt, Print):
            self.value(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, ExprStmt):
            self.infer_expr(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, If):
            self.unify(self.infer_expr(stmt.cond), BOOL)
            self.infer_stmt(stmt.then)
            if stmt.else_ is not None:
                self.infer_stmt(stmt.else_)
        elif isinstance(stmt, While):
            self.unify(self.infer_expr(stmt.cond), BOOL)
            self.infer_stmt(stmt.body)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Block):
            self.infer_block(stmt.stmts)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Return):
            if not self.returns:
                raise TypeCheckError("return outside a function")
            t = VOID if stmt.expr is None else self.value(stmt.expr)
            self.unify(t, self.returns[-1])
        elif isinstance(stmt, Fn):
            self.infer_fn(stmt)

    def infer_fn(self, stmt):
        params = [TCon(t) if t is not None else self.fresh() for _, t in stmt.params]
        ret = TCon(stmt.ret) if stmt.ret is not None else self.fresh()
        fn_type = TFun(tuple(params), ret)
        self.declare(stmt.name, Scheme((), fn_type))
        self.scopes.append({})
        self.returns.append(ret)
        try:
            for (name, _), t in zip(stmt.params, params):
                self.declare(name, Scheme((), t))
            for inner in stmt.body.stmts:
                self.infer_stmt(inner)
        finally:
            self.returns.pop()
            self.scopes.pop()
        if not always_returns(stmt.body.stmts):
            self.unify(ret, VOID)
        self.settle_plus()
        del self.scopes[-1][stmt.name]
        self.scopes[-1][stmt.name] = self.generalize(fn_type)

    def infer_expr(self, expr):
        if isinstance(expr, Num):
            return INT
        if isinstance(expr, Str):
            return STR
        if isinstance(expr, Bool):
            return BOOL
        if isinstance(expr, Var):
            return self.instantiate(self.lookup(expr.name))
        if isinstance(expr, Unary):
            wanted = INT if expr.op == "-" else BOOL
            self.unify(self.infer_expr(expr.expr), wanted)
            return wanted
        if isinstance(expr, Binary):
            return self.infer_binary(expr)
        if isinstance(expr, Call):
            callee = self.infer_expr(expr.callee)
            args = tuple(self.value(arg) for arg in expr.args)
            result = self.fresh()
            self.unify(callee, TFun(args, result))
            return result
        raise TypeCheckError(f"unknown expression {type(expr).__name__}")

    def infer_binary(self, expr):
        op = expr.op
        left = self.value(expr.left)
        right = self.value(expr.right)
        if op in ("and", "or"):
            self.unify(left, BOOL)
            self.unify(right, BOOL)
            return BOOL
        if op in ("==", "!="):
            self.unify(left, right)
            return BOOL
        if op == "+":
            self.unify(left, right)
            t = self.resolve(left)
            if isinstance(t, TVar):
                self.pending.append(t)
            elif t not in (INT, STR):
                raise TypeCheckError(f"'+' needs two ints or two strs, not {show_type(t)}")
            return t
        self.unify(left, INT)
        self.unify(right, INT)
        return BOOL if op in ("<", "<=", ">", ">=") else INT


def infer_source(source):
    """The inferred type of every top-level name, as text."""
    inf = Inferencer()
    inf.infer_program(parse_program(tokenize(source)))
    return {name: show_type(inf.resolve(s.type)) for name, s in inf.scopes[-1].items()}


def type_error(source):
    try:
        infer_source(source)
    except TypeCheckError as e:
        return str(e)
    return None


def signatures(source):
    raise TypeCheckError("signatures is not written yet")

from dataclasses import dataclass

KEYWORDS = {"let", "fn", "return", "if", "else", "while", "print",
            "true", "false", "and", "or", "not"}
TWO_CHAR = {"==", "!=", "<=", ">=", "->"}
ONE_CHAR = set("+-*/%<>=(){},;:")
ESCAPES = {'"': '"', "\\": "\\", "n": "\n"}
DIGITS = "0123456789"
LETTERS = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ_"


@dataclass
class Token:
    kind: str
    text: str
    line: int
    col: int


class LexError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


def tokenize(source):
    tokens = []
    i = 0
    line = 1
    col = 1
    n = len(source)

    def advance(count):
        nonlocal i, line, col
        for _ in range(count):
            if source[i] == "\n":
                line += 1
                col = 1
            else:
                col += 1
            i += 1

    while i < n:
        ch = source[i]
        start_line, start_col = line, col
        if ch in " \t\r\n":
            advance(1)
        elif ch == "#":
            while i < n and source[i] != "\n":
                advance(1)
        elif ch in DIGITS:
            j = i
            while j < n and source[j] in DIGITS:
                j += 1
            tokens.append(Token("NUMBER", source[i:j], start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch in LETTERS:
            j = i
            while j < n and (source[j] in LETTERS or source[j] in DIGITS):
                j += 1
            word = source[i:j]
            kind = "KEYWORD" if word in KEYWORDS else "IDENT"
            tokens.append(Token(kind, word, start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch == '"':
            advance(1)
            chars = []
            while True:
                if i >= n or source[i] == "\n":
                    raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                c = source[i]
                if c == '"':
                    advance(1)
                    break
                if c == "\\":
                    if i + 1 >= n or source[i + 1] == "\n":
                        raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                    if source[i + 1] not in ESCAPES:
                        raise LexError("unknown escape", line, col)
                    chars.append(ESCAPES[source[i + 1]])
                    advance(2)
                else:
                    chars.append(c)
                    advance(1)
            tokens.append(Token("STRING", "".join(chars), start_line, start_col))
        elif source[i:i + 2] in TWO_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", source[i:i + 2], start_line, start_col))
            advance(2)
        elif ch in ONE_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", ch, start_line, start_col))
            advance(1)
        else:
            raise LexError(f"unexpected character {ch!r}", start_line, start_col)
    tokens.append(Token("EOF", "", line, col))
    return tokens

class ParseError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


COMPARE = ("==", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">=")
TYPES = ("int", "bool", "str")


class Parser:
    def __init__(self, tokens):
        self.tokens = tokens
        self.pos = 0

    def peek(self, ahead=0):
        return self.tokens[min(self.pos + ahead, len(self.tokens) - 1)]

    def at(self, *texts):
        tok = self.peek()
        return tok.kind in ("OP", "KEYWORD") and tok.text in texts

    def advance(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "EOF":
            self.pos += 1
        return tok

    def error(self, message):
        tok = self.peek()
        return ParseError(message, tok.line, tok.col)

    def expect(self, text):
        if not self.at(text):
            raise self.error(f"expected '{text}'")
        return self.advance()

    def expr(self):
        return self.or_expr()

    def or_expr(self):
        left = self.and_expr()
        while self.at("or"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.and_expr())
        return left

    def and_expr(self):
        left = self.not_expr()
        while self.at("and"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.not_expr())
        return left

    def not_expr(self):
        if self.at("not"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("not", self.not_expr())
        return self.compare()

    def compare(self):
        left = self.sum()
        if self.at(*COMPARE):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.sum())
            if self.at(*COMPARE):
                raise self.error("comparisons cannot be chained")
        return left

    def sum(self):
        left = self.product()
        while self.at("+", "-"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.product())
        return left

    def product(self):
        left = self.unary()
        while self.at("*", "/", "%"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.unary())
        return left

    def unary(self):
        if self.at("-"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("-", self.unary())
        return self.call()

    def call(self):
        expr = self.primary()
        while self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            args = []
            if not self.at(")"):
                args.append(self.expr())
                while self.at(","):
                    self.advance()
                    args.append(self.expr())
            self.expect(")")
            expr = Call(expr, args)
        return expr

    def primary(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind == "NUMBER":
            self.advance()
            return Num(int(tok.text))
        if tok.kind == "STRING":
            self.advance()
            return Str(tok.text)
        if tok.kind == "IDENT":
            self.advance()
            return Var(tok.text)
        if self.at("true", "false"):
            self.advance()
            return Bool(tok.text == "true")
        if self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            inner = self.expr()
            self.expect(")")
            return inner
        raise self.error("expected an expression")

    def program(self):
        stmts = []
        while self.peek().kind != "EOF":
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        return Program(stmts)

    def statement(self):
        if self.at("let"):
            return self.let_stmt()
        if self.at("print"):
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Print(value)
        if self.at("if"):
            return self.if_stmt()
        if self.at("while"):
            self.advance()
            cond = self.expr()
            return While(cond, self.block())
        if self.at("fn"):
            return self.fn_stmt()
        if self.at("return"):
            self.advance()
            value = None if self.at(";") else self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Return(value)
        nxt = self.peek(1)
        if self.peek().kind == "IDENT" and nxt.kind == "OP" and nxt.text == "=":
            name = self.advance().text
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Assign(name, value)
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return ExprStmt(value)

    def name(self):
        if self.peek().kind != "IDENT":
            raise self.error("expected a name")
        return self.advance().text

    def type_name(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "IDENT" or tok.text not in TYPES:
            raise self.error("expected a type")
        return self.advance().text

    def let_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        self.expect("=")
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return Let(name, type_, value)

    def if_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        cond = self.expr()
        then = self.block()
        else_ = None
        if self.at("else"):
            self.advance()
            else_ = self.if_stmt() if self.at("if") else self.block()
        return If(cond, then, else_)

    def block(self):
        self.expect("{")
        stmts = []
        while not self.at("}"):
            if self.peek().kind == "EOF":
                raise self.error("expected '}'")
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        self.advance()
        return Block(stmts)

    def param(self):
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        return (name, type_)

    def fn_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        self.expect("(")
        params = []
        if not self.at(")"):
            params.append(self.param())
            while self.at(","):
                self.advance()
                params.append(self.param())
        self.expect(")")
        ret = None
        if self.at("->"):
            self.advance()
            ret = self.type_name()
        return Fn(name, params, ret, self.block())


def parse_program(tokens):
    return Parser(tokens).program()


class CometError(Exception):
    pass


def comet_div(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q


def comet_mod(a, b):
    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TVar:

    name: str
