    ret: object


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Scheme:
    vars: tuple
    type: object


INT, BOOL, STR, VOID = TCon("int"), TCon("bool"), TCon("str"), TCon("void")


class TypeCheckError(Exception):
    pass


def type_vars(t, found=None):
    """The names of the type variables in t, in order of first appearance."""
    if found is None:
        found = []
    if isinstance(t, TVar):
        if t.name not in found:
            found.append(t.name)
    elif isinstance(t, TFun):
        for p in t.params:
            type_vars(p, found)
        type_vars(t.ret, found)

    return found


def show_type(t, names=None):
    if names is None:
        names = {v: "'" + chr(ord("a") + i) for i, v in enumerate(type_vars(t))}
    if isinstance(t, TVar):
        return names.get(t.name, t.name)
    if isinstance(t, TFun):
        params = ", ".join(show_type(p, names) for p in t.params)
        return f"({params}) -> {show_type(t.ret, names)}"

    return t.name


def always_returns(stmts):
    for stmt in stmts:
        if isinstance(stmt, Return):
            return True
        if isinstance(stmt, Block) and always_returns(stmt.stmts):
            return True
        if isinstance(stmt, If) and stmt.else_ is not None:
            if always_returns([stmt.then]) and always_returns([stmt.else_]):
                return True
    return False


class Inferencer:
    def __init__(self):
        self.subst = {}
        self.count = 0
        self.scopes = [{}]
        self.returns = []
        self.pending = []


    def fresh(self):
        self.count += 1
        return TVar(f"t{self.count}")

    def resolve(self, t):
        """t with every bound type variable replaced by what it is bound to, all the way down."""
        if isinstance(t, TVar):
            if t.name in self.subst:
                return self.resolve(self.subst[t.name])
            return t
        if isinstance(t, TFun):
            return TFun(tuple(self.resolve(p) for p in t.params), self.resolve(t.ret))

        return t

    def env_vars(self):
        """The type variables that are free somewhere in the current scopes."""
        found = set()
        for scope in self.scopes:
            for scheme in scope.values():
                found.update(v for v in type_vars(self.resolve(scheme.type)) if v not in scheme.vars)
        return found

    def occurs(self, name, t):
        return name in type_vars(self.resolve(t))

    def unify(self, a, b):
        a = self.resolve(a)
        b = self.resolve(b)
        if a == b:
            return
        if isinstance(a, TVar):
            if self.occurs(a.name, b):
                raise TypeCheckError(f"infinite type: {show_type(a)} would contain itself")
            self.subst[a.name] = b
            return
        if isinstance(b, TVar):
            self.unify(b, a)
            return
        if isinstance(a, TFun) and isinstance(b, TFun):
            if len(a.params) != len(b.params):
                raise TypeCheckError(f"a function of {len(a.params)} arguments is not one of {len(b.params)}")
            for p, q in zip(a.params, b.params):
                self.unify(p, q)
            self.unify(a.ret, b.ret)
            return
        raise TypeCheckError(f"type mismatch: {show_type(a)} and {show_type(b)}")

    def generalize(self, t):
        t = self.resolve(t)
        env = self.env_vars()
        return Scheme(tuple(v for v in type_vars(t) if v not in env), t)

    def instantiate(self, scheme):
        mapping = {v: self.fresh() for v in scheme.vars}
        return self.replace(self.resolve(scheme.type), mapping)

    def replace(self, t, mapping):
        if isinstance(t, TVar):
            return mapping.get(t.name, t)
        if isinstance(t, TFun):
            return TFun(tuple(self.replace(p, mapping) for p in t.params), self.replace(t.ret, mapping))
        return t

    # ---- the walk over the program, given ----

    def declare(self, name, scheme):
        if name in self.scopes[-1]:
            raise TypeCheckError(f"{name} is already declared in this scope")
        self.scopes[-1][name] = scheme

    def lookup(self, name):
        for scope in reversed(self.scopes):
            if name in scope:
                return scope[name]
        raise TypeCheckError(f"undefined variable {name}")

    def infer_program(self, program):
        for stmt in program.stmts:
            self.infer_stmt(stmt)
        self.settle_plus()

    def settle_plus(self):
        """Each '+' whose operand type is still unknown adds ints, like a default."""
        for t in self.pending:
            if isinstance(self.resolve(t), TVar):
                self.unify(t, INT)
        self.pending = []

    def infer_block(self, stmts):
        self.scopes.append({})
        try:
            for stmt in stmts:
                self.infer_stmt(stmt)
        finally:
            self.scopes.pop()

    def value(self, expr):
        t = self.infer_expr(expr)
        if self.resolve(t) == VOID:
            raise TypeCheckError("a call that returns nothing has no value")
        return t

    def infer_stmt(self, stmt):
        if isinstance(stmt, Let):
            t = self.value(stmt.expr)
            if stmt.type is not None:
                self.unify(t, TCon(stmt.type))
            self.declare(stmt.name, Scheme((), t))
        elif isinstance(stmt, Assign):
            scheme = self.lookup(stmt.name)
            if scheme.vars:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"cannot assign to the polymorphic function {stmt.name}")
            self.unify(scheme.type, self.value(stmt.expr))
        elif isinstance(stmt, Print):
            self.value(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, ExprStmt):
            self.infer_expr(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, If):
            self.unify(self.infer_expr(stmt.cond), BOOL)
            self.infer_stmt(stmt.then)
            if stmt.else_ is not None:
                self.infer_stmt(stmt.else_)
        elif isinstance(stmt, While):
            self.unify(self.infer_expr(stmt.cond), BOOL)
            self.infer_stmt(stmt.body)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Block):
            self.infer_block(stmt.stmts)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Return):
            if not self.returns:
                raise TypeCheckError("return outside a function")
            t = VOID if stmt.expr is None else self.value(stmt.expr)
            self.unify(t, self.returns[-1])
        elif isinstance(stmt, Fn):
            self.infer_fn(stmt)

    def infer_fn(self, stmt):
        params = [TCon(t) if t is not None else self.fresh() for _, t in stmt.params]
        ret = TCon(stmt.ret) if stmt.ret is not None else self.fresh()
        fn_type = TFun(tuple(params), ret)
        self.declare(stmt.name, Scheme((), fn_type))
        self.scopes.append({})
        self.returns.append(ret)
        try:
            for (name, _), t in zip(stmt.params, params):
                self.declare(name, Scheme((), t))
            for inner in stmt.body.stmts:
                self.infer_stmt(inner)
        finally:
            self.returns.pop()
            self.scopes.pop()
        if not always_returns(stmt.body.stmts):
            self.unify(ret, VOID)
        self.settle_plus()
        del self.scopes[-1][stmt.name]
        self.scopes[-1][stmt.name] = self.generalize(fn_type)

    def infer_expr(self, expr):
        if isinstance(expr, Num):
            return INT
        if isinstance(expr, Str):
            return STR
        if isinstance(expr, Bool):
            return BOOL
        if isinstance(expr, Var):
            return self.instantiate(self.lookup(expr.name))
        if isinstance(expr, Unary):
            wanted = INT if expr.op == "-" else BOOL
            self.unify(self.infer_expr(expr.expr), wanted)
            return wanted
        if isinstance(expr, Binary):
            return self.infer_binary(expr)
        if isinstance(expr, Call):
            callee = self.infer_expr(expr.callee)
            args = tuple(self.value(arg) for arg in expr.args)
            result = self.fresh()
            self.unify(callee, TFun(args, result))
            return result
        raise TypeCheckError(f"unknown expression {type(expr).__name__}")

    def infer_binary(self, expr):
        op = expr.op
        left = self.value(expr.left)
        right = self.value(expr.right)
        if op in ("and", "or"):
            self.unify(left, BOOL)
            self.unify(right, BOOL)
            return BOOL
        if op in ("==", "!="):
            self.unify(left, right)
            return BOOL
        if op == "+":
            self.unify(left, right)
            t = self.resolve(left)
            if isinstance(t, TVar):
                self.pending.append(t)
            elif t not in (INT, STR):
                raise TypeCheckError(f"'+' needs two ints or two strs, not {show_type(t)}")
            return t
        self.unify(left, INT)
        self.unify(right, INT)
        return BOOL if op in ("<", "<=", ">", ">=") else INT


def infer_source(source):
    """The inferred type of every top-level name, as text."""
    inf = Inferencer()
    inf.infer_program(parse_program(tokenize(source)))
    return {name: show_type(inf.resolve(s.type)) for name, s in inf.scopes[-1].items()}


def type_error(source):
    try:
        infer_source(source)
    except TypeCheckError as e:
        return str(e)
    return None


class SignatureInferencer(Inferencer):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.found = []

    def infer_fn(self, stmt):
        index = len(self.found)
        self.found.append(None)
        super().infer_fn(stmt)
        self.found[index] = (stmt, self.scopes[-1][stmt.name].type)


def signatures(source):
    inf = SignatureInferencer()
    inf.infer_program(parse_program(tokenize(source)))
    lines = []
    for stmt, fn_type in inf.found:
        t = inf.resolve(fn_type)
        names = {v: "'" + chr(ord("a") + i) for i, v in enumerate(type_vars(t))}
        params = ", ".join(f"{name}: {show_type(p, names)}" for (name, _), p in zip(stmt.params, t.params))
        lines.append(f"fn {stmt.name}({params}) -> {show_type(t.ret, names)}")
    return lines
--- hint
Subclass `Inferencer` and override `infer_fn`: reserve a place in a list before calling `super().infer_fn(stmt)`, so that outer functions come before inner ones, and afterwards store the declaration with its type, which `infer_fn` has just put into `self.scopes[-1][stmt.name]`.
--- hint
After `infer_program`, resolve each stored type. Build the name map once per line with `type_vars` on the whole function type, `{v: "'" + chr(ord("a") + i) ...}`, and pass it to `show_type(t, names)` for each parameter and for the return type.
--- check case | Several functions, nested ones after their parent
signatures("fn compose(f, g) { fn h(x) { return f(g(x)); } return h; } fn add(a, b) { return a + b; } fn say(s) { print s; }")
=> ["fn compose(f: ('a) -> 'b, g: ('c) -> 'a) -> ('c) -> 'b", "fn h(x: 'a) -> 'b", "fn add(a: int, b: int) -> int", "fn say(s: 'a) -> void"]
--- check case | No parameters, and annotations
signatures("fn zero() { return 0; } fn half(n: int) { return n / 2; }")
=> ["fn zero() -> int", "fn half(n: int) -> int"]
--- check case | Types settled later in the program
signatures("fn outer(x) { fn inner(y) { return x == y; } return inner(1); }")
=> ["fn outer(x: int) -> bool", "fn inner(y: int) -> bool"]
--- check case | No functions
signatures("let x = 1;")
=> []
--- check test | Type errors raise
raises(TypeCheckError, lambda: signatures("fn f(x) { return x(x); }"))

+++ practice | Pairs: a polymorphic data type
--- task
Add a type constructor to the inferencer: `pair(A, B)`, the type of pairs whose first part has type A and second part type B. Comet gets three built-in functions, available everywhere:

- `pair(x, y)` of scheme ∀a b. (a, b) -> pair(a, b);
- `first(p)` of scheme ∀a b. (pair(a, b)) -> a;
- `second(p)` of scheme ∀a b. (pair(a, b)) -> b.

The starter gives the lesson's finished inferencer. Add a frozen dataclass `TPair(first, second)`, and extend `type_vars`, `show_type` (write `pair(A, B)`), `resolve`, `unify` and `instantiate` to handle it. Put the three schemes in a scope of built-ins **outside** the global scope (insert it at the front of `self.scopes`), so that `infer_source`, which reports `self.scopes[-1]`, still shows only the program's own names, and a program may declare its own `pair`.

For example, `infer_source("fn swap(p) { return pair(second(p), first(p)); }")` is `{"swap": "(pair('a, 'b)) -> pair('b, 'a)"}`.
--- starter
from dataclasses import dataclass

KEYWORDS = {"let", "fn", "return", "if", "else", "while", "print",
            "true", "false", "and", "or", "not"}
TWO_CHAR = {"==", "!=", "<=", ">=", "->"}
ONE_CHAR = set("+-*/%<>=(){},;:")
ESCAPES = {'"': '"', "\\": "\\", "n": "\n"}
DIGITS = "0123456789"
LETTERS = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ_"


@dataclass
class Token:
    kind: str
    text: str
    line: int
    col: int


class LexError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


def tokenize(source):
    tokens = []
    i = 0
    line = 1
    col = 1
    n = len(source)

    def advance(count):
        nonlocal i, line, col
        for _ in range(count):
            if source[i] == "\n":
                line += 1
                col = 1
            else:
                col += 1
            i += 1

    while i < n:
        ch = source[i]
        start_line, start_col = line, col
        if ch in " \t\r\n":
            advance(1)
        elif ch == "#":
            while i < n and source[i] != "\n":
                advance(1)
        elif ch in DIGITS:
            j = i
            while j < n and source[j] in DIGITS:
                j += 1
            tokens.append(Token("NUMBER", source[i:j], start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch in LETTERS:
            j = i
            while j < n and (source[j] in LETTERS or source[j] in DIGITS):
                j += 1
            word = source[i:j]
            kind = "KEYWORD" if word in KEYWORDS else "IDENT"
            tokens.append(Token(kind, word, start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch == '"':
            advance(1)
            chars = []
            while True:
                if i >= n or source[i] == "\n":
                    raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                c = source[i]
                if c == '"':
                    advance(1)
                    break
                if c == "\\":
                    if i + 1 >= n or source[i + 1] == "\n":
                        raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                    if source[i + 1] not in ESCAPES:
                        raise LexError("unknown escape", line, col)
                    chars.append(ESCAPES[source[i + 1]])
                    advance(2)
                else:
                    chars.append(c)
                    advance(1)
            tokens.append(Token("STRING", "".join(chars), start_line, start_col))
        elif source[i:i + 2] in TWO_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", source[i:i + 2], start_line, start_col))
            advance(2)
        elif ch in ONE_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", ch, start_line, start_col))
            advance(1)
        else:
            raise LexError(f"unexpected character {ch!r}", start_line, start_col)
    tokens.append(Token("EOF", "", line, col))
    return tokens

class ParseError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


COMPARE = ("==", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">=")
TYPES = ("int", "bool", "str")


class Parser:
    def __init__(self, tokens):
        self.tokens = tokens
        self.pos = 0

    def peek(self, ahead=0):
        return self.tokens[min(self.pos + ahead, len(self.tokens) - 1)]

    def at(self, *texts):
        tok = self.peek()
        return tok.kind in ("OP", "KEYWORD") and tok.text in texts

    def advance(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "EOF":
            self.pos += 1
        return tok

    def error(self, message):
        tok = self.peek()
        return ParseError(message, tok.line, tok.col)

    def expect(self, text):
        if not self.at(text):
            raise self.error(f"expected '{text}'")
        return self.advance()

    def expr(self):
        return self.or_expr()

    def or_expr(self):
        left = self.and_expr()
        while self.at("or"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.and_expr())
        return left

    def and_expr(self):
        left = self.not_expr()
        while self.at("and"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.not_expr())
        return left

    def not_expr(self):
        if self.at("not"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("not", self.not_expr())
        return self.compare()

    def compare(self):
        left = self.sum()
        if self.at(*COMPARE):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.sum())
            if self.at(*COMPARE):
                raise self.error("comparisons cannot be chained")
        return left

    def sum(self):
        left = self.product()
        while self.at("+", "-"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.product())
        return left

    def product(self):
        left = self.unary()
        while self.at("*", "/", "%"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.unary())
        return left

    def unary(self):
        if self.at("-"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("-", self.unary())
        return self.call()

    def call(self):
        expr = self.primary()
        while self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            args = []
            if not self.at(")"):
                args.append(self.expr())
                while self.at(","):
                    self.advance()
                    args.append(self.expr())
            self.expect(")")
            expr = Call(expr, args)
        return expr

    def primary(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind == "NUMBER":
            self.advance()
            return Num(int(tok.text))
        if tok.kind == "STRING":
            self.advance()
            return Str(tok.text)
        if tok.kind == "IDENT":
            self.advance()
            return Var(tok.text)
        if self.at("true", "false"):
            self.advance()
            return Bool(tok.text == "true")
        if self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            inner = self.expr()
            self.expect(")")
            return inner
        raise self.error("expected an expression")

    def program(self):
        stmts = []
        while self.peek().kind != "EOF":
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        return Program(stmts)

    def statement(self):
        if self.at("let"):
            return self.let_stmt()
        if self.at("print"):
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Print(value)
        if self.at("if"):
            return self.if_stmt()
        if self.at("while"):
            self.advance()
            cond = self.expr()
            return While(cond, self.block())
        if self.at("fn"):
            return self.fn_stmt()
        if self.at("return"):
            self.advance()
            value = None if self.at(";") else self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Return(value)
        nxt = self.peek(1)
        if self.peek().kind == "IDENT" and nxt.kind == "OP" and nxt.text == "=":
            name = self.advance().text
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Assign(name, value)
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return ExprStmt(value)

    def name(self):
        if self.peek().kind != "IDENT":
            raise self.error("expected a name")
        return self.advance().text

    def type_name(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "IDENT" or tok.text not in TYPES:
            raise self.error("expected a type")
        return self.advance().text

    def let_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        self.expect("=")
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return Let(name, type_, value)

    def if_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        cond = self.expr()
        then = self.block()
        else_ = None
        if self.at("else"):
            self.advance()
            else_ = self.if_stmt() if self.at("if") else self.block()
        return If(cond, then, else_)

    def block(self):
        self.expect("{")
        stmts = []
        while not self.at("}"):
            if self.peek().kind == "EOF":
                raise self.error("expected '}'")
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        self.advance()
        return Block(stmts)

    def param(self):
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        return (name, type_)

    def fn_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        self.expect("(")
        params = []
        if not self.at(")"):
            params.append(self.param())
            while self.at(","):
                self.advance()
                params.append(self.param())
        self.expect(")")
        ret = None
        if self.at("->"):
            self.advance()
            ret = self.type_name()
        return Fn(name, params, ret, self.block())


def parse_program(tokens):
    return Parser(tokens).program()


class CometError(Exception):
    pass


def comet_div(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q


def comet_mod(a, b):
    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TVar:
    name: str


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TCon:
    name: str


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TFun:
    params: tuple
    ret: object


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Scheme:
    vars: tuple
    type: object


INT, BOOL, STR, VOID = TCon("int"), TCon("bool"), TCon("str"), TCon("void")


class TypeCheckError(Exception):
    pass


def type_vars(t, found=None):
    """The names of the type variables in t, in order of first appearance."""
    if found is None:
        found = []
    if isinstance(t, TVar):
        if t.name not in found:
            found.append(t.name)
    elif isinstance(t, TFun):
        for p in t.params:
            type_vars(p, found)
        type_vars(t.ret, found)

    return found


def show_type(t, names=None):
    if names is None:
        names = {v: "'" + chr(ord("a") + i) for i, v in enumerate(type_vars(t))}
    if isinstance(t, TVar):
        return names.get(t.name, t.name)
    if isinstance(t, TFun):
        params = ", ".join(show_type(p, names) for p in t.params)
        return f"({params}) -> {show_type(t.ret, names)}"

    return t.name


def always_returns(stmts):
    for stmt in stmts:
        if isinstance(stmt, Return):
            return True
        if isinstance(stmt, Block) and always_returns(stmt.stmts):
            return True
        if isinstance(stmt, If) and stmt.else_ is not None:
            if always_returns([stmt.then]) and always_returns([stmt.else_]):
                return True
    return False


class Inferencer:
    def __init__(self):
        self.subst = {}
        self.count = 0
        self.scopes = [{}]
        self.returns = []
        self.pending = []


    def fresh(self):
        self.count += 1
        return TVar(f"t{self.count}")

    def resolve(self, t):
        """t with every bound type variable replaced by what it is bound to, all the way down."""
        if isinstance(t, TVar):
            if t.name in self.subst:
                return self.resolve(self.subst[t.name])
            return t
        if isinstance(t, TFun):
            return TFun(tuple(self.resolve(p) for p in t.params), self.resolve(t.ret))

        return t

    def env_vars(self):
        """The type variables that are free somewhere in the current scopes."""
        found = set()
        for scope in self.scopes:
            for scheme in scope.values():
                found.update(v for v in type_vars(self.resolve(scheme.type)) if v not in scheme.vars)
        return found

    def occurs(self, name, t):
        return name in type_vars(self.resolve(t))

    def unify(self, a, b):
        a = self.resolve(a)
        b = self.resolve(b)
        if a == b:
            return
        if isinstance(a, TVar):
            if self.occurs(a.name, b):
                raise TypeCheckError(f"infinite type: {show_type(a)} would contain itself")
            self.subst[a.name] = b
            return
        if isinstance(b, TVar):
            self.unify(b, a)
            return
        if isinstance(a, TFun) and isinstance(b, TFun):
            if len(a.params) != len(b.params):
                raise TypeCheckError(f"a function of {len(a.params)} arguments is not one of {len(b.params)}")
            for p, q in zip(a.params, b.params):
                self.unify(p, q)
            self.unify(a.ret, b.ret)
            return
        raise TypeCheckError(f"type mismatch: {show_type(a)} and {show_type(b)}")

    def generalize(self, t):
        t = self.resolve(t)
        env = self.env_vars()
        return Scheme(tuple(v for v in type_vars(t) if v not in env), t)

    def instantiate(self, scheme):
        mapping = {v: self.fresh() for v in scheme.vars}
        return self.replace(self.resolve(scheme.type), mapping)

    def replace(self, t, mapping):
        if isinstance(t, TVar):
            return mapping.get(t.name, t)
        if isinstance(t, TFun):
            return TFun(tuple(self.replace(p, mapping) for p in t.params), self.replace(t.ret, mapping))
        return t

    # ---- the walk over the program, given ----

    def declare(self, name, scheme):
        if name in self.scopes[-1]:
            raise TypeCheckError(f"{name} is already declared in this scope")
        self.scopes[-1][name] = scheme

    def lookup(self, name):
        for scope in reversed(self.scopes):
            if name in scope:
                return scope[name]
        raise TypeCheckError(f"undefined variable {name}")

    def infer_program(self, program):
        for stmt in program.stmts:
            self.infer_stmt(stmt)
        self.settle_plus()

    def settle_plus(self):
        """Each '+' whose operand type is still unknown adds ints, like a default."""
        for t in self.pending:
            if isinstance(self.resolve(t), TVar):
                self.unify(t, INT)
        self.pending = []

    def infer_block(self, stmts):
        self.scopes.append({})
        try:
            for stmt in stmts:
                self.infer_stmt(stmt)
        finally:
            self.scopes.pop()

    def value(self, expr):
        t = self.infer_expr(expr)
        if self.resolve(t) == VOID:
            raise TypeCheckError("a call that returns nothing has no value")
        return t

    def infer_stmt(self, stmt):
        if isinstance(stmt, Let):
            t = self.value(stmt.expr)
            if stmt.type is not None:
                self.unify(t, TCon(stmt.type))
            self.declare(stmt.name, Scheme((), t))
        elif isinstance(stmt, Assign):
            scheme = self.lookup(stmt.name)
            if scheme.vars:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"cannot assign to the polymorphic function {stmt.name}")
            self.unify(scheme.type, self.value(stmt.expr))
        elif isinstance(stmt, Print):
            self.value(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, ExprStmt):
            self.infer_expr(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, If):
            self.unify(self.infer_expr(stmt.cond), BOOL)
            self.infer_stmt(stmt.then)
            if stmt.else_ is not None:
                self.infer_stmt(stmt.else_)
        elif isinstance(stmt, While):
            self.unify(self.infer_expr(stmt.cond), BOOL)
            self.infer_stmt(stmt.body)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Block):
            self.infer_block(stmt.stmts)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Return):
            if not self.returns:
                raise TypeCheckError("return outside a function")
            t = VOID if stmt.expr is None else self.value(stmt.expr)
            self.unify(t, self.returns[-1])
        elif isinstance(stmt, Fn):
            self.infer_fn(stmt)

    def infer_fn(self, stmt):
        params = [TCon(t) if t is not None else self.fresh() for _, t in stmt.params]
        ret = TCon(stmt.ret) if stmt.ret is not None else self.fresh()
        fn_type = TFun(tuple(params), ret)
        self.declare(stmt.name, Scheme((), fn_type))
        self.scopes.append({})
        self.returns.append(ret)
        try:
            for (name, _), t in zip(stmt.params, params):
                self.declare(name, Scheme((), t))
            for inner in stmt.body.stmts:
                self.infer_stmt(inner)
        finally:
            self.returns.pop()
            self.scopes.pop()
        if not always_returns(stmt.body.stmts):
            self.unify(ret, VOID)
        self.settle_plus()
        del self.scopes[-1][stmt.name]
        self.scopes[-1][stmt.name] = self.generalize(fn_type)

    def infer_expr(self, expr):
        if isinstance(expr, Num):
            return INT
        if isinstance(expr, Str):
            return STR
        if isinstance(expr, Bool):
            return BOOL
        if isinstance(expr, Var):
            return self.instantiate(self.lookup(expr.name))
        if isinstance(expr, Unary):
            wanted = INT if expr.op == "-" else BOOL
            self.unify(self.infer_expr(expr.expr), wanted)
            return wanted
        if isinstance(expr, Binary):
            return self.infer_binary(expr)
        if isinstance(expr, Call):
            callee = self.infer_expr(expr.callee)
            args = tuple(self.value(arg) for arg in expr.args)
            result = self.fresh()
            self.unify(callee, TFun(args, result))
            return result
        raise TypeCheckError(f"unknown expression {type(expr).__name__}")

    def infer_binary(self, expr):
        op = expr.op
        left = self.value(expr.left)
        right = self.value(expr.right)
        if op in ("and", "or"):
            self.unify(left, BOOL)
            self.unify(right, BOOL)
            return BOOL
        if op in ("==", "!="):
            self.unify(left, right)
            return BOOL
        if op == "+":
            self.unify(left, right)
            t = self.resolve(left)
            if isinstance(t, TVar):
                self.pending.append(t)
            elif t not in (INT, STR):
                raise TypeCheckError(f"'+' needs two ints or two strs, not {show_type(t)}")
            return t
        self.unify(left, INT)
        self.unify(right, INT)
        return BOOL if op in ("<", "<=", ">", ">=") else INT


def infer_source(source):
    """The inferred type of every top-level name, as text."""
    inf = Inferencer()
    inf.infer_program(parse_program(tokenize(source)))
    return {name: show_type(inf.resolve(s.type)) for name, s in inf.scopes[-1].items()}


def type_error(source):
    try:
        infer_source(source)
    except TypeCheckError as e:
        return str(e)
    return None
--- solution
from dataclasses import dataclass

KEYWORDS = {"let", "fn", "return", "if", "else", "while", "print",
            "true", "false", "and", "or", "not"}
TWO_CHAR = {"==", "!=", "<=", ">=", "->"}
ONE_CHAR = set("+-*/%<>=(){},;:")
ESCAPES = {'"': '"', "\\": "\\", "n": "\n"}
DIGITS = "0123456789"
LETTERS = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ_"


@dataclass
class Token:
    kind: str
    text: str
    line: int
    col: int


class LexError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


def tokenize(source):
    tokens = []
    i = 0
    line = 1
    col = 1
    n = len(source)

    def advance(count):
        nonlocal i, line, col
        for _ in range(count):
            if source[i] == "\n":
                line += 1
                col = 1
            else:
                col += 1
            i += 1

    while i < n:
        ch = source[i]
        start_line, start_col = line, col
        if ch in " \t\r\n":
            advance(1)
        elif ch == "#":
            while i < n and source[i] != "\n":
                advance(1)
        elif ch in DIGITS:
            j = i
            while j < n and source[j] in DIGITS:
                j += 1
            tokens.append(Token("NUMBER", source[i:j], start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch in LETTERS:
            j = i
            while j < n and (source[j] in LETTERS or source[j] in DIGITS):
                j += 1
            word = source[i:j]
            kind = "KEYWORD" if word in KEYWORDS else "IDENT"
            tokens.append(Token(kind, word, start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch == '"':
            advance(1)
            chars = []
            while True:
                if i >= n or source[i] == "\n":
                    raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                c = source[i]
                if c == '"':
                    advance(1)
                    break
                if c == "\\":
                    if i + 1 >= n or source[i + 1] == "\n":
                        raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                    if source[i + 1] not in ESCAPES:
                        raise LexError("unknown escape", line, col)
                    chars.append(ESCAPES[source[i + 1]])
                    advance(2)
                else:
                    chars.append(c)
                    advance(1)
            tokens.append(Token("STRING", "".join(chars), start_line, start_col))
        elif source[i:i + 2] in TWO_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", source[i:i + 2], start_line, start_col))
            advance(2)
        elif ch in ONE_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", ch, start_line, start_col))
            advance(1)
        else:
            raise LexError(f"unexpected character {ch!r}", start_line, start_col)
    tokens.append(Token("EOF", "", line, col))
    return tokens

class ParseError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


COMPARE = ("==", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">=")
TYPES = ("int", "bool", "str")


class Parser:
    def __init__(self, tokens):
        self.tokens = tokens
        self.pos = 0

    def peek(self, ahead=0):
        return self.tokens[min(self.pos + ahead, len(self.tokens) - 1)]

    def at(self, *texts):
        tok = self.peek()
        return tok.kind in ("OP", "KEYWORD") and tok.text in texts

    def advance(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "EOF":
            self.pos += 1
        return tok

    def error(self, message):
        tok = self.peek()
        return ParseError(message, tok.line, tok.col)

    def expect(self, text):
        if not self.at(text):
            raise self.error(f"expected '{text}'")
        return self.advance()

    def expr(self):
        return self.or_expr()

    def or_expr(self):
        left = self.and_expr()
        while self.at("or"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.and_expr())
        return left

    def and_expr(self):
        left = self.not_expr()
        while self.at("and"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.not_expr())
        return left

    def not_expr(self):
        if self.at("not"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("not", self.not_expr())
        return self.compare()

    def compare(self):
        left = self.sum()
        if self.at(*COMPARE):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.sum())
            if self.at(*COMPARE):
                raise self.error("comparisons cannot be chained")
        return left

    def sum(self):
        left = self.product()
        while self.at("+", "-"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.product())
        return left

    def product(self):
        left = self.unary()
        while self.at("*", "/", "%"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.unary())
        return left

    def unary(self):
        if self.at("-"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("-", self.unary())
        return self.call()

    def call(self):
        expr = self.primary()
        while self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            args = []
            if not self.at(")"):
                args.append(self.expr())
                while self.at(","):
                    self.advance()
                    args.append(self.expr())
            self.expect(")")
            expr = Call(expr, args)
        return expr

    def primary(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind == "NUMBER":
            self.advance()
            return Num(int(tok.text))
        if tok.kind == "STRING":
            self.advance()
            return Str(tok.text)
        if tok.kind == "IDENT":
            self.advance()
            return Var(tok.text)
        if self.at("true", "false"):
            self.advance()
            return Bool(tok.text == "true")
        if self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            inner = self.expr()
            self.expect(")")
            return inner
        raise self.error("expected an expression")

    def program(self):
        stmts = []
        while self.peek().kind != "EOF":
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        return Program(stmts)

    def statement(self):
        if self.at("let"):
            return self.let_stmt()
        if self.at("print"):
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Print(value)
        if self.at("if"):
            return self.if_stmt()
        if self.at("while"):
            self.advance()
            cond = self.expr()
            return While(cond, self.block())
        if self.at("fn"):
            return self.fn_stmt()
        if self.at("return"):
            self.advance()
            value = None if self.at(";") else self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Return(value)
        nxt = self.peek(1)
        if self.peek().kind == "IDENT" and nxt.kind == "OP" and nxt.text == "=":
            name = self.advance().text
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Assign(name, value)
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return ExprStmt(value)

    def name(self):
        if self.peek().kind != "IDENT":
            raise self.error("expected a name")
        return self.advance().text

    def type_name(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "IDENT" or tok.text not in TYPES:
            raise self.error("expected a type")
        return self.advance().text

    def let_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        self.expect("=")
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return Let(name, type_, value)

    def if_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        cond = self.expr()
        then = self.block()
        else_ = None
        if self.at("else"):
            self.advance()
            else_ = self.if_stmt() if self.at("if") else self.block()
        return If(cond, then, else_)

    def block(self):
        self.expect("{")
        stmts = []
        while not self.at("}"):
            if self.peek().kind == "EOF":
                raise self.error("expected '}'")
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        self.advance()
        return Block(stmts)

    def param(self):
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        return (name, type_)

    def fn_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        self.expect("(")
        params = []
        if not self.at(")"):
            params.append(self.param())
            while self.at(","):
                self.advance()
                params.append(self.param())
        self.expect(")")
        ret = None
        if self.at("->"):
            self.advance()
            ret = self.type_name()
        return Fn(name, params, ret, self.block())


def parse_program(tokens):
    return Parser(tokens).program()


class CometError(Exception):
    pass


def comet_div(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q


def comet_mod(a, b):
    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TVar:
    name: str


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TCon:
    name: str


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TFun:
    params: tuple
    ret: object


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Scheme:
    vars: tuple
    type: object


INT, BOOL, STR, VOID = TCon("int"), TCon("bool"), TCon("str"), TCon("void")


class TypeCheckError(Exception):
    pass


def type_vars(t, found=None):
    """The names of the type variables in t, in order of first appearance."""
    if found is None:
        found = []
    if isinstance(t, TVar):
        if t.name not in found:
            found.append(t.name)
    elif isinstance(t, TFun):
        for p in t.params:
            type_vars(p, found)
        type_vars(t.ret, found)
    elif isinstance(t, TPair):
        type_vars(t.first, found)
        type_vars(t.second, found)
    return found


def show_type(t, names=None):
    if names is None:
        names = {v: "'" + chr(ord("a") + i) for i, v in enumerate(type_vars(t))}
    if isinstance(t, TVar):
        return names.get(t.name, t.name)
    if isinstance(t, TFun):
        params = ", ".join(show_type(p, names) for p in t.params)
        return f"({params}) -> {show_type(t.ret, names)}"
    if isinstance(t, TPair):
        return f"pair({show_type(t.first, names)}, {show_type(t.second, names)})"
    return t.name


def always_returns(stmts):
    for stmt in stmts:
        if isinstance(stmt, Return):
            return True
        if isinstance(stmt, Block) and always_returns(stmt.stmts):
            return True
        if isinstance(stmt, If) and stmt.else_ is not None:
            if always_returns([stmt.then]) and always_returns([stmt.else_]):
                return True
    return False


class Inferencer:
    def __init__(self):
        self.subst = {}
        self.count = 0
        self.scopes = [{}]
        self.returns = []
        self.pending = []
        self.scopes.insert(0, builtin_schemes())

    def fresh(self):
        self.count += 1
        return TVar(f"t{self.count}")

    def resolve(self, t):
        """t with every bound type variable replaced by what it is bound to, all the way down."""
        if isinstance(t, TVar):
            if t.name in self.subst:
                return self.resolve(self.subst[t.name])
            return t
        if isinstance(t, TFun):
            return TFun(tuple(self.resolve(p) for p in t.params), self.resolve(t.ret))
        if isinstance(t, TPair):
            return TPair(self.resolve(t.first), self.resolve(t.second))
        return t

    def env_vars(self):
        """The type variables that are free somewhere in the current scopes."""
        found = set()
        for scope in self.scopes:
            for scheme in scope.values():
                found.update(v for v in type_vars(self.resolve(scheme.type)) if v not in scheme.vars)
        return found

    def occurs(self, name, t):
        return name in type_vars(self.resolve(t))

    def unify(self, a, b):
        a = self.resolve(a)
        b = self.resolve(b)
        if a == b:
            return
        if isinstance(a, TVar):
            if self.occurs(a.name, b):
                raise TypeCheckError(f"infinite type: {show_type(a)} would contain itself")
            self.subst[a.name] = b
            return
        if isinstance(b, TVar):
            self.unify(b, a)
            return
        if isinstance(a, TFun) and isinstance(b, TFun):
            if len(a.params) != len(b.params):
                raise TypeCheckError(f"a function of {len(a.params)} arguments is not one of {len(b.params)}")
            for p, q in zip(a.params, b.params):
                self.unify(p, q)
            self.unify(a.ret, b.ret)
            return
        if isinstance(a, TPair) and isinstance(b, TPair):
            self.unify(a.first, b.first)
            self.unify(a.second, b.second)
            return
        raise TypeCheckError(f"type mismatch: {show_type(a)} and {show_type(b)}")

    def generalize(self, t):
        t = self.resolve(t)
        env = self.env_vars()
        return Scheme(tuple(v for v in type_vars(t) if v not in env), t)

    def instantiate(self, scheme):
        mapping = {v: self.fresh() for v in scheme.vars}
        return self.replace(self.resolve(scheme.type), mapping)

    def replace(self, t, mapping):
        if isinstance(t, TVar):
            return mapping.get(t.name, t)
        if isinstance(t, TFun):
            return TFun(tuple(self.replace(p, mapping) for p in t.params), self.replace(t.ret, mapping))
        if isinstance(t, TPair):
            return TPair(self.replace(t.first, mapping), self.replace(t.second, mapping))
        return t

    # ---- the walk over the program, given ----

    def declare(self, name, scheme):
        if name in self.scopes[-1]:
            raise TypeCheckError(f"{name} is already declared in this scope")
        self.scopes[-1][name] = scheme

    def lookup(self, name):
        for scope in reversed(self.scopes):
            if name in scope:
                return scope[name]
        raise TypeCheckError(f"undefined variable {name}")

    def infer_program(self, program):
        for stmt in program.stmts:
            self.infer_stmt(stmt)
        self.settle_plus()

    def settle_plus(self):
        """Each '+' whose operand type is still unknown adds ints, like a default."""
        for t in self.pending:
            if isinstance(self.resolve(t), TVar):
                self.unify(t, INT)
        self.pending = []

    def infer_block(self, stmts):
        self.scopes.append({})
        try:
            for stmt in stmts:
                self.infer_stmt(stmt)
        finally:
            self.scopes.pop()

    def value(self, expr):
        t = self.infer_expr(expr)
        if self.resolve(t) == VOID:
            raise TypeCheckError("a call that returns nothing has no value")
        return t

    def infer_stmt(self, stmt):
        if isinstance(stmt, Let):
            t = self.value(stmt.expr)
            if stmt.type is not None:
                self.unify(t, TCon(stmt.type))
            self.declare(stmt.name, Scheme((), t))
        elif isinstance(stmt, Assign):
            scheme = self.lookup(stmt.name)
            if scheme.vars:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"cannot assign to the polymorphic function {stmt.name}")
            self.unify(scheme.type, self.value(stmt.expr))
        elif isinstance(stmt, Print):
            self.value(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, ExprStmt):
            self.infer_expr(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, If):
            self.unify(self.infer_expr(stmt.cond), BOOL)
            self.infer_stmt(stmt.then)
            if stmt.else_ is not None:
                self.infer_stmt(stmt.else_)
        elif isinstance(stmt, While):
            self.unify(self.infer_expr(stmt.cond), BOOL)
            self.infer_stmt(stmt.body)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Block):
            self.infer_block(stmt.stmts)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Return):
            if not self.returns:
                raise TypeCheckError("return outside a function")
            t = VOID if stmt.expr is None else self.value(stmt.expr)
            self.unify(t, self.returns[-1])
        elif isinstance(stmt, Fn):
            self.infer_fn(stmt)

    def infer_fn(self, stmt):
        params = [TCon(t) if t is not None else self.fresh() for _, t in stmt.params]
        ret = TCon(stmt.ret) if stmt.ret is not None else self.fresh()
        fn_type = TFun(tuple(params), ret)
        self.declare(stmt.name, Scheme((), fn_type))
        self.scopes.append({})
        self.returns.append(ret)
        try:
            for (name, _), t in zip(stmt.params, params):
                self.declare(name, Scheme((), t))
            for inner in stmt.body.stmts:
                self.infer_stmt(inner)
        finally:
            self.returns.pop()
            self.scopes.pop()
        if not always_returns(stmt.body.stmts):
            self.unify(ret, VOID)
        self.settle_plus()
        del self.scopes[-1][stmt.name]
        self.scopes[-1][stmt.name] = self.generalize(fn_type)

    def infer_expr(self, expr):
        if isinstance(expr, Num):
            return INT
        if isinstance(expr, Str):
            return STR
        if isinstance(expr, Bool):
            return BOOL
        if isinstance(expr, Var):
            return self.instantiate(self.lookup(expr.name))
        if isinstance(expr, Unary):
            wanted = INT if expr.op == "-" else BOOL
            self.unify(self.infer_expr(expr.expr), wanted)
            return wanted
        if isinstance(expr, Binary):
            return self.infer_binary(expr)
        if isinstance(expr, Call):
            callee = self.infer_expr(expr.callee)
            args = tuple(self.value(arg) for arg in expr.args)
            result = self.fresh()
            self.unify(callee, TFun(args, result))
            return result
        raise TypeCheckError(f"unknown expression {type(expr).__name__}")

    def infer_binary(self, expr):
        op = expr.op
        left = self.value(expr.left)
        right = self.value(expr.right)
        if op in ("and", "or"):
            self.unify(left, BOOL)
            self.unify(right, BOOL)
            return BOOL
        if op in ("==", "!="):
            self.unify(left, right)
            return BOOL
        if op == "+":
            self.unify(left, right)
            t = self.resolve(left)
            if isinstance(t, TVar):
                self.pending.append(t)
            elif t not in (INT, STR):
                raise TypeCheckError(f"'+' needs two ints or two strs, not {show_type(t)}")
            return t
        self.unify(left, INT)
        self.unify(right, INT)
        return BOOL if op in ("<", "<=", ">", ">=") else INT


def infer_source(source):
    """The inferred type of every top-level name, as text."""
    inf = Inferencer()
    inf.infer_program(parse_program(tokenize(source)))
    return {name: show_type(inf.resolve(s.type)) for name, s in inf.scopes[-1].items()}


def type_error(source):
    try:
        infer_source(source)
    except TypeCheckError as e:
        return str(e)
    return None


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TPair:
    first: object
    second: object


def builtin_schemes():
    a, b = TVar("a"), TVar("b")
    return {
        "pair": Scheme(("a", "b"), TFun((a, b), TPair(a, b))),
        "first": Scheme(("a", "b"), TFun((TPair(a, b),), a)),
        "second": Scheme(("a", "b"), TFun((TPair(a, b),), b)),
    }
--- hint
Every function that looks inside types needs one more case, `isinstance(t, TPair)`, that handles the two parts the way the `TFun` case handles parameters. In `unify`, two pairs unify when their first parts unify and their second parts unify.
--- hint
Build the schemes with shared variables, for example `a, b = TVar("a"), TVar("b")` and `Scheme(("a", "b"), TFun((TPair(a, b),), a))` for `first`. Instantiation gives each use fresh copies. In `__init__`, `self.scopes.insert(0, schemes)`.
--- check case | The example from the task
infer_source("fn swap(p) { return pair(second(p), first(p)); }")
=> {"swap": "(pair('a, 'b)) -> pair('b, 'a)"}
--- check case | Pairs of concrete types
infer_source('let q = pair(1, "a"); let n = second(q); fn dup(x) { return pair(x, x); } let d = dup(true);')
=> {"q": "pair(int, str)", "n": "str", "dup": "('a) -> pair('a, 'a)", "d": "pair(bool, bool)"}
--- check test | Wrong uses are type errors
type_error("print first(pair(1, true)) + 1; print second(pair(1, true)) + 1;") is not None and type_error("print first(3);") is not None and type_error("let p = pair(1, 2); p = pair(1, true);") is not None
--- check test | Pairs of functions and nested pairs
infer_source("fn inc(n) { return n + 1; } let fp = pair(inc, pair(inc, 0)); let r = first(fp)(first(second(fp))(second(second(fp))));")["r"] == "int"
--- check test | The program may shadow a built-in
type_error("let pair = 1; print pair + 1;") is None and type_error("fn first(x) { return x; } print first(3) + 1;") is None
--- check test | The occurs check still works through pairs
type_error("fn f(x) { return x == pair(x, 1); }") is not None

+++ practice | Solving a system of type equations
--- task
Inference produces many equations; they must all hold at once. Use the representation of the first practice problem: constants `"int"`, `"bool"`, `"str"`, `"void"`; variables like `"'a"`; function types `("fn", params, ret)`. Write `solve(equations)`, where `equations` is a list of pairs of types, each meaning "these two types are equal". Return the most general solution as a dictionary from each bound variable to its fully resolved type, or `None` if no substitution satisfies every equation.

Get the edge cases right: an empty list has the solution `{}`; `'a = 'a` binds nothing; a chain like `'a = 'b`, `'b = 'c`, `'c = int` binds all three to `int`; the occurs check must see through chains of variables; and a contradiction found only at the very end still means `None`. The answer must not depend on the order of the equations.
--- starter
def solve(equations):
    raise NotImplementedError("solve is not written yet")
--- solution
def is_var(t):
    return isinstance(t, str) and t.startswith("'")


def walk(t, subst):
    while is_var(t) and t in subst:
        t = subst[t]
    return t


def resolve(t, subst):
    t = walk(t, subst)
    if isinstance(t, tuple):
        return ("fn", tuple(resolve(p, subst) for p in t[1]), resolve(t[2], subst))
    return t


def occurs(v, t, subst):
    t = walk(t, subst)
    if t == v:
        return True
    if isinstance(t, tuple):
        return any(occurs(v, p, subst) for p in t[1]) or occurs(v, t[2], subst)
    return False


def unify(a, b, subst):
    a = walk(a, subst)
    b = walk(b, subst)
    if a == b:
        return True
    if is_var(a):
        if occurs(a, b, subst):
            return False
        subst[a] = b
        return True
    if is_var(b):
        return unify(b, a, subst)
    if isinstance(a, tuple) and isinstance(b, tuple) and len(a[1]) == len(b[1]):
        return all(unify(p, q, subst) for p, q in zip(a[1], b[1])) and unify(a[2], b[2], subst)
    return False


def mgu(a, b):
    subst = {}
    if not unify(a, b, subst):
        return None
    return {v: resolve(t, subst) for v, t in subst.items()}


def solve(equations):
    subst = {}
    for a, b in equations:
        if not unify(a, b, subst):
            return None
    return {v: resolve(t, subst) for v, t in subst.items()}
--- hint
Use one substitution for the whole system: unify the equations one after another into the same dictionary, and stop with `None` at the first failure. Unification with a shared substitution is exactly "solve these together".
--- hint
The occurs check through chains works if it looks through bound variables before comparing: walk the type, and for a function type check every part. Resolve every bound variable fully only at the end.
--- check test | Empty and trivial systems
solve([]) == {} and solve([("'a", "'a")]) == {} and solve([("int", "int")]) == {}
--- check case | A chain of variables
solve([("'a", "'b"), ("'b", "'c"), ("'c", "int")])
=> {"'a": "int", "'b": "int", "'c": "int"}
--- check test | The same chain in every order gives the same types
(lambda eqs: all((lambda s: s is not None and all(s.get(v) == "int" for v in ["'a", "'b", "'c"]))(solve([eqs[i] for i in order])) for order in [(0, 1, 2), (2, 1, 0), (1, 2, 0), (2, 0, 1)]))([("'a", "'b"), ("'b", "'c"), ("'c", "int")])
--- check test | The occurs check through a chain
solve([("'a", "'b"), ("'b", ("fn", ("'a",), "int"))]) is None and solve([("'x", ("fn", ("'y",), "int")), ("'y", "'z"), ("'z", "'x")]) is None
--- check test | A contradiction at the end
solve([("'a", "int"), ("'b", "'a"), ("'b", "str")]) is None and solve([("'f", ("fn", ("'x",), "'x")), ("'f", ("fn", ("int",), "'r")), ("'r", "bool")]) is None
--- check case | Function types solved together
solve([("'f", ("fn", ("'x",), "'y")), ("'x", "int"), ("'y", "'x"), ("'g", ("fn", ("'f",), "void"))])
=> {"'f": ("fn", ("int",), "int"), "'x": "int", "'y": "int", "'g": ("fn", (("fn", ("int",), "int"),), "void")}

+++ practice | Debug: types that promise too much
--- task
The starter's inferencer accepts a program it should reject. `fn f(x) { fn g() { return x; } let a = g() + 1; let b = g() + "s"; return 0; }` type checks, although `f(1)` would add `"s"` to an int at run time. And `infer_source("fn keep(v) { fn get() { return v; } return get; }")` gives `keep` the type `('a) -> () -> 'b`, which claims that the returned function produces a value of any type at all; the right type is `('a) -> () -> 'a`.

Find the bug in `generalize` and fix it.
--- starter
from dataclasses import dataclass

KEYWORDS = {"let", "fn", "return", "if", "else", "while", "print",
            "true", "false", "and", "or", "not"}
TWO_CHAR = {"==", "!=", "<=", ">=", "->"}
ONE_CHAR = set("+-*/%<>=(){},;:")
ESCAPES = {'"': '"', "\\": "\\", "n": "\n"}
DIGITS = "0123456789"
LETTERS = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ_"


@dataclass
class Token:
    kind: str
    text: str
    line: int
    col: int


class LexError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


def tokenize(source):
    tokens = []
    i = 0
    line = 1
    col = 1
    n = len(source)

    def advance(count):
        nonlocal i, line, col
        for _ in range(count):
            if source[i] == "\n":
                line += 1
                col = 1
            else:
                col += 1
            i += 1

    while i < n:
        ch = source[i]
        start_line, start_col = line, col
        if ch in " \t\r\n":
            advance(1)
        elif ch == "#":
            while i < n and source[i] != "\n":
                advance(1)
        elif ch in DIGITS:
            j = i
            while j < n and source[j] in DIGITS:
                j += 1
            tokens.append(Token("NUMBER", source[i:j], start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch in LETTERS:
            j = i
            while j < n and (source[j] in LETTERS or source[j] in DIGITS):
                j += 1
            word = source[i:j]
            kind = "KEYWORD" if word in KEYWORDS else "IDENT"
            tokens.append(Token(kind, word, start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch == '"':
            advance(1)
            chars = []
            while True:
                if i >= n or source[i] == "\n":
                    raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                c = source[i]
                if c == '"':
                    advance(1)
                    break
                if c == "\\":
                    if i + 1 >= n or source[i + 1] == "\n":
                        raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                    if source[i + 1] not in ESCAPES:
                        raise LexError("unknown escape", line, col)
                    chars.append(ESCAPES[source[i + 1]])
                    advance(2)
                else:
                    chars.append(c)
                    advance(1)
            tokens.append(Token("STRING", "".join(chars), start_line, start_col))
        elif source[i:i + 2] in TWO_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", source[i:i + 2], start_line, start_col))
            advance(2)
        elif ch in ONE_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", ch, start_line, start_col))
            advance(1)
        else:
            raise LexError(f"unexpected character {ch!r}", start_line, start_col)
    tokens.append(Token("EOF", "", line, col))
    return tokens

class ParseError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


COMPARE = ("==", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">=")
TYPES = ("int", "bool", "str")


class Parser:
    def __init__(self, tokens):
        self.tokens = tokens
        self.pos = 0

    def peek(self, ahead=0):
        return self.tokens[min(self.pos + ahead, len(self.tokens) - 1)]

    def at(self, *texts):
        tok = self.peek()
        return tok.kind in ("OP", "KEYWORD") and tok.text in texts

    def advance(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "EOF":
            self.pos += 1
        return tok

    def error(self, message):
        tok = self.peek()
        return ParseError(message, tok.line, tok.col)

    def expect(self, text):
        if not self.at(text):
            raise self.error(f"expected '{text}'")
        return self.advance()

    def expr(self):
        return self.or_expr()

    def or_expr(self):
        left = self.and_expr()
        while self.at("or"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.and_expr())
        return left

    def and_expr(self):
        left = self.not_expr()
        while self.at("and"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.not_expr())
        return left

    def not_expr(self):
        if self.at("not"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("not", self.not_expr())
        return self.compare()

    def compare(self):
        left = self.sum()
        if self.at(*COMPARE):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.sum())
            if self.at(*COMPARE):
                raise self.error("comparisons cannot be chained")
        return left

    def sum(self):
        left = self.product()
        while self.at("+", "-"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.product())
        return left

    def product(self):
        left = self.unary()
        while self.at("*", "/", "%"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.unary())
        return left

    def unary(self):
        if self.at("-"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("-", self.unary())
        return self.call()

    def call(self):
        expr = self.primary()
        while self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            args = []
            if not self.at(")"):
                args.append(self.expr())
                while self.at(","):
                    self.advance()
                    args.append(self.expr())
            self.expect(")")
            expr = Call(expr, args)
        return expr

    def primary(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind == "NUMBER":
            self.advance()
            return Num(int(tok.text))
        if tok.kind == "STRING":
            self.advance()
            return Str(tok.text)
        if tok.kind == "IDENT":
            self.advance()
            return Var(tok.text)
        if self.at("true", "false"):
            self.advance()
            return Bool(tok.text == "true")
        if self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            inner = self.expr()
            self.expect(")")
            return inner
        raise self.error("expected an expression")

    def program(self):
        stmts = []
        while self.peek().kind != "EOF":
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        return Program(stmts)

    def statement(self):
        if self.at("let"):
            return self.let_stmt()
        if self.at("print"):
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Print(value)
        if self.at("if"):
            return self.if_stmt()
        if self.at("while"):
            self.advance()
            cond = self.expr()
            return While(cond, self.block())
        if self.at("fn"):
            return self.fn_stmt()
        if self.at("return"):
            self.advance()
            value = None if self.at(";") else self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Return(value)
        nxt = self.peek(1)
        if self.peek().kind == "IDENT" and nxt.kind == "OP" and nxt.text == "=":
            name = self.advance().text
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Assign(name, value)
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return ExprStmt(value)

    def name(self):
        if self.peek().kind != "IDENT":
            raise self.error("expected a name")
        return self.advance().text

    def type_name(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "IDENT" or tok.text not in TYPES:
            raise self.error("expected a type")
        return self.advance().text

    def let_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        self.expect("=")
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return Let(name, type_, value)

    def if_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        cond = self.expr()
        then = self.block()
        else_ = None
        if self.at("else"):
            self.advance()
            else_ = self.if_stmt() if self.at("if") else self.block()
        return If(cond, then, else_)

    def block(self):
        self.expect("{")
        stmts = []
        while not self.at("}"):
            if self.peek().kind == "EOF":
                raise self.error("expected '}'")
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        self.advance()
        return Block(stmts)

    def param(self):
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        return (name, type_)

    def fn_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        self.expect("(")
        params = []
        if not self.at(")"):
            params.append(self.param())
            while self.at(","):
                self.advance()
                params.append(self.param())
        self.expect(")")
        ret = None
        if self.at("->"):
            self.advance()
            ret = self.type_name()
        return Fn(name, params, ret, self.block())


def parse_program(tokens):
    return Parser(tokens).program()


class CometError(Exception):
    pass


def comet_div(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q


def comet_mod(a, b):
    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TVar:
    name: str


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TCon:
    name: str


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TFun:
    params: tuple
    ret: object


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Scheme:
    vars: tuple
    type: object


INT, BOOL, STR, VOID = TCon("int"), TCon("bool"), TCon("str"), TCon("void")


class TypeCheckError(Exception):
    pass


def type_vars(t, found=None):
    """The names of the type variables in t, in order of first appearance."""
    if found is None:
        found = []
    if isinstance(t, TVar):
        if t.name not in found:
            found.append(t.name)
    elif isinstance(t, TFun):
        for p in t.params:
            type_vars(p, found)
        type_vars(t.ret, found)

    return found


def show_type(t, names=None):
    if names is None:
        names = {v: "'" + chr(ord("a") + i) for i, v in enumerate(type_vars(t))}
    if isinstance(t, TVar):
        return names.get(t.name, t.name)
    if isinstance(t, TFun):
        params = ", ".join(show_type(p, names) for p in t.params)
        return f"({params}) -> {show_type(t.ret, names)}"

    return t.name


def always_returns(stmts):
    for stmt in stmts:
        if isinstance(stmt, Return):
            return True
        if isinstance(stmt, Block) and always_returns(stmt.stmts):
            return True
        if isinstance(stmt, If) and stmt.else_ is not None:
            if always_returns([stmt.then]) and always_returns([stmt.else_]):
                return True
    return False


class Inferencer:
    def __init__(self):
        self.subst = {}
        self.count = 0
        self.scopes = [{}]
        self.returns = []
        self.pending = []


    def fresh(self):
        self.count += 1
        return TVar(f"t{self.count}")

    def resolve(self, t):
        """t with every bound type variable replaced by what it is bound to, all the way down."""
        if isinstance(t, TVar):
            if t.name in self.subst:
                return self.resolve(self.subst[t.name])
            return t
        if isinstance(t, TFun):
            return TFun(tuple(self.resolve(p) for p in t.params), self.resolve(t.ret))

        return t

    def env_vars(self):
        """The type variables that are free somewhere in the current scopes."""
        found = set()
        for scope in self.scopes:
            for scheme in scope.values():
                found.update(v for v in type_vars(self.resolve(scheme.type)) if v not in scheme.vars)
        return found

    def occurs(self, name, t):
        return name in type_vars(self.resolve(t))

    def unify(self, a, b):
        a = self.resolve(a)
        b = self.resolve(b)
        if a == b:
            return
        if isinstance(a, TVar):
            if self.occurs(a.name, b):
                raise TypeCheckError(f"infinite type: {show_type(a)} would contain itself")
            self.subst[a.name] = b
            return
        if isinstance(b, TVar):
            self.unify(b, a)
            return
        if isinstance(a, TFun) and isinstance(b, TFun):
            if len(a.params) != len(b.params):
                raise TypeCheckError(f"a function of {len(a.params)} arguments is not one of {len(b.params)}")
            for p, q in zip(a.params, b.params):
                self.unify(p, q)
            self.unify(a.ret, b.ret)
            return
        raise TypeCheckError(f"type mismatch: {show_type(a)} and {show_type(b)}")

    def generalize(self, t):
        t = self.resolve(t)
        return Scheme(tuple(type_vars(t)), t)

    def instantiate(self, scheme):
        mapping = {v: self.fresh() for v in scheme.vars}
        return self.replace(self.resolve(scheme.type), mapping)

    def replace(self, t, mapping):
        if isinstance(t, TVar):
            return mapping.get(t.name, t)
        if isinstance(t, TFun):
            return TFun(tuple(self.replace(p, mapping) for p in t.params), self.replace(t.ret, mapping))
        return t

    # ---- the walk over the program, given ----

    def declare(self, name, scheme):
        if name in self.scopes[-1]:
            raise TypeCheckError(f"{name} is already declared in this scope")
        self.scopes[-1][name] = scheme

    def lookup(self, name):
        for scope in reversed(self.scopes):
            if name in scope:
                return scope[name]
        raise TypeCheckError(f"undefined variable {name}")

    def infer_program(self, program):
        for stmt in program.stmts:
            self.infer_stmt(stmt)
        self.settle_plus()

    def settle_plus(self):
        """Each '+' whose operand type is still unknown adds ints, like a default."""
        for t in self.pending:
            if isinstance(self.resolve(t), TVar):
                self.unify(t, INT)
        self.pending = []

    def infer_block(self, stmts):
        self.scopes.append({})
        try:
            for stmt in stmts:
                self.infer_stmt(stmt)
        finally:
            self.scopes.pop()

    def value(self, expr):
        t = self.infer_expr(expr)
        if self.resolve(t) == VOID:
            raise TypeCheckError("a call that returns nothing has no value")
        return t

    def infer_stmt(self, stmt):
        if isinstance(stmt, Let):
            t = self.value(stmt.expr)
            if stmt.type is not None:
                self.unify(t, TCon(stmt.type))
            self.declare(stmt.name, Scheme((), t))
        elif isinstance(stmt, Assign):
            scheme = self.lookup(stmt.name)
            if scheme.vars:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"cannot assign to the polymorphic function {stmt.name}")
            self.unify(scheme.type, self.value(stmt.expr))
        elif isinstance(stmt, Print):
            self.value(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, ExprStmt):
            self.infer_expr(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, If):
            self.unify(self.infer_expr(stmt.cond), BOOL)
            self.infer_stmt(stmt.then)
            if stmt.else_ is not None:
                self.infer_stmt(stmt.else_)
        elif isinstance(stmt, While):
            self.unify(self.infer_expr(stmt.cond), BOOL)
            self.infer_stmt(stmt.body)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Block):
            self.infer_block(stmt.stmts)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Return):
            if not self.returns:
                raise TypeCheckError("return outside a function")
            t = VOID if stmt.expr is None else self.value(stmt.expr)
            self.unify(t, self.returns[-1])
        elif isinstance(stmt, Fn):
            self.infer_fn(stmt)

    def infer_fn(self, stmt):
        params = [TCon(t) if t is not None else self.fresh() for _, t in stmt.params]
        ret = TCon(stmt.ret) if stmt.ret is not None else self.fresh()
        fn_type = TFun(tuple(params), ret)
        self.declare(stmt.name, Scheme((), fn_type))
        self.scopes.append({})
        self.returns.append(ret)
        try:
            for (name, _), t in zip(stmt.params, params):
                self.declare(name, Scheme((), t))
            for inner in stmt.body.stmts:
                self.infer_stmt(inner)
        finally:
            self.returns.pop()
            self.scopes.pop()
        if not always_returns(stmt.body.stmts):
            self.unify(ret, VOID)
        self.settle_plus()
        del self.scopes[-1][stmt.name]
        self.scopes[-1][stmt.name] = self.generalize(fn_type)

    def infer_expr(self, expr):
        if isinstance(expr, Num):
            return INT
        if isinstance(expr, Str):
            return STR
        if isinstance(expr, Bool):
            return BOOL
        if isinstance(expr, Var):
            return self.instantiate(self.lookup(expr.name))
        if isinstance(expr, Unary):
            wanted = INT if expr.op == "-" else BOOL
            self.unify(self.infer_expr(expr.expr), wanted)
            return wanted
        if isinstance(expr, Binary):
            return self.infer_binary(expr)
        if isinstance(expr, Call):
            callee = self.infer_expr(expr.callee)
            args = tuple(self.value(arg) for arg in expr.args)
            result = self.fresh()
            self.unify(callee, TFun(args, result))
            return result
        raise TypeCheckError(f"unknown expression {type(expr).__name__}")

    def infer_binary(self, expr):
        op = expr.op
        left = self.value(expr.left)
        right = self.value(expr.right)
        if op in ("and", "or"):
            self.unify(left, BOOL)
            self.unify(right, BOOL)
            return BOOL
        if op in ("==", "!="):
            self.unify(left, right)
            return BOOL
        if op == "+":
            self.unify(left, right)
            t = self.resolve(left)
            if isinstance(t, TVar):
                self.pending.append(t)
            elif t not in (INT, STR):
                raise TypeCheckError(f"'+' needs two ints or two strs, not {show_type(t)}")
            return t
        self.unify(left, INT)
        self.unify(right, INT)
        return BOOL if op in ("<", "<=", ">", ">=") else INT


def infer_source(source):
    """The inferred type of every top-level name, as text."""
    inf = Inferencer()
    inf.infer_program(parse_program(tokenize(source)))
    return {name: show_type(inf.resolve(s.type)) for name, s in inf.scopes[-1].items()}


def type_error(source):
    try:
        infer_source(source)
    except TypeCheckError as e:
        return str(e)
    return None
