from dataclasses import dataclass

KEYWORDS = {"let", "fn", "return", "if", "else", "while", "print",
            "true", "false", "and", "or", "not"}
TWO_CHAR = {"==", "!=", "<=", ">=", "->"}
ONE_CHAR = set("+-*/%<>=(){},;:")
ESCAPES = {'"': '"', "\\": "\\", "n": "\n"}
DIGITS = "0123456789"
LETTERS = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ_"


@dataclass
class Token:
    kind: str
    text: str
    line: int
    col: int


class LexError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


def tokenize(source):
    tokens = []
    i = 0
    line = 1
    col = 1
    n = len(source)

    def advance(count):
        nonlocal i, line, col
        for _ in range(count):
            if source[i] == "\n":
                line += 1
                col = 1
            else:
                col += 1
            i += 1

    while i < n:
        ch = source[i]
        start_line, start_col = line, col
        if ch in " \t\r\n":
            advance(1)
        elif ch == "#":
            while i < n and source[i] != "\n":
                advance(1)
        elif ch in DIGITS:
            j = i
            while j < n and source[j] in DIGITS:
                j += 1
            tokens.append(Token("NUMBER", source[i:j], start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch in LETTERS:
            j = i
            while j < n and (source[j] in LETTERS or source[j] in DIGITS):
                j += 1
            word = source[i:j]
            kind = "KEYWORD" if word in KEYWORDS else "IDENT"
            tokens.append(Token(kind, word, start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch == '"':
            advance(1)
            chars = []
            while True:
                if i >= n or source[i] == "\n":
                    raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                c = source[i]
                if c == '"':
                    advance(1)
                    break
                if c == "\\":
                    if i + 1 >= n or source[i + 1] == "\n":
                        raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                    if source[i + 1] not in ESCAPES:
                        raise LexError("unknown escape", line, col)
                    chars.append(ESCAPES[source[i + 1]])
                    advance(2)
                else:
                    chars.append(c)
                    advance(1)
            tokens.append(Token("STRING", "".join(chars), start_line, start_col))
        elif source[i:i + 2] in TWO_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", source[i:i + 2], start_line, start_col))
            advance(2)
        elif ch in ONE_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", ch, start_line, start_col))
            advance(1)
        else:
            raise LexError(f"unexpected character {ch!r}", start_line, start_col)
    tokens.append(Token("EOF", "", line, col))
    return tokens

class ParseError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


COMPARE = ("==", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">=")
TYPES = ("int", "bool", "str")


class Parser:
    def __init__(self, tokens):
        self.tokens = tokens
        self.pos = 0

    def peek(self, ahead=0):
        return self.tokens[min(self.pos + ahead, len(self.tokens) - 1)]

    def at(self, *texts):
        tok = self.peek()
        return tok.kind in ("OP", "KEYWORD") and tok.text in texts

    def advance(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "EOF":
            self.pos += 1
        return tok

    def error(self, message):
        tok = self.peek()
        return ParseError(message, tok.line, tok.col)

    def expect(self, text):
        if not self.at(text):
            raise self.error(f"expected '{text}'")
        return self.advance()

    def expr(self):
        return self.or_expr()

    def or_expr(self):
        left = self.and_expr()
        while self.at("or"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.and_expr())
        return left

    def and_expr(self):
        left = self.not_expr()
        while self.at("and"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.not_expr())
        return left

    def not_expr(self):
        if self.at("not"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("not", self.not_expr())
        return self.compare()

    def compare(self):
        left = self.sum()
        if self.at(*COMPARE):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.sum())
            if self.at(*COMPARE):
                raise self.error("comparisons cannot be chained")
        return left

    def sum(self):
        left = self.product()
        while self.at("+", "-"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.product())
        return left

    def product(self):
        left = self.unary()
        while self.at("*", "/", "%"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.unary())
        return left

    def unary(self):
        if self.at("-"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("-", self.unary())
        return self.call()

    def call(self):
        expr = self.primary()
        while self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            args = []
            if not self.at(")"):
                args.append(self.expr())
                while self.at(","):
                    self.advance()
                    args.append(self.expr())
            self.expect(")")
            expr = Call(expr, args)
        return expr

    def primary(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind == "NUMBER":
            self.advance()
            return Num(int(tok.text))
        if tok.kind == "STRING":
            self.advance()
            return Str(tok.text)
        if tok.kind == "IDENT":
            self.advance()
            return Var(tok.text)
        if self.at("true", "false"):
            self.advance()
            return Bool(tok.text == "true")
        if self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            inner = self.expr()
            self.expect(")")
            return inner
        raise self.error("expected an expression")

    def program(self):
        stmts = []
        while self.peek().kind != "EOF":
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        return Program(stmts)

    def statement(self):
        if self.at("let"):
            return self.let_stmt()
        if self.at("print"):
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Print(value)
        if self.at("if"):
            return self.if_stmt()
        if self.at("while"):
            self.advance()
            cond = self.expr()
            return While(cond, self.block())
        if self.at("fn"):
            return self.fn_stmt()
        if self.at("return"):
            self.advance()
            value = None if self.at(";") else self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Return(value)
        nxt = self.peek(1)
        if self.peek().kind == "IDENT" and nxt.kind == "OP" and nxt.text == "=":
            name = self.advance().text
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Assign(name, value)
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return ExprStmt(value)

    def name(self):
        if self.peek().kind != "IDENT":
            raise self.error("expected a name")
        return self.advance().text

    def type_name(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "IDENT" or tok.text not in TYPES:
            raise self.error("expected a type")
        return self.advance().text

    def let_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        self.expect("=")
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return Let(name, type_, value)

    def if_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        cond = self.expr()
        then = self.block()
        else_ = None
        if self.at("else"):
            self.advance()
            else_ = self.if_stmt() if self.at("if") else self.block()
        return If(cond, then, else_)

    def block(self):
        self.expect("{")
        stmts = []
        while not self.at("}"):
            if self.peek().kind == "EOF":
                raise self.error("expected '}'")
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        self.advance()
        return Block(stmts)

    def param(self):
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        return (name, type_)

    def fn_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        self.expect("(")
        params = []
        if not self.at(")"):
            params.append(self.param())
            while self.at(","):
                self.advance()
                params.append(self.param())
        self.expect(")")
        ret = None
        if self.at("->"):
            self.advance()
            ret = self.type_name()
        return Fn(name, params, ret, self.block())


def parse_program(tokens):
    return Parser(tokens).program()


class CometError(Exception):
    pass


def comet_div(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q


def comet_mod(a, b):
    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TVar:
    name: str


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TCon:
    name: str


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TFun:
    params: tuple
    ret: object


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Scheme:
    vars: tuple
    type: object


INT, BOOL, STR, VOID = TCon("int"), TCon("bool"), TCon("str"), TCon("void")


class TypeCheckError(Exception):
    pass


def type_vars(t, found=None):
    """The names of the type variables in t, in order of first appearance."""
    if found is None:
        found = []
    if isinstance(t, TVar):
        if t.name not in found:
            found.append(t.name)
    elif isinstance(t, TFun):
        for p in t.params:
            type_vars(p, found)
        type_vars(t.ret, found)

    return found


def show_type(t, names=None):
    if names is None:
        names = {v: "'" + chr(ord("a") + i) for i, v in enumerate(type_vars(t))}
    if isinstance(t, TVar):
        return names.get(t.name, t.name)
    if isinstance(t, TFun):
        params = ", ".join(show_type(p, names) for p in t.params)
        return f"({params}) -> {show_type(t.ret, names)}"

    return t.name


def always_returns(stmts):
    for stmt in stmts:
        if isinstance(stmt, Return):
            return True
        if isinstance(stmt, Block) and always_returns(stmt.stmts):
            return True
        if isinstance(stmt, If) and stmt.else_ is not None:
            if always_returns([stmt.then]) and always_returns([stmt.else_]):
                return True
    return False


class Inferencer:
    def __init__(self):
        self.subst = {}
        self.count = 0
        self.scopes = [{}]
        self.returns = []
        self.pending = []


    def fresh(self):
        self.count += 1
        return TVar(f"t{self.count}")

    def resolve(self, t):
        """t with every bound type variable replaced by what it is bound to, all the way down."""
        if isinstance(t, TVar):
            if t.name in self.subst:
                return self.resolve(self.subst[t.name])
            return t
        if isinstance(t, TFun):
            return TFun(tuple(self.resolve(p) for p in t.params), self.resolve(t.ret))

        return t

    def env_vars(self):
        """The type variables that are free somewhere in the current scopes."""
        found = set()
        for scope in self.scopes:
            for scheme in scope.values():
                found.update(v for v in type_vars(self.resolve(scheme.type)) if v not in scheme.vars)
        return found

    def occurs(self, name, t):
        return name in type_vars(self.resolve(t))

    def unify(self, a, b):
        a = self.resolve(a)
        b = self.resolve(b)
        if a == b:
            return
        if isinstance(a, TVar):
            if self.occurs(a.name, b):
                raise TypeCheckError(f"infinite type: {show_type(a)} would contain itself")
            self.subst[a.name] = b
            return
        if isinstance(b, TVar):
            self.unify(b, a)
            return
        if isinstance(a, TFun) and isinstance(b, TFun):
            if len(a.params) != len(b.params):
                raise TypeCheckError(f"a function of {len(a.params)} arguments is not one of {len(b.params)}")
            for p, q in zip(a.params, b.params):
                self.unify(p, q)
            self.unify(a.ret, b.ret)
            return
        raise TypeCheckError(f"type mismatch: {show_type(a)} and {show_type(b)}")

    def generalize(self, t):
        t = self.resolve(t)
        env = self.env_vars()
        return Scheme(tuple(v for v in type_vars(t) if v not in env), t)

    def instantiate(self, scheme):
        mapping = {v: self.fresh() for v in scheme.vars}
        return self.replace(self.resolve(scheme.type), mapping)

    def replace(self, t, mapping):
        if isinstance(t, TVar):
            return mapping.get(t.name, t)
        if isinstance(t, TFun):
            return TFun(tuple(self.replace(p, mapping) for p in t.params), self.replace(t.ret, mapping))
        return t

    # ---- the walk over the program, given ----

    def declare(self, name, scheme):
        if name in self.scopes[-1]:
            raise TypeCheckError(f"{name} is already declared in this scope")
        self.scopes[-1][name] = scheme

    def lookup(self, name):
        for scope in reversed(self.scopes):
            if name in scope:
                return scope[name]
        raise TypeCheckError(f"undefined variable {name}")

    def infer_program(self, program):
        for stmt in program.stmts:
            self.infer_stmt(stmt)
        self.settle_plus()

    def settle_plus(self):
        """Each '+' whose operand type is still unknown adds ints, like a default."""
        for t in self.pending:
            if isinstance(self.resolve(t), TVar):
                self.unify(t, INT)
        self.pending = []

    def infer_block(self, stmts):
        self.scopes.append({})
        try:
            for stmt in stmts:
                self.infer_stmt(stmt)
        finally:
            self.scopes.pop()

    def value(self, expr):
        t = self.infer_expr(expr)
        if self.resolve(t) == VOID:
            raise TypeCheckError("a call that returns nothing has no value")
        return t

    def infer_stmt(self, stmt):
        if isinstance(stmt, Let):
            t = self.value(stmt.expr)
            if stmt.type is not None:
                self.unify(t, TCon(stmt.type))
            self.declare(stmt.name, Scheme((), t))
        elif isinstance(stmt, Assign):
            scheme = self.lookup(stmt.name)
            if scheme.vars:
                raise TypeCheckError(f"cannot assign to the polymorphic function {stmt.name}")
            self.unify(scheme.type, self.value(stmt.expr))
        elif isinstance(stmt, Print):
            self.value(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, ExprStmt):
            self.infer_expr(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, If):
            self.unify(self.infer_expr(stmt.cond), BOOL)
            self.infer_stmt(stmt.then)
            if stmt.else_ is not None:
                self.infer_stmt(stmt.else_)
        elif isinstance(stmt, While):
            self.unify(self.infer_expr(stmt.cond), BOOL)
            self.infer_stmt(stmt.body)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Block):
            self.infer_block(stmt.stmts)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Return):
            if not self.returns:
                raise TypeCheckError("return outside a function")
            t = VOID if stmt.expr is None else self.value(stmt.expr)
            self.unify(t, self.returns[-1])
        elif isinstance(stmt, Fn):
            self.infer_fn(stmt)

    def infer_fn(self, stmt):
        params = [TCon(t) if t is not None else self.fresh() for _, t in stmt.params]
        ret = TCon(stmt.ret) if stmt.ret is not None else self.fresh()
        fn_type = TFun(tuple(params), ret)
        self.declare(stmt.name, Scheme((), fn_type))
        self.scopes.append({})
        self.returns.append(ret)
        try:
            for (name, _), t in zip(stmt.params, params):
                self.declare(name, Scheme((), t))
            for inner in stmt.body.stmts:
                self.infer_stmt(inner)
        finally:
            self.returns.pop()
            self.scopes.pop()
        if not always_returns(stmt.body.stmts):
            self.unify(ret, VOID)
        self.settle_plus()
        del self.scopes[-1][stmt.name]
        self.scopes[-1][stmt.name] = self.generalize(fn_type)

    def infer_expr(self, expr):
        if isinstance(expr, Num):
            return INT
        if isinstance(expr, Str):
            return STR
        if isinstance(expr, Bool):
            return BOOL
        if isinstance(expr, Var):
            return self.instantiate(self.lookup(expr.name))
        if isinstance(expr, Unary):
            wanted = INT if expr.op == "-" else BOOL
            self.unify(self.infer_expr(expr.expr), wanted)
            return wanted
        if isinstance(expr, Binary):
            return self.infer_binary(expr)
        if isinstance(expr, Call):
            callee = self.infer_expr(expr.callee)
            args = tuple(self.value(arg) for arg in expr.args)
            result = self.fresh()
            self.unify(callee, TFun(args, result))
            return result
        raise TypeCheckError(f"unknown expression {type(expr).__name__}")

    def infer_binary(self, expr):
        op = expr.op
        left = self.value(expr.left)
        right = self.value(expr.right)
        if op in ("and", "or"):
            self.unify(left, BOOL)
            self.unify(right, BOOL)
            return BOOL
        if op in ("==", "!="):
            self.unify(left, right)
            return BOOL
        if op == "+":
            self.unify(left, right)
            t = self.resolve(left)
            if isinstance(t, TVar):
                self.pending.append(t)
            elif t not in (INT, STR):
                raise TypeCheckError(f"'+' needs two ints or two strs, not {show_type(t)}")
            return t
        self.unify(left, INT)
        self.unify(right, INT)
        return BOOL if op in ("<", "<=", ">", ">=") else INT


def infer_source(source):
    """The inferred type of every top-level name, as text."""
    inf = Inferencer()
    inf.infer_program(parse_program(tokenize(source)))
    return {name: show_type(inf.resolve(s.type)) for name, s in inf.scopes[-1].items()}


def type_error(source):
    try:
        infer_source(source)
    except TypeCheckError as e:
        return str(e)
    return None
--- hint
Which type variables of `get`'s type may become parameters of its scheme? Is v's type variable one of them, while `v` is still in scope?
--- hint
Only variables that are not free in the current scopes may be generalized. The inferencer already computes those with `self.env_vars()`.

+++ practice | Unification with union-find
--- task
A dictionary substitution can be slow: after `'a0 = 'a1`, `'a0 = 'a2`, `'a0 = 'a3`, … each new equation must follow a longer chain of bindings from `'a0`, so n equations cost O(n²). Union-find, from DSA I, keeps each class of equal variables as a tree with path compression and union by size, and makes this nearly linear.

Use the representation of the first practice problem (constants, `"'x"` variables, `("fn", params, ret)`). Write `solve_fast(equations, queries)`: unify all the equations, then return a list with the fully resolved type of each query variable, or `None` in place of a type that still contains a variable. Return `None` instead of the list if the equations have no solution (including the occurs check). A check solves 30,000 equations `'a0 = 'ai` followed by `'a29999 = int`, which a quadratic solution cannot finish in time.

Suggested design: a class with a `parent` dictionary for the union-find forest, and a `bound` dictionary from the root of a class to the non-variable type that class equals, if any.
--- starter
def solve_fast(equations, queries):
    raise NotImplementedError("solve_fast is not written yet")
--- solution
def is_var(t):
    return isinstance(t, str) and t.startswith("'")


class UnionFind:
    def __init__(self):
        self.parent = {}
        self.size = {}
        self.bound = {}

    def find(self, v):
        if v not in self.parent:
            self.parent[v] = v
            self.size[v] = 1
        root = v
        while self.parent[root] != root:
            root = self.parent[root]
        while self.parent[v] != root:
            self.parent[v], v = root, self.parent[v]
        return root

    def shallow(self, t):
        if is_var(t):
            root = self.find(t)
            return self.bound.get(root, root)
        return t

    def occurs(self, root, t):
        todo = [t]
        while todo:
            t = self.shallow(todo.pop())
            if t == root:
                return True
            if isinstance(t, tuple):
                todo.extend(t[1])
                todo.append(t[2])
        return False

    def unify(self, a, b):
        todo = [(a, b)]
        while todo:
            a, b = todo.pop()
            a = self.shallow(a)
            b = self.shallow(b)
            if a == b:
                continue
            if is_var(a) and is_var(b):
                if self.size[a] < self.size[b]:
                    a, b = b, a
                self.parent[b] = a
                self.size[a] += self.size[b]
            elif is_var(a) or is_var(b):
                if is_var(b):
                    a, b = b, a
                if self.occurs(a, b):
                    return False
                self.bound[a] = b
            elif isinstance(a, tuple) and isinstance(b, tuple) and len(a[1]) == len(b[1]):
                todo.extend(zip(a[1], b[1]))
                todo.append((a[2], b[2]))
            else:
                return False
        return True

    def resolve(self, t):
        t = self.shallow(t)
        if is_var(t):
            return None
        if isinstance(t, tuple):
            params = tuple(self.resolve(p) for p in t[1])
            ret = self.resolve(t[2])
            if ret is None or None in params:
                return None
            return ("fn", params, ret)
        return t


def solve_fast(equations, queries):
    uf = UnionFind()
    for a, b in equations:
        if not uf.unify(a, b):
            return None
    return [uf.resolve(q) for q in queries]
--- hint
`find(v)` walks up the parents to the root and then points every visited variable straight at it. The "shallow" form of a type is: for a variable, the bound type of its root if there is one, otherwise the root itself; any other type is its own shallow form.
--- hint
Unify with an explicit stack of pairs instead of recursion. Two roots: link the smaller class under the larger. A root and a non-variable type: run the occurs check (look for the root among the shallow forms inside the type), then record the type in `bound`. Two function types: push their parts.
--- check test | 30,000 equations
solve_fast([("'a0", "'a%d" % i) for i in range(1, 30000)] + [("'a29999", "int")], ["'a0", "'a15000", "'zz"]) == ["int", "int", None]
--- check case | Function types
solve_fast([("'f", ("fn", ("'x",), "'y")), ("'x", "int"), ("'y", "'x")], ["'f", "'y"])
=> [("fn", ("int",), "int"), "int"]
--- check test | The occurs check and contradictions
solve_fast([("'a", ("fn", ("'b",), "int")), ("'b", "'a")], ["'a"]) is None and solve_fast([("'a", "int"), ("'b", "'a"), ("'b", "str")], ["'a"]) is None
--- check test | Unknown results and the empty system
solve_fast([("'p", ("fn", ("'q",), "int"))], ["'p", "'q"]) == [None, None] and solve_fast([], ["'k"]) == [None]
--- check test | A long chain built backwards
solve_fast([("'b%d" % (i + 1), "'b%d" % i) for i in range(20000)] + [("'b0", ("fn", (), "bool"))], ["'b20000"]) == [("fn", (), "bool")]

+++ question | The type of twice
--- ask
What is the principal type of `fn twice(f, x) { return f(f(x)); }`? Write it the way this lesson prints types.
--- answer
(('a) -> 'a, 'a) -> 'a
--- why
`f(x)` makes f a function from x's type, 'a, to some 'b. Then `f(f(x))` passes that 'b to f, so 'b must equal 'a. The result of the outer call is again 'a. So twice takes a function from 'a to 'a and an 'a, and returns an 'a.

+++ question | Why let is not generalized
--- ask
Comet does not generalize `let g = id;`, even though `id` has type ∀a. (a) -> a. What would go wrong if it did?
--- choice
Nothing: it is only a speed optimisation.
--- choice correct
g could be assigned a function on ints and then called with a bool, and the checker would accept a program that fails at run time.
--- choice
The occurs check would reject every program that uses g.
--- choice
g would be printed with the wrong type name.
--- why
A polymorphic g can be instantiated differently at each use. `g = inc;` would unify one instance with (int) -> int, and `g(true)` would use another, fresh instance, so both pass. At run time g holds inc, and `true + 1` fails. This is the unsoundness that ML's value restriction removes: variables that can change stay monomorphic.

+++ question | What the occurs check prevents
--- ask
What happens if unification binds t1 to fn(t1) -> t2 without the occurs check, and the inferencer then resolves t1?
--- choice
t1 resolves to fn(t1) -> t2 and inference continues normally.
--- choice correct
Resolving replaces t1 inside the result by fn(t1) -> t2 again and again, without end, because the type would have to be infinite.
--- choice
The binding is ignored and t1 stays unknown.
--- choice
t2 is set to t1.
--- why
A substitution with t1 ↦ fn(t1) -> t2 has no finite fixed point: every resolution step makes a bigger type that still contains t1. In the lesson's recursive `resolve` that ends with Python's recursion limit. The occurs check refuses the binding, and the program, such as `fn f(x) { return x(x); }`, is reported as a type error.
=== plc-11 | Functional programming: immutability, recursion, folds and algebraic data types
--- teach
The last four lessons built closures and a type system in the style of ML. Those two features are the heart of **functional programming**, a way of writing programs that languages such as ML, OCaml, Haskell, F#, Elm and Clojure are designed around, and that every mainstream language has borrowed from. This lesson teaches its core ideas in Python: pure functions, immutable data, algebraic data types with pattern matching, and the higher-order functions map, filter and fold, with the proofs and costs that go with them.

### Pure functions and immutable data

A function is **pure** when its result depends only on its arguments and calling it changes nothing: no assignment to outside variables, no mutation of its arguments, no printing. `len` is pure; `list.append` is not. An expression is **referentially transparent**, a term with [[a history|reftrans]], when it can be replaced by its value without changing what the program does. With pure functions, that is always true, so you can reason about code the way you reason about algebra: if `area(3, 4)` is 12 once, it is 12 everywhere.

Data is **immutable** when it cannot change after it is made. Python's tuples, strings and frozen dataclasses are immutable. A program that never mutates can **share** freely: two values can use the same part without either one being surprised later. In everyday words, a pure function is a vending machine that always gives the same can for the same coins, and immutable data is a printed page instead of a whiteboard: to change it you print a new page, and everyone who holds the old one still has exactly what they had.

### Algebraic data types

An **algebraic data type** is a type built from two operations:

- a **product** holds several values together: a point is an x **and** a y;
- a **sum** is one of several alternatives: a shape is a circle **or** a rectangle.

Each alternative of a sum is a **constructor** with its own fields. In Python each constructor is a frozen dataclass:

```python
from dataclasses import dataclass

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Circle:
    r: float

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Rect:
    w: float
    h: float

def area(shape):
    match shape:
        case Circle(r=r):
            return 3.14159 * r * r
        case Rect(w=w, h=h) if w == h:
            return w * w
        case Rect(w=w, h=h):
            return w * h
        case _:
            raise TypeError(f"not a shape: {shape!r}")

print(area(Rect(2, 3)), round(area(Circle(1)), 2))   # 6 3.14
```

`match` tries each `case` in order. A **class pattern** such as `Rect(w=w, h=h)` checks the constructor and binds the fields to names; `if w == h` is a **guard** that must also hold. You have used an algebraic data type all course: Comet's AST is a sum of node kinds, each a product of its fields. [[The name "algebraic"|algebraic]] comes from counting values.

A `match` should be **exhaustive**: it should handle every constructor. ML and Haskell compilers warn when a case is missing. Python does not check, so end with `case _:` that raises, and a missing case at least fails loudly.

### Lists as an algebraic data type

The classic functional list is a sum of two constructors: `Nil`, the empty list, and `Cons(head, tail)`, one item in front of a smaller list. [1, 2, 3] is `Cons(1, Cons(2, Cons(3, Nil())))`. It is a linked list whose cells never change. Putting an item in front makes one new cell that points to the old list, which stays valid and is shared: a **persistent** data structure, one where old versions survive every update.

### Recursion and structural induction

A function on an algebraic type is naturally defined by one case per constructor, calling itself on the smaller parts. The matching proof method is **structural induction**: to prove a property P for every list, prove P(Nil), and prove that P(t) implies P(Cons(h, t)).

For example, define `length(Nil) = 0`, `length(Cons(h, t)) = 1 + length(t)`, and `append(Nil, b) = b`, `append(Cons(h, t), b) = Cons(h, append(t, b))`. Claim: length(append(a, b)) = length(a) + length(b) for all lists a and b.

- **Base case**, a = Nil: length(append(Nil, b)) = length(b) = 0 + length(b).
- **Step**, a = Cons(h, t), assuming the claim for t: length(append(Cons(h, t), b)) = length(Cons(h, append(t, b))) = 1 + length(append(t, b)) = 1 + length(t) + length(b) = length(Cons(h, t)) + length(b).

Every step is replacing equals by equals, which is only valid because the functions are pure.

### Map, filter and fold

Three higher-order functions capture most loops over a list:

- **map(f, xs)** applies f to every item: map(double, [1, 2, 3]) is [2, 4, 6].
- **filter(p, xs)** keeps the items for which p is true.
- **fold** combines all the items into one value, starting from an initial value. It comes in two directions:
  - **foldl(f, z, [x₁, …, xₙ])** = f(… f(f(z, x₁), x₂) …, xₙ): from the left, like a loop with an accumulator.
  - **foldr(f, z, [x₁, …, xₙ])** = f(x₁, f(x₂, … f(xₙ, z) …)): from the right, the shape of the list itself, with each `Cons` replaced by f and `Nil` by z.

The direction matters when f is not associative:

```python
from functools import reduce

def foldr_tuple(f, z, xs):
    return z if not xs else f(xs[0], foldr_tuple(f, z, xs[1:]))

print(reduce(lambda acc, x: acc - x, (10, 3, 2), 0))   # ((0 - 10) - 3) - 2 = -15
print(foldr_tuple(lambda x, acc: x - acc, 0, (10, 3, 2)))   # 10 - (3 - (2 - 0)) = 9
```

Python's `functools.reduce` is foldl. The recursive `foldr_tuple` shows the definition, but it copies the tuple at every step and uses one stack frame per item, so it is only good for showing the idea.

foldr is **universal** for lists: every function defined by structural recursion on lists is a foldr. Map is foldr with f(x, rest) = Cons(g(x), rest) and z = Nil; filter keeps or skips x in the same way; append(a, b) is foldr(Cons, b, a). A program built from these parts has its loops written once, correctly, and can be reasoned about with laws. One law, **map fusion**: map(f, map(g, xs)) = map(λx. f(g(x)), xs). Proof by structural induction: both sides are Nil for Nil, and for Cons(h, t) both start with f(g(h)) followed by the two sides for t, which are equal by the induction hypothesis. Compilers use such laws to merge loops.

### Tail calls, and why Python needs loops here

foldl's recursive definition, foldl(f, z, Cons(h, t)) = foldl(f, f(z, h), t), ends in a call to itself with nothing left to do: a **tail call**, like lesson 8's practice problem. Languages with proper tail calls run it in constant stack space; it is a loop. Python has [[no tail-call elimination|python-tco]], and its stack holds about a thousand frames, so in Python, foldl is written as a `while` loop.

foldr is not tail recursive: after the recursive call returns, f still has to be applied. But a foldr over a list gives the same result as a foldl over the **reversed** list with the arguments of f swapped: both apply f to xₙ first and x₁ last. Reversing is itself a foldl, so foldr can be computed with loops only, in O(n) time and O(n) extra space, on lists of any length.

### What it costs

For persistent Cons lists of length n:

- putting an item in front, reading the head, and the tail: O(1);
- `append(a, b)`: O(length of a), because a's cells are copied, while b is shared, not copied;
- `reverse`, map, filter and both folds: O(n) time; foldl needs O(1) extra space, the loop-based foldr O(n) for the reversed copy;
- indexing the k-th item: O(k), unlike an array.

Sharing makes immutability cheap: keeping every old version costs only the new cells. Where a persistent structure needs to change something deep inside, it copies the path from the root to that place and shares the rest, **path copying**, which costs O(depth).

One practical note for the browser: a Cons list is a linked list, and dropping one of more than a few thousand cells in one go overflows the browser's stack, as DSA I showed for linked lists. So the long checks here take their big lists apart cell by cell when they are done. On a laptop this is never needed.

### Where it is used

- Haskell, OCaml and F# are built on these ideas; Clojure, Scala, Elixir and Erlang make immutable data the default. Rust's pattern matching on enums is `match` on algebraic data types, with exhaustiveness checked.
- Redux and React state updates are pure functions (old state, action) → new state: a foldl over the stream of actions. [[Git|git-persistent]] stores files and directories as immutable, shared objects.
- MapReduce and Spark are map and fold over data spread across a cluster, possible because pure functions can run anywhere, in any order.
- Compilers are written as pure passes over algebraic data types: parse, then check, then transform tree to tree. The Comet passes in this course are exactly that, and lessons 13 and 14 continue it.

**Watch out:**

- Mixing up foldl and foldr: with `-`, or with building a list, the order changes the answer.
- Forgetting the empty list. Every fold needs an initial value, and `reduce` without one raises on an empty sequence.
- Mutating data that is shared. If two versions share a Python list and one of them appends, the other changes too: use tuples or build a new list.
- Deep recursion in Python. A list of 10,000 items is fine for a loop and fatal for a recursive function.
- A `match` without a final `case _:`. A missing constructor then returns `None` silently.

::: context reftrans Where "referential transparency" comes from
The philosopher W. V. Quine used the term for positions in a sentence where one name can be swapped for another name of the same thing without changing the truth of the sentence. Christopher Strachey brought it into programming in 1967. In a referentially transparent language the compiler, like the reader, may replace a call by its result, compute it earlier or later, or share it between two uses, because no one can tell the difference.
:::

::: context algebraic Why "algebraic" data types
Count the values. A product of a type with 2 values and one with 3 has 2 × 3 = 6 values; a sum has 2 + 3 = 5. A type with no information, like Python's `None`, has 1 value and plays the role of the number 1. The laws of algebra then hold for types: a sum distributes over a product, just as a × (b + c) = a × b + a × c. A recursive type like the list solves an equation: L = 1 + item × L.
:::

::: context python-tco Why Python keeps every frame
Guido van Rossum explained in 2009 why Python will not eliminate tail calls: the reused frames would vanish from tracebacks, making errors harder to debug, and Python programmers write loops for iteration anyway. Scheme, by contrast, requires proper tail calls in its standard, and loops in Scheme are usually written as tail-recursive functions. JavaScript's ES2015 standard required them too, but most engines never implemented them.
:::

::: context git-persistent Git as a persistent data structure
A Git commit points to a tree object, which points to file contents and to subtrees, and every object is named by the hash of its contents, so it can never change. A new commit that edits one file creates new objects only along the path from that file to the root, and shares every other file and folder with the previous commit. That is path copying, and it is why keeping the entire history of a project is affordable.
:::
--- task
The starter gives the persistent list type: frozen dataclasses `Nil()` and `Cons(head, tail)`, the constant `NIL`, and two converters, `from_list(items)` and `to_list(lst)`, between Python lists and Cons lists. Write six functions. None may change an existing list, and all must work on lists of 100,000 items, so use loops, not recursion.

- `foldl(f, acc, lst)`: fold from the left, f(… f(f(acc, x₁), x₂) …, xₙ).
- `reverse(lst)`: a new list with the items in the opposite order, written with `foldl`.
- `foldr(f, acc, lst)`: fold from the right, f(x₁, f(x₂, … f(xₙ, acc) …)), without recursion.
- `map_list(f, lst)`, `filter_list(keep, lst)` and `append(a, b)`, each written with `foldr`. `append` must **share** b: the result's cells after a's items are b's own cells, not copies.

For example, `to_list(append(from_list([1, 2]), from_list([3])))` is `[1, 2, 3]`, and `foldr(lambda x, acc: x - acc, 0, from_list([10, 3, 2]))` is `9`.
--- starter

    return result

        lst = lst.tail

--- solution
from dataclasses import dataclass


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Nil:
    pass


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Cons:
    head: object
    tail: object


NIL = Nil()


def from_list(items):
    result = NIL
    for item in reversed(items):
        result = Cons(item, result)
    return result


def to_list(lst):
    items = []
    while isinstance(lst, Cons):
        items.append(lst.head)
        lst = lst.tail
    return items


def foldl(f, acc, lst):
    while isinstance(lst, Cons):
        acc = f(acc, lst.head)
        lst = lst.tail
    return acc


def reverse(lst):
    return foldl(lambda acc, x: Cons(x, acc), NIL, lst)


def foldr(f, acc, lst):
    return foldl(lambda a, x: f(x, a), acc, reverse(lst))


def map_list(f, lst):
    return foldr(lambda x, rest: Cons(f(x), rest), NIL, lst)


def filter_list(keep, lst):
    return foldr(lambda x, rest: Cons(x, rest) if keep(x) else rest, NIL, lst)


def append(a, b):
    return foldr(Cons, b, a)
--- hint
`foldl` is a `while` loop that walks `lst.tail` while `lst` is a `Cons`, replacing `acc` with `f(acc, lst.head)`. `reverse` is a foldl that builds a new list by putting each item in front of the accumulator.
--- hint
`foldr(f, acc, lst)` gives the same answer as a foldl over `reverse(lst)` whose step function calls `f(x, a)` with the arguments swapped.
--- hint
With foldr, `map_list` puts `f(x)` in front of the already built rest, `filter_list` puts x in front only when `keep(x)` is true, and `append(a, b)` is a foldr over a that starts from b and uses `Cons` itself as the step.
--- check case | foldl, from the left
foldl(lambda acc, x: acc - x, 0, from_list([10, 3, 2]))
=> -15
--- check case | foldr, from the right
foldr(lambda x, acc: x - acc, 0, from_list([10, 3, 2]))
=> 9
--- check case | foldr keeps the shape of the list
foldr(lambda x, acc: f"({x}{acc})", "", from_list([1, 2, 3]))
=> "(1(2(3)))"
--- check test | The empty list gives the initial value
foldl(lambda a, x: a + x, 7, NIL) == 7 and foldr(lambda x, a: a + x, 7, NIL) == 7 and reverse(NIL) == NIL and map_list(abs, NIL) == NIL and filter_list(bool, NIL) == NIL
--- check test | reverse, map_list and filter_list

+++ practice | Pattern matching on telemetry
--- task
A spacecraft's telemetry stream carries three kinds of reading, given in the starter as frozen dataclasses: `Temp(celsius)`, `Pressure(kpa)` and `Fault(code)`. Write three functions, using `match` with class patterns in `describe`:

- `describe(reading)`: `"HOT 95C"` for a temperature above 80, otherwise `"temp 20C"`; `"VACUUM"` for a pressure of exactly 0, otherwise `"pressure 101kPa"`; `"FAULT E7"` for a fault. Anything else raises `TypeError`.
- `fault_codes(readings)`: a tuple of the codes of the faults in a list of readings, in order, written with `map` and `filter`.
- `hottest(readings)`: the highest temperature in celsius among the readings, or `None` if there is no temperature reading, written with `functools.reduce`.

For example, `describe(Temp(95))` is `"HOT 95C"`.
--- starter

--- solution
from dataclasses import dataclass


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Temp:
    celsius: int


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Pressure:
    kpa: int


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Fault:
    code: str


from functools import reduce


def describe(reading):
    match reading:
        case Temp(celsius=c) if c > 80:
            return f"HOT {c}C"
        case Temp(celsius=c):
            return f"temp {c}C"
        case Pressure(kpa=0):
            return "VACUUM"
        case Pressure(kpa=p):
            return f"pressure {p}kPa"
        case Fault(code=code):
            return f"FAULT {code}"
        case _:
            raise TypeError(f"not a reading: {reading!r}")


def fault_codes(readings):
    return tuple(map(lambda r: r.code, filter(lambda r: isinstance(r, Fault), readings)))


def hottest(readings):
    def step(best, r):
        match r:
            case Temp(celsius=c) if best is None or c > best:
                return c
            case _:
                return best
    return reduce(step, readings, None)
--- hint
In `describe`, order the cases from specific to general: `case Temp(celsius=c) if c > 80:` comes before `case Temp(celsius=c):`, and a literal pattern `Pressure(kpa=0)` before `Pressure(kpa=p)`. Finish with `case _:` that raises.
--- hint
`fault_codes` filters with `isinstance(r, Fault)`, maps each fault to `r.code`, and turns the result into a tuple. `hottest` reduces with the initial value `None` and a step function that returns the reading's celsius when it is a `Temp` hotter than the best so far, and the best so far otherwise.
--- check test | describe covers every case
[describe(r) for r in [Temp(20), Pressure(101), Fault("E7"), Temp(95), Pressure(0), Temp(80)]] == ["temp 20C", "pressure 101kPa", "FAULT E7", "HOT 95C", "VACUUM", "temp 80C"]
--- check test | Anything else raises TypeError
raises(TypeError, lambda: describe(42)) and raises(TypeError, lambda: describe(None))
--- check case | fault_codes
fault_codes([Temp(20), Fault("E7"), Pressure(3), Fault("B2")])
=> ("E7", "B2")
--- check test | hottest, including below zero and no temperatures at all
hottest([Temp(20), Pressure(101), Temp(95), Fault("X")]) == 95 and hottest([Temp(-5), Temp(-9)]) == -5 and hottest([Pressure(1)]) is None and hottest([]) is None and fault_codes([]) == ()
--- check source | describe uses match
\bmatch\b

+++ practice | A fold over expression trees
--- task
foldr replaces each `Cons` of a list by a function. The same idea works for any algebraic data type: a **fold** over expression trees replaces each kind of node by a function that receives the node's fields, with its sub-expressions already folded. Write `fold_expr(expr, on)`, where `on` is a dictionary of functions:

- `on["num"](value)`, `on["str"](value)`, `on["bool"](value)`, `on["var"](name)` for the leaves;
- `on["unary"](op, inner)`, `on["binary"](op, left, right)` and `on["call"](callee, args)`, where `inner`, `left`, `right`, `callee` and every item of the list `args` are the results of folding the sub-expressions.

Then write three functions that take an expression's source text (the starter gives `parse_expr(source)`), each as one call of `fold_expr` with a suitable dictionary: `size(source)`, the number of nodes; `depth(source)`, the number of nodes on the longest path from the root to a leaf, where a leaf has depth 1; and `names(source)`, the sorted list of the distinct variable names used.

For example, `size("1 + 2 * x")` is 5 and `depth("1 + 2 * x")` is 3.
--- starter
from dataclasses import dataclass

KEYWORDS = {"let", "fn", "return", "if", "else", "while", "print",
            "true", "false", "and", "or", "not"}
TWO_CHAR = {"==", "!=", "<=", ">=", "->"}
ONE_CHAR = set("+-*/%<>=(){},;:")
ESCAPES = {'"': '"', "\\": "\\", "n": "\n"}
DIGITS = "0123456789"
LETTERS = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ_"


@dataclass
class Token:
    kind: str
    text: str
    line: int
    col: int


class LexError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


def tokenize(source):
    tokens = []
    i = 0
    line = 1
    col = 1
    n = len(source)

    def advance(count):
        nonlocal i, line, col
        for _ in range(count):
            if source[i] == "\n":
                line += 1
                col = 1
            else:
                col += 1
            i += 1

    while i < n:
        ch = source[i]
        start_line, start_col = line, col
        if ch in " \t\r\n":
            advance(1)
        elif ch == "#":
            while i < n and source[i] != "\n":
                advance(1)
        elif ch in DIGITS:
            j = i
            while j < n and source[j] in DIGITS:
                j += 1
            tokens.append(Token("NUMBER", source[i:j], start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch in LETTERS:
            j = i
            while j < n and (source[j] in LETTERS or source[j] in DIGITS):
                j += 1
            word = source[i:j]
            kind = "KEYWORD" if word in KEYWORDS else "IDENT"
            tokens.append(Token(kind, word, start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch == '"':
            advance(1)
            chars = []
            while True:
                if i >= n or source[i] == "\n":
                    raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                c = source[i]
                if c == '"':
                    advance(1)
                    break
                if c == "\\":
                    if i + 1 >= n or source[i + 1] == "\n":
                        raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                    if source[i + 1] not in ESCAPES:
                        raise LexError("unknown escape", line, col)
                    chars.append(ESCAPES[source[i + 1]])
                    advance(2)
                else:
                    chars.append(c)
                    advance(1)
            tokens.append(Token("STRING", "".join(chars), start_line, start_col))
        elif source[i:i + 2] in TWO_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", source[i:i + 2], start_line, start_col))
            advance(2)
        elif ch in ONE_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", ch, start_line, start_col))
            advance(1)
        else:
            raise LexError(f"unexpected character {ch!r}", start_line, start_col)
    tokens.append(Token("EOF", "", line, col))
    return tokens

class ParseError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


COMPARE = ("==", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">=")
TYPES = ("int", "bool", "str")


class Parser:
    def __init__(self, tokens):
        self.tokens = tokens
        self.pos = 0

    def peek(self, ahead=0):
        return self.tokens[min(self.pos + ahead, len(self.tokens) - 1)]

    def at(self, *texts):
        tok = self.peek()
        return tok.kind in ("OP", "KEYWORD") and tok.text in texts

    def advance(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "EOF":
            self.pos += 1
        return tok

    def error(self, message):
        tok = self.peek()
        return ParseError(message, tok.line, tok.col)

    def expect(self, text):
        if not self.at(text):
            raise self.error(f"expected '{text}'")
        return self.advance()

    def expr(self):
        return self.or_expr()

    def or_expr(self):
        left = self.and_expr()
        while self.at("or"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.and_expr())
        return left

    def and_expr(self):
        left = self.not_expr()
        while self.at("and"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.not_expr())
        return left

    def not_expr(self):
        if self.at("not"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("not", self.not_expr())
        return self.compare()

    def compare(self):
        left = self.sum()
        if self.at(*COMPARE):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.sum())
            if self.at(*COMPARE):
                raise self.error("comparisons cannot be chained")
        return left

    def sum(self):
        left = self.product()
        while self.at("+", "-"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.product())
        return left

    def product(self):
        left = self.unary()
        while self.at("*", "/", "%"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.unary())
        return left

    def unary(self):
        if self.at("-"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("-", self.unary())
        return self.call()

    def call(self):
        expr = self.primary()
        while self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            args = []
            if not self.at(")"):
                args.append(self.expr())
                while self.at(","):
                    self.advance()
                    args.append(self.expr())
            self.expect(")")
            expr = Call(expr, args)
        return expr

    def primary(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind == "NUMBER":
            self.advance()
            return Num(int(tok.text))
        if tok.kind == "STRING":
            self.advance()
            return Str(tok.text)
        if tok.kind == "IDENT":
            self.advance()
            return Var(tok.text)
        if self.at("true", "false"):
            self.advance()
            return Bool(tok.text == "true")
        if self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            inner = self.expr()
            self.expect(")")
            return inner
        raise self.error("expected an expression")

    def program(self):
        stmts = []
        while self.peek().kind != "EOF":
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        return Program(stmts)

    def statement(self):
        if self.at("let"):
            return self.let_stmt()
        if self.at("print"):
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Print(value)
        if self.at("if"):
            return self.if_stmt()
        if self.at("while"):
            self.advance()
            cond = self.expr()
            return While(cond, self.block())
        if self.at("fn"):
            return self.fn_stmt()
        if self.at("return"):
            self.advance()
            value = None if self.at(";") else self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Return(value)
        nxt = self.peek(1)
        if self.peek().kind == "IDENT" and nxt.kind == "OP" and nxt.text == "=":
            name = self.advance().text
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Assign(name, value)
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return ExprStmt(value)

    def name(self):
        if self.peek().kind != "IDENT":
            raise self.error("expected a name")
        return self.advance().text

    def type_name(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "IDENT" or tok.text not in TYPES:
            raise self.error("expected a type")
        return self.advance().text

    def let_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        self.expect("=")
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return Let(name, type_, value)

    def if_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        cond = self.expr()
        then = self.block()
        else_ = None
        if self.at("else"):
            self.advance()
            else_ = self.if_stmt() if self.at("if") else self.block()
        return If(cond, then, else_)

    def block(self):
        self.expect("{")
        stmts = []
        while not self.at("}"):
            if self.peek().kind == "EOF":
                raise self.error("expected '}'")
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        self.advance()
        return Block(stmts)

    def param(self):
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        return (name, type_)

    def fn_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        self.expect("(")
        params = []
        if not self.at(")"):
            params.append(self.param())
            while self.at(","):
                self.advance()
                params.append(self.param())
        self.expect(")")
        ret = None
        if self.at("->"):
            self.advance()
            ret = self.type_name()
        return Fn(name, params, ret, self.block())


def parse_program(tokens):
    return Parser(tokens).program()


class CometError(Exception):
    pass


def comet_div(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q


def comet_mod(a, b):
    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)


def parse_expr(source):
    return parse_program(tokenize(source + ";")).stmts[0].expr

    raise NotImplementedError("depth is not written yet")

    raise NotImplementedError("names is not written yet")

            self.advance()

        return self.call()

    def call(self):

    def primary(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind == "NUMBER":
            self.advance()
            return Num(int(tok.text))
        if tok.kind == "STRING":
            self.advance()
            return Str(tok.text)
        if tok.kind == "IDENT":
            self.advance()
            return Var(tok.text)
        if self.at("true", "false"):
            self.advance()
            return Bool(tok.text == "true")
        if self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            inner = self.expr()
            self.expect(")")
            return inner
        raise self.error("expected an expression")

    def program(self):
        stmts = []
        while self.peek().kind != "EOF":
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        return Program(stmts)

    def statement(self):
        if self.at("let"):
            return self.let_stmt()
        if self.at("print"):
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Print(value)
        if self.at("if"):
            return self.if_stmt()
        if self.at("while"):
            self.advance()
            cond = self.expr()
            return While(cond, self.block())
        if self.at("fn"):
            return self.fn_stmt()
        if self.at("return"):
            self.advance()
            value = None if self.at(";") else self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Return(value)
        nxt = self.peek(1)
        if self.peek().kind == "IDENT" and nxt.kind == "OP" and nxt.text == "=":
            name = self.advance().text
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Assign(name, value)
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return ExprStmt(value)

    def name(self):
        if self.peek().kind != "IDENT":
            raise self.error("expected a name")
        return self.advance().text

    def type_name(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "IDENT" or tok.text not in TYPES:
            raise self.error("expected a type")
        return self.advance().text

    def let_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        self.expect("=")
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return Let(name, type_, value)

    def if_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        cond = self.expr()
        then = self.block()
        else_ = None
        if self.at("else"):
            self.advance()
            else_ = self.if_stmt() if self.at("if") else self.block()
        return If(cond, then, else_)

    def block(self):
        self.expect("{")
        stmts = []
        while not self.at("}"):
            if self.peek().kind == "EOF":
                raise self.error("expected '}'")
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        self.advance()
        return Block(stmts)

    def param(self):
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        return (name, type_)

    def fn_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        self.expect("(")
        params = []
        if not self.at(")"):
            params.append(self.param())
            while self.at(","):
                self.advance()
                params.append(self.param())
        self.expect(")")
        ret = None
        if self.at("->"):
            self.advance()
            ret = self.type_name()
        return Fn(name, params, ret, self.block())


def parse_program(tokens):
    return Parser(tokens).program()


class CometError(Exception):
    pass


def comet_div(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q


def comet_mod(a, b):
    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)


def fold_expr(expr, on):
    match expr:
        case Num(value=v):
            return on["num"](v)
        case Str(value=v):
            return on["str"](v)
        case Bool(value=v):
            return on["bool"](v)
        case Var(name=n):
            return on["var"](n)
        case Unary(op=op, expr=inner):
            return on["unary"](op, fold_expr(inner, on))
        case Binary(op=op, left=l, right=r):
            return on["binary"](op, fold_expr(l, on), fold_expr(r, on))
        case Call(callee=c, args=args):
            return on["call"](fold_expr(c, on), [fold_expr(a, on) for a in args])
        case _:
            raise TypeError(f"not an expression: {expr!r}")


def leaf(value):
    return lambda *_: value


SIZE = {"num": leaf(1), "str": leaf(1), "bool": leaf(1), "var": leaf(1),
        "unary": lambda op, e: 1 + e,
        "binary": lambda op, l, r: 1 + l + r,
        "call": lambda c, args: 1 + c + sum(args)}

DEPTH = {"num": leaf(1), "str": leaf(1), "bool": leaf(1), "var": leaf(1),
         "unary": lambda op, e: 1 + e,
         "binary": lambda op, l, r: 1 + max(l, r),
         "call": lambda c, args: 1 + max([c] + args)}

NAMES = {"num": leaf(frozenset()), "str": leaf(frozenset()), "bool": leaf(frozenset()),
         "var": lambda n: frozenset([n]),
         "unary": lambda op, e: e,
         "binary": lambda op, l, r: l | r,
         "call": lambda c, args: c.union(*args)}


def parse_expr(source):
    return parse_program(tokenize(source + ";")).stmts[0].expr


def size(source):
    return fold_expr(parse_expr(source), SIZE)


def depth(source):
    return fold_expr(parse_expr(source), DEPTH)


def names(source):
    return sorted(fold_expr(parse_expr(source), NAMES))
--- hint
`fold_expr` is one `match` with a case per node class: for `Binary(op=op, left=l, right=r)` return `on["binary"](op, fold_expr(l, on), fold_expr(r, on))`, and for a `Call` fold the callee and each argument.
--- hint
For `size`, every leaf gives 1 and every inner node gives 1 plus the sum of its folded children. For `depth`, 1 plus the maximum. For `names`, leaves give an empty set except `var`, which gives a set of one name; inner nodes take the union. Sort at the end.
--- check test | The examples from the task
size("1 + 2 * x") == 5 and depth("1 + 2 * x") == 3
--- check test | Calls and unary operators
size("f(a, b + a) - -c") == 9 and depth("f(a, b + a) - -c") == 4 and depth("f()") == 2 and names("f(a, b + a) - -c") == ["a", "b", "c", "f"]
--- check test | Leaves
size('"s"') == 1 and depth("true") == 1 and names("1") == [] and names("x == x") == ["x"]
--- check test | Any other fold, such as evaluation
fold_expr(parse_expr("2 * (3 + 4) - -1"), {"num": lambda v: v, "str": lambda v: v, "bool": lambda v: v, "var": lambda n: 0, "unary": lambda op, e: -e, "binary": lambda op, l, r: {"+": l + r, "-": l - r, "*": l * r}[op], "call": lambda c, a: 0}) == 15
--- check test | Printing with full parentheses
fold_expr(parse_expr("a + b * c(d)"), {"num": str, "str": repr, "bool": str, "var": str, "unary": lambda op, e: f"({op}{e})", "binary": lambda op, l, r: f"({l} {op} {r})", "call": lambda c, a: c + "(" + ", ".join(a) + ")"}) == "(a + (b * c(d)))"

+++ practice | Lists made of closures
--- task
Comet has no lists, but closures are enough to build them. Represent a list as a **function of one argument**: called with 0 it says whether the list is empty (a bool); a non-empty list called with 1 returns its head and called with 2 returns its tail. The starter gives the lesson 8 interpreter and a Comet program that already declares the empty list, `fn nil(which) { return true; }`. Add Comet functions to `PROGRAM`:

- `cons(h, t)`, returning a new list; `is_empty(list)`, `head(list)` and `tail(list)`;
- `foldl(f, acc, list)`, a left fold, with a `while` loop;
- `map(f, list)`, returning a new list, recursively;
- `length(list)`, written with your `foldl`.

The checks run `run_source(PROGRAM + more)`, with lists of at most 10 items. For example, after `let l = cons(1, cons(2, cons(3, nil)));`, `print length(l);` prints `3`.
--- starter
from dataclasses import dataclass

KEYWORDS = {"let", "fn", "return", "if", "else", "while", "print",
            "true", "false", "and", "or", "not"}
TWO_CHAR = {"==", "!=", "<=", ">=", "->"}
ONE_CHAR = set("+-*/%<>=(){},;:")
ESCAPES = {'"': '"', "\\": "\\", "n": "\n"}
DIGITS = "0123456789"
LETTERS = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ_"


@dataclass
class Token:
    kind: str
    text: str
    line: int
    col: int


class LexError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


def tokenize(source):
    tokens = []
    i = 0
    line = 1
    col = 1
    n = len(source)

    def advance(count):
        nonlocal i, line, col
        for _ in range(count):
            if source[i] == "\n":
                line += 1
                col = 1
            else:
                col += 1
            i += 1

    while i < n:
        ch = source[i]
        start_line, start_col = line, col
        if ch in " \t\r\n":
            advance(1)
        elif ch == "#":
            while i < n and source[i] != "\n":
                advance(1)
        elif ch in DIGITS:
            j = i
            while j < n and source[j] in DIGITS:
                j += 1
            tokens.append(Token("NUMBER", source[i:j], start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch in LETTERS:
            j = i
            while j < n and (source[j] in LETTERS or source[j] in DIGITS):
                j += 1
            word = source[i:j]
            kind = "KEYWORD" if word in KEYWORDS else "IDENT"
            tokens.append(Token(kind, word, start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch == '"':
            advance(1)
            chars = []
            while True:
                if i >= n or source[i] == "\n":
                    raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                c = source[i]
                if c == '"':
                    advance(1)
                    break
                if c == "\\":
                    if i + 1 >= n or source[i + 1] == "\n":
                        raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                    if source[i + 1] not in ESCAPES:
                        raise LexError("unknown escape", line, col)
                    chars.append(ESCAPES[source[i + 1]])
                    advance(2)
                else:
                    chars.append(c)
                    advance(1)
            tokens.append(Token("STRING", "".join(chars), start_line, start_col))
        elif source[i:i + 2] in TWO_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", source[i:i + 2], start_line, start_col))
            advance(2)
        elif ch in ONE_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", ch, start_line, start_col))
            advance(1)
        else:
            raise LexError(f"unexpected character {ch!r}", start_line, start_col)
    tokens.append(Token("EOF", "", line, col))
    return tokens
