class ParseError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


COMPARE = ("==", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">=")
TYPES = ("int", "bool", "str")


class Parser:
    def __init__(self, tokens):
        self.tokens = tokens
        self.pos = 0

    def peek(self, ahead=0):
        return self.tokens[min(self.pos + ahead, len(self.tokens) - 1)]

    def at(self, *texts):
        tok = self.peek()
        return tok.kind in ("OP", "KEYWORD") and tok.text in texts

    def advance(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "EOF":
            self.pos += 1
        return tok

    def error(self, message):
        tok = self.peek()
        return ParseError(message, tok.line, tok.col)

    def expect(self, text):
        if not self.at(text):
            raise self.error(f"expected '{text}'")
        return self.advance()

    def expr(self):
        return self.or_expr()

    def or_expr(self):
        left = self.and_expr()
        while self.at("or"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.and_expr())
        return left

    def and_expr(self):
        left = self.not_expr()
        while self.at("and"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.not_expr())
        return left

    def not_expr(self):
        if self.at("not"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("not", self.not_expr())
        return self.compare()

    def compare(self):
        left = self.sum()
        if self.at(*COMPARE):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.sum())
            if self.at(*COMPARE):
                raise self.error("comparisons cannot be chained")
        return left

    def sum(self):
        left = self.product()
        while self.at("+", "-"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.product())
        return left

    def product(self):
        left = self.unary()
        while self.at("*", "/", "%"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.unary())
        return left

    def unary(self):
        if self.at("-"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("-", self.unary())
        return self.call()

    def call(self):
        expr = self.primary()
        while self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            args = []
            if not self.at(")"):
                args.append(self.expr())
                while self.at(","):
                    self.advance()
                    args.append(self.expr())
            self.expect(")")
            expr = Call(expr, args)
        return expr

    def primary(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind == "NUMBER":
            self.advance()
            return Num(int(tok.text))
        if tok.kind == "STRING":
            self.advance()
            return Str(tok.text)
        if tok.kind == "IDENT":
            self.advance()
            return Var(tok.text)
        if self.at("true", "false"):
            self.advance()
            return Bool(tok.text == "true")
        if self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            inner = self.expr()
            self.expect(")")
            return inner
        raise self.error("expected an expression")

    def program(self):
        stmts = []
        while self.peek().kind != "EOF":
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        return Program(stmts)

    def statement(self):
        if self.at("let"):
            return self.let_stmt()
        if self.at("print"):
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Print(value)
        if self.at("if"):
            return self.if_stmt()
        if self.at("while"):
            self.advance()
            cond = self.expr()
            return While(cond, self.block())
        if self.at("fn"):
            return self.fn_stmt()
        if self.at("return"):
            self.advance()
            value = None if self.at(";") else self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Return(value)
        nxt = self.peek(1)
        if self.peek().kind == "IDENT" and nxt.kind == "OP" and nxt.text == "=":
            name = self.advance().text
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Assign(name, value)
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return ExprStmt(value)

    def name(self):
        if self.peek().kind != "IDENT":
            raise self.error("expected a name")
        return self.advance().text

    def type_name(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "IDENT" or tok.text not in TYPES:
            raise self.error("expected a type")
        return self.advance().text

    def let_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        self.expect("=")
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return Let(name, type_, value)

    def if_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        cond = self.expr()
        then = self.block()
        else_ = None
        if self.at("else"):
            self.advance()
            else_ = self.if_stmt() if self.at("if") else self.block()
        return If(cond, then, else_)

    def block(self):
        self.expect("{")
        stmts = []
        while not self.at("}"):
            if self.peek().kind == "EOF":
                raise self.error("expected '}'")
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        self.advance()
        return Block(stmts)

    def param(self):
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        return (name, type_)

    def fn_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        self.expect("(")
        params = []
        if not self.at(")"):
            params.append(self.param())
            while self.at(","):
                self.advance()
                params.append(self.param())
        self.expect(")")
        ret = None
        if self.at("->"):
            self.advance()
            ret = self.type_name()
        return Fn(name, params, ret, self.block())


def parse_program(tokens):
    return Parser(tokens).program()


class CometError(Exception):
    pass


def comet_div(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q


def comet_mod(a, b):
    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)


MAX_DEPTH = 40


class Closure:
    def __init__(self, decl, env):
        self.decl = decl
        self.env = env


class ReturnSignal(Exception):
    def __init__(self, value):
        super().__init__("return")
        self.value = value


def type_name(value):
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "bool"
    if isinstance(value, int):
        return "int"
    if isinstance(value, str):
        return "str"
    if isinstance(value, Closure):
        return "fn"

    return "nothing"


def show(value):
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "true" if value else "false"
    if isinstance(value, Closure):
        return f"<fn {value.decl.name}>"

    if value is None:
        raise CometError("cannot print nothing")
    return str(value)


class Environment:
    def __init__(self, parent=None):
        self.values = {}
        self.parent = parent

    def define(self, name, value):
        if name in self.values:
            raise CometError(f"{name} is already declared in this scope")
        self.values[name] = value

    def find(self, name):
        env = self
        while env is not None:
            if name in env.values:
                return env
            env = env.parent
        return None

    def lookup(self, name):
        env = self.find(name)
        if env is None:
            raise CometError(f"undefined variable {name}")
        return env.values[name]

    def assign(self, name, value):
        env = self.find(name)
        if env is None:
            raise CometError(f"assignment to undeclared variable {name}")
        env.values[name] = value


class Interpreter:
    def __init__(self):
        self.globals = Environment()
        self.env = self.globals
        self.output = []
        self.frames = []


    def run(self, program):
        for stmt in program.stmts:
            self.execute(stmt)

    def execute_block(self, stmts, env):
        previous = self.env
        self.env = env
        try:
            for stmt in stmts:
                self.execute(stmt)
        finally:
            self.env = previous

    def execute(self, stmt):
        if isinstance(stmt, Let):
            self.env.define(stmt.name, self.evaluate(stmt.expr))
        elif isinstance(stmt, Assign):
            value = self.evaluate(stmt.expr)
            self.env.assign(stmt.name, value)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Print):
            self.output.append(show(self.evaluate(stmt.expr)))
        elif isinstance(stmt, ExprStmt):
            self.evaluate(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, If):
            if self.condition(stmt.cond):
                self.execute(stmt.then)
            elif stmt.else_ is not None:
                self.execute(stmt.else_)
        elif isinstance(stmt, While):
            while self.condition(stmt.cond):
                self.execute(stmt.body)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Block):
            self.execute_block(stmt.stmts, Environment(self.env))
        elif isinstance(stmt, Fn):
            self.env.define(stmt.name, Closure(stmt, self.env))
        elif isinstance(stmt, Return):
            if not self.frames:
                raise CometError("return outside a function")
            value = None if stmt.expr is None else self.evaluate(stmt.expr)
            raise ReturnSignal(value)
        else:
            raise CometError(f"{type(stmt).__name__} is not supported yet")

    def condition(self, expr):
        value = self.evaluate(expr)
        if not isinstance(value, bool):
            raise CometError(f"condition must be bool, not {type_name(value)}")
        return value

    def evaluate(self, expr):
        if isinstance(expr, (Num, Str, Bool)):
            return expr.value
        if isinstance(expr, Var):
            return self.env.lookup(expr.name)
        if isinstance(expr, Unary):
            value = self.evaluate(expr.expr)
            if expr.op == "-":
                self.need("int", value, "-")
                return -value
            self.need("bool", value, "not")
            return not value
        if isinstance(expr, Binary):
            return self.binary(expr)
        if isinstance(expr, Call):
            callee = self.evaluate(expr.callee)
            args = [self.evaluate(arg) for arg in expr.args]
            return self.call(callee, args)
        raise CometError(f"{type(expr).__name__} is not supported yet")

    def call(self, callee, args):
        if not isinstance(callee, Closure):
            raise CometError(f"cannot call a value of type {type_name(callee)}")
        decl = callee.decl
        if len(args) != len(decl.params):
            raise CometError(f"{decl.name} expects {len(decl.params)} arguments, got {len(args)}")
        if len(self.frames) >= MAX_DEPTH:
            raise CometError("stack overflow")
        env = Environment(callee.env)
        for (name, _), value in zip(decl.params, args):
            env.define(name, value)
        self.frames.append(decl.name)
        try:
            self.execute_block(decl.body.stmts, env)
        except ReturnSignal as signal:
            return signal.value
        finally:
            self.frames.pop()
        return None

    def need(self, wanted, value, op):
        if type_name(value) != wanted:
            raise CometError(f"'{op}' needs {wanted}, not {type_name(value)}")

    def binary(self, expr):
        op = expr.op
        left = self.evaluate(expr.left)
        if op in ("and", "or"):
            self.need("bool", left, op)
            if (op == "and" and not left) or (op == "or" and left):
                return left
            right = self.evaluate(expr.right)
            self.need("bool", right, op)
            return right
        right = self.evaluate(expr.right)
        if op in ("==", "!="):
            if type_name(left) != type_name(right):
                raise CometError(f"cannot compare {type_name(left)} with {type_name(right)}")
            return (left is right if isinstance(left, Closure) else left == right) == (op == "==")
        if op == "+" and type_name(left) == "str" and type_name(right) == "str":
            return left + right
        self.need("int", left, op)
        self.need("int", right, op)
        if op == "+":
            return left + right
        if op == "-":
            return left - right
        if op == "*":
            return left * right
        if op == "/":
            return comet_div(left, right)
        if op == "%":
            return comet_mod(left, right)
        if op == "<":
            return left < right
        if op == "<=":
            return left <= right
        if op == ">":
            return left > right
        return left >= right


def run_source(source):
    interp = Interpreter()
    try:
        interp.run(parse_program(tokenize(source)))
    except CometError as e:
        return interp.output, str(e)
    return interp.output, None


PROGRAM = """
fn nil(which) {
    return true;
}

# Write cons, is_empty, head, tail, foldl, map and length here, in Comet.
"""
--- solution
from dataclasses import dataclass

KEYWORDS = {"let", "fn", "return", "if", "else", "while", "print",
            "true", "false", "and", "or", "not"}
TWO_CHAR = {"==", "!=", "<=", ">=", "->"}
ONE_CHAR = set("+-*/%<>=(){},;:")
ESCAPES = {'"': '"', "\\": "\\", "n": "\n"}
DIGITS = "0123456789"
LETTERS = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ_"


@dataclass
class Token:
    kind: str
    text: str
    line: int
    col: int


class LexError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


def tokenize(source):
    tokens = []
    i = 0
    line = 1
    col = 1
    n = len(source)

    def advance(count):
        nonlocal i, line, col
        for _ in range(count):
            if source[i] == "\n":
                line += 1
                col = 1
            else:
                col += 1
            i += 1

    while i < n:
        ch = source[i]
        start_line, start_col = line, col
        if ch in " \t\r\n":
            advance(1)
        elif ch == "#":
            while i < n and source[i] != "\n":
                advance(1)
        elif ch in DIGITS:
            j = i
            while j < n and source[j] in DIGITS:
                j += 1
            tokens.append(Token("NUMBER", source[i:j], start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch in LETTERS:
            j = i
            while j < n and (source[j] in LETTERS or source[j] in DIGITS):
                j += 1
            word = source[i:j]
            kind = "KEYWORD" if word in KEYWORDS else "IDENT"
            tokens.append(Token(kind, word, start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch == '"':
            advance(1)
            chars = []
            while True:
                if i >= n or source[i] == "\n":
                    raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                c = source[i]
                if c == '"':
                    advance(1)
                    break
                if c == "\\":
                    if i + 1 >= n or source[i + 1] == "\n":
                        raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                    if source[i + 1] not in ESCAPES:
                        raise LexError("unknown escape", line, col)
                    chars.append(ESCAPES[source[i + 1]])
                    advance(2)
                else:
                    chars.append(c)
                    advance(1)
            tokens.append(Token("STRING", "".join(chars), start_line, start_col))
        elif source[i:i + 2] in TWO_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", source[i:i + 2], start_line, start_col))
            advance(2)
        elif ch in ONE_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", ch, start_line, start_col))
            advance(1)
        else:
            raise LexError(f"unexpected character {ch!r}", start_line, start_col)
    tokens.append(Token("EOF", "", line, col))
    return tokens


@dataclass
class Num:
    value: int


@dataclass

    value: str


@dataclass

    value: bool


@dataclass

@dataclass

@dataclass

    left: object
    right: object


@dataclass

    callee: object
    args: list


@dataclass

    name: str

    expr: object


@dataclass

    expr: object

    cond: object
    then: object
    else_: object

class ParseError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


COMPARE = ("==", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">=")
TYPES = ("int", "bool", "str")


class Parser:
    def __init__(self, tokens):
        self.tokens = tokens
        self.pos = 0

    def peek(self, ahead=0):
        return self.tokens[min(self.pos + ahead, len(self.tokens) - 1)]

    def at(self, *texts):
        tok = self.peek()
        return tok.kind in ("OP", "KEYWORD") and tok.text in texts

    def advance(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "EOF":
            self.pos += 1
        return tok

    def error(self, message):
        tok = self.peek()
        return ParseError(message, tok.line, tok.col)

    def expect(self, text):
        if not self.at(text):
            raise self.error(f"expected '{text}'")
        return self.advance()

    def expr(self):
        return self.or_expr()

    def or_expr(self):
        left = self.and_expr()
        while self.at("or"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.and_expr())
        return left

    def and_expr(self):
        left = self.not_expr()
        while self.at("and"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.not_expr())
        return left

    def not_expr(self):
        if self.at("not"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("not", self.not_expr())
        return self.compare()

    def compare(self):
        left = self.sum()
        if self.at(*COMPARE):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.sum())
            if self.at(*COMPARE):
                raise self.error("comparisons cannot be chained")
        return left

    def sum(self):
        left = self.product()
        while self.at("+", "-"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.product())
        return left

    def product(self):
        left = self.unary()
        while self.at("*", "/", "%"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.unary())
        return left

    def unary(self):
        if self.at("-"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("-", self.unary())
        return self.call()

    def call(self):
        expr = self.primary()
        while self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            args = []
            if not self.at(")"):
                args.append(self.expr())
                while self.at(","):
                    self.advance()
                    args.append(self.expr())
            self.expect(")")
            expr = Call(expr, args)
        return expr

    def primary(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind == "NUMBER":
            self.advance()
            return Num(int(tok.text))
        if tok.kind == "STRING":
            self.advance()
            return Str(tok.text)
        if tok.kind == "IDENT":
            self.advance()
            return Var(tok.text)
        if self.at("true", "false"):
            self.advance()
            return Bool(tok.text == "true")
        if self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            inner = self.expr()
            self.expect(")")
            return inner
        raise self.error("expected an expression")

    def program(self):
        stmts = []
        while self.peek().kind != "EOF":
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        return Program(stmts)

    def statement(self):
        if self.at("let"):
            return self.let_stmt()
        if self.at("print"):
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Print(value)
        if self.at("if"):
            return self.if_stmt()
        if self.at("while"):
            self.advance()
            cond = self.expr()
            return While(cond, self.block())
        if self.at("fn"):
            return self.fn_stmt()
        if self.at("return"):
            self.advance()
            value = None if self.at(";") else self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Return(value)
        nxt = self.peek(1)
        if self.peek().kind == "IDENT" and nxt.kind == "OP" and nxt.text == "=":
            name = self.advance().text
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Assign(name, value)
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return ExprStmt(value)

    def name(self):
        if self.peek().kind != "IDENT":
            raise self.error("expected a name")
        return self.advance().text

    def type_name(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "IDENT" or tok.text not in TYPES:
            raise self.error("expected a type")
        return self.advance().text

    def let_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        self.expect("=")
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return Let(name, type_, value)

    def if_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        cond = self.expr()
        then = self.block()
        else_ = None
        if self.at("else"):
            self.advance()
            else_ = self.if_stmt() if self.at("if") else self.block()
        return If(cond, then, else_)

    def block(self):
        self.expect("{")
        stmts = []
        while not self.at("}"):
            if self.peek().kind == "EOF":
                raise self.error("expected '}'")
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        self.advance()
        return Block(stmts)

    def param(self):
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        return (name, type_)

    def fn_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        self.expect("(")
        params = []
        if not self.at(")"):
            params.append(self.param())
            while self.at(","):
                self.advance()
                params.append(self.param())
        self.expect(")")
        ret = None
        if self.at("->"):
            self.advance()
            ret = self.type_name()
        return Fn(name, params, ret, self.block())


def parse_program(tokens):
    return Parser(tokens).program()


class CometError(Exception):
    pass


def comet_div(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q


def comet_mod(a, b):
    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)


MAX_DEPTH = 40


class Closure:
    def __init__(self, decl, env):
        self.decl = decl
        self.env = env


class ReturnSignal(Exception):
    def __init__(self, value):
        super().__init__("return")
        self.value = value


def type_name(value):
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "bool"
    if isinstance(value, int):
        return "int"
    if isinstance(value, str):
        return "str"
    if isinstance(value, Closure):
        return "fn"

    return "nothing"


def show(value):
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "true" if value else "false"
    if isinstance(value, Closure):
        return f"<fn {value.decl.name}>"

    if value is None:
        raise CometError("cannot print nothing")
    return str(value)


class Environment:
    def __init__(self, parent=None):
        self.values = {}
        self.parent = parent

    def define(self, name, value):
        if name in self.values:
            raise CometError(f"{name} is already declared in this scope")
        self.values[name] = value

    def find(self, name):
        env = self
        while env is not None:
            if name in env.values:
                return env
            env = env.parent
        return None

    def lookup(self, name):
        env = self.find(name)
        if env is None:
            raise CometError(f"undefined variable {name}")
        return env.values[name]

    def assign(self, name, value):
        env = self.find(name)
        if env is None:
            raise CometError(f"assignment to undeclared variable {name}")
        env.values[name] = value


class Interpreter:
    def __init__(self):
        self.globals = Environment()
        self.env = self.globals
        self.output = []
        self.frames = []


    def run(self, program):
        for stmt in program.stmts:
            self.execute(stmt)

    def execute_block(self, stmts, env):
        previous = self.env
        self.env = env
        try:
            for stmt in stmts:
                self.execute(stmt)
        finally:
            self.env = previous

    def execute(self, stmt):
        if isinstance(stmt, Let):
            self.env.define(stmt.name, self.evaluate(stmt.expr))
        elif isinstance(stmt, Assign):
            value = self.evaluate(stmt.expr)
            self.env.assign(stmt.name, value)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Print):
            self.output.append(show(self.evaluate(stmt.expr)))
        elif isinstance(stmt, ExprStmt):
            self.evaluate(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, If):
            if self.condition(stmt.cond):
                self.execute(stmt.then)
            elif stmt.else_ is not None:
                self.execute(stmt.else_)
        elif isinstance(stmt, While):
            while self.condition(stmt.cond):
                self.execute(stmt.body)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Block):
            self.execute_block(stmt.stmts, Environment(self.env))
        elif isinstance(stmt, Fn):
            self.env.define(stmt.name, Closure(stmt, self.env))
        elif isinstance(stmt, Return):
            if not self.frames:
                raise CometError("return outside a function")
            value = None if stmt.expr is None else self.evaluate(stmt.expr)
            raise ReturnSignal(value)
        else:
            raise CometError(f"{type(stmt).__name__} is not supported yet")

    def condition(self, expr):
        value = self.evaluate(expr)
        if not isinstance(value, bool):
            raise CometError(f"condition must be bool, not {type_name(value)}")
        return value

    def evaluate(self, expr):
        if isinstance(expr, (Num, Str, Bool)):
            return expr.value
        if isinstance(expr, Var):
            return self.env.lookup(expr.name)
        if isinstance(expr, Unary):
            value = self.evaluate(expr.expr)
            if expr.op == "-":
                self.need("int", value, "-")
                return -value
            self.need("bool", value, "not")
            return not value
        if isinstance(expr, Binary):
            return self.binary(expr)
        if isinstance(expr, Call):
            callee = self.evaluate(expr.callee)
            args = [self.evaluate(arg) for arg in expr.args]
            return self.call(callee, args)
        raise CometError(f"{type(expr).__name__} is not supported yet")

    def call(self, callee, args):
        if not isinstance(callee, Closure):
            raise CometError(f"cannot call a value of type {type_name(callee)}")
        decl = callee.decl
        if len(args) != len(decl.params):
            raise CometError(f"{decl.name} expects {len(decl.params)} arguments, got {len(args)}")
        if len(self.frames) >= MAX_DEPTH:
            raise CometError("stack overflow")
        env = Environment(callee.env)
        for (name, _), value in zip(decl.params, args):
            env.define(name, value)
        self.frames.append(decl.name)
        try:
            self.execute_block(decl.body.stmts, env)
        except ReturnSignal as signal:
            return signal.value
        finally:
            self.frames.pop()
        return None

    def need(self, wanted, value, op):
        if type_name(value) != wanted:
            raise CometError(f"'{op}' needs {wanted}, not {type_name(value)}")

    def binary(self, expr):
        op = expr.op
        left = self.evaluate(expr.left)
        if op in ("and", "or"):
            self.need("bool", left, op)
            if (op == "and" and not left) or (op == "or" and left):
                return left
            right = self.evaluate(expr.right)
            self.need("bool", right, op)
            return right
        right = self.evaluate(expr.right)
        if op in ("==", "!="):
            if type_name(left) != type_name(right):
                raise CometError(f"cannot compare {type_name(left)} with {type_name(right)}")
            return (left is right if isinstance(left, Closure) else left == right) == (op == "==")
        if op == "+" and type_name(left) == "str" and type_name(right) == "str":
            return left + right
        self.need("int", left, op)
        self.need("int", right, op)
        if op == "+":
            return left + right
        if op == "-":
            return left - right
        if op == "*":
            return left * right
        if op == "/":
            return comet_div(left, right)
        if op == "%":
            return comet_mod(left, right)
        if op == "<":
            return left < right
        if op == "<=":
            return left <= right
        if op == ">":
            return left > right
        return left >= right


def run_source(source):
    interp = Interpreter()
    try:
        interp.run(parse_program(tokenize(source)))
    except CometError as e:
        return interp.output, str(e)
    return interp.output, None


PROGRAM = """
fn nil(which) {
    return true;
}

fn cons(h, t) {
    fn node(which) {
        if which == 0 {
            return false;
        }
        if which == 1 {
            return h;
        }
        return t;
    }
    return node;
}

fn is_empty(list) {
    return list(0);
}

fn head(list) {
    return list(1);
}

fn tail(list) {
    return list(2);
}

fn foldl(f, acc, list) {
    while not is_empty(list) {
        acc = f(acc, head(list));
        list = tail(list);
    }
    return acc;
}

fn map(f, list) {
    if is_empty(list) {
        return nil;
    }
    return cons(f(head(list)), map(f, tail(list)));
}

fn length(list) {
    fn count(n, x) {
        return n + 1;
    }
    return foldl(count, 0, list);
}
"""
--- hint
`cons` declares an inner function `node(which)` that returns `false` for 0, `h` for 1 and `t` otherwise, and returns `node`. The inner function is a closure over `h` and `t`, so each list cell keeps its own values.
--- hint
`is_empty(list)` is `return list(0);`, and `head` and `tail` call it with 1 and 2. `foldl` loops `while not is_empty(list)`, updating `acc` and moving `list` to its tail. `length` needs a two-argument step function that ignores the item and adds 1.
--- check case | The example from the task, and more
run_source(PROGRAM + "let l = cons(1, cons(2, cons(3, nil))); print length(l); print head(tail(l)); print is_empty(nil); print is_empty(l); print length(nil);")
=> (["3", "2", "true", "false", "0"], None)
--- check case | map and foldl
run_source(PROGRAM + "let l = cons(1, cons(2, cons(3, nil))); fn sq(x) { return x * x; } fn add(a, b) { return a + b; } print foldl(add, 0, map(sq, l)); fn sub(a, b) { return a - b; } print foldl(sub, 0, l);")
=> (["14", "-6"], None)
--- check case | Lists are persistent: map leaves the original alone
run_source(PROGRAM + "let l = cons(5, nil); fn neg(x) { return -x; } let m = map(neg, l); print head(l); print head(m); let l2 = cons(4, l); print length(l2); print length(l);")
=> (["5", "-5", "2", "1"], None)
--- check case | Strings and a longer list
run_source(PROGRAM + "let words = cons(\"a\", cons(\"b\", cons(\"c\", cons(\"d\", cons(\"e\", cons(\"f\", cons(\"g\", cons(\"h\", cons(\"i\", cons(\"j\", nil)))))))))); fn join(acc, w) { return acc + w; } print foldl(join, \">\", words); print length(map(join, nil));")
=> ([">abcdefghij", "0"], None)
--- check test | head of the empty list is not a string or number

+++ practice | scanl, zip_with and take
--- task
Three more classic list functions, on the lesson's persistent lists (the starter gives `Nil`, `Cons`, `NIL`, `from_list` and `to_list`). Each returns a new list, changes nothing, and must work on lists of 50,000 items, so use loops.

- `scanl(f, acc, lst)`: the list of every accumulator a left fold passes through, starting with `acc` itself, so the result has one more item than `lst`. `scanl(add, 0, [1, 2, 3])` is `[0, 1, 3, 6]`, the running totals of a telemetry counter, and on the empty list it is `[acc]`.
- `zip_with(f, a, b)`: `f(a₁, b₁), f(a₂, b₂), …`, stopping at the end of the **shorter** list.
- `take(n, lst)`: the first n items; the whole list if it has fewer than n; the empty list if n is 0 or negative.
--- starter
from dataclasses import dataclass


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Nil:
    pass


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Cons:
    head: object
    tail: object


NIL = Nil()


def from_list(items):
    result = NIL
    for item in reversed(items):
        result = Cons(item, result)
    return result


def to_list(lst):
    items = []
    while isinstance(lst, Cons):
        items.append(lst.head)
        lst = lst.tail
    return items

    raise NotImplementedError("scanl is not written yet")


def zip_with(f, a, b):
    raise NotImplementedError("zip_with is not written yet")


def take(n, lst):
    raise NotImplementedError("take is not written yet")
--- solution
from dataclasses import dataclass


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Nil:
    pass


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Cons:
    head: object
    tail: object


NIL = Nil()


def from_list(items):
    result = NIL
    for item in reversed(items):
        result = Cons(item, result)
    return result


def to_list(lst):
    items = []
    while isinstance(lst, Cons):
        items.append(lst.head)
        lst = lst.tail
    return items


def scanl(f, acc, lst):
    steps = [acc]
    while isinstance(lst, Cons):
        acc = f(acc, lst.head)
        steps.append(acc)
        lst = lst.tail
    return from_list(steps)


def zip_with(f, a, b):
    items = []
    while isinstance(a, Cons) and isinstance(b, Cons):
        items.append(f(a.head, b.head))
        a, b = a.tail, b.tail
    return from_list(items)


def take(n, lst):
    items = []
    while n > 0 and isinstance(lst, Cons):
        items.append(lst.head)
        lst = lst.tail
        n -= 1
    return from_list(items)
--- hint
Walk the list with a `while` loop, collect the results in a Python list, and turn it into a Cons list at the end with `from_list`. For `scanl`, put `acc` in the Python list before the loop, and append after each step.
--- hint
`zip_with` loops while **both** lists are `Cons`, moving both along. `take` loops while `n > 0` and the list is a `Cons`, counting n down.
--- check case | scanl gives running totals, starting with the initial value

+++ practice | Debug: an undo history that rewrites the past
--- task
The starter's `History` class keeps an undo history of command strings for a ground-station console. It is meant to be persistent: `push` and `undo` return a **new** version and leave the old one exactly as it was, so the console can jump back to any earlier version. But old versions change. After `h0 = History()`, `h1 = h0.push("arm")` and `h2 = h1.push("fire")`, the size of `h1` should still be 1; it is 2, and even `h0` has size 2.

Find the bug and fix it, keeping the same methods: `push(command)`, `undo()`, `latest()` (the most recent command, or `None`) and `size()`.
--- starter
class History:
    """An undo history of command strings. Every change returns a new version."""

    def __init__(self, commands=()):
        self.commands = list(commands)

    def push(self, command):
        self.commands.append(command)
        return History(self.commands)

    def undo(self):
        if not self.commands:
            return self
        return History(self.commands[:-1])

    def latest(self):
        return self.commands[-1] if self.commands else None

    def size(self):
        return len(self.commands)
--- solution
class History:
    """An undo history of command strings. Every change returns a new version."""

    def __init__(self, commands=()):
        self.commands = tuple(commands)

    def push(self, command):
        return History(self.commands + (command,))

    def undo(self):
        if not self.commands:
            return self
        return History(self.commands[:-1])

    def latest(self):
        return self.commands[-1] if self.commands else None

    def size(self):
        return len(self.commands)
--- hint
After `push`, how many `History` objects refer to the very same Python list? What does `append` do to all of them?
--- hint
Never change a list that another version may be holding. Build a new sequence for the new version, for example `self.commands + (command,)` with a tuple, and store tuples, which cannot be changed at all.

+++ practice | A persistent map with path copying
--- task
An interpreter that keeps every past state, or a configuration store with undo, needs a map whose updates return a new version while old versions stay valid. Build one as a **persistent binary search tree**. The starter gives the frozen dataclass `Node(key, value, left, right)`; the empty tree is `None`. Write:

- `insert(tree, key, value)`: a new tree with the key bound to the value (replacing an old binding). Copy only the nodes on the path from the root to the key, and **share** every other subtree with the old tree. The old tree must not change.
- `lookup(tree, key, default=None)`: the value bound to the key, or `default`.
- `items(tree)`: the list of `(key, value)` pairs in increasing key order.

A check inserts 20,000 keys in a shuffled order, so the tree stays about 40 levels deep; `items` must also work on such trees, so write it with a loop and an explicit stack. `lookup` should walk down with a loop too.
--- starter

--- solution
from dataclasses import dataclass


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Node:
    key: object
    value: object
    left: object
    right: object


def insert(tree, key, value):
    if tree is None:
        return Node(key, value, None, None)
    if key < tree.key:
        return Node(tree.key, tree.value, insert(tree.left, key, value), tree.right)
    if key > tree.key:
        return Node(tree.key, tree.value, tree.left, insert(tree.right, key, value))
    return Node(key, value, tree.left, tree.right)


def lookup(tree, key, default=None):
    while tree is not None:
        if key < tree.key:
            tree = tree.left
        elif key > tree.key:
            tree = tree.right
        else:
            return tree.value
    return default


def items(tree):
    out = []
    stack = []
    while stack or tree is not None:
        while tree is not None:
            stack.append(tree)
            tree = tree.left
        tree = stack.pop()
        out.append((tree.key, tree.value))
        tree = tree.right
    return out
--- hint
`insert` is recursive with one case per situation: an empty tree gives a new leaf; a smaller key gives a new node with the same key, value and right subtree and a new left subtree from inserting into the old left one; a larger key the mirror image; an equal key a new node with the new value and both old subtrees.
--- hint
For `items`, the classic iterative in-order walk: go left pushing nodes on a stack; when you cannot go left, pop a node, record it, and continue from its right child.
--- check test | Insert and look up
(lambda t: lookup(t, "b") == 2 and lookup(t, "a") == 1 and lookup(t, "z") is None and lookup(t, "z", 0) == 0 and items(t) == [("a", 1), ("b", 2), ("c", 3)])(insert(insert(insert(None, "b", 2), "a", 1), "c", 3))
--- check test | The old version is unchanged, and the untouched side is shared
(lambda t: (lambda t2: lookup(t, "a") == 1 and lookup(t2, "a") == 10 and t2.right is t.right and t2 is not t and items(t) == [("a", 1), ("b", 2), ("c", 3)])(insert(t, "a", 10)))(insert(insert(insert(None, "b", 2), "a", 1), "c", 3))

(lambda t: (lambda t2: t2.left is t.left and t2.right.left is t.right.left and t2.right.right is not t.right.right and lookup(t2, 7) == "new" and lookup(t, 7) is None)(insert(t, 7, "new")))(insert(insert(insert(insert(insert(None, 4, "d"), 2, "b"), 6, "f"), 8, "h"), 5, "e"))
--- check test | The empty tree
items(None) == [] and lookup(None, 1) is None
--- check test | 20,000 shuffled keys, and one more version
(lambda keys: (lambda t: (lambda t2: lookup(t, 5) == 10 and lookup(t2, 5) == "five" and len(items(t2)) == 20000 and items(t2)[:3] == [(0, 0), (1, 2), (2, 4)] and items(t)[5] == (5, 10))(insert(t, 5, "five")))(__import__("functools").reduce(lambda tr, k: insert(tr, k, k * 2), keys, None)))((lambda r: (r.shuffle(ks := list(range(20000))), ks)[1])(__import__("random").Random(7)))

+++ question | foldl or foldr
--- ask
What is `foldr(lambda x, acc: x - acc, 0, [8, 5, 1])`, using the lesson's definition of foldr?
--- answer
4
--- why
foldr combines from the right: 8 − (5 − (1 − 0)) = 8 − (5 − 1) = 8 − 4 = 4. The left fold `reduce(lambda acc, x: acc - x, [8, 5, 1], 0)` would give ((0 − 8) − 5) − 1 = −14. The two agree only when the operation is associative and the initial value fits.

+++ question | What append copies
--- ask
`append(a, b)` on persistent Cons lists, with a of length m and b of length n. How much work does it do, and what happens to b?
--- choice
O(m + n): both lists are copied so that the result is independent.
--- choice correct
O(m): a's cells are copied, and the result's last copied cell points to b itself, which is shared.
--- choice
O(n): b is copied onto the end of a, which is changed in place.
--- choice
O(1): only one pointer is changed.
--- why
a's cells must be copied, because the last one has to point somewhere new, and changing it in place would change a for everyone who holds it. b needs no change at all, so it is shared. Sharing is safe precisely because no one can mutate b.

+++ question | The induction step
--- ask
In the proof that length(append(a, b)) = length(a) + length(b), the step case takes a = Cons(h, t). Which fact does the step use that the base case does not?
--- choice
That b is not empty.
--- choice correct
The induction hypothesis: that the claim already holds for the shorter list t.
--- choice
That length is a tail-recursive function.
--- choice
That append copies b.
--- why
The step rewrites length(append(Cons(h, t), b)) as 1 + length(append(t, b)) using the definitions, then replaces length(append(t, b)) by length(t) + length(b): that replacement is the induction hypothesis for t. Structural induction is exactly this: assume the property for the parts, prove it for the whole.
=== plc-12 | Semantic analysis: resolving names and catching errors before running
--- teach
Lessons 9 and 10 found type errors before the program runs. But the interpreter still discovers some mistakes only when it reaches them, like a misspelled variable in a branch that rarely runs, and lesson 8 left a subtle problem: a closure can see a variable declared **after** it. This lesson adds the pass that fixes both. It **resolves** every name to its declaration before running, reports every name error at once, and hands the interpreter the exact place of each variable.

### What semantic analysis is

A parser checks the **syntax**: that the tokens form a program the grammar allows. Many rules of a language cannot be written in a grammar at all. "A variable must be declared before it is used" is one: the language of programs that obey it is not context-free, for the same reason the pumping lemma of the Theory course rules out { w c w }: a declaration and its use are two matching pieces arbitrarily far apart. [[Why grammars cannot do it|context]]. **Semantic analysis** is the compiler pass after parsing that checks these rules on the tree: every name refers to a declaration, no name is declared twice in one scope, `return` appears only inside functions, and the types fit. It also computes facts later passes need, such as where each variable lives.

The core of it is **name resolution**: for every use of a name, find the declaration it refers to. In everyday words, the resolver reads the program once with a pencil and, next to every variable, writes an arrow to the `let` it means.

### The bug resolution fixes

Run this with lesson 8's interpreter:

```text
let sensor = "primary";
if true {
    fn report() { print sensor; }
    report();
    let sensor = "backup";
    report();
}
```

It prints `primary`, then `backup`. The function `report` did not change, and by lesson 7's rule the name `sensor` inside it means the declaration visible where `report` was written: the global one, since the block's `sensor` is declared later. But the closure holds the **live** block environment, and the second `let` adds `sensor` to that very environment, so the second lookup finds it. The meaning of a name changed while the program ran. That breaks lexical scope, and it would make code that is correct today silently wrong after someone adds a declaration further down a block.

The cure is to decide which declaration each name means **once, from the text**, and record it. Then the run-time lookup follows the recorded answer instead of searching by name.

### Comet's rules for names, precisely

- A name declared in a block or a function (a **local** name) is visible from just after its declaration to the end of that block. Parameters are visible in the whole function body.
- A name declared at the top level (a **global** name) is visible in top-level code from just after its declaration. **Inside function bodies**, every global name of the program is visible, wherever it is declared. So two top-level functions may call each other, and a function may use a global variable declared below it, as long as it is only called after that. This is called **late binding** of globals; most scripting languages do the same.
- A use that no declaration covers is an error: "undefined variable x", or, for an assignment, "assignment to undeclared variable x". So are "x is already declared in this scope" for a second declaration in the same scope (the parameters of a function and the top-level statements of its body share one scope, as at run time), and "return outside a function".

### Recording where each variable lives

For each use of a local name, the resolver records its **depth**: the number of scopes between the use and the declaration, 0 when they are in the same scope. For a global name it records `None`. At run time, the environment chain has exactly one environment per scope, in the same order, so the interpreter reaches the right environment by following `parent` exactly depth times, and looks the name up only there. In the program above, the `sensor` inside `report` is global, so both calls print `primary`.

A compiler goes one step further and numbers the variables within each scope: the pair (depth, index) is the variable's **lexical address**, and an environment becomes an array indexed by it, so a variable read is one step and one array access, no hashing at all. Practice problem 2 computes lexical addresses.

### The resolver

The resolver walks the tree once, keeping a stack of scopes. Each scope is the set of names declared in it **so far**; the bottom one is the global scope. It opens and closes scopes exactly where the interpreter creates and discards environments: one for each block, and one for each function holding its parameters and its body's statements.

- `let x = e;`: resolve e **first**, then declare x. The order matters: in `let x = x + 1;` inside a block, the x on the right must resolve to an outer x.
- `fn f(…) { … }`: declare f first, so that the body can call it; then open the function's scope, declare the parameters, resolve the body, and close it.
- A use of x: search the scopes from the innermost outwards, stopping before the global one. If a local scope has x, record the distance. Otherwise record `None`, and report an error unless x is declared globally so far, or the use is inside a function and x is declared at the top level anywhere.

To know whether a global is declared anywhere, the resolver first collects the names of all top-level `let` and `fn` statements.

The resolver does not stop at the first error. It records it and carries on, so one run reports every name error in the program. [[Error recovery|recovery]] is one of the things that separates a usable compiler from a toy.

Python's compiler does the same analysis, and its results can be inspected:

```python
import symtable

code = """
def outer(a):
    b = 1
    def inner():
        return a + b + len("xy")
    return inner
"""
top = symtable.symtable(code, "<orbit>", "exec")
outer = top.get_children()[0]
inner = outer.get_children()[0]
print(sorted(outer.get_locals()), sorted(inner.get_frees()), inner.get_globals())
# ['a', 'b', 'inner'] ['a', 'b'] ('len',)
```

Python's resolver found that `a` and `b` are local to `outer`, that `inner` uses them as free variables, which Python then stores in shared cells, and that `len` is global.

### Why it is correct

**The recorded depth is right.** The resolver's scope stack and the interpreter's environment chain are pushed and popped at the same places in the tree: a block, or a function body, opens one of each. So at every node, the number of scopes above the global one in the resolver equals the number of environments above the global one at run time, and the i-th scope from the top corresponds to the i-th environment. If the resolver finds x d scopes up, x's environment is d parents up at run time. [[Why the function case also matches|closure-shape]].

**It finds the declaration the lexical rule picks.** When the resolver reaches a use, each local scope holds exactly the names declared **earlier in the text** of that block or function, because declarations are added in text order as the walk passes them. So the innermost scope containing x holds the innermost declaration of x whose scope, "from after the declaration to the end of the block", contains the use. That is the definition of lexical scope, now enforced by recording the answer instead of searching a live environment. At run time, the recorded environment really has x when the use runs, because its declaration comes earlier in the same block and has executed.

**What it does not promise.** Late-bound globals are checked only for existence somewhere at the top level. A function that uses a global declared below it, called before that declaration runs, still fails at run time with "undefined variable". Deciding exactly which calls happen before which declarations is undecidable in general, so the rule is a deliberate approximation.

### What it costs

The resolver visits every node once. A declaration is an O(1) set insertion; a use searches up to d scopes, O(d), with d the nesting depth. The total is O(n · d) for n nodes, in practice O(n). Space is one set entry per declared name in the open scopes. The payoff is at run time: every variable access in a loop that runs a million times now skips the search, and a compiler with lexical addresses makes it a single array access.

### Where it is used

- Every compiler has this pass: Clang calls it Sema, javac's is Attr, rustc has a whole resolver crate. It runs before type checking, since the types of names depend on which declarations they refer to.
- Editors ask the same pass "go to definition", "find all references" and "rename this variable safely", through the [[Language Server Protocol|lsp]].
- Linters such as pyflakes and ESLint report undefined and unused names, the kind of mistake that in a script only shows up when the line runs.
- In flight software, static analysis of names, types and data flow is required before code is certified; nothing is allowed to fail on a misspelled name in orbit.

**Watch out:**

- Declaring the name of a `let` before resolving its right-hand side. Then `let x = x + 1;` in an inner block refers to itself.
- Opening no scope for a function's parameters, or a different number of scopes than the interpreter creates environments. Every depth is then off.
- Treating globals like locals. Then two top-level functions can no longer call each other.
- Stopping at the first error. Users fix one mistake per compile and hate it.
- Forgetting that an assignment is a use too: `x = 1;` must resolve x, and record its depth, exactly like reading it.

::: context context Why grammars cannot check declarations
A context-free grammar decides each part of a program on its own; nothing connects a use of `x` to a declaration of `x` far away. Programs where every used name is declared contain, in effect, pairs of equal strings at arbitrary distances, like the language { w c w }, which the pumping lemma for context-free languages shows is not context-free. So compilers parse with a context-free grammar and check the context-dependent rules in a separate pass.
:::

::: context recovery Reporting every error
A compiler that stops at the first error makes users fix one mistake per run. After an undefined name, the resolver can simply note the error and continue, because nothing later depends on it. Parsers recover too, usually by skipping tokens up to a semicolon or a closing brace. The art is to avoid a cascade of follow-on errors caused by the first one: many compilers suppress errors about a name once it has been reported undefined.
:::

::: context closure-shape Scopes inside functions
A function body is resolved at its declaration, with the declaration's scopes below it; at run time it runs in a new environment whose parent is the closure's environment, which is the environment of the declaration's scope. So in both, the function's own scope sits directly on top of the scopes of the place where the function was written, whoever calls it later. That is why a depth computed at the declaration stays right at every call.
:::

::: context lsp The Language Server Protocol
Microsoft published the Language Server Protocol in 2016 so that one program, a language server, can give every editor the same features for a language: completion, go to definition, find references, rename and diagnostics. A language server is mostly a compiler's front end, lexer, parser, resolver and type checker, kept running and updated on every keystroke. The resolver's table from uses to declarations is exactly what "go to definition" needs.
:::
--- task
The starter gives the lexer and parser, lesson 8's interpreter, and a `Resolver` class with most of its walk: `resolve(program)` (which collects the names of all top-level `let` and `fn` statements into `self.top_level`, walks the program, and returns `self.errors`), `statements(stmts)`, `block(stmts)` (a new scope around a list of statements) and `expr(e)`. Its scopes are `self.scopes`, a list of sets of names with the global scope first, and `self.functions` counts the functions the walk is inside. The starter also gives `ResolvedInterpreter`, which reads and assigns variables at the depth you record, and two functions: `check(source)` returns the list of errors, and `run_resolved(source)` runs a program only if it has none. Write three methods:

- `declare(name)`: add the name to the innermost scope; if that scope already has it, append the error `"NAME is already declared in this scope"` (and keep going).
- `use(node, name, message)`: find the innermost **local** scope (any but the global one) that has the name, and set `node.depth` to the number of scopes between, 0 for the innermost. If none has it, set `node.depth = None`, and append the error `message + " " + name` unless the name is in the global scope, or the walk is inside a function and the name is in `self.top_level`.
- `stmt(s)`: resolve one statement. `Let` resolves its expression, then declares. `Assign` resolves its expression, then calls `use(s, s.name, "assignment to undeclared variable")`. `If`, `While`, `Print`, `ExprStmt` and `Return` resolve their parts (a `Block` goes to `self.block`); `Return` outside any function appends `"return outside a function"`. `Fn` declares its name, then, inside one new scope with `self.functions` one higher, declares the parameters and resolves the body's statements with `self.statements`.

`expr` already calls `self.use(e, e.name, "undefined variable")` for every `Var`. For example, `check("print x; let x = 1; x = y;")` is `["undefined variable x", "undefined variable y"]`: the first `x` comes before its declaration, and by the assignment `x` is declared but `y` is not.
--- starter
from dataclasses import dataclass

KEYWORDS = {"let", "fn", "return", "if", "else", "while", "print",
            "true", "false", "and", "or", "not"}
TWO_CHAR = {"==", "!=", "<=", ">=", "->"}
ONE_CHAR = set("+-*/%<>=(){},;:")
ESCAPES = {'"': '"', "\\": "\\", "n": "\n"}
DIGITS = "0123456789"
LETTERS = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ_"


@dataclass
class Token:
    kind: str
    text: str
    line: int
    col: int


class LexError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


def tokenize(source):
    tokens = []
    i = 0
    line = 1
    col = 1
    n = len(source)

    def advance(count):
        nonlocal i, line, col
        for _ in range(count):
            if source[i] == "\n":
                line += 1
                col = 1
            else:
                col += 1
            i += 1

    while i < n:
        ch = source[i]
        start_line, start_col = line, col
        if ch in " \t\r\n":
            advance(1)
        elif ch == "#":
            while i < n and source[i] != "\n":
                advance(1)
        elif ch in DIGITS:
            j = i
            while j < n and source[j] in DIGITS:
                j += 1
            tokens.append(Token("NUMBER", source[i:j], start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch in LETTERS:
            j = i
            while j < n and (source[j] in LETTERS or source[j] in DIGITS):
                j += 1
            word = source[i:j]
            kind = "KEYWORD" if word in KEYWORDS else "IDENT"
            tokens.append(Token(kind, word, start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch == '"':
            advance(1)
            chars = []
            while True:
                if i >= n or source[i] == "\n":
                    raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                c = source[i]
                if c == '"':
                    advance(1)
                    break
                if c == "\\":
                    if i + 1 >= n or source[i + 1] == "\n":
                        raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                    if source[i + 1] not in ESCAPES:
                        raise LexError("unknown escape", line, col)
                    chars.append(ESCAPES[source[i + 1]])
                    advance(2)
                else:
                    chars.append(c)
                    advance(1)
            tokens.append(Token("STRING", "".join(chars), start_line, start_col))
        elif source[i:i + 2] in TWO_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", source[i:i + 2], start_line, start_col))
            advance(2)
        elif ch in ONE_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", ch, start_line, start_col))
            advance(1)
        else:
            raise LexError(f"unexpected character {ch!r}", start_line, start_col)
    tokens.append(Token("EOF", "", line, col))
    return tokens


@dataclass
class Num:
    value: int


@dataclass
class Str:
    value: str


@dataclass
class Bool:
    value: bool


@dataclass
class Var:
    name: str


@dataclass
class Unary:
    op: str
    expr: object


@dataclass
class Binary:
    op: str
    left: object
    right: object


@dataclass
class Call:
    callee: object
    args: list


@dataclass

class ParseError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


COMPARE = ("==", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">=")
TYPES = ("int", "bool", "str")


class Parser:
    def __init__(self, tokens):
        self.tokens = tokens
        self.pos = 0

    def peek(self, ahead=0):
        return self.tokens[min(self.pos + ahead, len(self.tokens) - 1)]

    def at(self, *texts):
        tok = self.peek()
        return tok.kind in ("OP", "KEYWORD") and tok.text in texts

    def advance(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "EOF":
            self.pos += 1
        return tok

    def error(self, message):
        tok = self.peek()
        return ParseError(message, tok.line, tok.col)

    def expect(self, text):
        if not self.at(text):
            raise self.error(f"expected '{text}'")
        return self.advance()

    def expr(self):
        return self.or_expr()

    def or_expr(self):
        left = self.and_expr()
        while self.at("or"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.and_expr())
        return left

    def and_expr(self):
        left = self.not_expr()
        while self.at("and"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.not_expr())
        return left

    def not_expr(self):
        if self.at("not"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("not", self.not_expr())
        return self.compare()

    def compare(self):
        left = self.sum()
        if self.at(*COMPARE):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.sum())
            if self.at(*COMPARE):
                raise self.error("comparisons cannot be chained")
        return left

    def sum(self):
        left = self.product()
        while self.at("+", "-"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.product())
        return left

    def product(self):
        left = self.unary()
        while self.at("*", "/", "%"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.unary())
        return left

    def unary(self):
        if self.at("-"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("-", self.unary())
        return self.call()

    def call(self):
        expr = self.primary()
        while self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            args = []
            if not self.at(")"):
                args.append(self.expr())
                while self.at(","):
                    self.advance()
                    args.append(self.expr())
            self.expect(")")
            expr = Call(expr, args)
        return expr

    def primary(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind == "NUMBER":
            self.advance()
            return Num(int(tok.text))
        if tok.kind == "STRING":
            self.advance()
            return Str(tok.text)
        if tok.kind == "IDENT":
            self.advance()
            return Var(tok.text)
        if self.at("true", "false"):
            self.advance()
            return Bool(tok.text == "true")
        if self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            inner = self.expr()
            self.expect(")")
            return inner
        raise self.error("expected an expression")

    def program(self):
        stmts = []
        while self.peek().kind != "EOF":
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        return Program(stmts)

    def statement(self):
        if self.at("let"):
            return self.let_stmt()
        if self.at("print"):
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Print(value)
        if self.at("if"):
            return self.if_stmt()
        if self.at("while"):
            self.advance()
            cond = self.expr()
            return While(cond, self.block())
        if self.at("fn"):
            return self.fn_stmt()
        if self.at("return"):
            self.advance()
            value = None if self.at(";") else self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Return(value)
        nxt = self.peek(1)
        if self.peek().kind == "IDENT" and nxt.kind == "OP" and nxt.text == "=":
            name = self.advance().text
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Assign(name, value)
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return ExprStmt(value)

    def name(self):
        if self.peek().kind != "IDENT":
            raise self.error("expected a name")
        return self.advance().text

    def type_name(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "IDENT" or tok.text not in TYPES:
            raise self.error("expected a type")
        return self.advance().text

    def let_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        self.expect("=")
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return Let(name, type_, value)

    def if_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        cond = self.expr()
        then = self.block()
        else_ = None
        if self.at("else"):
            self.advance()
            else_ = self.if_stmt() if self.at("if") else self.block()
        return If(cond, then, else_)

    def block(self):
        self.expect("{")
        stmts = []
        while not self.at("}"):
            if self.peek().kind == "EOF":
                raise self.error("expected '}'")
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        self.advance()
        return Block(stmts)

    def param(self):
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        return (name, type_)

    def fn_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        self.expect("(")
        params = []
        if not self.at(")"):
            params.append(self.param())
            while self.at(","):
                self.advance()
                params.append(self.param())
        self.expect(")")
        ret = None
        if self.at("->"):
            self.advance()
            ret = self.type_name()
        return Fn(name, params, ret, self.block())


def parse_program(tokens):
    return Parser(tokens).program()


class CometError(Exception):
    pass


def comet_div(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q


def comet_mod(a, b):
    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)


MAX_DEPTH = 40


class Closure:
    def __init__(self, decl, env):
        self.decl = decl
        self.env = env


class ReturnSignal(Exception):
    def __init__(self, value):
        super().__init__("return")
        self.value = value


def type_name(value):
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "bool"
    if isinstance(value, int):
        return "int"
    if isinstance(value, str):
        return "str"
    if isinstance(value, Closure):
        return "fn"

    return "nothing"


def show(value):
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "true" if value else "false"
    if isinstance(value, Closure):
        return f"<fn {value.decl.name}>"

    if value is None:
        raise CometError("cannot print nothing")
    return str(value)


class Environment:
    def __init__(self, parent=None):
        self.values = {}
        self.parent = parent

    def define(self, name, value):
        if name in self.values:
            raise CometError(f"{name} is already declared in this scope")
        self.values[name] = value

    def find(self, name):
        env = self
        while env is not None:
            if name in env.values:
                return env
            env = env.parent
        return None

    def lookup(self, name):
        env = self.find(name)
        if env is None:
            raise CometError(f"undefined variable {name}")
        return env.values[name]

    def assign(self, name, value):
        env = self.find(name)
        if env is None:
            raise CometError(f"assignment to undeclared variable {name}")
        env.values[name] = value


class Interpreter:
    def __init__(self):
        self.globals = Environment()
        self.env = self.globals
        self.output = []
        self.frames = []


    def run(self, program):
        for stmt in program.stmts:
            self.execute(stmt)

    def execute_block(self, stmts, env):
        previous = self.env
        self.env = env
        try:
            for stmt in stmts:
                self.execute(stmt)
        finally:
            self.env = previous

    def execute(self, stmt):
        if isinstance(stmt, Let):
            self.env.define(stmt.name, self.evaluate(stmt.expr))
        elif isinstance(stmt, Assign):
            value = self.evaluate(stmt.expr)
            self.env.assign(stmt.name, value)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Print):
            self.output.append(show(self.evaluate(stmt.expr)))
        elif isinstance(stmt, ExprStmt):
            self.evaluate(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, If):
            if self.condition(stmt.cond):
                self.execute(stmt.then)
            elif stmt.else_ is not None:
                self.execute(stmt.else_)
        elif isinstance(stmt, While):
            while self.condition(stmt.cond):
                self.execute(stmt.body)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Block):
            self.execute_block(stmt.stmts, Environment(self.env))
        elif isinstance(stmt, Fn):
            self.env.define(stmt.name, Closure(stmt, self.env))
        elif isinstance(stmt, Return):
            if not self.frames:
                raise CometError("return outside a function")
            value = None if stmt.expr is None else self.evaluate(stmt.expr)
            raise ReturnSignal(value)
        else:
            raise CometError(f"{type(stmt).__name__} is not supported yet")

    def condition(self, expr):
        value = self.evaluate(expr)
        if not isinstance(value, bool):
            raise CometError(f"condition must be bool, not {type_name(value)}")
        return value

    def evaluate(self, expr):
        if isinstance(expr, (Num, Str, Bool)):
            return expr.value
        if isinstance(expr, Var):
            return self.env.lookup(expr.name)
        if isinstance(expr, Unary):
            value = self.evaluate(expr.expr)
            if expr.op == "-":
                self.need("int", value, "-")
                return -value
            self.need("bool", value, "not")
            return not value
        if isinstance(expr, Binary):
            return self.binary(expr)
        if isinstance(expr, Call):
            callee = self.evaluate(expr.callee)
            args = [self.evaluate(arg) for arg in expr.args]
            return self.call(callee, args)
        raise CometError(f"{type(expr).__name__} is not supported yet")

    def call(self, callee, args):
        if not isinstance(callee, Closure):
            raise CometError(f"cannot call a value of type {type_name(callee)}")
        decl = callee.decl
        if len(args) != len(decl.params):
            raise CometError(f"{decl.name} expects {len(decl.params)} arguments, got {len(args)}")
        if len(self.frames) >= MAX_DEPTH:
            raise CometError("stack overflow")
        env = Environment(callee.env)
        for (name, _), value in zip(decl.params, args):
            env.define(name, value)
        self.frames.append(decl.name)
        try:
            self.execute_block(decl.body.stmts, env)
        except ReturnSignal as signal:
            return signal.value
        finally:
            self.frames.pop()
        return None

    def need(self, wanted, value, op):
        if type_name(value) != wanted:
            raise CometError(f"'{op}' needs {wanted}, not {type_name(value)}")

    def binary(self, expr):
        op = expr.op
        left = self.evaluate(expr.left)
        if op in ("and", "or"):
            self.need("bool", left, op)
            if (op == "and" and not left) or (op == "or" and left):
                return left
            right = self.evaluate(expr.right)
            self.need("bool", right, op)
            return right
        right = self.evaluate(expr.right)
        if op in ("==", "!="):
            if type_name(left) != type_name(right):
                raise CometError(f"cannot compare {type_name(left)} with {type_name(right)}")
            return (left is right if isinstance(left, Closure) else left == right) == (op == "==")
        if op == "+" and type_name(left) == "str" and type_name(right) == "str":
            return left + right
        self.need("int", left, op)
        self.need("int", right, op)
        if op == "+":
            return left + right
        if op == "-":
            return left - right
        if op == "*":
            return left * right
        if op == "/":
            return comet_div(left, right)
        if op == "%":
            return comet_mod(left, right)
        if op == "<":
            return left < right
        if op == "<=":
            return left <= right
        if op == ">":
            return left > right
        return left >= right


def run_source(source):
    interp = Interpreter()
    try:
        interp.run(parse_program(tokenize(source)))
    except CometError as e:
        return interp.output, str(e)
    return interp.output, None


class Resolver:
    def __init__(self):
        self.scopes = [set()]
        self.top_level = set()
        self.functions = 0
        self.errors = []

    def resolve(self, program):
        for stmt in program.stmts:
            if isinstance(stmt, (Let, Fn)):
                self.top_level.add(stmt.name)
        self.statements(program.stmts)
        return self.errors

    def declare(self, name):
        raise NotImplementedError("declare is not written yet")

    def use(self, node, name, message):
        raise NotImplementedError("use is not written yet")

    def statements(self, stmts):
        for stmt in stmts:
            self.stmt(stmt)

    def block(self, stmts):
        self.scopes.append(set())
        self.statements(stmts)
        self.scopes.pop()

    def stmt(self, s):
        raise NotImplementedError("stmt is not written yet")

    def expr(self, e):
        if isinstance(e, Var):
            self.use(e, e.name, "undefined variable")
        elif isinstance(e, Unary):
            self.expr(e.expr)
        elif isinstance(e, Binary):
            self.expr(e.left)
            self.expr(e.right)
        elif isinstance(e, Call):
            self.expr(e.callee)
            for arg in e.args:
                self.expr(arg)


class ResolvedInterpreter(Interpreter):
    """The lesson 8 interpreter, reading and assigning variables at the distances the resolver found."""

    def evaluate(self, expr):
        if isinstance(expr, Var):
            return self.at(expr).values[expr.name] if expr.depth is not None else self.globals.lookup(expr.name)
        return super().evaluate(expr)

    def execute(self, stmt):
        if isinstance(stmt, Assign):
            value = self.evaluate(stmt.expr)
            if stmt.depth is not None:
                self.at(stmt).values[stmt.name] = value
            else:
                self.globals.assign(stmt.name, value)
            return
        super().execute(stmt)

    def at(self, node):
        env = self.env
        for _ in range(node.depth):
            env = env.parent
        return env


def check(source):
    return Resolver().resolve(parse_program(tokenize(source)))


def run_resolved(source):
    program = parse_program(tokenize(source))
    errors = Resolver().resolve(program)
    if errors:
        return [], errors[0]
    interp = ResolvedInterpreter()
    try:
        interp.run(program)
    except CometError as e:
        return interp.output, str(e)
    return interp.output, None
