from dataclasses import dataclass

KEYWORDS = {"let", "fn", "return", "if", "else", "while", "print",
            "true", "false", "and", "or", "not"}
TWO_CHAR = {"==", "!=", "<=", ">=", "->"}
ONE_CHAR = set("+-*/%<>=(){},;:")
ESCAPES = {'"': '"', "\\": "\\", "n": "\n"}
DIGITS = "0123456789"
LETTERS = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ_"


@dataclass
class Token:
    kind: str
    text: str
    line: int
    col: int


class LexError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


def tokenize(source):
    tokens = []
    i = 0
    line = 1
    col = 1
    n = len(source)

    def advance(count):
        nonlocal i, line, col
        for _ in range(count):
            if source[i] == "\n":
                line += 1
                col = 1
            else:
                col += 1
            i += 1

    while i < n:
        ch = source[i]
        start_line, start_col = line, col
        if ch in " \t\r\n":
            advance(1)
        elif ch == "#":
            while i < n and source[i] != "\n":
                advance(1)
        elif ch in DIGITS:
            j = i
            while j < n and source[j] in DIGITS:
                j += 1
            tokens.append(Token("NUMBER", source[i:j], start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch in LETTERS:
            j = i
            while j < n and (source[j] in LETTERS or source[j] in DIGITS):
                j += 1
            word = source[i:j]
            kind = "KEYWORD" if word in KEYWORDS else "IDENT"
            tokens.append(Token(kind, word, start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch == '"':
            advance(1)
            chars = []
            while True:
                if i >= n or source[i] == "\n":
                    raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                c = source[i]
                if c == '"':
                    advance(1)
                    break
                if c == "\\":
                    if i + 1 >= n or source[i + 1] == "\n":
                        raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                    if source[i + 1] not in ESCAPES:
                        raise LexError("unknown escape", line, col)
                    chars.append(ESCAPES[source[i + 1]])
                    advance(2)
                else:
                    chars.append(c)
                    advance(1)
            tokens.append(Token("STRING", "".join(chars), start_line, start_col))
        elif source[i:i + 2] in TWO_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", source[i:i + 2], start_line, start_col))
            advance(2)
        elif ch in ONE_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", ch, start_line, start_col))
            advance(1)
        else:
            raise LexError(f"unexpected character {ch!r}", start_line, start_col)
    tokens.append(Token("EOF", "", line, col))
    return tokens

class ParseError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


COMPARE = ("==", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">=")
TYPES = ("int", "bool", "str")


class Parser:
    def __init__(self, tokens):
        self.tokens = tokens
        self.pos = 0

    def peek(self, ahead=0):
        return self.tokens[min(self.pos + ahead, len(self.tokens) - 1)]

    def at(self, *texts):
        tok = self.peek()
        return tok.kind in ("OP", "KEYWORD") and tok.text in texts

    def advance(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "EOF":
            self.pos += 1
        return tok

    def error(self, message):
        tok = self.peek()
        return ParseError(message, tok.line, tok.col)

    def expect(self, text):
        if not self.at(text):
            raise self.error(f"expected '{text}'")
        return self.advance()

    def expr(self):
        return self.or_expr()

    def or_expr(self):
        left = self.and_expr()
        while self.at("or"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.and_expr())
        return left

    def and_expr(self):
        left = self.not_expr()
        while self.at("and"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.not_expr())
        return left

    def not_expr(self):
        if self.at("not"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("not", self.not_expr())
        return self.compare()

    def compare(self):
        left = self.sum()
        if self.at(*COMPARE):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.sum())
            if self.at(*COMPARE):
                raise self.error("comparisons cannot be chained")
        return left

    def sum(self):
        left = self.product()
        while self.at("+", "-"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.product())
        return left

    def product(self):
        left = self.unary()
        while self.at("*", "/", "%"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.unary())
        return left

    def unary(self):
        if self.at("-"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("-", self.unary())
        return self.call()

    def call(self):
        expr = self.primary()
        while self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            args = []
            if not self.at(")"):
                args.append(self.expr())
                while self.at(","):
                    self.advance()
                    args.append(self.expr())
            self.expect(")")
            expr = Call(expr, args)
        return expr

    def primary(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind == "NUMBER":
            self.advance()
            return Num(int(tok.text))
        if tok.kind == "STRING":
            self.advance()
            return Str(tok.text)
        if tok.kind == "IDENT":
            self.advance()
            return Var(tok.text)
        if self.at("true", "false"):
            self.advance()
            return Bool(tok.text == "true")
        if self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            inner = self.expr()
            self.expect(")")
            return inner
        raise self.error("expected an expression")

    def program(self):
        stmts = []
        while self.peek().kind != "EOF":
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        return Program(stmts)

    def statement(self):
        if self.at("let"):
            return self.let_stmt()
        if self.at("print"):
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Print(value)
        if self.at("if"):
            return self.if_stmt()
        if self.at("while"):
            self.advance()
            cond = self.expr()
            return While(cond, self.block())
        if self.at("fn"):
            return self.fn_stmt()
        if self.at("return"):
            self.advance()
            value = None if self.at(";") else self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Return(value)
        nxt = self.peek(1)
        if self.peek().kind == "IDENT" and nxt.kind == "OP" and nxt.text == "=":
            name = self.advance().text
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Assign(name, value)
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return ExprStmt(value)

    def name(self):
        if self.peek().kind != "IDENT":
            raise self.error("expected a name")
        return self.advance().text

    def type_name(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "IDENT" or tok.text not in TYPES:
            raise self.error("expected a type")
        return self.advance().text

    def let_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        self.expect("=")
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return Let(name, type_, value)

    def if_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        cond = self.expr()
        then = self.block()
        else_ = None
        if self.at("else"):
            self.advance()
            else_ = self.if_stmt() if self.at("if") else self.block()
        return If(cond, then, else_)

    def block(self):
        self.expect("{")
        stmts = []
        while not self.at("}"):
            if self.peek().kind == "EOF":
                raise self.error("expected '}'")
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        self.advance()
        return Block(stmts)

    def param(self):
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        return (name, type_)

    def fn_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        self.expect("(")
        params = []
        if not self.at(")"):
            params.append(self.param())
            while self.at(","):
                self.advance()
                params.append(self.param())
        self.expect(")")
        ret = None
        if self.at("->"):
            self.advance()
            ret = self.type_name()
        return Fn(name, params, ret, self.block())


def parse_program(tokens):
    return Parser(tokens).program()


class CometError(Exception):
    pass


def comet_div(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q


def comet_mod(a, b):
    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)


MAX_DEPTH = 40


class Closure:
    def __init__(self, decl, env):
        self.decl = decl
        self.env = env


class ReturnSignal(Exception):
    def __init__(self, value):
        super().__init__("return")
        self.value = value


def type_name(value):
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "bool"
    if isinstance(value, int):
        return "int"
    if isinstance(value, str):
        return "str"
    if isinstance(value, Closure):
        return "fn"

    return "nothing"


def show(value):
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "true" if value else "false"
    if isinstance(value, Closure):
        return f"<fn {value.decl.name}>"

    if value is None:
        raise CometError("cannot print nothing")
    return str(value)


class Environment:
    def __init__(self, parent=None):
        self.values = {}
        self.parent = parent

    def define(self, name, value):
        if name in self.values:
            raise CometError(f"{name} is already declared in this scope")
        self.values[name] = value

    def find(self, name):
        env = self
        while env is not None:
            if name in env.values:
                return env
            env = env.parent
        return None

    def lookup(self, name):
        env = self.find(name)
        if env is None:
            raise CometError(f"undefined variable {name}")
        return env.values[name]

    def assign(self, name, value):
        env = self.find(name)
        if env is None:
            raise CometError(f"assignment to undeclared variable {name}")
        env.values[name] = value


class Interpreter:
    def __init__(self):
        self.globals = Environment()
        self.env = self.globals
        self.output = []
        self.frames = []


    def run(self, program):
        for stmt in program.stmts:
            self.execute(stmt)

    def execute_block(self, stmts, env):
        previous = self.env
        self.env = env
        try:
            for stmt in stmts:
                self.execute(stmt)
        finally:
            self.env = previous

    def execute(self, stmt):
        if isinstance(stmt, Let):
            self.env.define(stmt.name, self.evaluate(stmt.expr))
        elif isinstance(stmt, Assign):
            value = self.evaluate(stmt.expr)
            self.env.assign(stmt.name, value)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Print):
            self.output.append(show(self.evaluate(stmt.expr)))
        elif isinstance(stmt, ExprStmt):
            self.evaluate(stmt.expr)
        elif isinstance(stmt, If):
            if self.condition(stmt.cond):
                self.execute(stmt.then)
            elif stmt.else_ is not None:
                self.execute(stmt.else_)
        elif isinstance(stmt, While):
            while self.condition(stmt.cond):
                self.execute(stmt.body)
        elif isinstance(stmt, Block):
            self.execute_block(stmt.stmts, Environment(self.env))
        elif isinstance(stmt, Fn):
            self.env.define(stmt.name, Closure(stmt, self.env))
        elif isinstance(stmt, Return):
            if not self.frames:
                raise CometError("return outside a function")
            value = None if stmt.expr is None else self.evaluate(stmt.expr)
            raise ReturnSignal(value)
        else:
            raise CometError(f"{type(stmt).__name__} is not supported yet")

    def condition(self, expr):
        value = self.evaluate(expr)
        if not isinstance(value, bool):
            raise CometError(f"condition must be bool, not {type_name(value)}")
        return value

    def evaluate(self, expr):
        if isinstance(expr, (Num, Str, Bool)):
            return expr.value
        if isinstance(expr, Var):
            return self.env.lookup(expr.name)
        if isinstance(expr, Unary):
            value = self.evaluate(expr.expr)
            if expr.op == "-":
                self.need("int", value, "-")
                return -value
            self.need("bool", value, "not")
            return not value
        if isinstance(expr, Binary):
            return self.binary(expr)
        if isinstance(expr, Call):
            callee = self.evaluate(expr.callee)
            args = [self.evaluate(arg) for arg in expr.args]
            return self.call(callee, args)
        raise CometError(f"{type(expr).__name__} is not supported yet")

    def call(self, callee, args):
        if not isinstance(callee, Closure):
            raise CometError(f"cannot call a value of type {type_name(callee)}")
        decl = callee.decl
        if len(args) != len(decl.params):
            raise CometError(f"{decl.name} expects {len(decl.params)} arguments, got {len(args)}")
        if len(self.frames) >= MAX_DEPTH:
            raise CometError("stack overflow")
        env = Environment(callee.env)
        for (name, _), value in zip(decl.params, args):
            env.define(name, value)
        self.frames.append(decl.name)
        try:
            self.execute_block(decl.body.stmts, env)
        except ReturnSignal as signal:
            return signal.value
        finally:
            self.frames.pop()
        return None

    def need(self, wanted, value, op):
        if type_name(value) != wanted:
            raise CometError(f"'{op}' needs {wanted}, not {type_name(value)}")

    def binary(self, expr):
        op = expr.op
        left = self.evaluate(expr.left)
        if op in ("and", "or"):
            self.need("bool", left, op)
            if (op == "and" and not left) or (op == "or" and left):
                return left
            right = self.evaluate(expr.right)
            self.need("bool", right, op)
            return right
        right = self.evaluate(expr.right)
        if op in ("==", "!="):
            if type_name(left) != type_name(right):
                raise CometError(f"cannot compare {type_name(left)} with {type_name(right)}")
            return (left is right if isinstance(left, Closure) else left == right) == (op == "==")
        if op == "+" and type_name(left) == "str" and type_name(right) == "str":
            return left + right
        self.need("int", left, op)
        self.need("int", right, op)
        if op == "+":
            return left + right
        if op == "-":
            return left - right
        if op == "*":
            return left * right
        if op == "/":
            return comet_div(left, right)
        if op == "%":
            return comet_mod(left, right)
        if op == "<":
            return left < right
        if op == "<=":
            return left <= right
        if op == ">":
            return left > right
        return left >= right


def run_source(source):
    interp = Interpreter()
    try:
        interp.run(parse_program(tokenize(source)))
    except CometError as e:
        return interp.output, str(e)
    return interp.output, None


class Resolver:
    def __init__(self):
        self.scopes = [set()]
        self.top_level = set()
        self.functions = 0
        self.errors = []

    def resolve(self, program):
        for stmt in program.stmts:
            if isinstance(stmt, (Let, Fn)):
                self.top_level.add(stmt.name)
        self.statements(program.stmts)
        return self.errors

    def declare(self, name):
        if name in self.scopes[-1]:
            self.errors.append(f"{name} is already declared in this scope")
        self.scopes[-1].add(name)

    def use(self, node, name, message):
        for i in range(len(self.scopes) - 1, 0, -1):
            if name in self.scopes[i]:
                node.depth = len(self.scopes) - 1 - i
                return
        node.depth = None
        if name in self.scopes[0]:
            return
        if self.functions > 0 and name in self.top_level:
            return
        self.errors.append(f"{message} {name}")

    def statements(self, stmts):
        for stmt in stmts:
            self.stmt(stmt)

    def block(self, stmts):
        self.scopes.append(set())
        self.statements(stmts)
        self.scopes.pop()

    def stmt(self, s):
        if isinstance(s, Let):
            self.expr(s.expr)
            self.declare(s.name)
        elif isinstance(s, Assign):
            self.expr(s.expr)
            self.use(s, s.name, "assignment to undeclared variable")
        elif isinstance(s, (Print, ExprStmt)):
            self.expr(s.expr)
        elif isinstance(s, If):
            self.expr(s.cond)
            self.stmt(s.then)
            if s.else_ is not None:
                self.stmt(s.else_)
        elif isinstance(s, While):
            self.expr(s.cond)
            self.stmt(s.body)
        elif isinstance(s, Block):
            self.block(s.stmts)
        elif isinstance(s, Return):
            if self.functions == 0:
                self.errors.append("return outside a function")
            if s.expr is not None:
                self.expr(s.expr)
        elif isinstance(s, Fn):
            self.declare(s.name)
            self.function(s)

    def function(self, s):
        self.functions += 1
        self.scopes.append(set())
        for name, _ in s.params:
            self.declare(name)
        self.statements(s.body.stmts)
        self.scopes.pop()
        self.functions -= 1

    def expr(self, e):
        if isinstance(e, Var):
            self.use(e, e.name, "undefined variable")
        elif isinstance(e, Unary):
            self.expr(e.expr)
        elif isinstance(e, Binary):
            self.expr(e.left)
            self.expr(e.right)
        elif isinstance(e, Call):
            self.expr(e.callee)
            for arg in e.args:
                self.expr(arg)


class ResolvedInterpreter(Interpreter):
    """The lesson 8 interpreter, reading and assigning variables at the distances the resolver found."""

    def evaluate(self, expr):
        if isinstance(expr, Var):
            return self.at(expr).values[expr.name] if expr.depth is not None else self.globals.lookup(expr.name)
        return super().evaluate(expr)

    def execute(self, stmt):
        if isinstance(stmt, Assign):
            value = self.evaluate(stmt.expr)
            if stmt.depth is not None:
                self.at(stmt).values[stmt.name] = value
            else:
                self.globals.assign(stmt.name, value)
            return
        super().execute(stmt)

    def at(self, node):
        env = self.env
        for _ in range(node.depth):
            env = env.parent
        return env


def check(source):
    return Resolver().resolve(parse_program(tokenize(source)))


def run_resolved(source):
    program = parse_program(tokenize(source))
    errors = Resolver().resolve(program)
    if errors:
        return [], errors[0]
    interp = ResolvedInterpreter()
    try:
        interp.run(program)
    except CometError as e:
        return interp.output, str(e)
    return interp.output, None
--- hint
`use` loops `for i in range(len(self.scopes) - 1, 0, -1)`: stopping before index 0 leaves the global scope out. The depth for a hit at index i is `len(self.scopes) - 1 - i`.
--- hint
After the loop in `use`, set the depth to `None` and return quietly if `name in self.scopes[0]`, or if `self.functions > 0 and name in self.top_level`; otherwise record the error.
--- hint
For `Fn` in `stmt`: `self.declare(s.name)`, then `self.functions += 1`, `self.scopes.append(set())`, declare each parameter name from `s.params`, `self.statements(s.body.stmts)`, and undo both.

+++ practice | A symbol table
--- task
A compiler's **symbol table** lists every declaration with what kind of name it is and where it lives. Write `symbols(source)`, which parses the program and returns a list of `(name, kind, depth)` triples, one for every declaration, in the order the declarations appear in the text.

- `kind` is `"var"` for a `let`, `"fn"` for a function, and `"param"` for a parameter.
- `depth` is the number of scopes around the declaration, counting the scopes the interpreter creates: 0 at the top level; each block adds 1, and so does a function's own scope, which holds its parameters and its body's top-level statements. So a function declared at the top level has depth 0 and its parameters depth 1.
- A function's parameters come right after the function, before anything in its body.

For example, `symbols("let x = 1; fn f(a) { let c = a; }")` is `[("x", "var", 0), ("f", "fn", 0), ("a", "param", 1), ("c", "var", 1)]`.
--- starter
from dataclasses import dataclass

KEYWORDS = {"let", "fn", "return", "if", "else", "while", "print",
            "true", "false", "and", "or", "not"}
TWO_CHAR = {"==", "!=", "<=", ">=", "->"}
ONE_CHAR = set("+-*/%<>=(){},;:")
ESCAPES = {'"': '"', "\\": "\\", "n": "\n"}
DIGITS = "0123456789"
LETTERS = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ_"


@dataclass
class Token:
    kind: str
    text: str
    line: int
    col: int


class LexError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


def tokenize(source):
    tokens = []
    i = 0
    line = 1
    col = 1
    n = len(source)

    def advance(count):
        nonlocal i, line, col
        for _ in range(count):
            if source[i] == "\n":
                line += 1
                col = 1
            else:
                col += 1
            i += 1

    while i < n:
        ch = source[i]
        start_line, start_col = line, col
        if ch in " \t\r\n":
            advance(1)
        elif ch == "#":
            while i < n and source[i] != "\n":
                advance(1)
        elif ch in DIGITS:
            j = i
            while j < n and source[j] in DIGITS:
                j += 1
            tokens.append(Token("NUMBER", source[i:j], start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch in LETTERS:
            j = i
            while j < n and (source[j] in LETTERS or source[j] in DIGITS):
                j += 1
            word = source[i:j]
            kind = "KEYWORD" if word in KEYWORDS else "IDENT"
            tokens.append(Token(kind, word, start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch == '"':
            advance(1)
            chars = []
            while True:
                if i >= n or source[i] == "\n":
                    raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                c = source[i]
                if c == '"':
                    advance(1)
                    break
                if c == "\\":
                    if i + 1 >= n or source[i + 1] == "\n":
                        raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                    if source[i + 1] not in ESCAPES:
                        raise LexError("unknown escape", line, col)
                    chars.append(ESCAPES[source[i + 1]])
                    advance(2)
                else:
                    chars.append(c)
                    advance(1)
            tokens.append(Token("STRING", "".join(chars), start_line, start_col))
        elif source[i:i + 2] in TWO_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", source[i:i + 2], start_line, start_col))
            advance(2)
        elif ch in ONE_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", ch, start_line, start_col))
            advance(1)
        else:
            raise LexError(f"unexpected character {ch!r}", start_line, start_col)
    tokens.append(Token("EOF", "", line, col))
    return tokens

class ParseError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


COMPARE = ("==", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">=")
TYPES = ("int", "bool", "str")


class Parser:
    def __init__(self, tokens):
        self.tokens = tokens
        self.pos = 0

    def peek(self, ahead=0):
        return self.tokens[min(self.pos + ahead, len(self.tokens) - 1)]

    def at(self, *texts):
        tok = self.peek()
        return tok.kind in ("OP", "KEYWORD") and tok.text in texts

    def advance(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "EOF":
            self.pos += 1
        return tok

    def error(self, message):
        tok = self.peek()
        return ParseError(message, tok.line, tok.col)

    def expect(self, text):
        if not self.at(text):
            raise self.error(f"expected '{text}'")
        return self.advance()

    def expr(self):
        return self.or_expr()

    def or_expr(self):
        left = self.and_expr()
        while self.at("or"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.and_expr())
        return left

    def and_expr(self):
        left = self.not_expr()
        while self.at("and"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.not_expr())
        return left

    def not_expr(self):
        if self.at("not"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("not", self.not_expr())
        return self.compare()

    def compare(self):
        left = self.sum()
        if self.at(*COMPARE):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.sum())
            if self.at(*COMPARE):
                raise self.error("comparisons cannot be chained")
        return left

    def sum(self):
        left = self.product()
        while self.at("+", "-"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.product())
        return left

    def product(self):
        left = self.unary()
        while self.at("*", "/", "%"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.unary())
        return left

    def unary(self):
        if self.at("-"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("-", self.unary())
        return self.call()

    def call(self):
        expr = self.primary()
        while self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            args = []
            if not self.at(")"):
                args.append(self.expr())
                while self.at(","):
                    self.advance()
                    args.append(self.expr())
            self.expect(")")
            expr = Call(expr, args)
        return expr

    def primary(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind == "NUMBER":
            self.advance()
            return Num(int(tok.text))
        if tok.kind == "STRING":
            self.advance()
            return Str(tok.text)
        if tok.kind == "IDENT":
            self.advance()
            return Var(tok.text)
        if self.at("true", "false"):
            self.advance()
            return Bool(tok.text == "true")
        if self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            inner = self.expr()
            self.expect(")")
            return inner
        raise self.error("expected an expression")

    def program(self):
        stmts = []
        while self.peek().kind != "EOF":
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        return Program(stmts)

    def statement(self):
        if self.at("let"):
            return self.let_stmt()
        if self.at("print"):
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Print(value)
        if self.at("if"):
            return self.if_stmt()
        if self.at("while"):
            self.advance()
            cond = self.expr()
            return While(cond, self.block())
        if self.at("fn"):
            return self.fn_stmt()
        if self.at("return"):
            self.advance()
            value = None if self.at(";") else self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Return(value)
        nxt = self.peek(1)
        if self.peek().kind == "IDENT" and nxt.kind == "OP" and nxt.text == "=":
            name = self.advance().text
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Assign(name, value)
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return ExprStmt(value)

    def name(self):
        if self.peek().kind != "IDENT":
            raise self.error("expected a name")
        return self.advance().text

    def type_name(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "IDENT" or tok.text not in TYPES:
            raise self.error("expected a type")
        return self.advance().text

    def let_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        self.expect("=")
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return Let(name, type_, value)

    def if_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        cond = self.expr()
        then = self.block()
        else_ = None
        if self.at("else"):
            self.advance()
            else_ = self.if_stmt() if self.at("if") else self.block()
        return If(cond, then, else_)

    def block(self):
        self.expect("{")
        stmts = []
        while not self.at("}"):
            if self.peek().kind == "EOF":
                raise self.error("expected '}'")
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        self.advance()
        return Block(stmts)

    def param(self):
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        return (name, type_)

    def fn_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        self.expect("(")
        params = []
        if not self.at(")"):
            params.append(self.param())
            while self.at(","):
                self.advance()
                params.append(self.param())
        self.expect(")")
        ret = None
        if self.at("->"):
            self.advance()
            ret = self.type_name()
        return Fn(name, params, ret, self.block())


def parse_program(tokens):
    return Parser(tokens).program()

    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q

    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)

from dataclasses import dataclass

KEYWORDS = {"let", "fn", "return", "if", "else", "while", "print",
            "true", "false", "and", "or", "not"}
TWO_CHAR = {"==", "!=", "<=", ">=", "->"}
ONE_CHAR = set("+-*/%<>=(){},;:")
ESCAPES = {'"': '"', "\\": "\\", "n": "\n"}
DIGITS = "0123456789"
LETTERS = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ_"

    kind: str
    text: str

class LexError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


def tokenize(source):
    tokens = []
    i = 0
    line = 1
    col = 1
    n = len(source)

    def advance(count):
        nonlocal i, line, col
        for _ in range(count):
            if source[i] == "\n":
                line += 1
                col = 1
            else:
                col += 1
            i += 1

    while i < n:
        ch = source[i]
        start_line, start_col = line, col
        if ch in " \t\r\n":
            advance(1)
        elif ch == "#":
            while i < n and source[i] != "\n":
                advance(1)
        elif ch in DIGITS:
            j = i
            while j < n and source[j] in DIGITS:
                j += 1
            tokens.append(Token("NUMBER", source[i:j], start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch in LETTERS:
            j = i
            while j < n and (source[j] in LETTERS or source[j] in DIGITS):
                j += 1
            word = source[i:j]
            kind = "KEYWORD" if word in KEYWORDS else "IDENT"
            tokens.append(Token(kind, word, start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch == '"':
            advance(1)
            chars = []
            while True:
                if i >= n or source[i] == "\n":
                    raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                c = source[i]
                if c == '"':
                    advance(1)
                    break
                if c == "\\":
                    if i + 1 >= n or source[i + 1] == "\n":
                        raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                    if source[i + 1] not in ESCAPES:
                        raise LexError("unknown escape", line, col)
                    chars.append(ESCAPES[source[i + 1]])
                    advance(2)
                else:
                    chars.append(c)
                    advance(1)
            tokens.append(Token("STRING", "".join(chars), start_line, start_col))
        elif source[i:i + 2] in TWO_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", source[i:i + 2], start_line, start_col))
            advance(2)
        elif ch in ONE_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", ch, start_line, start_col))
            advance(1)
        else:
            raise LexError(f"unexpected character {ch!r}", start_line, start_col)
    tokens.append(Token("EOF", "", line, col))
    return tokens

class ParseError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


COMPARE = ("==", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">=")
TYPES = ("int", "bool", "str")


class Parser:
    def __init__(self, tokens):
        self.tokens = tokens
        self.pos = 0

    def peek(self, ahead=0):
        return self.tokens[min(self.pos + ahead, len(self.tokens) - 1)]

    def at(self, *texts):
        tok = self.peek()
        return tok.kind in ("OP", "KEYWORD") and tok.text in texts

    def advance(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "EOF":
            self.pos += 1
        return tok

    def error(self, message):
        tok = self.peek()
        return ParseError(message, tok.line, tok.col)

    def expect(self, text):
        if not self.at(text):
            raise self.error(f"expected '{text}'")
        return self.advance()

    def expr(self):
        return self.or_expr()

    def or_expr(self):
        left = self.and_expr()
        while self.at("or"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.and_expr())
        return left

    def and_expr(self):
        left = self.not_expr()
        while self.at("and"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.not_expr())
        return left

    def not_expr(self):
        if self.at("not"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("not", self.not_expr())
        return self.compare()

    def compare(self):
        left = self.sum()
        if self.at(*COMPARE):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.sum())
            if self.at(*COMPARE):
                raise self.error("comparisons cannot be chained")
        return left

    def sum(self):
        left = self.product()
        while self.at("+", "-"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.product())
        return left

    def product(self):
        left = self.unary()
        while self.at("*", "/", "%"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.unary())
        return left

    def unary(self):
        if self.at("-"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("-", self.unary())
        return self.call()

    def call(self):
        expr = self.primary()
        while self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            args = []
            if not self.at(")"):
                args.append(self.expr())
                while self.at(","):
                    self.advance()
                    args.append(self.expr())
            self.expect(")")
            expr = Call(expr, args)
        return expr

    def primary(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind == "NUMBER":
            self.advance()
            return Num(int(tok.text))
        if tok.kind == "STRING":
            self.advance()
            return Str(tok.text)
        if tok.kind == "IDENT":
            self.advance()
            return Var(tok.text)
        if self.at("true", "false"):
            self.advance()
            return Bool(tok.text == "true")
        if self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            inner = self.expr()
            self.expect(")")
            return inner
        raise self.error("expected an expression")

    def program(self):
        stmts = []
        while self.peek().kind != "EOF":
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        return Program(stmts)

    def statement(self):
        if self.at("let"):
            return self.let_stmt()
        if self.at("print"):
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Print(value)
        if self.at("if"):
            return self.if_stmt()
        if self.at("while"):
            self.advance()
            cond = self.expr()
            return While(cond, self.block())
        if self.at("fn"):
            return self.fn_stmt()
        if self.at("return"):
            self.advance()
            value = None if self.at(";") else self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Return(value)
        nxt = self.peek(1)
        if self.peek().kind == "IDENT" and nxt.kind == "OP" and nxt.text == "=":
            name = self.advance().text
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Assign(name, value)
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return ExprStmt(value)

    def name(self):
        if self.peek().kind != "IDENT":
            raise self.error("expected a name")
        return self.advance().text

    def type_name(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "IDENT" or tok.text not in TYPES:
            raise self.error("expected a type")
        return self.advance().text

    def let_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        self.expect("=")
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return Let(name, type_, value)

    def if_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        cond = self.expr()
        then = self.block()
        else_ = None
        if self.at("else"):
            self.advance()
            else_ = self.if_stmt() if self.at("if") else self.block()
        return If(cond, then, else_)

    def block(self):
        self.expect("{")
        stmts = []
        while not self.at("}"):
            if self.peek().kind == "EOF":
                raise self.error("expected '}'")
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        self.advance()
        return Block(stmts)

    def param(self):
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        return (name, type_)

    def fn_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        self.expect("(")
        params = []
        if not self.at(")"):
            params.append(self.param())
            while self.at(","):
                self.advance()
                params.append(self.param())
        self.expect(")")
        ret = None
        if self.at("->"):
            self.advance()
            ret = self.type_name()
        return Fn(name, params, ret, self.block())


def parse_program(tokens):
    return Parser(tokens).program()

def comet_div(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q

def symbols(source):
    program = parse_program(tokenize(source))
    table = []

    def stmts(items, depth):
        for s in items:
            stmt(s, depth)

    def stmt(s, depth):
        if isinstance(s, Let):
            table.append((s.name, "var", depth))
        elif isinstance(s, Fn):
            table.append((s.name, "fn", depth))
            for name, _ in s.params:
                table.append((name, "param", depth + 1))
            stmts(s.body.stmts, depth + 1)
        elif isinstance(s, If):
            stmt(s.then, depth)
            if s.else_ is not None:
                stmt(s.else_, depth)
        elif isinstance(s, While):
            stmt(s.body, depth)
        elif isinstance(s, Block):
            stmts(s.stmts, depth + 1)

    stmts(program.stmts, 0)
    return table
--- hint
Walk the statements recursively, passing the current depth down. A `Block` walks its statements at depth + 1; `If` and `While` pass their blocks on at the same depth, since the block itself adds the 1.
--- hint
For an `Fn` at depth d: record the function at d, each parameter at d + 1, then walk the body's statements (not the body block itself) at d + 1, since the parameters and the body share one scope.
--- check case | The example from the task
symbols("let x = 1; fn f(a) { let c = a; }")
=> [("x", "var", 0), ("f", "fn", 0), ("a", "param", 1), ("c", "var", 1)]
--- check case | Blocks, loops and nested functions
symbols("let x = 1; fn f(a, b) { let c = a; if true { let d = c; fn g(e) { } } } while x < 0 { let w = 1; }")
=> [("x", "var", 0), ("f", "fn", 0), ("a", "param", 1), ("b", "param", 1), ("c", "var", 1), ("d", "var", 2), ("g", "fn", 2), ("e", "param", 3), ("w", "var", 1)]
--- check case | else if chains and else blocks
symbols("if true { let a = 1; } else if false { let b = 2; } else { if true { let c = 3; } }")
=> [("a", "var", 1), ("b", "var", 1), ("c", "var", 2)]
--- check case | No declarations
symbols("print 1;")
=> []

+++ practice | Lexical addresses
--- task
Compilers turn each local variable into a **lexical address** (depth, index): how many scopes up its declaration is, and its position among the names declared in that scope, counting from 0 in declaration order, where a function's parameters come first in its scope. Global variables stay names. Write `addresses(source)`, which returns one triple for every **read** of a name (every `Var` node, including a function name in a call), in the order the reads appear in the text:

- `(name, depth, index)` for a local variable, with depth 0 for the use's own scope;
- `(name, None, None)` for a name found in no local scope (global or undeclared).

Scopes follow the interpreter: one per block, and one per function for its parameters and body. A declaration counts from just after it, so the right side of a `let` cannot see the name it declares. Assignment targets are not reads, but their right sides may contain reads.

For example, `addresses("fn f(a, b) { let c = a + b; print c; }")` is `[("a", 0, 0), ("b", 0, 1), ("c", 0, 2)]`.

TYPES = ("int", "bool", "str")


class Parser:
    def __init__(self, tokens):
        self.tokens = tokens
        self.pos = 0

    def peek(self, ahead=0):

    def at(self, *texts):

    def advance(self):

        if tok.kind != "EOF":
            self.pos += 1
        return tok

    def error(self, message):

        return ParseError(message, tok.line, tok.col)

    def expect(self, text):
        if not self.at(text):
            raise self.error(f"expected '{text}'")
        return self.advance()

    def expr(self):
        return self.or_expr()

    def or_expr(self):

            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.and_expr())
        return left

    def and_expr(self):
        left = self.not_expr()

            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.not_expr())
        return left

    def not_expr(self):
        if self.at("not"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("not", self.not_expr())
        return self.compare()

    def compare(self):
        left = self.sum()
        if self.at(*COMPARE):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.sum())
            if self.at(*COMPARE):
                raise self.error("comparisons cannot be chained")
        return left

    def sum(self):
        left = self.product()
        while self.at("+", "-"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.product())
        return left

    def product(self):
        left = self.unary()
        while self.at("*", "/", "%"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.unary())
        return left

    def unary(self):
        if self.at("-"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("-", self.unary())
        return self.call()

    def call(self):
        expr = self.primary()
        while self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            args = []
            if not self.at(")"):
                args.append(self.expr())
                while self.at(","):
                    self.advance()
                    args.append(self.expr())
            self.expect(")")
            expr = Call(expr, args)
        return expr

    def primary(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind == "NUMBER":
            self.advance()
            return Num(int(tok.text))
        if tok.kind == "STRING":
            self.advance()
            return Str(tok.text)
        if tok.kind == "IDENT":
            self.advance()
            return Var(tok.text)
        if self.at("true", "false"):
            self.advance()
            return Bool(tok.text == "true")
        if self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            inner = self.expr()
            self.expect(")")
            return inner
        raise self.error("expected an expression")

    def program(self):
        stmts = []
        while self.peek().kind != "EOF":
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        return Program(stmts)

    def statement(self):
        if self.at("let"):
            return self.let_stmt()
        if self.at("print"):
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Print(value)
        if self.at("if"):
            return self.if_stmt()
        if self.at("while"):
            self.advance()
            cond = self.expr()
            return While(cond, self.block())
        if self.at("fn"):
            return self.fn_stmt()
        if self.at("return"):
            self.advance()
            value = None if self.at(";") else self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Return(value)
        nxt = self.peek(1)
        if self.peek().kind == "IDENT" and nxt.kind == "OP" and nxt.text == "=":
            name = self.advance().text
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Assign(name, value)
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return ExprStmt(value)

    def name(self):
        if self.peek().kind != "IDENT":
            raise self.error("expected a name")
        return self.advance().text

    def type_name(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "IDENT" or tok.text not in TYPES:
            raise self.error("expected a type")
        return self.advance().text

    def let_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        self.expect("=")
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return Let(name, type_, value)

    def if_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        cond = self.expr()
        then = self.block()
        else_ = None
        if self.at("else"):
            self.advance()
            else_ = self.if_stmt() if self.at("if") else self.block()
        return If(cond, then, else_)

    def block(self):
        self.expect("{")
        stmts = []
        while not self.at("}"):
            if self.peek().kind == "EOF":
                raise self.error("expected '}'")
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        self.advance()
        return Block(stmts)

    def param(self):
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        return (name, type_)

    def fn_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        self.expect("(")
        params = []
        if not self.at(")"):
            params.append(self.param())
            while self.at(","):
                self.advance()
                params.append(self.param())
        self.expect(")")
        ret = None
        if self.at("->"):
            self.advance()
            ret = self.type_name()
        return Fn(name, params, ret, self.block())


def parse_program(tokens):
    return Parser(tokens).program()

    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q

from dataclasses import dataclass

KEYWORDS = {"let", "fn", "return", "if", "else", "while", "print",
            "true", "false", "and", "or", "not"}
TWO_CHAR = {"==", "!=", "<=", ">=", "->"}
ONE_CHAR = set("+-*/%<>=(){},;:")
ESCAPES = {'"': '"', "\\": "\\", "n": "\n"}
DIGITS = "0123456789"
LETTERS = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ_"


@dataclass
class Token:
    kind: str
    text: str
    line: int
    col: int


class LexError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


def tokenize(source):
    tokens = []
    i = 0
    line = 1
    col = 1
    n = len(source)

    def advance(count):
        nonlocal i, line, col
        for _ in range(count):
            if source[i] == "\n":
                line += 1
                col = 1
            else:
                col += 1
            i += 1

    while i < n:
        ch = source[i]
        start_line, start_col = line, col
        if ch in " \t\r\n":
            advance(1)
        elif ch == "#":
            while i < n and source[i] != "\n":
                advance(1)
        elif ch in DIGITS:
            j = i
            while j < n and source[j] in DIGITS:
                j += 1
            tokens.append(Token("NUMBER", source[i:j], start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch in LETTERS:
            j = i
            while j < n and (source[j] in LETTERS or source[j] in DIGITS):
                j += 1
            word = source[i:j]
            kind = "KEYWORD" if word in KEYWORDS else "IDENT"
            tokens.append(Token(kind, word, start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch == '"':
            advance(1)
            chars = []
            while True:
                if i >= n or source[i] == "\n":
                    raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                c = source[i]
                if c == '"':
                    advance(1)
                    break
                if c == "\\":
                    if i + 1 >= n or source[i + 1] == "\n":
                        raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                    if source[i + 1] not in ESCAPES:
                        raise LexError("unknown escape", line, col)
                    chars.append(ESCAPES[source[i + 1]])
                    advance(2)
                else:
                    chars.append(c)
                    advance(1)
            tokens.append(Token("STRING", "".join(chars), start_line, start_col))
        elif source[i:i + 2] in TWO_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", source[i:i + 2], start_line, start_col))
            advance(2)
        elif ch in ONE_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", ch, start_line, start_col))
            advance(1)
        else:
            raise LexError(f"unexpected character {ch!r}", start_line, start_col)
    tokens.append(Token("EOF", "", line, col))
    return tokens

class ParseError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


COMPARE = ("==", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">=")
TYPES = ("int", "bool", "str")


class Parser:
    def __init__(self, tokens):
        self.tokens = tokens
        self.pos = 0

    def peek(self, ahead=0):
        return self.tokens[min(self.pos + ahead, len(self.tokens) - 1)]

    def at(self, *texts):
        tok = self.peek()
        return tok.kind in ("OP", "KEYWORD") and tok.text in texts

    def advance(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "EOF":
            self.pos += 1
        return tok

    def error(self, message):
        tok = self.peek()
        return ParseError(message, tok.line, tok.col)

    def expect(self, text):
        if not self.at(text):
            raise self.error(f"expected '{text}'")
        return self.advance()

    def expr(self):
        return self.or_expr()

    def or_expr(self):
        left = self.and_expr()
        while self.at("or"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.and_expr())
        return left

    def and_expr(self):
        left = self.not_expr()
        while self.at("and"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.not_expr())
        return left

    def not_expr(self):
        if self.at("not"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("not", self.not_expr())
        return self.compare()

    def compare(self):
        left = self.sum()
        if self.at(*COMPARE):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.sum())
            if self.at(*COMPARE):
                raise self.error("comparisons cannot be chained")
        return left

    def sum(self):
        left = self.product()
        while self.at("+", "-"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.product())
        return left

    def product(self):
        left = self.unary()
        while self.at("*", "/", "%"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.unary())
        return left

    def unary(self):
        if self.at("-"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("-", self.unary())
        return self.call()

    def call(self):
        expr = self.primary()
        while self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            args = []
            if not self.at(")"):
                args.append(self.expr())
                while self.at(","):
                    self.advance()
                    args.append(self.expr())
            self.expect(")")
            expr = Call(expr, args)
        return expr

    def primary(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind == "NUMBER":
            self.advance()
            return Num(int(tok.text))
        if tok.kind == "STRING":
            self.advance()
            return Str(tok.text)
        if tok.kind == "IDENT":
            self.advance()
            return Var(tok.text)
        if self.at("true", "false"):
            self.advance()
            return Bool(tok.text == "true")
        if self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            inner = self.expr()
            self.expect(")")
            return inner
        raise self.error("expected an expression")

    def program(self):
        stmts = []
        while self.peek().kind != "EOF":
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        return Program(stmts)

    def statement(self):
        if self.at("let"):
            return self.let_stmt()
        if self.at("print"):
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Print(value)
        if self.at("if"):
            return self.if_stmt()
        if self.at("while"):
            self.advance()
            cond = self.expr()
            return While(cond, self.block())
        if self.at("fn"):
            return self.fn_stmt()
        if self.at("return"):
            self.advance()
            value = None if self.at(";") else self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Return(value)
        nxt = self.peek(1)
        if self.peek().kind == "IDENT" and nxt.kind == "OP" and nxt.text == "=":
            name = self.advance().text
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Assign(name, value)
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return ExprStmt(value)

    def name(self):
        if self.peek().kind != "IDENT":
            raise self.error("expected a name")
        return self.advance().text

    def type_name(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "IDENT" or tok.text not in TYPES:
            raise self.error("expected a type")
        return self.advance().text

    def let_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        self.expect("=")
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return Let(name, type_, value)

    def if_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        cond = self.expr()
        then = self.block()
        else_ = None
        if self.at("else"):
            self.advance()
            else_ = self.if_stmt() if self.at("if") else self.block()
        return If(cond, then, else_)

    def block(self):
        self.expect("{")
        stmts = []
        while not self.at("}"):
            if self.peek().kind == "EOF":
                raise self.error("expected '}'")
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        self.advance()
        return Block(stmts)

    def param(self):
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        return (name, type_)

    def fn_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        self.expect("(")
        params = []
        if not self.at(")"):
            params.append(self.param())
            while self.at(","):
                self.advance()
                params.append(self.param())
        self.expect(")")
        ret = None
        if self.at("->"):
            self.advance()
            ret = self.type_name()
        return Fn(name, params, ret, self.block())


def parse_program(tokens):
    return Parser(tokens).program()


class CometError(Exception):
    pass


def comet_div(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q


def comet_mod(a, b):
    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)


def addresses(source):
    program = parse_program(tokenize(source))
    scopes = [[]]
    found = []

    def use(name):
        for i in range(len(scopes) - 1, 0, -1):
            if name in scopes[i]:
                found.append((name, len(scopes) - 1 - i, scopes[i].index(name)))
                return
        found.append((name, None, None))

    def expr(e):
        if isinstance(e, Var):
            use(e.name)
        elif isinstance(e, Unary):
            expr(e.expr)
        elif isinstance(e, Binary):
            expr(e.left)
            expr(e.right)
        elif isinstance(e, Call):
            expr(e.callee)
            for arg in e.args:
                expr(arg)

    def block(items, names=()):
        scopes.append(list(names))
        for s in items:
            stmt(s)
        scopes.pop()

    def stmt(s):
        if isinstance(s, Let):
            expr(s.expr)
            scopes[-1].append(s.name)
        elif isinstance(s, (Assign, Print, ExprStmt)):
            expr(s.expr)
        elif isinstance(s, Return):
            if s.expr is not None:
                expr(s.expr)
        elif isinstance(s, If):
            expr(s.cond)
            stmt(s.then)
            if s.else_ is not None:
                stmt(s.else_)
        elif isinstance(s, While):
            expr(s.cond)
            stmt(s.body)
        elif isinstance(s, Block):
            block(s.stmts)
        elif isinstance(s, Fn):
            scopes[-1].append(s.name)
            block(s.body.stmts, [name for name, _ in s.params])

    for s in program.stmts:
        stmt(s)
    return found
--- hint
Keep a stack of **lists** of names instead of sets, so the position of a name is `scope.index(name)`. The global scope is the first list; searching stops before it.
--- hint
An `Fn` adds its own name to the current list, then opens a new list that starts with its parameter names and walks the body's statements in it. A `Let` walks its right side first, then appends its name.
--- check case | The example from the task
addresses("fn f(a, b) { let c = a + b; print c; }")
=> [("a", 0, 0), ("b", 0, 1), ("c", 0, 2)]
--- check case | Blocks, globals and a call of the function itself
addresses("let x = 1; fn f(a, b) { let c = a + b; if true { let d = c; print d + x + f(a); } } print zz;")
=> [("a", 0, 0), ("b", 0, 1), ("c", 1, 2), ("d", 0, 0), ("x", None, None), ("f", None, None), ("a", 1, 0), ("zz", None, None)]
--- check case | The right side of a let sees the outer variable
addresses("fn f(v) { if true { let v = v + 1; print v; } }")
=> [("v", 1, 0), ("v", 0, 0)]
--- check case | A nested function reaching two levels up
addresses("fn outer(p) { let q = 1; fn inner(r) { return p + q + r + inner(0); } return inner; }")
=> [("p", 1, 0), ("q", 1, 1), ("r", 0, 0), ("inner", 1, 2), ("inner", 0, 2)]

+++ practice | Unused names
--- task
A linter built on name resolution warns about local names that are declared and never read. Write `warnings(source)`, which returns a list of warning strings in the order the declarations appear in the text:

- `"unused variable x"` for a `let`, `"unused parameter p"` for a parameter, and `"unused function f"` for a function, but only for names declared **inside** a block or a function; top-level names may be used by code elsewhere and are never reported.
- A name is read when a `Var` node resolves to it under Comet's scope rules (a call of a function reads its name). An assignment to a name is not a read of it.
- Names starting with `_` are never reported: that is how programmers mark a name as unused on purpose.

For example, `warnings("fn f(a, b) { return a; }")` is `["unused parameter b"]`.

def tokenize(source):

    i = 0
    line = 1
    col = 1
    n = len(source)

        for _ in range(count):

                col = 1
            else:
                col += 1
            i += 1

    while i < n:
        ch = source[i]
        start_line, start_col = line, col
        if ch in " \t\r\n":
            advance(1)
        elif ch == "#":
            while i < n and source[i] != "\n":
                advance(1)
        elif ch in DIGITS:
            j = i
            while j < n and source[j] in DIGITS:
                j += 1
            tokens.append(Token("NUMBER", source[i:j], start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch in LETTERS:
            j = i
            while j < n and (source[j] in LETTERS or source[j] in DIGITS):
                j += 1
            word = source[i:j]
            kind = "KEYWORD" if word in KEYWORDS else "IDENT"
            tokens.append(Token(kind, word, start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch == '"':

                if i >= n or source[i] == "\n":
                    raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                c = source[i]
                if c == '"':
                    advance(1)
                    break
                if c == "\\":
                    if i + 1 >= n or source[i + 1] == "\n":
                        raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                    if source[i + 1] not in ESCAPES:
                        raise LexError("unknown escape", line, col)
                    chars.append(ESCAPES[source[i + 1]])
                    advance(2)
                else:
                    chars.append(c)
                    advance(1)
            tokens.append(Token("STRING", "".join(chars), start_line, start_col))
        elif source[i:i + 2] in TWO_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", source[i:i + 2], start_line, start_col))
            advance(2)
        elif ch in ONE_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", ch, start_line, start_col))
            advance(1)
        else:
            raise LexError(f"unexpected character {ch!r}", start_line, start_col)
    tokens.append(Token("EOF", "", line, col))
    return tokens

class ParseError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


COMPARE = ("==", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">=")
TYPES = ("int", "bool", "str")


class Parser:
    def __init__(self, tokens):
        self.tokens = tokens
        self.pos = 0

    def peek(self, ahead=0):
        return self.tokens[min(self.pos + ahead, len(self.tokens) - 1)]

    def at(self, *texts):
        tok = self.peek()
        return tok.kind in ("OP", "KEYWORD") and tok.text in texts

    def advance(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "EOF":
            self.pos += 1
        return tok

    def error(self, message):
        tok = self.peek()
        return ParseError(message, tok.line, tok.col)

    def expect(self, text):
        if not self.at(text):
            raise self.error(f"expected '{text}'")
        return self.advance()

    def expr(self):
        return self.or_expr()

    def or_expr(self):
        left = self.and_expr()
        while self.at("or"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.and_expr())
        return left

    def and_expr(self):
        left = self.not_expr()
        while self.at("and"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.not_expr())
        return left

    def not_expr(self):
        if self.at("not"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("not", self.not_expr())
        return self.compare()

    def compare(self):
        left = self.sum()
        if self.at(*COMPARE):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.sum())
            if self.at(*COMPARE):
                raise self.error("comparisons cannot be chained")
        return left

    def sum(self):
        left = self.product()
        while self.at("+", "-"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.product())
        return left

    def product(self):
        left = self.unary()
        while self.at("*", "/", "%"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.unary())
        return left

    def unary(self):
        if self.at("-"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("-", self.unary())
        return self.call()

    def call(self):
        expr = self.primary()
        while self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            args = []
            if not self.at(")"):
                args.append(self.expr())
                while self.at(","):
                    self.advance()
                    args.append(self.expr())
            self.expect(")")
            expr = Call(expr, args)
        return expr

    def primary(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind == "NUMBER":
            self.advance()
            return Num(int(tok.text))
        if tok.kind == "STRING":
            self.advance()
            return Str(tok.text)
        if tok.kind == "IDENT":
            self.advance()
            return Var(tok.text)
        if self.at("true", "false"):
            self.advance()
            return Bool(tok.text == "true")
        if self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            inner = self.expr()
            self.expect(")")
            return inner
        raise self.error("expected an expression")

    def program(self):
        stmts = []
        while self.peek().kind != "EOF":
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        return Program(stmts)

    def statement(self):
        if self.at("let"):
            return self.let_stmt()
        if self.at("print"):
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Print(value)
        if self.at("if"):
            return self.if_stmt()
        if self.at("while"):
            self.advance()
            cond = self.expr()
            return While(cond, self.block())
        if self.at("fn"):
            return self.fn_stmt()
        if self.at("return"):
            self.advance()
            value = None if self.at(";") else self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Return(value)
        nxt = self.peek(1)
        if self.peek().kind == "IDENT" and nxt.kind == "OP" and nxt.text == "=":
            name = self.advance().text
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Assign(name, value)
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return ExprStmt(value)

    def name(self):
        if self.peek().kind != "IDENT":
            raise self.error("expected a name")
        return self.advance().text

    def type_name(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "IDENT" or tok.text not in TYPES:
            raise self.error("expected a type")
        return self.advance().text

    def let_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        self.expect("=")
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return Let(name, type_, value)

    def if_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        cond = self.expr()
        then = self.block()
        else_ = None
        if self.at("else"):
            self.advance()
            else_ = self.if_stmt() if self.at("if") else self.block()
        return If(cond, then, else_)

    def block(self):
        self.expect("{")
        stmts = []
        while not self.at("}"):
            if self.peek().kind == "EOF":
                raise self.error("expected '}'")
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        self.advance()
        return Block(stmts)

    def param(self):
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        return (name, type_)

    def fn_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        self.expect("(")
        params = []
        if not self.at(")"):
            params.append(self.param())
            while self.at(","):
                self.advance()
                params.append(self.param())
        self.expect(")")
        ret = None
        if self.at("->"):
            self.advance()
            ret = self.type_name()
        return Fn(name, params, ret, self.block())


def parse_program(tokens):
    return Parser(tokens).program()

    pass


def comet_div(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q

from dataclasses import dataclass

KEYWORDS = {"let", "fn", "return", "if", "else", "while", "print",
            "true", "false", "and", "or", "not"}
TWO_CHAR = {"==", "!=", "<=", ">=", "->"}
ONE_CHAR = set("+-*/%<>=(){},;:")
ESCAPES = {'"': '"', "\\": "\\", "n": "\n"}
DIGITS = "0123456789"
LETTERS = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ_"


@dataclass
class Token:
    kind: str
    text: str
    line: int
    col: int


class LexError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


def tokenize(source):
    tokens = []
    i = 0
    line = 1
    col = 1
    n = len(source)

    def advance(count):
        nonlocal i, line, col
        for _ in range(count):
            if source[i] == "\n":
                line += 1
                col = 1
            else:
                col += 1
            i += 1

    while i < n:
        ch = source[i]
        start_line, start_col = line, col
        if ch in " \t\r\n":
            advance(1)
        elif ch == "#":
            while i < n and source[i] != "\n":
                advance(1)
        elif ch in DIGITS:
            j = i
            while j < n and source[j] in DIGITS:
                j += 1
            tokens.append(Token("NUMBER", source[i:j], start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch in LETTERS:
            j = i
            while j < n and (source[j] in LETTERS or source[j] in DIGITS):
                j += 1
            word = source[i:j]
            kind = "KEYWORD" if word in KEYWORDS else "IDENT"
            tokens.append(Token(kind, word, start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch == '"':
            advance(1)
            chars = []
            while True:
                if i >= n or source[i] == "\n":
                    raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                c = source[i]
                if c == '"':
                    advance(1)
                    break
                if c == "\\":
                    if i + 1 >= n or source[i + 1] == "\n":
                        raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                    if source[i + 1] not in ESCAPES:
                        raise LexError("unknown escape", line, col)
                    chars.append(ESCAPES[source[i + 1]])
                    advance(2)
                else:
                    chars.append(c)
                    advance(1)
            tokens.append(Token("STRING", "".join(chars), start_line, start_col))
        elif source[i:i + 2] in TWO_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", source[i:i + 2], start_line, start_col))
            advance(2)
        elif ch in ONE_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", ch, start_line, start_col))
            advance(1)
        else:
            raise LexError(f"unexpected character {ch!r}", start_line, start_col)
    tokens.append(Token("EOF", "", line, col))
    return tokens
