class ParseError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col

COMPARE = ("==", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">=")
TYPES = ("int", "bool", "str")

class Parser:
    def __init__(self, tokens):
        self.tokens = tokens
        self.pos = 0

    def peek(self, ahead=0):
        return self.tokens[min(self.pos + ahead, len(self.tokens) - 1)]

    def at(self, *texts):
        tok = self.peek()
        return tok.kind in ("OP", "KEYWORD") and tok.text in texts

    def advance(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "EOF":
            self.pos += 1
        return tok

    def error(self, message):
        tok = self.peek()
        return ParseError(message, tok.line, tok.col)

    def expect(self, text):
        if not self.at(text):
            raise self.error(f"expected '{text}'")
        return self.advance()

    def expr(self):
        return self.or_expr()

    def or_expr(self):
        left = self.and_expr()
        while self.at("or"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.and_expr())
        return left

    def and_expr(self):
        left = self.not_expr()
        while self.at("and"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.not_expr())
        return left

    def not_expr(self):
        if self.at("not"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("not", self.not_expr())
        return self.compare()

    def compare(self):
        left = self.sum()
        if self.at(*COMPARE):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.sum())
            if self.at(*COMPARE):
                raise self.error("comparisons cannot be chained")
        return left

    def sum(self):
        left = self.product()
        while self.at("+", "-"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.product())
        return left

    def product(self):
        left = self.unary()
        while self.at("*", "/", "%"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.unary())
        return left

    def unary(self):
        if self.at("-"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("-", self.unary())
        return self.call()

    def call(self):
        expr = self.primary()
        while self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            args = []
            if not self.at(")"):
                args.append(self.expr())
                while self.at(","):
                    self.advance()
                    args.append(self.expr())
            self.expect(")")
            expr = Call(expr, args)
        return expr

    def primary(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind == "NUMBER":
            self.advance()
            return Num(int(tok.text))
        if tok.kind == "STRING":
            self.advance()
            return Str(tok.text)
        if tok.kind == "IDENT":
            self.advance()
            return Var(tok.text)
        if self.at("true", "false"):
            self.advance()
            return Bool(tok.text == "true")
        if self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            inner = self.expr()
            self.expect(")")
            return inner
        raise self.error("expected an expression")

    def program(self):
        stmts = []
        while self.peek().kind != "EOF":
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        return Program(stmts)

    def statement(self):
        if self.at("let"):
            return self.let_stmt()
        if self.at("print"):
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Print(value)
        if self.at("if"):
            return self.if_stmt()
        if self.at("while"):
            self.advance()
            cond = self.expr()
            return While(cond, self.block())
        if self.at("fn"):
            return self.fn_stmt()
        if self.at("return"):
            self.advance()
            value = None if self.at(";") else self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Return(value)
        nxt = self.peek(1)
        if self.peek().kind == "IDENT" and nxt.kind == "OP" and nxt.text == "=":
            name = self.advance().text
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Assign(name, value)
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return ExprStmt(value)

    def name(self):
        if self.peek().kind != "IDENT":
            raise self.error("expected a name")
        return self.advance().text

    def type_name(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "IDENT" or tok.text not in TYPES:
            raise self.error("expected a type")
        return self.advance().text

    def let_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        self.expect("=")
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return Let(name, type_, value)

    def if_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        cond = self.expr()
        then = self.block()
        else_ = None
        if self.at("else"):
            self.advance()
            else_ = self.if_stmt() if self.at("if") else self.block()
        return If(cond, then, else_)

    def block(self):
        self.expect("{")
        stmts = []
        while not self.at("}"):
            if self.peek().kind == "EOF":
                raise self.error("expected '}'")
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        self.advance()
        return Block(stmts)

    def param(self):
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        return (name, type_)

    def fn_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        self.expect("(")
        params = []
        if not self.at(")"):
            params.append(self.param())
            while self.at(","):
                self.advance()
                params.append(self.param())
        self.expect(")")
        ret = None
        if self.at("->"):
            self.advance()
            ret = self.type_name()
        return Fn(name, params, ret, self.block())

def parse_program(tokens):
    return Parser(tokens).program()



def parse_expr(tokens):
    parser = Parser(tokens)
    tree = parser.expr()
    if parser.peek().kind != "EOF":
        raise parser.error("expected end of input")
    return tree


class CometError(Exception):
    pass


def comet_div(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q


def comet_mod(a, b):
    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)


def show(value):
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "true" if value else "false"
    return str(value)


TAC_OPS = {
    "+": lambda a, b: a + b,
    "-": lambda a, b: a - b,
    "*": lambda a, b: a * b,
    "/": comet_div,
    "%": comet_mod,
    "==": lambda a, b: a == b,
    "!=": lambda a, b: a != b,
    "<": lambda a, b: a < b,
    "<=": lambda a, b: a <= b,
    ">": lambda a, b: a > b,
    ">=": lambda a, b: a >= b,
}


def run_tac(code, limit=200000):
    labels = {ins[1]: i for i, ins in enumerate(code) if ins[0] == "label"}
    env = {}
    output = []

    def value(a):
        if isinstance(a, str):
            if a not in env:
                raise CometError(f"undefined variable {a}")
            return env[a]
        return a

    pc = 0
    steps = 0
    try:
        while pc < len(code):
            steps += 1
            if steps > limit:
                raise CometError("step limit reached")
            ins = code[pc]
            op = ins[0]
            pc += 1
            if op == "label":
                continue
            if op == "jump":
                pc = labels[ins[1]]
            elif op == "iffalse":
                if value(ins[1]) is False:
                    pc = labels[ins[2]]
            elif op == "print":
                output.append(show(value(ins[1])))
            elif op == "copy":
                env[ins[1]] = value(ins[2])
            elif op == "neg":
                env[ins[1]] = -value(ins[2])
            elif op == "not":
                env[ins[1]] = not value(ins[2])
            else:
                env[ins[1]] = TAC_OPS[op](value(ins[2]), value(ins[3]))
    except CometError as e:
        return output, str(e)
    return output, None


class Lowerer:
    def __init__(self):
        self.code = []
        self.temps = 0
        self.labels = 0

    def new_temp(self):
        self.temps += 1
        return f"%{self.temps}"

    def new_label(self):
        self.labels += 1
        return f"L{self.labels}"

    def emit(self, *ins):
        self.code.append(ins)

    def expr(self, e):
        if isinstance(e, (Num, Bool)):
            return e.value
        if isinstance(e, Var):
            return e.name
        if isinstance(e, Unary):
            a = self.expr(e.expr)
            t = self.new_temp()
            self.emit("neg" if e.op == "-" else "not", t, a)
            return t
        if isinstance(e, Binary) and e.op == "and":
            left = self.expr(e.left)
            t = self.new_temp()
            self.emit("copy", t, left)
            end = self.new_label()
            self.emit("iffalse", t, end)
            self.emit("copy", t, self.expr(e.right))
            self.emit("label", end)
            return t
        if isinstance(e, Binary) and e.op == "or":
            left = self.expr(e.left)
            t = self.new_temp()
            self.emit("copy", t, left)
            right = self.new_label()
            end = self.new_label()
            self.emit("iffalse", t, right)
            self.emit("jump", end)
            self.emit("label", right)
            self.emit("copy", t, self.expr(e.right))
            self.emit("label", end)
            return t
        if isinstance(e, Binary):
            a = self.expr(e.left)
            b = self.expr(e.right)
            t = self.new_temp()
            self.emit(e.op, t, a, b)
            return t
        raise CometError(f"{type(e).__name__} is not part of the IR")

    def stmt(self, s):
        if isinstance(s, (Let, Assign)):
            self.emit("copy", s.name, self.expr(s.expr))
        elif isinstance(s, Print):
            self.emit("print", self.expr(s.expr))
        elif isinstance(s, ExprStmt):
            self.expr(s.expr)
        elif isinstance(s, Block):
            for inner in s.stmts:
                self.stmt(inner)
        elif isinstance(s, If):
            cond = self.expr(s.cond)
            if s.else_ is None:
                end = self.new_label()
                self.emit("iffalse", cond, end)
                self.stmt(s.then)
                self.emit("label", end)
            else:
                other = self.new_label()
                end = self.new_label()
                self.emit("iffalse", cond, other)
                self.stmt(s.then)
                self.emit("jump", end)
                self.emit("label", other)
                self.stmt(s.else_)
                self.emit("label", end)
        elif isinstance(s, While):
            top = self.new_label()
            end = self.new_label()
            self.emit("label", top)
            cond = self.expr(s.cond)
            self.emit("iffalse", cond, end)
            self.stmt(s.body)
            self.emit("jump", top)
            self.emit("label", end)
        else:
            raise CometError(f"{type(s).__name__} is not part of the IR")


def lower(program):
    lowerer = Lowerer()
    for s in program.stmts:
        lowerer.stmt(s)
    return lowerer.code


def build_cfg(code):
    leaders = set()
    for i, ins in enumerate(code):
        if i == 0 or ins[0] == "label":
            leaders.add(i)
        if ins[0] in ("jump", "iffalse") and i + 1 < len(code):
            leaders.add(i + 1)
    starts = sorted(leaders)
    ends = starts[1:] + [len(code)]
    blocks = [code[s:e] for s, e in zip(starts, ends)]
    block_of = {b[0][1]: i for i, b in enumerate(blocks) if b[0][0] == "label"}
    succ = []
    for i, block in enumerate(blocks):
        last = block[-1]
        out = set()
        if last[0] == "jump":
            out.add(block_of[last[1]])
        else:
            if last[0] == "iffalse":
                out.add(block_of[last[2]])
            if i + 1 < len(blocks):
                out.add(i + 1)
        succ.append(sorted(out))
    return blocks, succ


def tac(source):
    return lower(parse_program(tokenize(source)))


NAC = "not a constant"


def meet(a, b):
    result = {}
    for name in set(a) | set(b):
        if name in a and name in b and a[name] == b[name] and type(a[name]) is type(b[name]):
            result[name] = a[name]
        else:
            result[name] = NAC
    return result


def transfer(block, facts):
    facts = dict(facts)
    for ins in block:
        op = ins[0]
        if op in ("label", "jump", "iffalse", "print"):
            continue
        args = [facts.get(a, NAC) if isinstance(a, str) else a for a in ins[2:]]
        value = NAC
        if all(x is not NAC for x in args):
            if op == "copy":
                value = args[0]
            elif op == "neg":
                value = -args[0]
            elif op == "not":
                value = not args[0]
            elif not (op in ("/", "%") and args[1] == 0):
                value = TAC_OPS[op](args[0], args[1])
        facts[ins[1]] = value
    return facts


def constants_at_entry(code):
    blocks, succ = build_cfg(code)
    preds = [[] for _ in blocks]
    for i, s in enumerate(succ):
        for j in s:
            preds[j].append(i)
    entry = [None] * len(blocks)
    exit_ = [None] * len(blocks)
    changed = True
    while changed:
        changed = False
        for i, block in enumerate(blocks):
            if i == 0:
                facts = {}
            else:
                known = [exit_[p] for p in preds[i] if exit_[p] is not None]
                if not known:
                    continue
                facts = known[0]
                for other in known[1:]:
                    facts = meet(facts, other)
            out = transfer(block, facts)
            if facts != entry[i] or out != exit_[i]:
                entry[i], exit_[i] = facts, out
                changed = True
    return [None if e is None else {k: v for k, v in e.items() if v is not NAC} for e in entry]
--- hint
Compute the predecessors of every block from `succ`. Keep two lists, the facts at the entry and at the exit of each block, both starting as `None` (not reached). Represent "not a constant" by a unique marker object or string.
--- hint
In each pass, for each block: block 0 starts from `{}`; any other block meets the exit facts of its reached predecessors, and is skipped if none is reached. Run the transfer to get its exit facts. If either changed, note that another pass is needed.
--- hint
The meet of two dictionaries goes over the union of their names: a name keeps its value only if both have it with the same value and the same type, otherwise it becomes "not a constant". At the end, drop the "not a constant" names from each entry dictionary.
--- check case | The example
constants_at_entry(tac("let a = 1; let b = 2; if c { b = 3; } print a + b;"))[-1]
=> {'a': 1}
--- check case | Every block of a straight if-else
constants_at_entry(tac("let a = 1; if c { a = 1; } else { a = 1; } print a;"))
=> [{}, {'a': 1}, {'a': 1}, {'a': 1}]
--- check case | A loop variable is not a constant, a loop-invariant one is
constants_at_entry(tac("let i = 0; let k = 5; while i < 3 { i = i + 1; } print k;"))
=> [{}, {'k': 5}, {'k': 5}, {'k': 5}]
?? The loop test's block is reached from the start (i = 0) and from the body (i = 1, 2, ...): after the meet, i is not a constant.
--- check case | Unreachable blocks give None, and empty code gives []
(constants_at_entry([('jump', 'L1'), ('copy', 'x', 1), ('label', 'L1'), ('print', 2)]), constants_at_entry([]))
=> ([{}, None, {}], [])
--- check case | Folding through a chain
constants_at_entry([('copy', 'a', 6), ('*', 'b', 'a', 7), ('/', 'z', 1, 0), ('iffalse', 'c', 'L1'), ('label', 'L1'), ('print', 'b')])
=> [{}, {'a': 6, 'b': 42}]
--- check case | A value that changes inside the loop but returns to the same constant
constants_at_entry(tac("let t = 1; while go { t = 2; t = t - 1; } print t;"))
=> [{}, {'t': 1}, {'t': 1}, {'t': 1}]

=== plc-15 | A stack VM: bytecode and the machine that runs it
--- teach
Lesson 1 compiled arithmetic into code for a tiny stack machine, and lessons 13 and 14 built and improved a flat representation of programs. This lesson designs the machine that Comet's compiler will target: a **virtual machine**, or **VM**, that runs **bytecode**, a flat list of simple instructions. It has variables, jumps, functions and closures, so it can run every Comet program. Next lesson writes the compiler that produces its bytecode.

### What a virtual machine is

A **virtual machine** is a processor defined in software: an instruction set, a state, and a loop that runs the instructions one at a time. In everyday words, it is an imaginary computer, simple enough to build in an afternoon, whose programs you can run on any real computer that runs the VM.

Why not keep the tree-walking interpreter? Three reasons.

- **Speed.** Lesson 6 noted that a tree walker pays, at every node, for finding the node's kind and following pointers scattered in memory. Bytecode is one flat list, and each instruction does one small, fixed job.
- **Portability.** The compiler targets one instruction set; the VM, written once per platform, runs the same bytecode everywhere. That was Java's promise, "write once, run anywhere".
- **A clean split.** Everything that depends on the source language (names, scopes, `and`, `while`) is settled by the compiler. The VM knows only instructions.

### The state and the loop

The machine's state is:

- `code`, the list of instructions being run, and `pc`, the **program counter**: the index of the next instruction;
- the **operand stack**, where instructions take their operands and leave their results;
- the current **environment**, where variables live;
- a stack of **frames**, one per function call that has not yet returned.

The heart of the VM is the **fetch-decode-execute loop** from the Computer Organization course: fetch `code[pc]`, move `pc` on to the next instruction, look at the instruction's name, and do what it says. Moving `pc` on **before** executing matters: a jump then simply overwrites `pc`, and nothing else has to know that a jump happened.

Here is that loop for a machine with only two instructions, on different data from Comet's:

```python
def run_counter(code):
    total = 0
    pc = 0
    while pc < len(code):
        op, arg = code[pc]
        pc += 1
        if op == "ADD":
            total += arg
        elif op == "SKIP_IF_OVER":
            if total > arg:
                pc += 1
    return total

print(run_counter([("ADD", 5), ("SKIP_IF_OVER", 3), ("ADD", 100), ("ADD", 1)]))    # 6
```

### Comet's instructions

Each instruction is a tuple. The **stack effect** column shows the top of the stack before and after, with the top on the right: `… a b → … r` means "pops b, then a, and pushes r". As in lesson 1, b, the value on top, is the **right** operand.

| instruction | stack effect | what it does |
|---|---|---|
| `('CONST', v)` | `… → … v` | push a constant |
| `('LOAD', x)` | `… → … value` | push the value of variable x |
| `('STORE', x)` | `… v → …` | assign v to the existing variable x |
| `('DEFINE', x)` | `… v → …` | declare x in the current environment with value v |
| `('ADD',)` `('SUB',)` `('MUL',)` `('DIV',)` `('MOD',)` | `… a b → … a op b` | arithmetic; `ADD` also joins two strings |
| `('EQ',)` `('NE',)` `('LT',)` `('LE',)` `('GT',)` `('GE',)` | `… a b → … bool` | comparisons |
| `('NEG',)` `('NOT',)` | `… a → … r` | minus, and not |
| `('JUMP', t)` | `… → …` | continue at index t |
| `('JUMP_IF_FALSE', t)` | `… c → …` | pop c; if it is false, continue at index t |
| `('PRINT',)` | `… v → …` | print v |
| `('POP',)` | `… v → …` | throw v away |
| `('CALL', n)` | `… f a1 … an → … result` | call f with n arguments |
| `('RET',)` | `… v → (caller's stack) … v` | return v to the caller |
| `('HALT',)` | | stop |

The VM checks Comet's types itself, exactly like lesson 6's interpreter: `ADD` needs two ints or two strings, `LT` two ints, `EQ` two values of the same type, `JUMP_IF_FALSE` and `NOT` a bool. A wrong type, a zero divisor or an unknown variable raises `CometError`.

### Jumps

A jump target is an instruction index. Here is a loop that prints 3, 2, 1, written by hand:

```text
 0  CONST 3
 1  DEFINE n
 2  LOAD n            <- the loop test starts here
 3  CONST 0
 4  GT
 5  JUMP_IF_FALSE 13  pops the bool; leaves the loop when it is false
 6  LOAD n
 7  PRINT
 8  LOAD n
 9  CONST 1
10  SUB
11  STORE n
12  JUMP 2
13  HALT
```

`JUMP_IF_FALSE` **pops** its condition, so after the test the stack is as it was before the test. That is what lets a loop run a million times without the stack growing.

### Variables and environments

The VM's variables live in the same kind of **environment** as lesson 7's interpreter: an `Environment` holds a dictionary of values and a pointer to its parent.

- `DEFINE x` creates x in the **current** environment, or replaces it there. (Lesson 7's `define` refused a second declaration in one scope. In the VM that check has already been done by the compiler, and a `DEFINE` runs again only when a loop body repeats, so replacing is right.)
- `LOAD x` and `STORE x` look for x in the current environment, then its parent, and so on outwards; if no environment has x, that is a `CometError`.

At the top level the current environment is the VM's `globals`. Blocks do not get environments of their own in this VM; next lesson's compiler deals with that by renaming variables, as lesson 7's practice did.

### Functions, calls and frames

A compiled function is a `FunctionCode(name, params, code)`: its name, its parameter names, and its own list of instructions, whose jump targets count from 0 in that list. A function is a **value**, so it enters the program through `CONST`. When the constant is a `FunctionCode`, `CONST` pushes a `Closure(decl, env)` that captures the current environment. That is lesson 8's closure, the function together with the environment it was defined in, except that `decl` is now the compiled `FunctionCode` instead of the `Fn` node. (Real VMs give this its own instruction, such as CPython's `MAKE_FUNCTION` or Lua's `CLOSURE`; Comet keeps its instruction set small and folds it into `CONST`.)

`('CALL', n)` finds the callee **below** its n arguments, which the caller pushed in order:

```text
stack before CALL 2:   … f 10 32
```

It pops the arguments and the callee, checks that the callee is a `Closure` whose function has n parameters, and then:

1. saves a **frame** holding the caller's `code`, its `pc` (already pointing after the `CALL`), its environment, and the stack height;
2. makes a new environment whose parent is the **closure's** environment, not the caller's (that is what makes scope lexical), and defines each parameter in it;
3. switches `code` to the function's code and `pc` to 0.

`('RET',)` pops the return value, pops the newest frame, cuts the operand stack back to the saved height, pushes the value, and continues the caller from its saved `code`, `pc` and environment. A `RET` with no frame to return to is an error: "return outside a function".

The frames live in a Python list, not in Python's own call stack. So a Comet recursion 10,000 calls deep is 10,000 list entries, and the VM never hits Python's recursion limit. Lesson 8's tree-walking interpreter recursed in Python for every Comet call, which is why it had to stop at `MAX_DEPTH = 40` frames; the VM needs no such cap.

Here is the shape of a frame stack, on a different machine: a list of saved return points, pushed on a call and popped on a return.

```python
frames = []
frames.append(("main", 7))        # call from main, resume at 7
frames.append(("area", 3))        # area calls another function
where, resume = frames.pop()      # that function returns
print(where, resume, len(frames)) # area 3 1
```

### Why the VM is correct

The VM's specification is its table of instructions: each one is a function from a machine state to the next state. The VM is correct when every step it takes is exactly the transition its instruction's row describes, and every error it raises is one the row describes. That is checked row by row: it is one case of the `if` chain per instruction.

The interesting part is that calls and returns fit together. **Claim:** if a function's code, run from an empty stack in a fresh environment, returns the value v, then a `CALL n` whose callee is that function takes the caller's stack from `S f a1 … an` to `S v`, and leaves the caller's `pc` right after the `CALL` and its environment unchanged. The proof: `CALL` removes `f a1 … an` and records the height of S. The callee's instructions only push on top of that height (they cannot reach below it: the saved height is where their stack starts). The callee's `RET` cuts back to that height, which leaves exactly S, pushes v, and restores the saved `pc` and environment. Nested calls inside the callee are the same claim for a shorter run, so the proof is induction on the number of steps the call takes.

A second guarantee comes from the compiler rather than the VM: in compiled code, the stack height at each instruction is the same every time that instruction runs. Java's VM checks this property before running any class file, a job called [[bytecode verification|verifier]], and one of this lesson's practice problems builds a checker for it.

### What it costs

- Each instruction does O(1) work, apart from a variable lookup, which walks the environment chain (as deep as the functions are nested, usually 1 to 3), and joining strings, O(length).
- So a run costs time proportional to the number of instructions executed. A loop body of k instructions run m times costs Θ(k·m).
- Space: the operand stack is as deep as the most nested expression; the frame list is as long as the deepest chain of calls; each environment holds its own variables.

Against the tree walker, the number of steps is about the same (roughly one instruction per tree node), but each step is cheaper: no recursion per node, no search for the node's kind in a chain of `isinstance` tests, and no pointer chasing. Production VMs go further: CPython uses a computed [[jump table|dispatch]] instead of an `if` chain.

### Where it is used

- **The JVM** runs Java, Kotlin and Scala bytecode on a stack machine very much like this one, and **.NET's CLR** runs C# the same way.
- **CPython** compiles every module to bytecode for a stack VM; `dis.dis(f)` lists a function's instructions, and `f.__code__` is its `FunctionCode`.
- **WebAssembly**, which runs ORBIT's C++ in your browser, is a stack machine too.
- [[Register VMs|register-vm]] such as Lua 5 and Android's Dalvik name their operands instead of using a stack.
- Small VMs run inside larger systems: eBPF runs verified bytecode inside the Linux kernel, and spacecraft run command sequences on onboard VMs that can be updated from the ground without replacing the flight software.

**Watch out:** the classic VM bugs.

- Popping operands in the wrong order, so `10 - 3` computes 3 − 10. The first pop is the **right** operand.
- Forgetting that `JUMP_IF_FALSE` pops its condition, which leaves one value on the stack for every pass of a loop.
- Adding 1 to `pc` after a jump has set it, so every jump lands one instruction too far.
- Making the new call's environment a child of the **caller's** environment. That is dynamic scope, and closures stop working.
- Testing `isinstance(v, int)` before excluding `bool`, as in lesson 6.

::: context verifier Checking bytecode before it runs
A Java class file may come from anywhere, so before running it the JVM checks it: every instruction gets operands of the right kinds, every jump lands on an instruction, and at each instruction the stack has the same height and types on every path that reaches it. Code that passes can skip many checks while it runs. The check is a dataflow analysis over the bytecode's control-flow graph, the same fixed-point idea as lesson 14.
:::

::: context dispatch Faster instruction dispatch
An `if` chain tests instruction names one by one. CPython compiled with GCC or Clang instead keeps a table of addresses, one per opcode, and ends each instruction's code with a jump straight to the next instruction's handler, called "computed goto" or threaded code. It avoids the shared loop test and helps the processor predict each jump, which made CPython's loop roughly 15 to 20 percent faster when it was added.
:::

::: context register-vm Stack VMs and register VMs
A stack VM's `ADD` takes its operands from the stack, so instructions are short but many: `a = b + c` is four instructions. A register VM names its operands, `ADD a b c`, like three-address code: fewer instructions, each longer. Lua switched from a stack VM to a register VM in version 5.0 in 2003 and measured a clear speedup. The trade-off is still debated; both kinds are fast when well built.
:::
--- task
The starter gives `CometError`, the division helpers, `show`, `type_name` (which returns `"bool"`, `"int"`, `"str"`, `"nothing"` for `None`, or `"fn"`), `Environment` with `define`, `lookup` and `assign` (raising `CometError` for an unknown name), `FunctionCode(name, params, code)`, `Closure(decl, env)` (here `decl` is a `FunctionCode`), `Frame(code, pc, env, base)`, and `run_code(code)`, which runs a program on a new `VM` and returns `(output, error)`. Write the `VM` class's `run(code)` method, following the lesson's table exactly. You may add helper methods.

- Keep the operand stack in `self.stack`, the frames in `self.frames`, printed lines in `self.output`, and start in the environment `self.globals`. Add 1 to `self.steps` for every instruction executed.
- Arithmetic, comparisons, `NEG`, `NOT`, `PRINT` and `JUMP_IF_FALSE` check types as lesson 6 did and raise `CometError` on a wrong type or a zero divisor. As in lesson 8, `PRINT` of `None` raises `CometError` ("cannot print nothing"), a function prints as `<fn name>`, and `EQ` on two functions compares identity.
- `CONST` of a `FunctionCode` pushes `Closure(function_code, current environment)`.
- `CALL n` raises `CometError` if the callee is not a `Closure` or has a different number of parameters; otherwise it saves `Frame(code, pc, env, base)` with `base` the stack height after popping the callee and the arguments, and runs the function in a new `Environment` whose parent is the closure's environment, with the parameters defined.
- `RET` raises `CometError` when there is no frame; otherwise it restores the frame, cuts the stack to `base`, and pushes the return value.
- `HALT`, or running past the last instruction, ends `run`. Any unknown instruction raises `CometError`.

For example, `run_code([('CONST', 7), ('CONST', 2), ('SUB',), ('PRINT',), ('HALT',)])` is `(["5"], None)`.

class CometError(Exception):
    pass


def comet_div(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q


def comet_mod(a, b):
    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)


def show(value):
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "true" if value else "false"
    return str(value)


def type_name(value):
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "bool"
    if isinstance(value, int):
        return "int"
    if isinstance(value, str):
        return "str"
    if value is None:
        return "nothing"
    return "fn"


class Environment:
    def __init__(self, parent=None):
        self.values = {}
        self.parent = parent

    def define(self, name, value):
        self.values[name] = value

    def lookup(self, name):
        env = self
        while env is not None:
            if name in env.values:
                return env.values[name]
            env = env.parent
        raise CometError(f"undefined variable {name}")

    def assign(self, name, value):
        env = self
        while env is not None:
            if name in env.values:
                env.values[name] = value
                return
            env = env.parent
        raise CometError(f"assignment to undeclared variable {name}")


class FunctionCode:
    def __init__(self, name, params, code):
        self.name = name
        self.params = params
        self.code = code

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"FunctionCode({self.name!r}, {self.params!r}, {self.code!r})"

    def __eq__(self, other):
        return isinstance(other, FunctionCode) and (self.name, self.params, self.code) == (other.name, other.params, other.code)


class Closure:
    def __init__(self, decl, env):
        self.decl = decl
        self.env = env


class Frame:
    def __init__(self, code, pc, env, base):
        self.code = code
        self.pc = pc
        self.env = env
        self.base = base


class VM:
    def __init__(self):
        self.stack = []
        self.frames = []
        self.globals = Environment()
        self.output = []
        self.steps = 0

    def run(self, code):
        raise CometError("run is not written yet")


def run_code(code):
    vm = VM()
    try:
        vm.run(code)
    except CometError as e:
        return vm.output, str(e)
    return vm.output, None
--- solution
class CometError(Exception):
    pass


def comet_div(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q


def comet_mod(a, b):
    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)


def show(value):
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "true" if value else "false"
    return str(value)


def type_name(value):
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "bool"
    if isinstance(value, int):
        return "int"
    if isinstance(value, str):
        return "str"
    if value is None:
        return "nothing"
    return "fn"


class Environment:
    def __init__(self, parent=None):
        self.values = {}
        self.parent = parent

    def define(self, name, value):
        self.values[name] = value

    def lookup(self, name):
        env = self
        while env is not None:
            if name in env.values:
                return env.values[name]
            env = env.parent
        raise CometError(f"undefined variable {name}")

    def assign(self, name, value):
        env = self
        while env is not None:
            if name in env.values:
                env.values[name] = value
                return
            env = env.parent
        raise CometError(f"assignment to undeclared variable {name}")


class FunctionCode:
    def __init__(self, name, params, code):
        self.name = name
        self.params = params
        self.code = code

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"FunctionCode({self.name!r}, {self.params!r}, {self.code!r})"

    def __eq__(self, other):
        return isinstance(other, FunctionCode) and (self.name, self.params, self.code) == (other.name, other.params, other.code)


class Closure:
    def __init__(self, decl, env):
        self.decl = decl
        self.env = env


class Frame:
    def __init__(self, code, pc, env, base):
        self.code = code
        self.pc = pc
        self.env = env
        self.base = base


class VM:
    def __init__(self):
        self.stack = []
        self.frames = []
        self.globals = Environment()
        self.output = []
        self.steps = 0

    def pop(self):
        return self.stack.pop()

    def need(self, wanted, value, op):
        if type_name(value) != wanted:
            raise CometError(f"'{op}' needs {wanted}, not {type_name(value)}")

    def run(self, code):
        pc = 0
        env = self.globals
        while True:
            if pc >= len(code):
                return
            ins = code[pc]
            op = ins[0]
            pc += 1
            self.steps += 1
            if op == "CONST":
                value = ins[1]
                if isinstance(value, FunctionCode):
                    value = Closure(value, env)
                self.stack.append(value)
            elif op == "LOAD":
                self.stack.append(env.lookup(ins[1]))
            elif op == "STORE":
                env.assign(ins[1], self.pop())
            elif op == "DEFINE":
                env.define(ins[1], self.pop())
            elif op in ("ADD", "SUB", "MUL", "DIV", "MOD", "LT", "LE", "GT", "GE", "EQ", "NE"):
                b = self.pop()
                a = self.pop()
                self.stack.append(self.binary(op, a, b))
            elif op == "NEG":
                a = self.pop()
                self.need("int", a, "-")
                self.stack.append(-a)
            elif op == "NOT":
                a = self.pop()
                self.need("bool", a, "not")
                self.stack.append(not a)
            elif op == "JUMP":
                pc = ins[1]
            elif op == "JUMP_IF_FALSE":
                cond = self.pop()
                self.need("bool", cond, "condition")
                if not cond:
                    pc = ins[1]
            elif op == "PRINT":
                value = self.pop()
                if value is None:
                    raise CometError("cannot print nothing")
                if isinstance(value, Closure):
                    self.output.append(f"<fn {value.decl.name}>")
                else:
                    self.output.append(show(value))
            elif op == "POP":
                self.pop()
            elif op == "CALL":
                argc = ins[1]
                args = self.stack[len(self.stack) - argc:]
                del self.stack[len(self.stack) - argc:]
                callee = self.pop()
                if not isinstance(callee, Closure):
                    raise CometError(f"cannot call a value of type {type_name(callee)}")
                fn = callee.decl
                if len(fn.params) != argc:
                    raise CometError(f"{fn.name} takes {len(fn.params)} arguments, not {argc}")
                self.frames.append(Frame(code, pc, env, len(self.stack)))
                env = Environment(callee.env)
                for name, value in zip(fn.params, args):
                    env.define(name, value)
                code = fn.code
                pc = 0
            elif op == "RET":
                if not self.frames:
                    raise CometError("return outside a function")
                value = self.pop()
                frame = self.frames.pop()
                del self.stack[frame.base:]
                self.stack.append(value)
                code, pc, env = frame.code, frame.pc, frame.env
            elif op == "HALT":
                return
            else:
                raise CometError(f"unknown instruction {op}")

    def binary(self, op, a, b):
        if op in ("EQ", "NE"):
            if type_name(a) != type_name(b):
                raise CometError(f"cannot compare {type_name(a)} with {type_name(b)}")
            return (a == b) == (op == "EQ")
        if op == "ADD" and type_name(a) == "str" and type_name(b) == "str":
            return a + b
        self.need("int", a, op)
        self.need("int", b, op)
        if op == "ADD":
            return a + b
        if op == "SUB":
            return a - b
        if op == "MUL":
            return a * b
        if op == "DIV":
            return comet_div(a, b)
        if op == "MOD":
            return comet_mod(a, b)
        if op == "LT":
            return a < b
        if op == "LE":
            return a <= b
        if op == "GT":
            return a > b
        return a >= b


def run_code(code):
    vm = VM()
    try:
        vm.run(code)
    except CometError as e:
        return vm.output, str(e)
    return vm.output, None
--- hint
Keep `code`, `pc` and `env` as local variables of `run`. Each pass of the loop: stop if `pc` is past the end, fetch `code[pc]`, add 1 to `pc` and to `self.steps`, then one `if`/`elif` case per instruction. Put the eleven binary operators in one case that pops b, then a, and calls a helper.
--- hint
The binary helper follows lesson 6: `EQ` and `NE` compare type names first; `ADD` of two strings joins them; everything else needs two ints (use `type_name`, which tests bool before int). `DIV` and `MOD` call `comet_div` and `comet_mod`.
--- hint
For `CALL n`: take `args = self.stack[len(self.stack) - n:]`, delete them, pop the callee, check it, append `Frame(code, pc, env, len(self.stack))`, then set `env = Environment(callee.env)`, define the parameters, and switch `code` and `pc`. `RET` pops the value and the frame, does `del self.stack[frame.base:]`, pushes the value, and restores `code`, `pc` and `env` from the frame.

+++ question | Predict the stack machine
--- ask
What does this bytecode print?

```text
0  CONST 10
1  CONST 4
2  CONST 3
3  SUB
4  MUL
5  CONST 2
6  MOD
7  PRINT
```
--- answer
0
--- why
After `CONST 4` and `CONST 3`, `SUB` pops 3 (the right operand) and 4, and pushes 4 − 3 = 1. `MUL` gives 10 × 1 = 10. `MOD` gives 10 % 2 = 0.

+++ question | Whose environment is the parent
--- ask
In `CALL`, the new environment's parent is the closure's captured environment. What changes if the VM used the caller's current environment as the parent instead?
--- choice
Nothing: the two are always the same environment.
--- choice correct
Scope becomes dynamic: a function sees the variables of whoever called it, so closures lose the variables they captured and a function can pick up a caller's local by accident.
--- choice
Recursion stops working, because a function cannot see its own name.
--- choice
The VM needs Python recursion for every call.
--- why
The captured environment is where the function was written; the caller's is where it happens to be called. They differ whenever a function is passed around or returned, which is exactly when closures matter. Lesson 8's lexical scope requires the captured one.

+++ question | Why frames in a list
--- ask
A tree-walking interpreter fails with `RecursionError` on a Comet recursion about 1,000 calls deep, while this VM handles 5,000. Why?
--- choice
The VM's instructions are faster, so it reaches the limit later.
--- choice correct
The VM keeps its frames in a Python list, so a Comet call does not become a Python call; the tree walker makes one or more Python calls per Comet call and hits Python's recursion limit.
--- choice
The VM does not support recursion; it only unrolls it.
--- choice
Python's recursion limit only applies to functions defined with `def`.
--- why
The limit is on Python's own call stack. The VM's loop is one Python call however deep the Comet program recurses; the frames are data, growing only as far as memory allows.

+++ practice | How deep does the stack get?
--- task
A VM must reserve room for its operand stack. For straight-line bytecode, the compiler can work out the deepest the stack ever gets without running anything, from each instruction's stack effect. Write `max_depth(code)`, which takes straight-line bytecode and returns the largest number of values on the stack at any moment, starting from an empty stack.

- `CONST` and `LOAD` push 1. `STORE`, `DEFINE`, `PRINT` and `POP` pop 1. `NEG` and `NOT` pop 1 and push 1. The eleven binary instructions pop 2 and push 1. `('CALL', n)` pops n + 1 and pushes 1. `HALT` does nothing.
- If an instruction needs more values than the stack holds, raise `CometError`: a stack underflow.
- `JUMP`, `JUMP_IF_FALSE`, `RET` and anything else are not straight-line code: raise `CometError`.

Empty code gives 0. For example, `max_depth([('CONST', 1), ('CONST', 2), ('CONST', 3), ('MUL',), ('ADD',), ('PRINT',)])` is 3.
--- starter
class CometError(Exception):
    pass


def comet_div(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q


def comet_mod(a, b):
    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)


def show(value):
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "true" if value else "false"
    return str(value)


def max_depth(code):
    return 0

class CometError(Exception):
    pass


def comet_div(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q


def comet_mod(a, b):
    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)


def show(value):
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "true" if value else "false"
    return str(value)


EFFECT = {"CONST": 1, "LOAD": 1, "STORE": -1, "DEFINE": -1, "PRINT": -1, "POP": -1,
          "NEG": 0, "NOT": 0, "HALT": 0}
NEEDS = {"STORE": 1, "DEFINE": 1, "PRINT": 1, "POP": 1, "NEG": 1, "NOT": 1}
BINARY = {"ADD", "SUB", "MUL", "DIV", "MOD", "EQ", "NE", "LT", "LE", "GT", "GE"}


def max_depth(code):
    depth = 0
    deepest = 0
    for i, ins in enumerate(code):
        op = ins[0]
        if op in BINARY:
            needs, effect = 2, -1
        elif op == "CALL":
            needs, effect = ins[1] + 1, -ins[1]
        elif op in EFFECT:
            needs, effect = NEEDS.get(op, 0), EFFECT[op]
        else:
            raise CometError(f"{op} is not straight-line code")
        if depth < needs:
            raise CometError(f"stack underflow at {i}")
        depth += effect
        deepest = max(deepest, depth)
    return deepest
--- hint
Keep the current depth and the deepest seen. For each instruction, find how many values it needs and how much it changes the depth; check the need before applying the change.
--- hint
A `('CALL', n)` needs n + 1 values and changes the depth by −n. Update the deepest value after each instruction.
--- check case | The example
max_depth([('CONST', 1), ('CONST', 2), ('CONST', 3), ('MUL',), ('ADD',), ('PRINT',)])
=> 3
--- check case | Empty code, and a left-leaning sum needs only 2
(max_depth([]), max_depth([('CONST', 1), ('CONST', 2), ('ADD',), ('CONST', 3), ('ADD',), ('CONST', 4), ('ADD',), ('DEFINE', 's')]))
=> (0, 2)
--- check case | A call with three arguments
max_depth([('LOAD', 'f'), ('CONST', 1), ('LOAD', 'x'), ('CONST', 2), ('NEG',), ('CALL', 3), ('POP',), ('HALT',)])
=> 4
--- check test | Underflow is an error
raises(CometError, lambda: max_depth([('CONST', 1), ('ADD',)])) and raises(CometError, lambda: max_depth([('PRINT',)])) and raises(CometError, lambda: max_depth([('LOAD', 'f'), ('CALL', 1)]))
--- check test | Jumps and returns are refused
all(raises(CometError, lambda c=c: max_depth(c)) for c in [[('JUMP', 0)], [('CONST', True), ('JUMP_IF_FALSE', 0)], [('CONST', 1), ('RET',)]])

+++ practice | A disassembler
--- task
Reading raw tuples is slow. Write `disassemble(code)`, which returns one text line per instruction, in the style of Python's `dis` module:

- each line starts with `">>"` if some `JUMP` or `JUMP_IF_FALSE` in the code targets this index, otherwise two spaces;
- then the index, right-aligned in 3 characters, a space, and the instruction's name;
- then, if the instruction has an argument, a space and the argument written with `repr`, except that a `FunctionCode` argument is written `<fn NAME>`.

The starter gives `FunctionCode`. For example, `disassemble([('LOAD', 'n'), ('JUMP_IF_FALSE', 0), ('HALT',)])` is `[">>  0 LOAD 'n'", "    1 JUMP_IF_FALSE 0", "    2 HALT"]`.

def disassemble(code):
    targets = {ins[1] for ins in code if ins[0] in ("JUMP", "JUMP_IF_FALSE")}
    lines = []
    for i, ins in enumerate(code):
        marker = ">>" if i in targets else "  "
        line = f"{marker}{i:>3} {ins[0]}"
        if len(ins) > 1:
            arg = ins[1]
            line += " " + (f"<fn {arg.name}>" if isinstance(arg, FunctionCode) else repr(arg))
        lines.append(line)
    return lines
--- hint
First collect the set of jump targets. Then build each line with an f-string: `f"{marker}{i:>3} {name}"`.
--- hint
Add the argument only when the tuple has more than one item, using `repr(arg)`, or `f"<fn {arg.name}>"` when it is a `FunctionCode`.
--- check case | The example
disassemble([('LOAD', 'n'), ('JUMP_IF_FALSE', 0), ('HALT',)])
=> [">>  0 LOAD 'n'", "    1 JUMP_IF_FALSE 0", "    2 HALT"]
--- check case | Constants of every kind, and a function
disassemble([('CONST', 5), ('CONST', "hi"), ('CONST', True), ('CONST', FunctionCode('sq', ['x'], [])), ('CALL', 1)])
=> ["    0 CONST 5", "    1 CONST 'hi'", "    2 CONST True", "    3 CONST <fn sq>", "    4 CALL 1"]
--- check case | A loop with two targets, and wide indexes
(lambda d: (d[2], d[12], d[13], len(d)))(disassemble([('CONST', 3), ('DEFINE', 'n'), ('LOAD', 'n'), ('CONST', 0), ('GT',), ('JUMP_IF_FALSE', 13), ('LOAD', 'n'), ('PRINT',), ('LOAD', 'n'), ('CONST', 1), ('SUB',), ('STORE', 'n'), ('JUMP', 2), ('HALT',)]))
=> (">>  2 LOAD 'n'", "   12 JUMP 2", ">> 13 HALT", 14)
--- check case | Empty code
disassemble([])
=> []

+++ practice | An assembler with labels
--- task
Writing jump targets as numbers is error-prone: add one instruction and every target after it moves. In Computer Organization you wrote an assembler that turned labels into addresses. Write `assemble(text)` for Comet bytecode. The starter gives the VM and `run_code`, so the checks run what you assemble.

- Each line holds one instruction, a label, or nothing. `#` starts a comment to the end of the line; blank lines are ignored; surrounding spaces do not matter.
- A label is a name followed by `:`, alone on its line. It stands for the index of the next instruction. Defining a label twice raises `CometError`.
- An instruction is its name, then (for instructions with an argument) a space and the argument. `LOAD`, `STORE` and `DEFINE` take a variable name; `JUMP` and `JUMP_IF_FALSE` take a label, which must be defined somewhere in the text (before or after), or `CometError`; `CALL` takes an integer; `CONST` takes an integer, `true`, `false`, or a string in double quotes (no escapes). An unknown instruction name raises `CometError`.

This needs **two passes**: the first finds each label's index, the second builds the tuples. For example, `assemble("CONST 1\nJUMP end\nCONST 2\nend:\nPRINT")` is `[('CONST', 1), ('JUMP', 3), ('CONST', 2), ('PRINT',)]`.
--- starter

    pass

        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q


def comet_mod(a, b):
    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)

    if isinstance(value, int):

class Environment:
    def __init__(self, parent=None):
        self.values = {}
        self.parent = parent

    def define(self, name, value):
        self.values[name] = value

    def lookup(self, name):
        env = self
        while env is not None:
            if name in env.values:
                return env.values[name]
            env = env.parent
        raise CometError(f"undefined variable {name}")

    def assign(self, name, value):
        env = self

class FunctionCode:
    def __init__(self, name, params, code):
        self.name = name
        self.params = params
        self.code = code

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"FunctionCode({self.name!r}, {self.params!r}, {self.code!r})"

    def __eq__(self, other):
        return isinstance(other, FunctionCode) and (self.name, self.params, self.code) == (other.name, other.params, other.code)


class Closure:
    def __init__(self, decl, env):
        self.decl = decl
        self.env = env


class Frame:
    def __init__(self, code, pc, env, base):
        self.code = code
        self.pc = pc
        self.env = env
        self.base = base


class VM:
    def __init__(self):
        self.stack = []
        self.frames = []
        self.globals = Environment()
        self.output = []
        self.steps = 0

    def pop(self):
        return self.stack.pop()

    def need(self, wanted, value, op):
        if type_name(value) != wanted:
            raise CometError(f"'{op}' needs {wanted}, not {type_name(value)}")

    def run(self, code):
        pc = 0
        env = self.globals
        while True:
            if pc >= len(code):
                return
            ins = code[pc]
            op = ins[0]
            pc += 1
            self.steps += 1
            if op == "CONST":
                value = ins[1]
                if isinstance(value, FunctionCode):
                    value = Closure(value, env)
                self.stack.append(value)
            elif op == "LOAD":
                self.stack.append(env.lookup(ins[1]))
            elif op == "STORE":
                env.assign(ins[1], self.pop())
            elif op == "DEFINE":
                env.define(ins[1], self.pop())
            elif op in ("ADD", "SUB", "MUL", "DIV", "MOD", "LT", "LE", "GT", "GE", "EQ", "NE"):
                b = self.pop()
                a = self.pop()
                self.stack.append(self.binary(op, a, b))
            elif op == "NEG":
                a = self.pop()
                self.need("int", a, "-")
                self.stack.append(-a)
            elif op == "NOT":
                a = self.pop()
                self.need("bool", a, "not")
                self.stack.append(not a)
            elif op == "JUMP":
                pc = ins[1]
            elif op == "JUMP_IF_FALSE":
                cond = self.pop()
                self.need("bool", cond, "condition")
                if not cond:
                    pc = ins[1]
            elif op == "PRINT":
                value = self.pop()
                if value is None:
                    raise CometError("cannot print nothing")
                if isinstance(value, Closure):
                    self.output.append(f"<fn {value.decl.name}>")
                else:
                    self.output.append(show(value))
            elif op == "POP":
                self.pop()
            elif op == "CALL":
                argc = ins[1]
                args = self.stack[len(self.stack) - argc:]
                del self.stack[len(self.stack) - argc:]
                callee = self.pop()
                if not isinstance(callee, Closure):
                    raise CometError(f"cannot call a value of type {type_name(callee)}")
                fn = callee.decl
                if len(fn.params) != argc:
                    raise CometError(f"{fn.name} takes {len(fn.params)} arguments, not {argc}")
                self.frames.append(Frame(code, pc, env, len(self.stack)))
                env = Environment(callee.env)
                for name, value in zip(fn.params, args):
                    env.define(name, value)
                code = fn.code
                pc = 0
            elif op == "RET":
                if not self.frames:
                    raise CometError("return outside a function")
                value = self.pop()
                frame = self.frames.pop()
                del self.stack[frame.base:]
                self.stack.append(value)
                code, pc, env = frame.code, frame.pc, frame.env
            elif op == "HALT":
                return
            else:
                raise CometError(f"unknown instruction {op}")

    def binary(self, op, a, b):
        if op in ("EQ", "NE"):
            if type_name(a) != type_name(b):
                raise CometError(f"cannot compare {type_name(a)} with {type_name(b)}")
            return (a == b) == (op == "EQ")
        if op == "ADD" and type_name(a) == "str" and type_name(b) == "str":
            return a + b
        self.need("int", a, op)
        self.need("int", b, op)
        if op == "ADD":
            return a + b
        if op == "SUB":
            return a - b
        if op == "MUL":
            return a * b
        if op == "DIV":
            return comet_div(a, b)
        if op == "MOD":
            return comet_mod(a, b)
        if op == "LT":
            return a < b
        if op == "LE":
            return a <= b
        if op == "GT":
            return a > b
        return a >= b


def run_code(code):
    vm = VM()
    try:
        vm.run(code)
    except CometError as e:
        return vm.output, str(e)
    return vm.output, None


def assemble(text):
    return []

          "NOT", "PRINT", "POP", "RET", "HALT"}
NAME_ARG = {"LOAD", "STORE", "DEFINE"}
LABEL_ARG = {"JUMP", "JUMP_IF_FALSE"}


def constant(text):
    if text == "true":
        return True
    if text == "false":
        return False
    if len(text) >= 2 and text[0] == '"' and text[-1] == '"':
        return text[1:-1]
    return int(text)


def assemble(text):
    labels = {}
    pending = []
    for raw in text.split("\n"):
        line = raw.split("#")[0].strip()
        if not line:
            continue
        if line.endswith(":"):
            name = line[:-1]
            if name in labels:
                raise CometError(f"label {name} defined twice")
            labels[name] = len(pending)
            continue
        op, _, arg = line.partition(" ")
        pending.append((op, arg.strip()))
    code = []
    for op, arg in pending:
        if op in NO_ARG:
            code.append((op,))
        elif op in NAME_ARG:
            code.append((op, arg))
        elif op in LABEL_ARG:
            if arg not in labels:
                raise CometError(f"unknown label {arg}")
            code.append((op, labels[arg]))
        elif op == "CALL":
            code.append((op, int(arg)))
        elif op == "CONST":
            code.append((op, constant(arg)))
        else:
            raise CometError(f"unknown instruction {op}")
    return code
--- hint
Pass one: go through the cleaned lines, keeping a count of instructions. A line ending in `:` records `labels[name] = count`; any other line is an instruction, saved as (name, argument text) for pass two.
--- hint
Pass two: turn each saved instruction into a tuple according to its name. Look labels up in the dictionary, and parse a `CONST` argument as `true`, `false`, a quoted string, or `int(text)`.
--- check case | The example
assemble("CONST 1\nJUMP end\nCONST 2\nend:\nPRINT")
=> [('CONST', 1), ('JUMP', 3), ('CONST', 2), ('PRINT',)]
--- check case | A countdown written with labels runs
run_code(assemble("\n".join(["    CONST 3", "    DEFINE n        # the counter", "top:", "    LOAD n", "    CONST 0", "    GT", "    JUMP_IF_FALSE done", "    LOAD n", "    PRINT", "    LOAD n", "    CONST 1", "    SUB", "    STORE n", "    JUMP top", "", "done:", "    HALT"])))
=> (["3", "2", "1"], None)
--- check case | Constants of each kind
assemble('CONST -4\nCONST true\nCONST false\nCONST "hi there"\nCALL 2\nRET')
=> [('CONST', -4), ('CONST', True), ('CONST', False), ('CONST', "hi there"), ('CALL', 2), ('RET',)]
--- check case | Two labels at the same place, and a label at the very end
assemble("a:\nb:\nJUMP b\nJUMP_IF_FALSE z\nz:")
=> [('JUMP', 0), ('JUMP_IF_FALSE', 2)]
--- check test | Bad programs raise CometError
all(raises(CometError, lambda t=t: assemble(t)) for t in ["JUMP nowhere", "x:\nx:\nHALT", "FLY 3", "CONST 1\nCOPY"])

+++ practice | A bytecode verifier
--- task
Before running bytecode from outside, a careful VM checks it, as the JVM does. Write `verify(code)` for top-level bytecode (no `RET`). Starting with an empty stack at index 0, follow every path through the code and work out the stack height **before** each reachable instruction. Return the largest height reached, or raise `CometError` when the code is unsafe.

- Stack effects: `CONST`, `LOAD` push 1; `STORE`, `DEFINE`, `PRINT`, `POP` and `JUMP_IF_FALSE` pop 1; `NEG`, `NOT` pop 1 and push 1; the eleven binary instructions pop 2 and push 1; `('CALL', n)` pops n + 1 and pushes 1; `JUMP` and `HALT` change nothing. Anything else, including `RET`, raises `CometError`.
- After an instruction, control goes to the next index; a `JUMP` goes only to its target; a `JUMP_IF_FALSE` to both; a `HALT` nowhere. Reaching index `len(code)` means the program ends there, which is fine.
- Raise `CometError` for: an instruction that needs more values than the height; a jump target below 0 or above `len(code)`; and two paths that reach the same instruction with **different** heights.
- Instructions that no path reaches are not checked.

Empty code gives 0. For example, a loop that pushes a value on every pass and jumps back is rejected, because the loop test is reached with two different heights.
--- starter
class CometError(Exception):
    pass


def comet_div(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q


def comet_mod(a, b):
    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)


def show(value):
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "true" if value else "false"
    return str(value)


def verify(code):
    return 0

class CometError(Exception):
    pass


def comet_div(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q


def comet_mod(a, b):
    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)


def show(value):
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "true" if value else "false"
    return str(value)


BINARY = {"ADD", "SUB", "MUL", "DIV", "MOD", "EQ", "NE", "LT", "LE", "GT", "GE"}


def effect(ins):
    op = ins[0]
    if op in BINARY:
        return 2, -1
    if op in ("CONST", "LOAD"):
        return 0, 1
    if op in ("STORE", "DEFINE", "PRINT", "POP", "JUMP_IF_FALSE"):
        return 1, -1
    if op in ("NEG", "NOT"):
        return 1, 0
    if op in ("JUMP", "HALT"):
        return 0, 0
    if op == "CALL":
        return ins[1] + 1, -ins[1]
    raise CometError(f"{op} is not allowed here")


def verify(code):
    depth = {}
    work = []
    if code:
        depth[0] = 0
        work.append(0)
    deepest = 0
    while work:
        i = work.pop()
        ins = code[i]
        needs, change = effect(ins)
        if depth[i] < needs:
            raise CometError(f"stack underflow at {i}")
        after = depth[i] + change
        deepest = max(deepest, after)
        nexts = []
        if ins[0] == "JUMP":
            nexts = [ins[1]]
        elif ins[0] == "JUMP_IF_FALSE":
            nexts = [ins[1], i + 1]
        elif ins[0] != "HALT":
            nexts = [i + 1]
        for j in nexts:
            if j == len(code):
                continue
            if not 0 <= j < len(code):
                raise CometError(f"jump target {j} out of range at {i}")
            if j not in depth:
                depth[j] = after
                work.append(j)
            elif depth[j] != after:
                raise CometError(f"stack depths {depth[j]} and {after} meet at {j}")
    return deepest
--- hint
Keep a dictionary from index to the height before it, and a work list of indexes to process, starting with index 0 at height 0. Processing an index checks the need, computes the height after, and hands that height to each successor.
--- hint
For a successor: equal to `len(code)`, skip it; out of range, raise; not seen, record its height and add it to the work list; seen with a different height, raise. Track the largest height after any instruction.
--- check case | Straight-line code
verify([('CONST', 1), ('CONST', 2), ('CONST', 3), ('MUL',), ('ADD',), ('PRINT',), ('HALT',)])
=> 3
--- check case | A balanced loop and an if-else that meet at the same height
(verify([('CONST', 3), ('DEFINE', 'n'), ('LOAD', 'n'), ('CONST', 0), ('GT',), ('JUMP_IF_FALSE', 13), ('LOAD', 'n'), ('PRINT',), ('LOAD', 'n'), ('CONST', 1), ('SUB',), ('STORE', 'n'), ('JUMP', 2), ('HALT',)]), verify([('LOAD', 'c'), ('JUMP_IF_FALSE', 4), ('CONST', 1), ('JUMP', 5), ('CONST', 2), ('PRINT',)]))
=> (2, 1)
--- check test | A loop that grows the stack is rejected
raises(CometError, lambda: verify([('CONST', 1), ('LOAD', 'go'), ('JUMP_IF_FALSE', 4), ('JUMP', 0), ('HALT',)]))
--- check test | Two branches that leave different heights are rejected
raises(CometError, lambda: verify([('LOAD', 'c'), ('JUMP_IF_FALSE', 3), ('CONST', 1), ('PRINT',)]))
--- check test | Underflow, bad targets and RET are rejected
all(raises(CometError, lambda c=c: verify(c)) for c in [[('ADD',)], [('JUMP', 7)], [('JUMP', -1)], [('CONST', 1), ('RET',)], [('CONST', True), ('JUMP_IF_FALSE', 2), ('POP',)]])
--- check case | Empty code, a jump to the end, and unreachable junk after HALT
(verify([]), verify([('JUMP', 1)]), verify([('CONST', 1), ('PRINT',), ('HALT',), ('ADD',), ('ADD',)]))
=> (0, 0, 1)

+++ practice | Debug: every jump lands one too far
--- task
`run_small(code)` is a cut-down VM with `CONST`, `LOAD`, `STORE`, `DEFINE`, a few binary instructions, `JUMP`, `JUMP_IF_FALSE`, `PRINT` and `HALT`. It returns the printed lines. Straight-line programs work, but loops and branches go wrong: the countdown `[('CONST', 2), ('DEFINE', 'n'), ('LOAD', 'n'), ('CONST', 0), ('GT',), ('JUMP_IF_FALSE', 13), ('LOAD', 'n'), ('PRINT',), ('LOAD', 'n'), ('CONST', 1), ('SUB',), ('STORE', 'n'), ('JUMP', 2), ('HALT',)]` should print `2` and `1`, but it crashes. Find the bug and fix it, so that a jump to index t runs the instruction at index t next.
--- starter
class CometError(Exception):

def comet_div(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q

    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)


def show(value):
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "true" if value else "false"
    return str(value)


ARITH = {
    "ADD": lambda a, b: a + b,
    "SUB": lambda a, b: a - b,
    "MUL": lambda a, b: a * b,
    "LT": lambda a, b: a < b,
    "GT": lambda a, b: a > b,
    "EQ": lambda a, b: a == b,
}


def run_small(code, limit=10000):
    stack = []
    env = {}
    output = []
    pc = 0
    steps = 0
    while pc < len(code):
        steps += 1
        if steps > limit:
            raise CometError("step limit reached")
        ins = code[pc]
        op = ins[0]
        if op == "CONST":
            stack.append(ins[1])
        elif op == "LOAD":
            if ins[1] not in env:
                raise CometError(f"undefined variable {ins[1]}")
            stack.append(env[ins[1]])
        elif op in ("STORE", "DEFINE"):
            env[ins[1]] = stack.pop()
        elif op in ARITH:
            b = stack.pop()
            a = stack.pop()
            stack.append(ARITH[op](a, b))
        elif op == "JUMP":
            pc = ins[1]
        elif op == "JUMP_IF_FALSE":
            if stack.pop() is False:
                pc = ins[1]
        elif op == "PRINT":
            output.append(show(stack.pop()))
        elif op == "HALT":
            break
        pc += 1
    return output

+++ practice | A guarded VM for uploaded scripts
--- task
Scripts uploaded to a spacecraft must never hang the computer or exhaust its memory. The starter holds the lesson's VM, renamed `GuardedVM`, whose `run` now takes `fuel` and `max_depth` but ignores them. Change it, and write `run_guarded(code, fuel, max_depth)`, which runs `code` on a new `GuardedVM` and returns `(status, output, trace)`:

- If executing another instruction would make more than `fuel` instructions in all, stop: the status is `"out of fuel"`.
- If a `CALL` would make more than `max_depth` frames, stop before calling: the status is `"stack overflow"`.
- If a `CometError` is raised, the status is `"error: "` followed by its message.
- Otherwise the status is `"ok"`.
- `output` is the lines printed so far. `trace` is the list of the names of the functions whose calls have not returned when the run stopped, outermost first; it is `[]` when the status is `"ok"`.

For example, a script that calls `f`, which calls `g`, which divides by zero, returns `("error: division by zero", [...], ["f", "g"])`, and `run_guarded([('JUMP', 0)], 1000, 10)` returns `("out of fuel", [], [])`.
--- starter
class CometError(Exception):
    pass


def comet_div(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q


def comet_mod(a, b):
    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)


def show(value):
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "true" if value else "false"
    return str(value)


def type_name(value):
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "bool"
    if isinstance(value, int):
        return "int"
    if isinstance(value, str):
        return "str"
    if value is None:
        return "nothing"
    return "fn"


class Environment:
    def __init__(self, parent=None):
        self.values = {}
        self.parent = parent

    def define(self, name, value):
        self.values[name] = value

    def lookup(self, name):
        env = self
        while env is not None:
            if name in env.values:
                return env.values[name]
            env = env.parent
        raise CometError(f"undefined variable {name}")

    def assign(self, name, value):
        env = self
        while env is not None:
            if name in env.values:
                env.values[name] = value
                return
            env = env.parent
        raise CometError(f"assignment to undeclared variable {name}")


class FunctionCode:
    def __init__(self, name, params, code):
        self.name = name
        self.params = params
        self.code = code

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"FunctionCode({self.name!r}, {self.params!r}, {self.code!r})"

    def __eq__(self, other):
        return isinstance(other, FunctionCode) and (self.name, self.params, self.code) == (other.name, other.params, other.code)


class Closure:
    def __init__(self, decl, env):
        self.decl = decl
        self.env = env


class Frame:
    def __init__(self, code, pc, env, base):
        self.code = code
        self.pc = pc
        self.env = env
        self.base = base


class GuardedVM:
    def __init__(self):
        self.stack = []
        self.frames = []
        self.globals = Environment()
        self.output = []
        self.steps = 0

    def pop(self):
        return self.stack.pop()

    def need(self, wanted, value, op):
        if type_name(value) != wanted:
            raise CometError(f"'{op}' needs {wanted}, not {type_name(value)}")

    def run(self, code, fuel, max_depth):
        pc = 0
        env = self.globals
        while True:
            if pc >= len(code):
                return
            ins = code[pc]
            op = ins[0]
            pc += 1
            self.steps += 1
            if op == "CONST":
                value = ins[1]
                if isinstance(value, FunctionCode):
                    value = Closure(value, env)
                self.stack.append(value)
            elif op == "LOAD":
                self.stack.append(env.lookup(ins[1]))
            elif op == "STORE":
                env.assign(ins[1], self.pop())
            elif op == "DEFINE":
                env.define(ins[1], self.pop())
            elif op in ("ADD", "SUB", "MUL", "DIV", "MOD", "LT", "LE", "GT", "GE", "EQ", "NE"):
                b = self.pop()
                a = self.pop()
                self.stack.append(self.binary(op, a, b))
            elif op == "NEG":
                a = self.pop()
                self.need("int", a, "-")
                self.stack.append(-a)
            elif op == "NOT":
                a = self.pop()
                self.need("bool", a, "not")
                self.stack.append(not a)
            elif op == "JUMP":
                pc = ins[1]
            elif op == "JUMP_IF_FALSE":
                cond = self.pop()
                self.need("bool", cond, "condition")
                if not cond:
                    pc = ins[1]
            elif op == "PRINT":
                value = self.pop()
                if value is None:
                    raise CometError("cannot print nothing")
                if isinstance(value, Closure):
                    self.output.append(f"<fn {value.decl.name}>")
                else:
                    self.output.append(show(value))
            elif op == "POP":
                self.pop()
            elif op == "CALL":
                argc = ins[1]
                args = self.stack[len(self.stack) - argc:]
                del self.stack[len(self.stack) - argc:]
                callee = self.pop()
                if not isinstance(callee, Closure):
                    raise CometError(f"cannot call a value of type {type_name(callee)}")
                fn = callee.decl
                if len(fn.params) != argc:
                    raise CometError(f"{fn.name} takes {len(fn.params)} arguments, not {argc}")
                self.frames.append(Frame(code, pc, env, len(self.stack)))
                env = Environment(callee.env)
                for name, value in zip(fn.params, args):
                    env.define(name, value)
                code = fn.code
                pc = 0
            elif op == "RET":
                if not self.frames:
                    raise CometError("return outside a function")
                value = self.pop()
                frame = self.frames.pop()
                del self.stack[frame.base:]
                self.stack.append(value)
                code, pc, env = frame.code, frame.pc, frame.env
            elif op == "HALT":
                return
            else:
                raise CometError(f"unknown instruction {op}")

    def binary(self, op, a, b):
        if op in ("EQ", "NE"):
            if type_name(a) != type_name(b):
                raise CometError(f"cannot compare {type_name(a)} with {type_name(b)}")
            return (a == b) == (op == "EQ")
        if op == "ADD" and type_name(a) == "str" and type_name(b) == "str":
            return a + b
        self.need("int", a, op)
        self.need("int", b, op)
        if op == "ADD":
            return a + b
        if op == "SUB":
            return a - b
        if op == "MUL":
            return a * b
        if op == "DIV":
            return comet_div(a, b)
        if op == "MOD":
            return comet_mod(a, b)
        if op == "LT":
            return a < b
        if op == "LE":
            return a <= b
        if op == "GT":
            return a > b
        return a >= b


def run_guarded(code, fuel, max_depth):
    raise NotImplementedError("write run_guarded")
