class ParseError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col

COMPARE = ("==", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">=")
TYPES = ("int", "bool", "str")

class Parser:
    def __init__(self, tokens):
        self.tokens = tokens
        self.pos = 0

    def peek(self, ahead=0):
        return self.tokens[min(self.pos + ahead, len(self.tokens) - 1)]

    def at(self, *texts):
        tok = self.peek()
        return tok.kind in ("OP", "KEYWORD") and tok.text in texts

    def advance(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "EOF":
            self.pos += 1
        return tok

    def error(self, message):
        tok = self.peek()
        return ParseError(message, tok.line, tok.col)

    def expect(self, text):
        if not self.at(text):
            raise self.error(f"expected '{text}'")
        return self.advance()

    def expr(self):
        return self.or_expr()

    def or_expr(self):
        left = self.and_expr()
        while self.at("or"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.and_expr())
        return left

    def and_expr(self):
        left = self.not_expr()
        while self.at("and"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.not_expr())
        return left

    def not_expr(self):
        if self.at("not"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("not", self.not_expr())
        return self.compare()

    def compare(self):
        left = self.sum()
        if self.at(*COMPARE):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.sum())
            if self.at(*COMPARE):
                raise self.error("comparisons cannot be chained")
        return left

    def sum(self):
        left = self.product()
        while self.at("+", "-"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.product())
        return left

    def product(self):
        left = self.unary()
        while self.at("*", "/", "%"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.unary())
        return left

    def unary(self):
        if self.at("-"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("-", self.unary())
        return self.call()

    def call(self):
        expr = self.primary()
        while self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            args = []
            if not self.at(")"):
                args.append(self.expr())
                while self.at(","):
                    self.advance()
                    args.append(self.expr())
            self.expect(")")
            expr = Call(expr, args)
        return expr

    def primary(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind == "NUMBER":
            self.advance()
            return Num(int(tok.text))
        if tok.kind == "STRING":
            self.advance()
            return Str(tok.text)
        if tok.kind == "IDENT":
            self.advance()
            return Var(tok.text)
        if self.at("true", "false"):
            self.advance()
            return Bool(tok.text == "true")
        if self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            inner = self.expr()
            self.expect(")")
            return inner
        raise self.error("expected an expression")

    def program(self):
        stmts = []
        while self.peek().kind != "EOF":
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        return Program(stmts)

    def statement(self):
        if self.at("let"):
            return self.let_stmt()
        if self.at("print"):
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Print(value)
        if self.at("if"):
            return self.if_stmt()
        if self.at("while"):
            self.advance()
            cond = self.expr()
            return While(cond, self.block())
        if self.at("fn"):
            return self.fn_stmt()
        if self.at("return"):
            self.advance()
            value = None if self.at(";") else self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Return(value)
        nxt = self.peek(1)
        if self.peek().kind == "IDENT" and nxt.kind == "OP" and nxt.text == "=":
            name = self.advance().text
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Assign(name, value)
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return ExprStmt(value)

    def name(self):
        if self.peek().kind != "IDENT":
            raise self.error("expected a name")
        return self.advance().text

    def type_name(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "IDENT" or tok.text not in TYPES:
            raise self.error("expected a type")
        return self.advance().text

    def let_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        self.expect("=")
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return Let(name, type_, value)

    def if_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        cond = self.expr()
        then = self.block()
        else_ = None
        if self.at("else"):
            self.advance()
            else_ = self.if_stmt() if self.at("if") else self.block()
        return If(cond, then, else_)

    def block(self):
        self.expect("{")
        stmts = []
        while not self.at("}"):
            if self.peek().kind == "EOF":
                raise self.error("expected '}'")
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        self.advance()
        return Block(stmts)

    def param(self):
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        return (name, type_)

    def fn_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        self.expect("(")
        params = []
        if not self.at(")"):
            params.append(self.param())
            while self.at(","):
                self.advance()
                params.append(self.param())
        self.expect(")")
        ret = None
        if self.at("->"):
            self.advance()
            ret = self.type_name()
        return Fn(name, params, ret, self.block())

def parse_program(tokens):
    return Parser(tokens).program()



def parse_expr(tokens):
    parser = Parser(tokens)
    tree = parser.expr()
    if parser.peek().kind != "EOF":
        raise parser.error("expected end of input")
    return tree


class CometError(Exception):
    pass


def comet_div(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q


def comet_mod(a, b):
    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)


def show(value):
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "true" if value else "false"
    return str(value)


TAC_OPS = {
    "+": lambda a, b: a + b,
    "-": lambda a, b: a - b,
    "*": lambda a, b: a * b,
    "/": comet_div,
    "%": comet_mod,
    "==": lambda a, b: a == b,
    "!=": lambda a, b: a != b,
    "<": lambda a, b: a < b,
    "<=": lambda a, b: a <= b,
    ">": lambda a, b: a > b,
    ">=": lambda a, b: a >= b,
}


def run_tac(code, limit=200000):
    labels = {ins[1]: i for i, ins in enumerate(code) if ins[0] == "label"}
    env = {}
    output = []

    def value(a):
        if isinstance(a, str):
            if a not in env:
                raise CometError(f"undefined variable {a}")
            return env[a]
        return a

    pc = 0
    steps = 0
    try:
        while pc < len(code):
            steps += 1
            if steps > limit:
                raise CometError("step limit reached")
            ins = code[pc]
            op = ins[0]
            pc += 1
            if op == "label":
                continue
            if op == "jump":
                pc = labels[ins[1]]
            elif op == "iffalse":
                if value(ins[1]) is False:
                    pc = labels[ins[2]]
            elif op == "print":
                output.append(show(value(ins[1])))
            elif op == "copy":
                env[ins[1]] = value(ins[2])
            elif op == "neg":
                env[ins[1]] = -value(ins[2])
            elif op == "not":
                env[ins[1]] = not value(ins[2])
            else:
                env[ins[1]] = TAC_OPS[op](value(ins[2]), value(ins[3]))
    except CometError as e:
        return output, str(e)
    return output, None


class Lowerer:
    def __init__(self):
        self.code = []
        self.temps = 0
        self.labels = 0

    def new_temp(self):
        self.temps += 1
        return f"%{self.temps}"

    def new_label(self):
        self.labels += 1
        return f"L{self.labels}"

    def emit(self, *ins):
        self.code.append(ins)

    def expr(self, e):
        if isinstance(e, (Num, Bool)):
            return e.value
        if isinstance(e, Var):
            return e.name
        if isinstance(e, Unary):
            a = self.expr(e.expr)
            t = self.new_temp()
            self.emit("neg" if e.op == "-" else "not", t, a)
            return t
        if isinstance(e, Binary) and e.op == "and":
            left = self.expr(e.left)
            t = self.new_temp()
            self.emit("copy", t, left)
            end = self.new_label()
            self.emit("iffalse", t, end)
            self.emit("copy", t, self.expr(e.right))
            self.emit("label", end)
            return t
        if isinstance(e, Binary) and e.op == "or":
            left = self.expr(e.left)
            t = self.new_temp()
            self.emit("copy", t, left)
            right = self.new_label()
            end = self.new_label()
            self.emit("iffalse", t, right)
            self.emit("jump", end)
            self.emit("label", right)
            self.emit("copy", t, self.expr(e.right))
            self.emit("label", end)
            return t
        if isinstance(e, Binary):
            a = self.expr(e.left)
            b = self.expr(e.right)
            t = self.new_temp()
            self.emit(e.op, t, a, b)
            return t
        raise CometError(f"{type(e).__name__} is not part of the IR")

    def stmt(self, s):
        if isinstance(s, (Let, Assign)):
            self.emit("copy", s.name, self.expr(s.expr))
        elif isinstance(s, Print):
            self.emit("print", self.expr(s.expr))
        elif isinstance(s, ExprStmt):
            self.expr(s.expr)
        elif isinstance(s, Block):
            for inner in s.stmts:
                self.stmt(inner)
        elif isinstance(s, If):
            cond = self.expr(s.cond)
            if s.else_ is None:
                end = self.new_label()
                self.emit("iffalse", cond, end)
                self.stmt(s.then)
                self.emit("label", end)
            else:
                other = self.new_label()
                end = self.new_label()
                self.emit("iffalse", cond, other)
                self.stmt(s.then)
                self.emit("jump", end)
                self.emit("label", other)
                self.stmt(s.else_)
                self.emit("label", end)
        elif isinstance(s, While):
            top = self.new_label()
            end = self.new_label()
            self.emit("label", top)
            cond = self.expr(s.cond)
            self.emit("iffalse", cond, end)
            self.stmt(s.body)
            self.emit("jump", top)
            self.emit("label", end)
        else:
            raise CometError(f"{type(s).__name__} is not part of the IR")


def lower(program):
    lowerer = Lowerer()
    for s in program.stmts:
        lowerer.stmt(s)
    return lowerer.code


def build_cfg(code):
    leaders = set()
    for i, ins in enumerate(code):
        if i == 0 or ins[0] == "label":
            leaders.add(i)
        if ins[0] in ("jump", "iffalse") and i + 1 < len(code):
            leaders.add(i + 1)
    starts = sorted(leaders)
    ends = starts[1:] + [len(code)]
    blocks = [code[s:e] for s, e in zip(starts, ends)]
    block_of = {b[0][1]: i for i, b in enumerate(blocks) if b[0][0] == "label"}
    succ = []
    for i, block in enumerate(blocks):
        last = block[-1]
        out = set()
        if last[0] == "jump":
            out.add(block_of[last[1]])
        else:
            if last[0] == "iffalse":
                out.add(block_of[last[2]])
            if i + 1 < len(blocks):
                out.add(i + 1)
        succ.append(sorted(out))
    return blocks, succ


def tac(source):
    return lower(parse_program(tokenize(source)))


def defs_uses(ins):
    op = ins[0]
    if op in ("label", "jump"):
        return None, []
    if op in ("print", "iffalse"):
        return None, [ins[1]] if isinstance(ins[1], str) else []
    return ins[1], [a for a in ins[2:] if isinstance(a, str)]


def liveness(blocks, succ):
    use = []
    define = []
    for block in blocks:
        u, d = set(), set()
        for ins in block:
            dst, uses = defs_uses(ins)
            u |= {a for a in uses if a not in d}
            if dst is not None:
                d.add(dst)
        use.append(u)
        define.append(d)
    live_in = [set() for _ in blocks]
    live_out = [set() for _ in blocks]
    changed = True
    while changed:
        changed = False
        for i in reversed(range(len(blocks))):
            out = set()
            for j in succ[i]:
                out |= live_in[j]
            new_in = use[i] | (out - define[i])
            if out != live_out[i] or new_in != live_in[i]:
                live_out[i], live_in[i] = out, new_in
                changed = True
    return live_in, live_out
--- hint
When the loop body's block is processed, has the loop test's block been processed yet? What does its `live_in` hold at that moment?
--- hint
One pass is not enough when there is a back edge. Repeat the pass until no set changes.

=> [{'keep', 'go'}, {'keep'}, {'keep', 'go'}, set()]

=> ([{'x', 'c', 'y'}, {'x'}, {'y'}, set()], [{'x', 'y'}, set(), set(), set()])

+++ practice | Linear scan allocation
--- task
Just-in-time compilers allocate registers with **linear scan**. Write two functions for a straight-line block.

`live_intervals(block, live_out)` returns a dictionary from every name in the block to its interval `(start, end)`: start is the index of the first instruction that mentions it (reading or writing), end is the index of the last one, or `len(block)` if the name is in `live_out`. For `print` and `iffalse` only the first operand is a name; `label` and `jump` mention none.

`linear_scan(intervals, k)` returns a dictionary from each name to a register from 0 to k − 1, or `None` if spilled:

1. Go through the names by start, breaking ties alphabetically.
2. Before placing a name, **expire** every active name whose end is less than the new start: its register becomes free.
3. If fewer than k names are active, give the new name the lowest free register and make it active.
4. Otherwise, look at the active name with the largest end (alphabetically largest among ties). If its end is greater than the new name's end, the new name takes its register and it becomes `None` (spilled) and inactive; otherwise the new name is spilled.

For example, for `[('copy', 'a', 1), ('copy', 'b', 2), ('+', 'c', 'a', 'b'), ('*', 'd', 'c', 'a'), ('print', 'd')]` with no live-out names, the intervals are a (0, 3), b (1, 2), c (2, 3), d (3, 4), and with k = 2, a gets 0, b gets 1, c is spilled (a ends no later than c), and d gets 1 after b expires.

--- solution
class CometError(Exception):
    pass


def comet_div(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q


def comet_mod(a, b):
    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)


def show(value):
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "true" if value else "false"
    return str(value)


def live_intervals(block, live_out):
    first = {}
    last = {}
    for i, ins in enumerate(block):
        if ins[0] in ("label", "jump"):
            names = []
        elif ins[0] in ("print", "iffalse"):
            names = [ins[1]]
        else:
            names = list(ins[1:])
        for a in names:
            if isinstance(a, str):
                first.setdefault(a, i)
                last[a] = i
    for a in live_out:
        if a in first:
            last[a] = len(block)
    return {a: (first[a], last[a]) for a in first}


def linear_scan(intervals, k):
    order = sorted(intervals, key=lambda n: (intervals[n][0], n))
    active = []
    assigned = {}
    free = list(range(k))
    for name in order:
        start, end = intervals[name]
        for other in list(active):
            if intervals[other][1] < start:
                active.remove(other)
                free.append(assigned[other])
        free.sort()
        if len(active) == k:
            victim = max(active, key=lambda n: (intervals[n][1], n)) if active else None
            if victim is not None and intervals[victim][1] > end:
                assigned[name] = assigned[victim]
                assigned[victim] = None
                active.remove(victim)
                active.append(name)
            else:
                assigned[name] = None
        else:
            assigned[name] = free.pop(0)
            active.append(name)
    return assigned
--- hint
For the intervals, walk the block once, recording the first index of each name with `setdefault` and overwriting its last index every time; then extend the names in `live_out` to `len(block)`.
--- hint
For the scan, keep a list of active names and a list of free registers (sort it before taking the lowest). Expire first, then either assign, or compare the new name's end with the largest active end.
--- check case | The example's intervals
live_intervals([('copy', 'a', 1), ('copy', 'b', 2), ('+', 'c', 'a', 'b'), ('*', 'd', 'c', 'a'), ('print', 'd')], [])
=> {'a': (0, 3), 'b': (1, 2), 'c': (2, 3), 'd': (3, 4)}
--- check case | The example with 2 registers and with 1
(linear_scan({'a': (0, 3), 'b': (1, 2), 'c': (2, 3), 'd': (3, 4)}, 2), linear_scan({'a': (0, 3), 'b': (1, 2), 'c': (2, 3), 'd': (3, 4)}, 1))
=> ({'a': 0, 'b': 1, 'c': None, 'd': 1}, {'a': None, 'b': 0, 'c': None, 'd': 0})
--- check case | A long interval gives its register to a short one
linear_scan({'long': (0, 10), 'x': (1, 2), 'y': (3, 4)}, 1)
=> {'long': None, 'x': 0, 'y': 0}
--- check case | Enough registers: nothing spills, freed registers are reused lowest first
linear_scan({'p': (0, 1), 'q': (0, 5), 'r': (2, 3), 's': (4, 6)}, 2)
=> {'p': 0, 'q': 1, 'r': 0, 's': 0}
--- check case | Live-out names last to the end; labels are not names; empty inputs
(live_intervals([('label', 'L1'), ('copy', 'x', 1), ('iffalse', 'x', 'L1')], ['x']), live_intervals([], ['x']), linear_scan({}, 3))
=> ({'x': (1, 3)}, {}, {})
--- check case | No registers at all
linear_scan({'a': (0, 1)}, 0)
=> {'a': None}

=== plc-gate | Programming Languages & Compilers: mastery gate
--- teach
This gate covers the whole course: lexing and parsing, interpreters, scope and closures, type checking and inference, functional programming, semantic analysis, intermediate representations, optimisation, the stack VM and code generation, garbage collection and register allocation. Each problem combines two or more of those ideas, in a setting you have not seen, and there are no hints. To get ready, redo the practice problems of the lessons that felt hardest, and make sure you can argue why each algorithm is correct, not only run it.

+++ problem | A power operator
--- task
Add a power operator `**` to Comet's expressions. The starter gives the lexer, the parser, `parse_expr`, `CometError`, the division helpers, and an evaluator `evaluate(e)` for arithmetic trees with `calc(source)`, which parses and evaluates an expression. Change three things:

- **Lexer:** `**` is one `OP` token (so `2**3` has three tokens).
- **Parser:** `**` binds tighter than unary minus on its **left** and is **right-associative**, and its right operand may start with a minus. Use this grammar in place of the old `unary` rule: `unary = "-" unary | power ;` and `power = call [ "**" unary ] ;`. A `**` builds `Binary("**", base, exponent)`.
- **Evaluator:** `**` computes a to the power b for integers; a negative exponent raises `CometError`.

So `calc("2 ** 3 ** 2")` is 512, `calc("-2 ** 2")` is −4 (as in Python and in mathematics), `calc("(-2) ** 2")` is 4, and `calc("2 * 3 ** 2")` is 18.
--- starter
from dataclasses import dataclass

KEYWORDS = {"let", "fn", "return", "if", "else", "while", "print",
            "true", "false", "and", "or", "not"}
TWO_CHAR = {"==", "!=", "<=", ">=", "->"}
ONE_CHAR = set("+-*/%<>=(){},;:")
ESCAPES = {'"': '"', "\\": "\\", "n": "\n"}
DIGITS = "0123456789"
LETTERS = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ_"

@dataclass
class Token:
    kind: str
    text: str
    line: int
    col: int

class LexError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col

def tokenize(source):
    tokens = []
    i = 0
    line = 1
    col = 1
    n = len(source)

    def advance(count):
        nonlocal i, line, col
        for _ in range(count):
            if source[i] == "\n":
                line += 1
                col = 1
            else:
                col += 1
            i += 1

    while i < n:
        ch = source[i]
        start_line, start_col = line, col
        if ch in " \t\r\n":
            advance(1)
        elif ch == "#":
            while i < n and source[i] != "\n":
                advance(1)
        elif ch in DIGITS:
            j = i
            while j < n and source[j] in DIGITS:
                j += 1
            tokens.append(Token("NUMBER", source[i:j], start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch in LETTERS:
            j = i
            while j < n and (source[j] in LETTERS or source[j] in DIGITS):
                j += 1
            word = source[i:j]
            kind = "KEYWORD" if word in KEYWORDS else "IDENT"
            tokens.append(Token(kind, word, start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch == '"':
            advance(1)
            chars = []
            while True:
                if i >= n or source[i] == "\n":
                    raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                c = source[i]
                if c == '"':
                    advance(1)
                    break
                if c == "\\":
                    if i + 1 >= n or source[i + 1] == "\n":
                        raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                    if source[i + 1] not in ESCAPES:
                        raise LexError("unknown escape", line, col)
                    chars.append(ESCAPES[source[i + 1]])
                    advance(2)
                else:
                    chars.append(c)
                    advance(1)
            tokens.append(Token("STRING", "".join(chars), start_line, start_col))
        elif source[i:i + 2] in TWO_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", source[i:i + 2], start_line, start_col))
            advance(2)
        elif ch in ONE_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", ch, start_line, start_col))
            advance(1)
        else:
            raise LexError(f"unexpected character {ch!r}", start_line, start_col)
    tokens.append(Token("EOF", "", line, col))
    return tokens

class ParseError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col

COMPARE = ("==", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">=")
TYPES = ("int", "bool", "str")

class Parser:
    def __init__(self, tokens):
        self.tokens = tokens
        self.pos = 0

    def peek(self, ahead=0):
        return self.tokens[min(self.pos + ahead, len(self.tokens) - 1)]

    def at(self, *texts):
        tok = self.peek()
        return tok.kind in ("OP", "KEYWORD") and tok.text in texts

    def advance(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "EOF":
            self.pos += 1
        return tok

    def error(self, message):
        tok = self.peek()
        return ParseError(message, tok.line, tok.col)

    def expect(self, text):
        if not self.at(text):
            raise self.error(f"expected '{text}'")
        return self.advance()

    def expr(self):
        return self.or_expr()

    def or_expr(self):
        left = self.and_expr()
        while self.at("or"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.and_expr())
        return left

    def and_expr(self):
        left = self.not_expr()
        while self.at("and"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.not_expr())
        return left

    def not_expr(self):
        if self.at("not"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("not", self.not_expr())
        return self.compare()

    def compare(self):
        left = self.sum()
        if self.at(*COMPARE):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.sum())
            if self.at(*COMPARE):
                raise self.error("comparisons cannot be chained")
        return left

    def sum(self):
        left = self.product()
        while self.at("+", "-"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.product())
        return left

    def product(self):
        left = self.unary()
        while self.at("*", "/", "%"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.unary())
        return left

    def unary(self):
        if self.at("-"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("-", self.unary())
        return self.call()

    def call(self):
        expr = self.primary()
        while self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            args = []
            if not self.at(")"):
                args.append(self.expr())
                while self.at(","):
                    self.advance()
                    args.append(self.expr())
            self.expect(")")
            expr = Call(expr, args)
        return expr

    def primary(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind == "NUMBER":
            self.advance()
            return Num(int(tok.text))
        if tok.kind == "STRING":
            self.advance()
            return Str(tok.text)
        if tok.kind == "IDENT":
            self.advance()
            return Var(tok.text)
        if self.at("true", "false"):
            self.advance()
            return Bool(tok.text == "true")
        if self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            inner = self.expr()
            self.expect(")")
            return inner
        raise self.error("expected an expression")

    def program(self):
        stmts = []
        while self.peek().kind != "EOF":
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        return Program(stmts)

    def statement(self):
        if self.at("let"):
            return self.let_stmt()
        if self.at("print"):
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Print(value)
        if self.at("if"):
            return self.if_stmt()
        if self.at("while"):
            self.advance()
            cond = self.expr()
            return While(cond, self.block())
        if self.at("fn"):
            return self.fn_stmt()
        if self.at("return"):
            self.advance()
            value = None if self.at(";") else self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Return(value)
        nxt = self.peek(1)
        if self.peek().kind == "IDENT" and nxt.kind == "OP" and nxt.text == "=":
            name = self.advance().text
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Assign(name, value)
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return ExprStmt(value)

    def name(self):
        if self.peek().kind != "IDENT":
            raise self.error("expected a name")
        return self.advance().text

    def type_name(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "IDENT" or tok.text not in TYPES:
            raise self.error("expected a type")
        return self.advance().text

    def let_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        self.expect("=")
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return Let(name, type_, value)

    def if_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        cond = self.expr()
        then = self.block()
        else_ = None
        if self.at("else"):
            self.advance()
            else_ = self.if_stmt() if self.at("if") else self.block()
        return If(cond, then, else_)

    def block(self):
        self.expect("{")
        stmts = []
        while not self.at("}"):
            if self.peek().kind == "EOF":
                raise self.error("expected '}'")
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        self.advance()
        return Block(stmts)

    def param(self):
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        return (name, type_)

    def fn_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        self.expect("(")
        params = []
        if not self.at(")"):
            params.append(self.param())
            while self.at(","):
                self.advance()
                params.append(self.param())
        self.expect(")")
        ret = None
        if self.at("->"):
            self.advance()
            ret = self.type_name()
        return Fn(name, params, ret, self.block())

def parse_program(tokens):
    return Parser(tokens).program()



def parse_expr(tokens):
    parser = Parser(tokens)
    tree = parser.expr()
    if parser.peek().kind != "EOF":
        raise parser.error("expected end of input")
    return tree


class CometError(Exception):
    pass


def comet_div(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q


def comet_mod(a, b):
    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)


def show(value):
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "true" if value else "false"
    return str(value)


def evaluate(e):
    if isinstance(e, Num):
        return e.value
    if isinstance(e, Unary) and e.op == "-":
        return -evaluate(e.expr)
    if isinstance(e, Binary):
        a = evaluate(e.left)
        b = evaluate(e.right)
        if e.op == "+":
            return a + b
        if e.op == "-":
            return a - b
        if e.op == "*":
            return a * b
        if e.op == "/":
            return comet_div(a, b)
        if e.op == "%":
            return comet_mod(a, b)
    raise CometError("not an arithmetic expression")


def calc(source):
    return evaluate(parse_expr(tokenize(source)))

        self.line = line
        self.col = col

TYPES = ("int", "bool", "str")

class Parser:
    def __init__(self, tokens):
        self.tokens = tokens
        self.pos = 0

    def peek(self, ahead=0):
        return self.tokens[min(self.pos + ahead, len(self.tokens) - 1)]

    def at(self, *texts):
        tok = self.peek()
        return tok.kind in ("OP", "KEYWORD") and tok.text in texts

    def advance(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "EOF":
            self.pos += 1
        return tok

    def error(self, message):
        tok = self.peek()
        return ParseError(message, tok.line, tok.col)

    def expect(self, text):
        if not self.at(text):
            raise self.error(f"expected '{text}'")
        return self.advance()

    def expr(self):
        return self.or_expr()

    def or_expr(self):
        left = self.and_expr()
        while self.at("or"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.and_expr())
        return left

    def and_expr(self):
        left = self.not_expr()
        while self.at("and"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.not_expr())
        return left

    def not_expr(self):
        if self.at("not"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("not", self.not_expr())
        return self.compare()

    def compare(self):
        left = self.sum()
        if self.at(*COMPARE):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.sum())
            if self.at(*COMPARE):
                raise self.error("comparisons cannot be chained")
        return left

    def sum(self):
        left = self.product()
        while self.at("+", "-"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.product())
        return left

    def product(self):
        left = self.unary()
        while self.at("*", "/", "%"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.unary())
        return left

    def unary(self):
        if self.at("-"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("-", self.unary())
        return self.power()

    def power(self):
        base = self.call()
        if self.at("**"):
            self.advance()
            return Binary("**", base, self.unary())
        return base

    def call(self):
        expr = self.primary()
        while self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            args = []
            if not self.at(")"):
                args.append(self.expr())
                while self.at(","):
                    self.advance()
                    args.append(self.expr())
            self.expect(")")
            expr = Call(expr, args)
        return expr

    def primary(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind == "NUMBER":
            self.advance()
            return Num(int(tok.text))
        if tok.kind == "STRING":
            self.advance()
            return Str(tok.text)
        if tok.kind == "IDENT":
            self.advance()
            return Var(tok.text)
        if self.at("true", "false"):
            self.advance()
            return Bool(tok.text == "true")
        if self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            inner = self.expr()
            self.expect(")")
            return inner
        raise self.error("expected an expression")

    def program(self):
        stmts = []
        while self.peek().kind != "EOF":
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        return Program(stmts)

    def statement(self):
        if self.at("let"):
            return self.let_stmt()
        if self.at("print"):
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Print(value)
        if self.at("if"):
            return self.if_stmt()
        if self.at("while"):
            self.advance()
            cond = self.expr()
            return While(cond, self.block())
        if self.at("fn"):
            return self.fn_stmt()
        if self.at("return"):
            self.advance()
            value = None if self.at(";") else self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Return(value)
        nxt = self.peek(1)
        if self.peek().kind == "IDENT" and nxt.kind == "OP" and nxt.text == "=":
            name = self.advance().text
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Assign(name, value)
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return ExprStmt(value)

    def name(self):
        if self.peek().kind != "IDENT":
            raise self.error("expected a name")
        return self.advance().text

    def type_name(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "IDENT" or tok.text not in TYPES:
            raise self.error("expected a type")
        return self.advance().text

    def let_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        self.expect("=")
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return Let(name, type_, value)

    def if_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        cond = self.expr()
        then = self.block()
        else_ = None
        if self.at("else"):
            self.advance()
            else_ = self.if_stmt() if self.at("if") else self.block()
        return If(cond, then, else_)

    def block(self):
        self.expect("{")
        stmts = []
        while not self.at("}"):
            if self.peek().kind == "EOF":
                raise self.error("expected '}'")
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        self.advance()
        return Block(stmts)

    def param(self):
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        return (name, type_)

    def fn_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        self.expect("(")
        params = []
        if not self.at(")"):
            params.append(self.param())
            while self.at(","):
                self.advance()
                params.append(self.param())
        self.expect(")")
        ret = None
        if self.at("->"):
            self.advance()
            ret = self.type_name()
        return Fn(name, params, ret, self.block())

def parse_program(tokens):
    return Parser(tokens).program()



def parse_expr(tokens):
    parser = Parser(tokens)
    tree = parser.expr()
    if parser.peek().kind != "EOF":
        raise parser.error("expected end of input")
    return tree


class CometError(Exception):
    pass


def comet_div(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q


def comet_mod(a, b):
    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)


def show(value):
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "true" if value else "false"
    return str(value)


def evaluate(e):
    if isinstance(e, Num):
        return e.value
    if isinstance(e, Unary) and e.op == "-":
        return -evaluate(e.expr)
    if isinstance(e, Binary):
        a = evaluate(e.left)
        b = evaluate(e.right)
        if e.op == "+":
            return a + b
        if e.op == "-":
            return a - b
        if e.op == "*":
            return a * b
        if e.op == "/":
            return comet_div(a, b)
        if e.op == "%":
            return comet_mod(a, b)
        if e.op == "**":
            if b < 0:
                raise CometError("negative exponent")
            return a ** b
    raise CometError("not an arithmetic expression")


def calc(source):
    return evaluate(parse_expr(tokenize(source)))

calc("2 ** 3 ** 2")
=> 512
--- check case | Tighter than unary minus on the left, parentheses override

=> (-4, 4, -4)
--- check case | Tighter than * and +, and the exponent may be negated twice
(calc("2 * 3 ** 2"), calc("1 + 2 ** 2 * 3"), calc("2 ** --3"), calc("10 ** 0"))
=> (18, 13, 8, 1)

--- check test | One token, and * still works

+++ problem | FIRST sets and LL(1) conflicts
--- task
A grammar is a dictionary from each nonterminal to a list of alternatives; an alternative is a list of symbols, and `[]` is the empty alternative (ε). Every symbol that is not a key is a terminal. Write two functions.

- `first_sets(grammar)` returns `(nullable, first)`: `nullable` is the set of nonterminals that can derive the empty string, and `first[N]` is the set of terminals that can begin a string derived from N. Compute both by repeating passes over the rules until nothing changes: for an alternative X1 X2 … Xk, FIRST(N) gains FIRST(X1), and also FIRST(X2) if X1 is nullable, and so on (a terminal's FIRST is itself, and it is never nullable); N is nullable if some alternative consists only of nullable nonterminals (the empty alternative included).
- `ll1_conflicts(grammar)` returns the sorted list of nonterminals that a one-token-lookahead recursive-descent parser could not decide on from FIRST sets alone: those with two alternatives whose FIRST sets (of the whole alternative, as above) share a terminal, or with two alternatives that can both derive the empty string.

For example, for `{"E": [["T", "+", "E"], ["T"]], "T": [["n"], ["(", "E", ")"]]}`, FIRST(E) and FIRST(T) are `{"n", "("}`, nothing is nullable, and E has a conflict: both of its alternatives start with T.

class CometError(Exception):
    pass


def comet_div(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q


def comet_mod(a, b):
    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)


def show(value):
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "true" if value else "false"
    return str(value)


def first_sets(grammar):
    nullable = set()
    first = {n: set() for n in grammar}
    changed = True
    while changed:
        changed = False
        for n, alts in grammar.items():
            for alt in alts:
                all_nullable = True
                for sym in alt:
                    if sym in grammar:
                        new = first[sym] - first[n]
                        if new:
                            first[n] |= new
                            changed = True
                        if sym not in nullable:
                            all_nullable = False
                            break
                    else:
                        if sym not in first[n]:
                            first[n].add(sym)
                            changed = True
                        all_nullable = False
                        break
                if all_nullable and n not in nullable:
                    nullable.add(n)
                    changed = True
    return nullable, first


def first_of(seq, grammar, nullable, first):
    out = set()
    for sym in seq:
        if sym in grammar:
            out |= first[sym]
            if sym not in nullable:
                return out, False
        else:
            out.add(sym)
            return out, False
    return out, True


def ll1_conflicts(grammar):
    nullable, first = first_sets(grammar)
    bad = []
    for n, alts in grammar.items():
        seen = set()
        empties = 0
        clash = False
        for alt in alts:
            f, can_be_empty = first_of(alt, grammar, nullable, first)
            if f & seen:
                clash = True
            seen |= f
            empties += can_be_empty
        if clash or empties > 1:
            bad.append(n)
    return sorted(bad)
--- check case | The example
(first_sets({"E": [["T", "+", "E"], ["T"]], "T": [["n"], ["(", "E", ")"]]}), ll1_conflicts({"E": [["T", "+", "E"], ["T"]], "T": [["n"], ["(", "E", ")"]]}))
=> ((set(), {"E": {"n", "("}, "T": {"n", "("}}), ["E"])
--- check case | After left-factoring there is no conflict
(first_sets({"E": [["T", "R"]], "R": [["+", "T", "R"], []], "T": [["n"]]}), ll1_conflicts({"E": [["T", "R"]], "R": [["+", "T", "R"], []], "T": [["n"]]}))
=> (({"R"}, {"E": {"n"}, "R": {"+"}, "T": {"n"}}), [])
--- check case | Nullable prefixes pass FIRST along
first_sets({"S": [["A", "B", "c"]], "A": [["a"], []], "B": [["b"], []]})
=> ({"A", "B"}, {"S": {"a", "b", "c"}, "A": {"a"}, "B": {"b"}})
--- check case | Two ways to derive nothing is a conflict
ll1_conflicts({"S": [["A"], ["B"]], "A": [["a"], []], "B": [["b"], []]})
=> ["S"]
--- check case | Left recursion is always a conflict
ll1_conflicts({"E": [["E", "-", "n"], ["n"]]})
=> ["E"]
--- check case | A nonterminal that needs several passes
first_sets({"A": [["B"]], "B": [["C"]], "C": [["D", "x"]], "D": [["A", "y"], []]})
=> ({"D"}, {"A": {"x"}, "B": {"x"}, "C": {"x"}, "D": {"x"}})

+++ problem | Closures in a tiny functional language
--- task
Write an interpreter `evaluate(e, env=None)` for a small functional language whose programs are nested tuples. Scope is **lexical**, and functions are first-class values that capture their defining environment. Environments are dictionaries from names to values; never change one in place (build a new one), so closures keep the bindings they captured.

- `("num", n)` is the integer n; `("var", x)` is the value bound to x, or `CometError` if x is unbound.
- `("add", a, b)`, `("sub", a, b)`, `("mul", a, b)` evaluate a, then b, and need two integers, or `CometError`.
- `("lam", x, body)` is a one-parameter function: return a `Closure` holding x, body and the current environment (define the `Closure` class yourself).
- `("app", f, a)` evaluates f, then a; f must be a `Closure`, or `CometError`; then it evaluates the closure's body in the closure's environment extended with the parameter bound to a's value.
- `("let", x, e1, e2)` evaluates e1, then e2 with x bound to that value.
- `("if0", c, t, e)` evaluates c; if it is 0, the value is t's, otherwise e's (only one branch is evaluated).
- Anything else raises `CometError`.

The starter's `run(e)` evaluates e and returns the value, or `"<fn>"` for a function. For example, `run(("app", ("lam", "x", ("add", ("var", "x"), ("num", 1))), ("num", 41)))` is 42.

--- solution
class CometError(Exception):
    pass


def comet_div(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q


def comet_mod(a, b):
    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)


def show(value):
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "true" if value else "false"
    return str(value)


class Closure:
    def __init__(self, param, body, env):
        self.param = param
        self.body = body
        self.env = env


def evaluate(e, env=None):
    env = env or {}
    kind = e[0]
    if kind == "num":
        return e[1]
    if kind == "var":
        if e[1] not in env:
            raise CometError(f"unbound variable {e[1]}")
        return env[e[1]]
    if kind in ("add", "sub", "mul"):
        a = evaluate(e[1], env)
        b = evaluate(e[2], env)
        if not (type(a) is int and type(b) is int):
            raise CometError(f"{kind} needs two numbers")
        return a + b if kind == "add" else a - b if kind == "sub" else a * b
    if kind == "lam":
        return Closure(e[1], e[2], env)
    if kind == "app":
        f = evaluate(e[1], env)
        arg = evaluate(e[2], env)
        if not isinstance(f, Closure):
            raise CometError("only functions can be applied")
        return evaluate(f.body, {**f.env, f.param: arg})
    if kind == "let":
        value = evaluate(e[2], env)
        return evaluate(e[3], {**env, e[1]: value})
    if kind == "if0":
        test = evaluate(e[1], env)
        return evaluate(e[2] if test == 0 else e[3], env)
    raise CometError(f"unknown expression {kind}")


def run(e):
    value = evaluate(e)
    return "<fn>" if isinstance(value, Closure) else value
--- check case | The example
run(("app", ("lam", "x", ("add", ("var", "x"), ("num", 1))), ("num", 41)))
=> 42
--- check case | Currying: a function that returns a function
run(("let", "adder", ("lam", "a", ("lam", "b", ("sub", ("var", "a"), ("var", "b")))), ("app", ("app", ("var", "adder"), ("num", 10)), ("num", 3))))
=> 7
--- check case | Lexical, not dynamic, scope
run(("let", "x", ("num", 1), ("let", "f", ("lam", "y", ("var", "x")), ("let", "x", ("num", 2), ("app", ("var", "f"), ("num", 0))))))
=> 1
--- check case | Shadowing, and a function value
(run(("let", "x", ("num", 1), ("let", "x", ("mul", ("var", "x"), ("num", 5)), ("var", "x")))), run(("lam", "z", ("var", "z"))))
=> (5, "<fn>")
--- check case | Recursion through a fixed-point combinator (factorial of 6)
run(("let", "Z", ("lam", "f", ("app", ("lam", "x", ("app", ("var", "f"), ("lam", "v", ("app", ("app", ("var", "x"), ("var", "x")), ("var", "v"))))), ("lam", "x", ("app", ("var", "f"), ("lam", "v", ("app", ("app", ("var", "x"), ("var", "x")), ("var", "v"))))))), ("app", ("app", ("var", "Z"), ("lam", "fact", ("lam", "n", ("if0", ("var", "n"), ("num", 1), ("mul", ("var", "n"), ("app", ("var", "fact"), ("sub", ("var", "n"), ("num", 1)))))))), ("num", 6))))
=> 720
--- check test | Errors, and if0 evaluates only one branch
all(raises(CometError, lambda e=e: run(e)) for e in [("var", "nope"), ("app", ("num", 3), ("num", 4)), ("add", ("lam", "x", ("var", "x")), ("num", 1)), ("mul", ("num", 2), ("lam", "y", ("num", 1))), ("bogus",)]) and run(("if0", ("num", 0), ("num", 7), ("var", "unbound"))) == 7

+++ problem | Type checking with function types
--- task
Write a type checker `type_of(e, env=None)` for a small typed expression language, written as nested tuples. Types are the strings `"int"` and `"bool"` and the starter's frozen `FnType(params, ret)`, where `params` is a tuple of types. Raise the starter's `TypeCheckError` for any ill-typed expression. `env` is a dictionary from names to types; do not change it.

- `("num", n)` is `int`; `("bool", b)` is `bool`; `("var", x)` has x's type from `env`, or `TypeCheckError` if x is not there.
- `("add", a, b)` needs two ints and is `int`; `("lt", a, b)` needs two ints and is `bool`.
- `("if", c, t, f)`: c must be `bool`, and t and f must have the same type, which is the result.
- `("lam", [(x1, T1), (x2, T2), …], body)` is `FnType((T1, T2, …), type of body)`, where the body is checked with the parameters added to `env`. Two parameters with the same name are an error.
- `("app", f, [a1, a2, …])`: f must have an `FnType`, with as many parameters as there are arguments, each argument's type equal to its parameter's type; the result is the return type.
- `("let", x, e1, e2)` is e2's type, with x bound to e1's type.

For example, `type_of(("lam", [("n", "int")], ("lt", ("var", "n"), ("num", 0))))` is `FnType(("int",), "bool")`.

from dataclasses import dataclass


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FnType:
    params: tuple
    ret: object


class TypeCheckError(Exception):
    pass


def type_of(e, env=None):
    env = env or {}
    kind = e[0]
    if kind == "num":
        return "int"
    if kind == "bool":
        return "bool"
    if kind == "var":
        if e[1] not in env:
            raise TypeCheckError(f"undefined name {e[1]}")
        return env[e[1]]
    if kind in ("add", "lt"):
        a, b = type_of(e[1], env), type_of(e[2], env)
        if a != "int" or b != "int":
            raise TypeCheckError(f"{kind} needs two ints")
        return "int" if kind == "add" else "bool"
    if kind == "if":
        if type_of(e[1], env) != "bool":
            raise TypeCheckError("the condition must be bool")
        t, f = type_of(e[2], env), type_of(e[3], env)
        if t != f:
            raise TypeCheckError("the branches have different types")
        return t
    if kind == "lam":
        inner = dict(env)
        for name, t in e[1]:
            inner[name] = t
        if len({name for name, _ in e[1]}) != len(e[1]):
            raise TypeCheckError("duplicate parameter")
        return FnType(tuple(t for _, t in e[1]), type_of(e[2], inner))
    if kind == "app":
        f = type_of(e[1], env)
        args = [type_of(a, env) for a in e[2]]
        if not isinstance(f, FnType):
            raise TypeCheckError("only functions can be called")
        if len(args) != len(f.params) or any(a != p for a, p in zip(args, f.params)):
            raise TypeCheckError("wrong arguments")
        return f.ret
    if kind == "let":
        return type_of(e[3], {**env, e[1]: type_of(e[2], env)})
    raise TypeCheckError(f"unknown expression {kind}")

--- check test | Applying functions, including a function that takes a function

--- check test | if, let, and an environment

+++ problem | Unification with the occurs check
--- task
Type inference solves equations between types by **unification**. The starter gives frozen dataclasses `TVar(name)` (a type variable), `TCon(name)` (a type such as `int`) and `TFun(params, ret)` with `params` a tuple, and `TypeCheckError`. A substitution is a dictionary from `TVar`s to types; it may bind a variable to a type that mentions other bound variables. Write two functions.

- `resolve(t, subst)`: t with every bound variable replaced, repeatedly, until no bound variable is left (inside function types too).
- `unify(a, b, subst)`: return a **new** substitution that extends `subst` and makes a and b equal, or raise `TypeCheckError`. Resolve both sides first. Equal types need nothing. A variable unifies with any type that does not contain it (the **occurs check**: `TVar("a")` against `TFun((TVar("a"),), TCon("int"))` would need an infinite type, so it is an error). Two function types unify when they have the same number of parameters, by unifying the parameters in order and then the return types. Anything else (two different constructors, a constructor against a function, different numbers of parameters) is an error. Never change the `subst` passed in.

For example, unifying `TFun((TVar("a"),), TVar("a"))` with `TFun((TCon("int"),), TVar("b"))` binds a and b so that both resolve to `TCon("int")`.

class CometError(Exception):

def comet_div(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q

    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)

    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "true" if value else "false"
    return str(value)


from dataclasses import dataclass


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TVar:
    name: str


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TCon:
    name: str


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TFun:
    params: tuple
    ret: object


class TypeCheckError(Exception):
    pass


def resolve(t, subst):
    if isinstance(t, TVar):
        return resolve(subst[t], subst) if t in subst else t
    if isinstance(t, TFun):
        return TFun(tuple(resolve(p, subst) for p in t.params), resolve(t.ret, subst))
    return t


def occurs(v, t, subst):
    t = resolve(t, subst)
    if t == v:
        return True
    if isinstance(t, TFun):
        return any(occurs(v, p, subst) for p in t.params) or occurs(v, t.ret, subst)
    return False


def unify(a, b, subst):
    subst = dict(subst)
    a, b = resolve(a, subst), resolve(b, subst)
    if a == b:
        return subst
    if isinstance(a, TVar):
        if occurs(a, b, subst):
            raise TypeCheckError("infinite type")
        subst[a] = b
        return subst
    if isinstance(b, TVar):
        return unify(b, a, subst)
    if isinstance(a, TFun) and isinstance(b, TFun) and len(a.params) == len(b.params):
        for p, q in zip(a.params, b.params):
            subst = unify(p, q, subst)
        return unify(a.ret, b.ret, subst)
    raise TypeCheckError("types do not match")
--- check test | The example
(lambda s: resolve(TVar("a"), s) == TCon("int") and resolve(TVar("b"), s) == TCon("int"))(unify(TFun((TVar("a"),), TVar("a")), TFun((TCon("int"),), TVar("b")), {}))
--- check test | Chains of variables resolve all the way, inside function types too
resolve(TFun((TVar("x"),), TVar("y")), {TVar("x"): TVar("y"), TVar("y"): TFun((), TVar("z")), TVar("z"): TCon("bool")}) == TFun((TFun((), TCon("bool")),), TFun((), TCon("bool")))

(lambda s: (unify(TVar("q"), TCon("int"), s), s)[1] == {TVar("p"): TCon("bool")} and unify(TVar("p"), TCon("bool"), s) == s and unify(TVar("v"), TVar("v"), {}) == {})({TVar("p"): TCon("bool")})

+++ problem | Names used before they exist
--- task
Semantic analysis catches misspelt and out-of-scope names before a program runs. Write `undefined_names(source)`, which parses a Comet program (the starter gives the lexer and parser) and returns the list of names, in the order they are met, used by a `Var` or an `Assign` that refer to no declaration in scope. The rules are lesson 7's and lesson 12's:

- Statements are checked in order. `let x = e;` checks e first, then declares x in the current scope. `x = e;` checks e, then the name x.
- A block (`if`, `else`, `while` bodies) opens a new scope that ends with the block.
- `fn f(params) { body }` declares f in the current scope **before** the body is checked (so recursion works); the parameters and the body share one new scope.
- Inside a function body (at any depth), a name that is declared at the **top level** of the program (by a top-level `let` or `fn`, even later in the text) counts as declared: top-level names are late-bound in function bodies. Outside functions there is no such exception.
- Expressions are checked left to right; a call checks its callee, then its arguments. The same undefined name used twice is reported twice.

For example, `undefined_names("let a = b; fn f(p) { print p + later + r; } let later = 1; if a { let t = 1; } print t;")` is `["b", "r", "t"]`.
--- starter
from dataclasses import dataclass

KEYWORDS = {"let", "fn", "return", "if", "else", "while", "print",
            "true", "false", "and", "or", "not"}
TWO_CHAR = {"==", "!=", "<=", ">=", "->"}
ONE_CHAR = set("+-*/%<>=(){},;:")
ESCAPES = {'"': '"', "\\": "\\", "n": "\n"}
DIGITS = "0123456789"
LETTERS = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ_"

@dataclass
class Token:
    kind: str
    text: str
    line: int
    col: int

class LexError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col

def tokenize(source):
    tokens = []
    i = 0
    line = 1
    col = 1
    n = len(source)

    def advance(count):
        nonlocal i, line, col
        for _ in range(count):
            if source[i] == "\n":
                line += 1
                col = 1
            else:
                col += 1
            i += 1

    while i < n:
        ch = source[i]
        start_line, start_col = line, col
        if ch in " \t\r\n":
            advance(1)
        elif ch == "#":
            while i < n and source[i] != "\n":
                advance(1)
        elif ch in DIGITS:
            j = i
            while j < n and source[j] in DIGITS:
                j += 1
            tokens.append(Token("NUMBER", source[i:j], start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch in LETTERS:
            j = i
            while j < n and (source[j] in LETTERS or source[j] in DIGITS):
                j += 1
            word = source[i:j]
            kind = "KEYWORD" if word in KEYWORDS else "IDENT"
            tokens.append(Token(kind, word, start_line, start_col))
            advance(j - i)
        elif ch == '"':
            advance(1)
            chars = []
            while True:
                if i >= n or source[i] == "\n":
                    raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                c = source[i]
                if c == '"':
                    advance(1)
                    break
                if c == "\\":
                    if i + 1 >= n or source[i + 1] == "\n":
                        raise LexError("unterminated string", start_line, start_col)
                    if source[i + 1] not in ESCAPES:
                        raise LexError("unknown escape", line, col)
                    chars.append(ESCAPES[source[i + 1]])
                    advance(2)
                else:
                    chars.append(c)
                    advance(1)
            tokens.append(Token("STRING", "".join(chars), start_line, start_col))
        elif source[i:i + 2] in TWO_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", source[i:i + 2], start_line, start_col))
            advance(2)
        elif ch in ONE_CHAR:
            tokens.append(Token("OP", ch, start_line, start_col))
            advance(1)
        else:
            raise LexError(f"unexpected character {ch!r}", start_line, start_col)
    tokens.append(Token("EOF", "", line, col))
    return tokens

class ParseError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.line = line
        self.col = col

COMPARE = ("==", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">=")
TYPES = ("int", "bool", "str")

class Parser:
    def __init__(self, tokens):
        self.tokens = tokens
        self.pos = 0

    def peek(self, ahead=0):
        return self.tokens[min(self.pos + ahead, len(self.tokens) - 1)]

    def at(self, *texts):
        tok = self.peek()
        return tok.kind in ("OP", "KEYWORD") and tok.text in texts

    def advance(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "EOF":
            self.pos += 1
        return tok

    def error(self, message):
        tok = self.peek()
        return ParseError(message, tok.line, tok.col)

    def expect(self, text):
        if not self.at(text):
            raise self.error(f"expected '{text}'")
        return self.advance()

    def expr(self):
        return self.or_expr()

    def or_expr(self):
        left = self.and_expr()
        while self.at("or"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.and_expr())
        return left

    def and_expr(self):
        left = self.not_expr()
        while self.at("and"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.not_expr())
        return left

    def not_expr(self):
        if self.at("not"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("not", self.not_expr())
        return self.compare()

    def compare(self):
        left = self.sum()
        if self.at(*COMPARE):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.sum())
            if self.at(*COMPARE):
                raise self.error("comparisons cannot be chained")
        return left

    def sum(self):
        left = self.product()
        while self.at("+", "-"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.product())
        return left

    def product(self):
        left = self.unary()
        while self.at("*", "/", "%"):
            op = self.advance().text
            left = Binary(op, left, self.unary())
        return left

    def unary(self):
        if self.at("-"):
            self.advance()
            return Unary("-", self.unary())
        return self.call()

    def call(self):
        expr = self.primary()
        while self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            args = []
            if not self.at(")"):
                args.append(self.expr())
                while self.at(","):
                    self.advance()
                    args.append(self.expr())
            self.expect(")")
            expr = Call(expr, args)
        return expr

    def primary(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind == "NUMBER":
            self.advance()
            return Num(int(tok.text))
        if tok.kind == "STRING":
            self.advance()
            return Str(tok.text)
        if tok.kind == "IDENT":
            self.advance()
            return Var(tok.text)
        if self.at("true", "false"):
            self.advance()
            return Bool(tok.text == "true")
        if self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            inner = self.expr()
            self.expect(")")
            return inner
        raise self.error("expected an expression")

    def program(self):
        stmts = []
        while self.peek().kind != "EOF":
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        return Program(stmts)

    def statement(self):
        if self.at("let"):
            return self.let_stmt()
        if self.at("print"):
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Print(value)
        if self.at("if"):
            return self.if_stmt()
        if self.at("while"):
            self.advance()
            cond = self.expr()
            return While(cond, self.block())
        if self.at("fn"):
            return self.fn_stmt()
        if self.at("return"):
            self.advance()
            value = None if self.at(";") else self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Return(value)
        nxt = self.peek(1)
        if self.peek().kind == "IDENT" and nxt.kind == "OP" and nxt.text == "=":
            name = self.advance().text
            self.advance()
            value = self.expr()
            self.expect(";")
            return Assign(name, value)
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return ExprStmt(value)

    def name(self):
        if self.peek().kind != "IDENT":
            raise self.error("expected a name")
        return self.advance().text

    def type_name(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "IDENT" or tok.text not in TYPES:
            raise self.error("expected a type")
        return self.advance().text

    def let_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        self.expect("=")
        value = self.expr()
        self.expect(";")
        return Let(name, type_, value)

    def if_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        cond = self.expr()
        then = self.block()
        else_ = None
        if self.at("else"):
            self.advance()
            else_ = self.if_stmt() if self.at("if") else self.block()
        return If(cond, then, else_)

    def block(self):
        self.expect("{")
        stmts = []
        while not self.at("}"):
            if self.peek().kind == "EOF":
                raise self.error("expected '}'")
            stmts.append(self.statement())
        self.advance()
        return Block(stmts)

    def param(self):
        name = self.name()
        type_ = None
        if self.at(":"):
            self.advance()
            type_ = self.type_name()
        return (name, type_)

    def fn_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        self.expect("(")
        params = []
        if not self.at(")"):
            params.append(self.param())
            while self.at(","):
                self.advance()
                params.append(self.param())
        self.expect(")")
        ret = None
        if self.at("->"):
            self.advance()
            ret = self.type_name()
        return Fn(name, params, ret, self.block())

def parse_program(tokens):
    return Parser(tokens).program()



def parse_expr(tokens):
    parser = Parser(tokens)
    tree = parser.expr()
    if parser.peek().kind != "EOF":
        raise parser.error("expected end of input")
    return tree


class CometError(Exception):
    pass


def comet_div(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q


def comet_mod(a, b):
    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)


def show(value):
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "true" if value else "false"
    return str(value)


def undefined_names(source):
    return []

            "true", "false", "and", "or", "not"}
